- [focus-ring](#focus-ring) replaces the neutral hairline with the stacked accent ring, 2px wide, which clears WCAG 3:1 and APCA Lc 30. The criteria above apply to it unchanged.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **The focus ring evidences 2.4.7, not 2.4.11, and 2.4.13 is not claimed (2026-09-17).** The earlier focus-ring contrast deferral and `GUIDELINES.md` §9 both cited 2.4.11 for the neutral hairline under the wrong criterion name. Both citations were wrong in the same way, and the deferral is where the error started. Verified against the W3C Understanding pages on the day of this entry: **2.4.11 is *Focus Not Obscured (Minimum)*, Level AA**, and ***Focus Appearance* is 2.4.13, Level AAA**. What the ring work actually evidences is **2.4.7 Focus Visible (A)**, plus a contribution to **1.4.11 (AA)** through the ≥3:1 hairline. It does not evidence 2.4.13 either, because that criterion's 2px-perimeter and area test has never been run here. **Corrected in place rather than silently**, the way [soft-fill-text-exception](#soft-fill-text-exception) corrected a misapplied large/bold provision for solid fills, because the wrong number was shipped to readers in `GUIDELINES.md` and in `dist/DECISIONS.md`. The real 2.4.11 is now claimed separately and on its own evidence in §9: the system ships no sticky or fixed page chrome, and the one obligation it hands a consumer is to pair `--ds-appshell-header-height` with `scroll-padding-top` if they make the header sticky themselves.

### form-error-contract

**Tags.** `ACCESSIBILITY`, `COMPONENTS`. **Ruled.** 2026-09-17.

**`Field` carries the system's form error contract, and success criterion 3.3.3 belongs to the system only where a component writes the message.**

**The contract.**

| Criterion | What the system does |
| --- | --- |
| 3.3.1 | A `validation` message is tied to its control by `aria-describedby`, and the error tone sets `aria-invalid`. |
| 1.4.1 | The tone glyph is `aria-hidden`, so the words carry the meaning and colour never carries it alone. |
| 3.3.2 | `Field.Label` is a real `htmlFor` label. A control whose focusable node cannot take that label names itself with `useOptionalFieldLabelId()`. Components warn in development when no accessible name is supplied. |

**Announcements.** `role="alert"` belongs to the error tone alone, so a warning or a success message does not interrupt.

**Groups.** `FieldGroup` omits `aria-invalid` on purpose, because on a group it announces on every item. It appends the group message id to each item's `aria-describedby` instead, so a tab stop that arrives after the error still announces it.

**Who owns 3.3.3.** The criterion asks the message to say what input would be accepted. This moves the obligation to whoever writes the message, and it is not a gap.

- `NumberInput`, `DateInput` and `TimeInput` write that message themselves, so the system owns the criterion there.
- For `TextField`, `TextArea` and `Select` the consumer writes the message, so the consumer owns the criterion.

The rule in [support-text-slot](#support-text-slot) that a message steers toward the fix is this criterion.

**Changed from.** `Field` carried the same contract before this entry, but no document named a single 3.3 criterion.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-09-17. No later ruling amends it.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **The form error contract is ruled, and 3.3.3 is only ours where the component writes the copy (2026-09-17).** `Field` has carried a complete error contract since it was built and **no document named a single 3.3.x criterion** until this entry, which made the system's largest area of genuine conformance also its largest documentation hole. The contract: a `validation` message is associated by `aria-describedby` with `aria-invalid` set from the error tone (**3.3.1**); `role="alert"` is reserved for the error tone so warning and success do not interrupt; the tone glyph is `aria-hidden` so the words carry the meaning, never the colour (**1.4.1**); `Field.Label` is a real `htmlFor` label with `useOptionalFieldLabelId()` for controls whose focusable node cannot be labelled that way, and ten components dev-warn when no name is supplied (**3.3.2**); `FieldGroup` deliberately omits `aria-invalid` because it over-announces on every item, and appends the group message id onto each item's `aria-describedby` instead, so a tab stop arriving after the error still hears it. **The limit, stated because it is a transfer of obligation rather than a gap:** 3.3.3 asks the message to say what would be *accepted*. `NumberInput`, `DateInput` and `TimeInput` generate exactly that copy themselves. For `TextField`, `TextArea` and `Select` the message is yours, and so is the criterion. [support-text-slot](#support-text-slot)'s "steers toward the fix" was always this rule; it just never cited the number.

### overlay-dismissible-gap

**Tags.** `ACCESSIBILITY`, `COMPONENTS`. **Ruled.** 2026-09-17.

**`Overlay`'s hover scrim fails WCAG 1.4.13 Dismissible, and the gap is recorded, not fixed.**

**What you see.** `Overlay` reveals its scrim with CSS `:hover` and `:focus-within` rules alone, with no keydown handler anywhere in the component. The scrim is hoverable and persistent, but nothing removes it short of moving the pointer or focus.

**Why it fails.** The Dismissible exemption does not apply, because the scrim covers `inset: 0` of the required `media` node and so hides real content. Every other hover-or-focus surface passes: Tooltip, HoverCard and menu submenus inherit the three properties from Radix, and the `TopNav` flyouts implement them by hand.

**Gap.** The fix is a `dismissed` state, set on Escape and cleared on pointer leave or focus out, expressed as a data attribute the reveal rules exclude. That is a component change with its own evidence to gather, so it stays outside this ruling, under the rule that a change contains only what it claims.

**Changed from.** No earlier ruling recorded the gap. [overlay-hover-scrim](#overlay-hover-scrim) defined the reveal with no way to dismiss it.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-09-17. No later ruling amends it.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **`Overlay`'s hover scrim fails 1.4.13 Dismissible, recorded not fixed (2026-09-17).** Every other hover-or-focus surface in the system passes the criterion's three properties: Tooltip, HoverCard and menu submenus inherit dismissible, hoverable and persistent from Radix, and the `TopNav` flyouts hand-wire the same three. `Overlay` is the one hand-rolled reveal, and it is CSS-only: `:hover` and `:focus-within` rules paint a scrim over the media, with no keydown handler anywhere in the component. It is hoverable (the scrim sits inside the hovered container) and persistent (nothing times out), and it is **not dismissible** — nothing removes it without moving the pointer or focus. The Dismissible exemption does not apply, because the scrim paints across `inset: 0` of a required `media` node, so it obscures real content. **Not fixed here** under the rule that a change contains only what it claims: the correct fix is a `dismissed` state set on Escape, cleared on pointer-leave or focus-out, expressed as a data attribute the reveal rules exclude, and that is a component change with its own evidence to gather.

### dragging-movement-gaps

**Tags.** `ACCESSIBILITY`, `COMPONENTS`. **Ruled.** 2026-09-17.

**`ResizeHandle` and `Lightbox` pan fail WCAG 2.5.7 Dragging Movements, and a keyboard alternative does not fix either.**

**Why a key path is not enough.** WCAG 2.5.7 asks for a single-pointer alternative to a drag. W3C states that keyboard equivalence does not meet the criterion by itself, so arrow keys satisfy 2.1.1 and nothing more. [reorder-single-pointer-path](#reorder-single-pointer-path) applies the same distinction to reorder.

**Failures.**

- `ResizeHandle`: a drag from `onPointerDown` is the only pointer route to a size. Its double-click toggles collapse, not resize, and does nothing unless `collapsible` is set, which defaults to false. The gap reaches the resizable panels of `Layout` and `SideNav`.
- `Lightbox` pan: drag only, with no key route, because the arrow keys move through the gallery. A zoom resets the pan to the origin, so without a drag the edges of a 2x image are out of reach. This half also fails 2.1.1, the cheaper failure to close.

**Not essential.** Neither drag is essential under the criterion's test. The worked example W3C gives is a map with direction buttons beside the drag.

**Passes.**

- `Slider`: a click on the track sets the value, technique G216.
- `ScrollArea` and `Carousel`: the user agent scrolls them, and the criterion exempts that.
- `Toast`: a Dismiss button sits beside the swipe at all times.
- `FileInput`: the drop adds to a native file input.

**Gap.** Recorded and not fixed, for the reason recorded in [overlay-dismissible-gap](#overlay-dismissible-gap): a change contains only what it claims, and each fix is a component change with its own evidence to gather.

**Changed from.** No earlier ruling covered this.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-09-17. No later ruling amends it.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **Two components fail 2.5.7 Dragging Movements, and a keyboard alternative does not fix either (2026-09-17).** The distinction, recorded so it is not re-litigated: W3C states that keyboard equivalence "does not automatically meet this success criterion", because 2.5.7 asks for a **single-pointer** alternative to a drag. Arrow keys earn 2.1.1 and nothing more. **`ResizeHandle`** exposes `onPointerDown` as the only pointer route to a size; its double-click toggles *collapse*, not resize, and early-returns unless `collapsible`, which defaults false. It reaches `Layout` resizable panels and `SideNav`. **`Lightbox` pan** is worse: it is drag-only *and* keyboard-less, because the arrow keys are already spent on gallery navigation and no branch touches pan. Zooming resets pan to origin, so without a drag the edges of a 2× image are unreachable by any means. That half is also a **2.1.1** failure, which is the cheaper one to close. Neither is essential under the criterion's two-limb test: W3C's own worked example is a map with directional buttons beside the drag. **What passes, and why, so it is not re-audited:** `Slider` (clicking the track sets the value, technique G216), `ScrollArea` and `Carousel` (the scrolling is the user agent's, which the criterion exempts), `Toast` (an unconditional Dismiss button beside the swipe), `FileInput` (the drop is additive to a native file input). **Recorded not fixed**, same reason as [overlay-dismissible-gap](#overlay-dismissible-gap).

### text-spacing-control-box

**Tags.** `ACCESSIBILITY`, `SIZING`. **Ruled.** 2026-09-17.

**The box law sets `height: auto` beside its `min-height`, so a button grows to hold a label that wraps under the WCAG 1.4.12 text spacing overrides.**

**What you see.** At default text metrics no control box moves. Under a reader's 1.4.12 overrides a label that wraps to two lines grows its button, and the glyphs stay on the fill their contrast was measured against.

**Why.** Radix writes `height: var(--base-button-height)` on every variant but ghost, and the `min-height` of [control-box-per-step](#control-box-per-step) resolved to the same value, so the box stayed fixed. A size 3 button with a wrapped label held 44px of text in a 40px box, and since `.rt-BaseButton` sets no `overflow`, the label escaped the fill.

**Rule.** `.radix-themes .rt-BaseButton` declares `height: auto` and `min-height: max(var(--base-button-height), 24px)` at the same (0,2,0) specificity, so the step height is a floor and not a fixed box. Ghost buttons and the menu, option, `ToggleGroup`, `TopNav` and `SideNav` rows sized on `min-height` already, and they grew before this ruling.

**Boundary.** Layer 1 of the box law, which says a control's box equals its step, holds at default text metrics. `TEXT_SPACING_STORIES` in `src/foundations/boxLaw.ts` names the one story that renders under the overrides, where layer 1 still measures and prints but does not fail.

**Guard.** The ControlBoxUnderTextSpacing story in `_internal/Control box` renders the twelve priority and size combinations at a width that forces a wrap under the overrides, and fails when a label lands outside its own box. Two fixture checks confirm that the overrides apply and that a label wraps.

**Changed from.** The box law set `min-height` alone, and its comment claimed that a taller control could still grow. The claim held only for ghost buttons, so under the overrides a wrapped label escaped a box of fixed height.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-09-17. No later ruling amends it.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **The control box is frozen, so 1.4.12 Text Spacing is an exposure, and [control-box-per-step](#control-box-per-step)'s comment claimed otherwise (2026-09-17).** [control-box-per-step](#control-box-per-step)'s box law writes `min-height: max(var(--base-button-height), 24px)`, and the comment beside it tells the next reader that `min-*` was chosen "so a control that legitimately needs to be taller (a wrapped label, a two-line composite) still can be". **That sentence is false for every variant except ghost**, and measurably so. Radix writes `height: var(--base-button-height)` on `.rt-BaseButton:where(:not(.rt-variant-ghost))`, and the system's `min-height` resolves to the *same value*, so it is inert at `scaling >= 1` and the used height is the vendor's. Measured in real Chrome at size 3: a 190px-wide solid button holding "Save and continue" renders one 20px line inside a 40px box at default spacing, and **two lines totalling 44px inside the same 40px box** under the 1.4.12 overrides. `.rt-BaseButton` sets no `overflow`, so the label is not clipped, it **escapes the fill** — which on a solid variant also means the glyphs leave the background their contrast was measured against. Single-line controls survive by arithmetic (1.5 × 14px inside 32px), and the menu, option, `ToggleGroup`, `TopNav` and `SideNav` geometries are all genuinely on `min-height` and do grow. **FIXED 2026-09-17, by ruling.** `height: auto` now sits beside the `min-height` in the box law at the same (0,2,0) specificity, handing the box back to the content so `min-height` is the floor it always claimed to be. **Re-measured before shipping, because the [control-box-per-step](#control-box-per-step) evidence had to survive it:** 548 `.rt-BaseButton` boxes across 72 docs pages, plus the 111 controls in both [control-box-per-step](#control-box-per-step) manifest stories including the 90% scaling one. **Nothing visible moved.** The single box that changed is a `visibility: hidden` specimen inside a `0x0; overflow: hidden` parent on the AlertDialog usage page, which was already overflowing at rest — so the fix repaired a latent defect rather than introducing a change. Under the overrides the size-3 specimen goes from a 44px label in a frozen 40px box to a 48px box with zero escape. **The law it contradicts, reconciled rather than ignored:** the box law's layer 1 asserts a control's box EQUALS its step and has no story exemptions, which forbids exactly the growth this fix introduces. `boxLaw.ts` now states the boundary — layer 1 is measured at DEFAULT text metrics and is not a claim about a page a reader has restyled — and `TEXT_SPACING_STORIES` names the one story that renders under the overrides, where layer 1 still measures and prints but does not throw. **Mechanism:** `_internal/Control box` → *ControlBoxUnderTextSpacing* renders all twelve priority-and-size combinations at a width that forces a wrap under the overrides and fails if any label lands outside its own box. It carries two fixture arms, because both failure modes pass vacuously: one asserting the overrides are actually in force, one asserting a label actually wrapped. Verified red by deleting the declaration and by restoring the vendor step, green again on restore.

### showcases-and-fixture

**Tags.** `DOCUMENTATION`, `ACCESSIBILITY`, `CONTRIBUTING`. **Ruled.** 2026-09-18.

**The scenario directory holds showcases that assert nothing and one composition fixture that does.**

**Showcases.** Eight recreations of familiar kinds of interface, at rest and full-bleed, with exactly one story and no `play`. Three are AI-native (code editor, assistant, agent run), two carry AI features and three are traditional, and each keeps a generic name, because it is a generic version of a familiar product.

**Fixture.** `src/scenarios/_composition.stories.tsx` is the dense page that composes many system components, carries a `play` and runs under axe.

**Axe.** Axe is off on every showcase, which `SHOWCASE_AXE_OFF` lists. The fixture stays in `SCENARIO_CONTRAST_EXEMPT` under the original rule of [scenario-axe-carve-outs](#scenario-axe-carve-outs), which exempts `color-contrast` and nothing else, and a file in both registers fails. The story suite still renders every showcase, so a crash still fails the run.

**Why.** A probe calls for density, minimal setup and interaction that runs itself, and a showcase calls for none of these, so one page cannot do both jobs. Axe is off rather than partly off, because a page that silences three named rules still implies the rest passed, and a showcase makes no such claim.

**Cost.** The fixture is the one page-level structural check in the system, and it found the unnamed `Popover` panel of [popover-accessible-name](#popover-accessible-name), which no unit story caught. A guard holds that the fixture exists, carries a `play` and imports at least twelve system components, and a fixture thinner than that reopens this ruling rather than relaxes the guard.

**Changed from.** Six scenario pages each ran a `play` on open, wrapped a main column of 460 to 760px in `_storyKit`'s `Page`, and showed invented screens for products no reader knows. [scenario-axe-carve-outs](#scenario-axe-carve-outs) covered all six, and this ruling narrows it to the fixture.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-09-18.

- [sidebar-order](#sidebar-order) moves the eight showcases from the sidebar root into the `UI examples` folder after `Components`, and leaves the rest of this ruling as it stands.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **The scenario directory splits into showcases that assert nothing and one fixture that does; [scenario-axe-carve-outs](#scenario-axe-carve-outs) is narrowed, not loosened (2026-09-18).** The six scenario pages failed for three reasons. **(1)** Every page carried a `play`, and Storybook runs `play` on open, so each screen greeted the reader mid-gesture. **(2)** Every page wrapped in `_storyKit`'s `Page`/`PageHeader` and hardcoded `maxWidth` on the main column — 460, 620, 700, 720, 720, 760 — which is the reading measure applied to app chrome. `--ds-text-measure` governs PROSE; nothing justified compressing a data table to 700px. **(3)** They depicted invented mid-workflow screens for products no reader knows, so a reader had no familiar behaviour to judge ours against. **The root cause behind all three is that they were built test-first.** They were composition probes for the axe suite that were also being asked to serve as the showcase, and a probe wants exactly what a showcase does not: maximum density, minimum setup, and self-driving interaction. **Ruling: separate the two jobs.** Eight **showcase recreations** of recognisable interface archetypes, rendered at rest, full-bleed, at root level in the sidebar, deliberately generic in name because they are generic versions of familiar products rather than depictions of any one. Three are AI-native (code editor, assistant, agent run), two carry AI affordances, three are traditional. One **composition fixture**, `_composition.stories.tsx`, inherits the probe role. **Axe is OFF wholesale on the showcases, and this is the part that amends [scenario-axe-carve-outs](#scenario-axe-carve-outs).** [scenario-axe-carve-outs](#scenario-axe-carve-outs)'s mechanism was an arm reading "a scenario page may scope off `color-contrast` and nothing else", which is precisely what turning axe off violates. Rather than widen that arm until it stops meaning anything, the register splits: `SHOWCASE_AXE_OFF` for pages that assert nothing, `SCENARIO_CONTRAST_EXEMPT` for the fixture under [scenario-axe-carve-outs](#scenario-axe-carve-outs)'s original rule, unchanged and still citation-checked. A file in both registers fails. **Why off rather than partly off:** a page that silences three named rules still implies the rest passed, and a showcase must make no such claim. Off or on. The showcases keep a free smoke test regardless, because the story suite renders every story and a crash still fails the lane. **The cost, stated rather than buried:** the fixture is now the only page-level structural check in the system, and the composition suite's one unique harvest in fifteen days was the unnamed `Popover` panel that became [popover-accessible-name](#popover-accessible-name), a defect no unit story caught. So a guard asserts the fixture still exists, still carries a `play` (axe cannot inspect a panel that never opened), and still imports at least twelve system components. If it is ever thinned below that, the trade stops being affordable and this entry should be revisited rather than the guard relaxed. **Correction recorded, because it was asserted before it was checked:** the claim that a third-party brand name in a title would trip a lineage guard was wrong. `no-lineage.node-check.ts` scans only `src/components/ui` and bans the porting-provenance vocabulary, not product names. Generic naming stands on the ruling's own reasoning alone, which is sufficient.

### avatar-shape-perceptibility

**Tags.** `ACCESSIBILITY`, `COMPONENTS`. **Ruled.** 2026-09-19.

**The soft `Avatar` circle reads far under 3:1 against the page, and the gap stays recorded and unfixed, because every fix repaints every avatar.**

**What you see.** Measured on 2026-09-19, the fallback circle read 1.09:1 against the page in light and 1.24:1 in dark. At 20px the circle disappears and only the initials read, so the element is not recognisable as an avatar.

**Cause.** `Avatar` is locked to `variant="soft"` and does not expose `variant`, because initials on a solid fill failed the floor for text on a solid fill. That lock fixed the text contrast and left the circle unmeasured.

**Not covered.** The initials are not a text-contrast defect: they read 4.77:1 to 13.38:1 across twelve accent and appearance pairs. Nor is the circle cleanly a WCAG 1.4.11 failure, because the letters carry the meaning and the circle is a decorative container. It is a perceptibility defect.

**Gap.** A 3:1 boundary is out of reach while the fill stays soft:

- No shipped stroke token clears 3:1 in light. A ring at `--ds-stroke-strong` reads 3.02:1 in dark and 1.91:1 in light.
- A stronger fill trades one floor for the other. At `accent-a7` the circle reaches 2.43:1 in dark and the initials drop to 3.69:1, under their floor.

The choice between a heavier ring, a stronger fill and the current state belongs to the maintainer, with a review of its own. On 2026-09-19 no contrast guard measured a part against the surface behind it, so no guard caught this pair.

**Changed from.** No earlier ruling covered the circle. The lock to `soft` came from the 3:1 floor of that date for text on a solid fill, which [text-on-solid-fill-contrast](#text-on-solid-fill-contrast) later raised.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-09-19. No later ruling amends it.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **The `Avatar` shape is imperceptible against the page, and the ruling that locked it to `soft` is why (2026-09-19).** The ruling that set the 3:1 floor for text on a solid fill locked `Avatar` to `variant="soft"` and stopped exposing `variant`, because solid-fill initials fail the AA large/bold guardrail. That solved the TEXT contrast and nobody measured the other half. **Measured 2026-09-19, compositing alpha over the page rather than rastering it opaque:** the fallback chip sits at **1.09:1 in light and 1.24:1 in dark** against the page behind it. The consequence: the element is not recognisable as an avatar, because at 20px the circle is invisible and only the initials read. **The initials themselves are fine and this is not a text-contrast defect:** measured across twelve accent and appearance combinations, 4.77:1 (tomato light) to 13.38:1 (gold light). **Nor is it cleanly a 1.4.11 failure**, because the letters carry the meaning and the circle is a decorative container, so the criterion's "graphical object required to understand the content" is arguable rather than settled. It is a perceptibility defect. **Why it is recorded rather than fixed: no option is free, and all of them repaint every avatar in the system.** Measured: a ring at `--ds-stroke-weak` reaches 1.66:1 dark and 1.41:1 light, at `--ds-stroke-strong` 3.02:1 dark but only 1.91:1 light — no shipped stroke token clears 3:1 in light. Strengthening the fill instead trades one floor for the other: `accent-a5` gives chip 1.67/1.34 with initials still at 5.38/5.10, `accent-a6` gives 1.99/1.53 with initials at 4.50/4.71, and `accent-a7` gets the chip to 2.43 dark but drops the initials to **3.69**, under the floor. **So a 3:1 avatar boundary is unreachable while the fill stays soft**, and choosing between a heavier ring, a stronger fill, and accepting the current state is a decision for the maintainer, with its own review. **Mechanism gap:** nothing measures a chip against the surface BEHIND it. Every contrast guard in this repo measures foreground against its own background, which is exactly why this survived — the pairing that failed is one no lane looks at.

## Component layer

### system-wrapper-layer

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`, `CONTRIBUTING`. **Ruled.** 2026-06-19.

**The system's opinionated wrappers narrow each Radix API to the options the system supports, and they are what the package exports.**

**What you see.** Each wrapper exposes only the options the system supports. In the repository the wrappers live in `src/components/ui/`, and their stories sit under `Components/<Category>/<Name>` in Storybook.

**Changed from.** No earlier ruling covered this.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-06-19.

- [sidebar-order](#sidebar-order) moves the wrapper stories from `System/*` to `Components/*`, the name this ruling first kept for raw Radix showcases. Those showcases no longer exist.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **Opinionated wrappers live in `src/components/ui/` (`System/*` stories); raw Radix showcases stay under `Components/*`.** Wrappers narrow the API to system-supported options.

### button-priority

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`. **Ruled.** 2026-06-19.

**`Button` and `IconButton` take a `priority` prop in place of Radix's `variant`, and a page holds one solid primary.**

**Priorities.**

| `priority` | Radix variant | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `primary` | `solid` | Opt in, for the one most consequential action on a page |
| `secondary` | `surface` | The default |
| `tertiary` | `ghost` | The lowest emphasis |

**Not exposed.** The `variant` prop, so the `soft`, `outline` and `classic` skins of Radix stay out of reach of the system buttons.

**Exception.** A danger solid from `tone="danger"` does not count against the one solid primary, so a safe `primary` and a danger solid may share a dialog ([destructive-tone](#destructive-tone)).

**Changed from.** No earlier ruling covered this.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-06-19.

- [destructive-tone](#destructive-tone) adds `tone="danger"` beside `priority` and exempts a danger solid from the one-solid-primary budget.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **`Button`/`IconButton` expose `priority` (primary/secondary/tertiary → solid/surface/ghost), not `variant`.** Default `secondary`; `primary` (solid) is opt-in — **one solid primary per page**.

### soft-variant-scope

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`, `COLOUR`. **Ruled.** 2026-06-19.

**The `soft` variant is for display parts only, and interactive and input components use `surface`.**

**Applies to.**

- Display and decorative parts, such as `Badge` and `Callout`, may use `soft`. `Progress` is the exception and does not offer it ([colour-prop-and-high-contrast](#colour-prop-and-high-contrast)).
- Interactive and input components use `surface`.
- The system uses neither `outline` nor `classic`. `Kbd` alone keeps `classic` available for a caller who asks for the raised key ([kbd-default-variant](#kbd-default-variant)).

**Why.** `surface` makes a control identifiable, separates it from the background and gives hover feedback. The flat `soft` tint does none of these.

**Changed from.** No earlier ruling covered this.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-06-19.

- [colour-prop-and-high-contrast](#colour-prop-and-high-contrast) removes `soft` from `Switch`, `Slider` and `Progress` as a type error, a display part included.
- [kbd-default-variant](#kbd-default-variant) defaults `Kbd` to `soft` and keeps `classic` available on it.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **`soft` is banned on inputs/interactive controls; allowed only on display/decorative UI** (Badge, Callout). Interactive/input components use **`surface`** (identifiable, separated from bg, hover feedback). `outline`/`classic` unused everywhere.

### floating-surface-fill

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`, `TOKENS`. **Ruled.** 2026-06-19.

**A floating surface paints an opaque fill.**

**Applies to.** `Select.Content` and every other menu and popover. Later rulings apply the same fill to the tooltip, the dialog panel, the date pickers, the command palette and the toast.

**What you see.** The panel takes the `solid` variant and paints `--ds-bg-overlay`, so no content beneath it is visible.

**Exception.** A `soft` or translucent fill is allowed only over an opaque backstop, such as the toast tint painted on an opaque `--ds-bg-overlay` base ([toast-feedback-tier](#toast-feedback-tier)).

**Changed from.** No earlier ruling covered this.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-06-19. No later ruling amends it.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **Floating surfaces are `solid` (opaque)** — `Select.Content` and other menus/popovers, per the layering rule. Never `soft`/translucent without an opaque backstop.

### docs-page-spine

**Tags.** `DOCUMENTATION`. **Ruled.** 2026-06-19.

**Every component page follows one story spine, and its token spec is read live from the CSS, never typed by hand.**

**The spine.**

| Story | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `Anatomy`, full pages only | The labelled callout diagram of the component, alone |
| `Usage` | The guidance, realistic situations that react to the appearance, accent and size toolbar, the do and do not pairs, and last the live token spec |
| `Keyboard`, `MenuStates`, where they apply | The keyboard contract and the menu states |
| `Props` | The args-driven controls and the full prop table, the only place Controls and Actions live |
| `History` | The rulings the component encodes and its changelog |

**Order.** A full page opens on `Anatomy` and a lite page on its single `Usage` story, and every page closes on `Props` and then `History`.

**Token spec.** The spec is parsed from the CSS and resolved against the rendered page, so it cannot drift from the tokens. The shared primitives live in `_storyKit.tsx`.

**Why.** A reader lands on the component itself, the diagram on a full page or the docs story on a lite one. History is provenance a reader consults, so it comes last, and a reader meets the tokens after the situations that motivate them.

**Changed from.** Each component had four stories, `History`, `Anatomy`, `Usage` and `Playground`, in that order, with the token spec under the Anatomy diagram, and a lite page named its single docs story `Overview`.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-06-19.

- Amended 2026-07-30: the token spec moved from `Anatomy` to the end of `Usage`, and the lite story `Overview` became `Usage`.
- Amended 2026-08-04: `History` moved from first to last, and `Playground` became `Props`, the name for a story that carries the full prop reference as well as the controls.
- [token-row-shape](#token-row-shape) sets the shape of a token row, and [measured-token-rows](#measured-token-rows) requires the row to measure the element that paints the part.
- [docs-page-header](#docs-page-header) rules how each page opens.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **Per-component Storybook story template (the `System/Button` reference, 2026-06-19).** Every `System/*` component gets four stories: **History** (rulings it encodes + Changelog), **Anatomy** (labeled callout diagram + token spec), **Usage** (guidance → realistic situations reacting to the appearance/accent/size toolbar → do/don't), **Playground** (args-driven; the only place Controls + Actions live). **Ruling:** the token spec MUST be read live from the CSS, never hand-typed, so it can't drift from the tokens. Implementation (the `?raw` alias parse, DOM-resolved hex, shared primitives) lives in `_storyKit.tsx`. **Amended 2026-07-30:** the token spec MOVES off Anatomy onto **Usage** on every full page. Anatomy is now the callout diagram **alone** — the labeled specimen and nothing under it; **Usage** carries the guidance, the realistic scenarios, the do/don'ts, and **closes with the live token spec**, so a reader meets the tokens after the situations that motivate them rather than before. The lite pages' single docs story is renamed **`Usage`** (was `Overview`) — same content, same floor — so ONE grammar reads across both tiers: History · Anatomy (full only) · Usage · [Keyboard] · Playground. The live-read requirement above is **unchanged** — the spec is still parsed from the CSS and resolved off the DOM, never hand-typed; only the story it lands in moved. **Amended 2026-08-04 (ruled) — the spine is REORDERED and `Playground` is RENAMED `Props`:** the grammar is now **Anatomy (full) | Usage (lite) · [Keyboard] · [MenuStates] · Props · History**. Two changes, one reason each. **(a) History moves from first to last.** It is the rulings a component encodes plus its changelog — provenance a reader consults, not the page they land on; opening on it put the least urgent page first on all 90 components. The landing page is now the component itself: the diagram on a full page, the single docs story on a lite one. **(b) `Playground` → `Props`.** The story had always carried the full prop reference as well as the args-driven controls — 89 of the 90 pages render `<PropTable>` inside it — and the old name advertised only half of that, so a reader looking for the properties had no reason to open it. Everything about the story's CONTENT is unchanged; it is still the only place Controls + Actions live. Enforced by `src/foundations/story-order.node-check.ts`, which now gates first-is-Anatomy-or-Usage, last-is-History, and Props-before-it, plus an anti-rot arm failing any story file that still mentions the old name. Two mechanisms keyed on the old name moved with it: `boxLaw.ts`'s Layer-2 exemption (the arg-driven story is excused from the box law because its size is whatever the reader last set) and `page-header.node-check.ts`'s STORY_ROLES vocabulary.

### field-shell

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`. **Ruled.** 2026-06-23.

**Every input renders inside one shared `Field` shell, which owns the label, the validation paint and the message.**

**Anatomy.** `Field.Root`, `Field.Label` and `Field.Message`, with `useFieldControl()`, own the label row and the validation row. The shell passes the control's `id` to `htmlFor`, `aria-describedby` and `aria-invalid` through context, and the control, such as `TextField`, renders as its body.

**Validation paint.** A validation state shows four cues, all from the accent-aware family tokens, so colour is never the only signal (WCAG 1.4.1) and every cue follows a brand collision shift:

- the input border, `--ds-stroke-{fam}` at step 8
- a tint, `--ds-fill-{fam}-weak`
- a Phosphor status glyph in the `fill` weight: `WarningCircle`, `Warning`, `CheckCircle` or `Info`
- a message in step-11 ink

**Mechanism.** A `[data-validation]` rule in `src/tokens/components.css` paints each state, with no `!important`. The value text stays neutral, `--ds-text-strong`.

**Focus.** A focused field wears the system ring of [focus-ring](#focus-ring), 2px outside its edge ([input-focus-ring-offset](#input-focus-ring-offset)). On focus, a validation state recolours only the border ([validation-focus-paint](#validation-focus-paint)).

**In-field controls.** An `inset` IconButton, `data-inset` and ghost by default, serves a control inside a field, with a hit area of at least 24 by 24 pixels (WCAG 2.5.8). A smaller visual size relative to the field is deferred.

**Changed from.** No shared shell existed, and the Radix text-field focus ring drew `accent-8` at 2.46:1, under the 3:1 that WCAG 1.4.11 sets for a focus indicator.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-06-23.

- [field-shell-adoption](#field-shell-adoption) puts `TextArea` and `Select` in the same shell.
- [horizontal-field-labels](#horizontal-field-labels) adds `direction`, which places the label beside the control.
- The two-colour focus ring, a ruling no longer in this ledger, replaced the neutral outer outline of this ruling with a `gray-12` hairline.
- [validation-focus-paint](#validation-focus-paint) removes the family glow from a focused field, so validation recolours only the border.
- [focus-ring](#focus-ring) replaces the ring with the stacked accent, 2px wide.
- [input-focus-ring-offset](#input-focus-ring-offset) places the ring 2px outside the field.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **Canonical input architecture — shared `Field` chrome (2026-06-23).** A compound `Field` shell (`Field.Root`/`Field.Label`/`Field.Message` + `useFieldControl()`) owns the label + validation rows and threads `id`→`htmlFor`/`aria-describedby`/`aria-invalid` via context; controls (`TextField`, later Select/TextArea) render as its body. Validation paints the input **border** (`--ds-stroke-{fam}`, step-8) + **tint** (`--ds-fill-{fam}-weak`) + a status **glyph** (Phosphor `fill`: WarningCircle/Warning/CheckCircle/Info) + a step-11 **message**, all from the accent-aware family tokens via `[data-validation]` in `tokens/components.css` (no `!important`) — colour-not-alone (1.4.1), brand-collision-following ([brand-collision-shift-table](#brand-collision-shift-table)/[oxblood-preset](#oxblood-preset)/[brand-status-collision-gate](#brand-status-collision-gate)). Input **value text stays neutral** (`--ds-text-strong`). **Resolves the earlier focus-ring contrast deferral:** rather than a parallel focus class, override Radix's own focus mechanism — `--text-field-focus-color` (was `--focus-8` = accent-8 = 2.46:1, fails 1.4.11) lifts to `accent-9`, and Radix's `:has(.rt-TextFieldInput:focus)` wrapper rule is overridden to a dual-tone ring: a **constant neutral outer outline** (`--ds-stroke-focus-outer`, light `#fff` / dark `gray-1` — the ≥3:1 backstop for pale families + the invariant "focused" affordance) + an **inner glow** that is `accent-9` by default and **adopts the validation family at step-9** (`--ds-fill-{fam}`) in a validation state, so focus reads as one coherent hue (the focus *signal* is the added ring + the user's navigation, not its colour). **(Focus-ring superseded by the two-colour focus ring: the "neutral outer outline" was the page colour in both modes and provided no contrast; replaced by a `gray-12` hairline.)** **New:** an `inset` IconButton (`data-inset`, ghost-default, ≥24×24 hit per 2.5.8) for in-field controls; the field-relative visual shrink is deferred.

### support-text-slot

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`. **Ruled.** 2026-06-23.

**`Field` and `TextField` show one support line under the control: the persistent description at rest, or the validation message in its place while a state is active.**

**What you see.**

- `description` is optional calm guidance in `--ds-text-weak`, shown at rest.
- A `validation.message` replaces it in the same slot while a state is active, and carries corrective copy that steers toward the fix.
- `aria-describedby` names whichever single line is shown.

**Why.** A field never shows a redundant helper and message together. Steady guidance belongs in `description`, so `info` is a flexible secondary tone and not a validation peer.

**Changed from.** `Field` and `TextField` had no persistent helper line, only the validation message.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-06-23. No later ruling amends it.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **Support-text slot — one slot, two sources (2026-06-23).** `Field`/`TextField` gain an optional persistent `description` (helper) — calm guidance shown at rest, in a weak neutral tone, wired into `aria-describedby`. A `validation.message` is conditional and **replaces** it in the same support-text slot when a state is active (carrying corrective copy that steers toward the fix), so the field never stacks a redundant helper + message; `aria-describedby` points to whichever single line is shown. This is the structural reason `info` is a flexible **secondary** tone, not a validation peer — steady guidance belongs in `description`, not a tone. Anatomy now leads with the **neutral default** state (decomposed into its real slots: label · info · end-slot · leading slot · value · trailing lane · description), validation moved to its own specimen, and the token table carries a **DEFAULT (rest)** group beside the four tones.

### group-validation

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`, `ACCESSIBILITY`. **Ruled.** 2026-06-23.

**A checkbox or radio group validates through one `FieldGroup` shell: the group name takes the status colour, the message sits below the set, and the group never carries `aria-invalid`.**

**What you see.** In a validation state the group label takes the family text colour (`--ds-text-{fam}`), and the corrective message with its status glyph sits below the whole set. The shell takes no tint and no border, and each checkbox or radio stays neutral.

**Applies to.** `CheckboxGroup` and `RadioGroup` inside `FieldGroup.Root`, with `FieldGroup.Label`, `FieldGroup.Description` and `FieldGroup.Message`.

**Semantics.**

- No `<fieldset>`: it would double the grouping with Radix's own `role="group"` or `radiogroup`, so the Radix group is the one named group.
- The root wires `aria-labelledby` to the label and `aria-describedby` to the active support text onto the Radix group.
- The message id also joins each item's `aria-describedby`, so a tab stop announces an error that already stands.
- `aria-invalid` never sits on the group, because it means nothing on `role="group"` or `radiogroup` and over-announces.

**Single checkbox.** A standalone `Checkbox` takes the same field treatment through optional `label`, `description` and `validation` props, and renders bare without `label`, as `TextField` does. This serves the consent or opt-in checkbox that can show an error, where `aria-invalid` is valid on the checkbox role.

**Gap.** The package does not export `FieldGroup`, and `CheckboxGroup` and `RadioGroup` take no `label` or `validation` of their own, so a consumer of the package has no published route to a group-level error message. The public entry point records this as a known gap.

**Changed from.** No earlier ruling covered group validation. [field-shell](#field-shell) gave a single control its label and validation shell on the same day.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-06-23. No later ruling amends it.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **Group validation — `FieldGroup`, one named group, no `aria-invalid` (2026-06-23).** `CheckboxGroup`/`RadioGroup` validate via a `FieldGroup` shell (`FieldGroup.Root`/`.Label`/`.Description`/`.Message`): a **non-fieldset** container where group-level validation is signalled by the **label (group name) adopting the family text colour** (`--ds-text-{fam}`) — **no shell tint or border** (kept flat); **individual item controls stay neutral**, and the corrective message sits **below the whole set**, so the group reads "has an error" via the red name + status glyph + message, not by recolouring every box or wrapping the set in a panel. **One named group (verified against the ARIA tree):** no `<fieldset>` — it would double-group with Radix's own `role=group`/`radiogroup`; instead the group root auto-wires `aria-labelledby` (the id'd label) + `aria-describedby` (active support text) onto the Radix group, and the message id is also appended to **each item's** `aria-describedby` so a tab stop announces a pre-existing error. **`aria-invalid` is never set on the group** (not meaningful on `role=group/radiogroup`; over-announces). A standalone single **`Checkbox` gains the same Field treatment via an optional `label`/`description`/`validation`** (bare without `label`; mirrors `TextField`) — the canonical consent/opt-in checkbox that can error (`aria-invalid` is valid on the checkbox role).

### item-description-slot

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`. **Ruled.** 2026-06-23.

**A CheckboxGroup or RadioGroup item can carry a description line under its label.**

**What you see.** `CheckboxGroup.Item` and `RadioGroup.Item` take an optional `description`, a secondary line under the item label for a price, a scope or a qualifier. It reads in `--ds-text-weak`, scaled to the group size.

**Accessibility.** The description is wired through `aria-describedby` to the item's checkbox or radio control.

**Alignment.** The control aligns to the title line, so a two-line option does not centre its box between the two lines. A `:has([data-field-item-desc])` rule overrides the centred alignment of the Radix item.

**Changed from.** A group item carried its label alone, with no slot for a secondary line.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-06-23. No later ruling amends it.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **Per-item description slot (2026-06-23).** `CheckboxGroup.Item`/`RadioGroup.Item` gain an optional `description` — a secondary line under the item label (price, scope, qualifier) in a weak neutral tone (`--ds-text-weak`, scaled to the group size), `aria-describedby`-wired to the item's `role=checkbox/radio` control. The control **top-aligns to the title line** (a `:has([data-field-item-desc])` override of Radix's centre-aligned item, so a two-line option doesn't float the box to the middle).

### field-shell-adoption

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`. **Ruled.** 2026-06-23.

**`TextArea` and `Select` take the same Field props as `TextField` and render inside `Field.Root`.**

**Props.** `label`, `info`, `endSlot`, `description` and `validation`, with the label above, accent-aware validation and the message below. A TextArea or Select given no label, validation or description stays bare, so existing usage is untouched.

**TextArea.** It mirrors TextField: validation paints a border and a tint on `.rt-TextAreaRoot`, and its focus ring keys on `:focus-within`. It keeps its resize handle, because the message sits below the control as a sibling and never meets the handle.

**Select.** The trigger is the form control, so `useOptionalFieldControl()` wires `id`, `aria-describedby` and `aria-invalid` onto the trigger's `role=combobox`. Validation paints `.rt-SelectTrigger` alone and holds through hover and open, because the `Content` panel is portaled out of the Field subtree, where no `[data-validation]` selector reaches it.

**Focus.** Each control overrides Radix's own focus selector, `:has(:focus)` on TextField, `:focus-within` on TextArea and `:focus-visible` on the Select trigger, with the system focus ring ([focus-ring](#focus-ring)). The `.radix-themes`-scoped selector outranks Radix's `:where()` rule, so no `!important` is needed.

**Changed from.** TextField alone took the Field props. TextArea and Select carried no label, description or validation of their own and kept Radix's focus ring.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-06-23.

- [validation-focus-paint](#validation-focus-paint) replaces the dual-tone ring with a neutral hairline, and validation recolours only the border.
- [focus-ring](#focus-ring) replaces the hairline with the accent ring, 2px wide, the same on every control.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **Select & TextArea adopt the Field shell (2026-06-23).** `TextArea` and `Select` gain the same `label`/`info`/`endSlot`/`description`/`validation` props as `TextField`, rendering inside `Field.Root` (label above, accent-aware validation, message below). **TextArea** mirrors TextField exactly (validation border+tint on `.rt-TextAreaRoot`; dual-tone focus ring on its `:focus-within` selector); **no resize lock** — the message is a sibling below, so the resize handle never collides with it. **Select** is compositional: the **trigger** is the form control, so `useOptionalFieldControl()` wires `id`/`aria-describedby`/`aria-invalid` onto it (valid on the trigger's `role=combobox`) and validation paints `.rt-SelectTrigger` (border+tint, persisting across hover/open) + a dual-tone ring on its `:focus-visible`. Both stay **bare** when no label/validation/description is passed (existing usage untouched). All validation CSS is **scoped to the trigger** — the `Content` panel is portaled out of the Field subtree, so a `[data-validation] .rt-SelectContent` selector would never match. Each control overrides Radix's OWN focus selector (TextField `:has(:focus)`, TextArea `:focus-within`, Select trigger `:focus-visible`) to the dual-tone WCAG ring — no `!important` (the `.radix-themes`-scoped selector beats Radix's `:where()`-wrapped rule). This shrinks the deferred focus-ring debt to Button/IconButton/Checkbox-Radio groups.

### field-family-anatomy

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`. **Ruled.** 2026-06-24.

**`TextField`, `Select` and `TextArea` share one label row and one support area, and differ only in the input between them.**

**Shared chrome.**

- The label row, `Field.Label`: label, info and end slot.
- The support area: `Field.Description`, which `Field.Message` replaces when a message shows.

**Select affixes.** The trigger reads, in order, leading icon, value or placeholder, clear control, caret.

- `icon` on `Select.Trigger` is a leading glyph that identifies the field and takes no input.
- `clearable` on the root adds a clear control that shows while a value is set, sits left of the caret, stays out of the tab order and resets the field to its placeholder.
- Both are overlays positioned in `components.css`, because Radix's `Select.Trigger` has no slots. The clear control's space comes from a `margin-right` on the inner box, because trigger padding would move Radix's caret, and the trigger takes `width: 100%` inside its wrapper.

**TextArea counter.** `showCount` with `maxLength` shows a live `current/max` counter at the bottom right of the support row, the dominant convention, and the label-row end slot stays free for general notes. The counter is `aria-hidden`, because the native `maxLength` conveys the limit.

**Not covered.** An inset loader on `Select`, which belongs to a searchable combobox rather than to shared input chrome. Only the `TextField` search keeps a transient spinner.

**Gap.** Three deferred items: a text prefix and suffix on `TextField`, a shared counter on `TextField`, and a convention for required and optional marking.

**Changed from.** No earlier ruling covered this.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-06-24.

- [select-selected-row](#select-selected-row) gives the clear control a keyboard equivalent: Backspace or Delete on the focused, closed trigger resets the value.
- [select-affix-width](#select-affix-width) removes the `width: 100%` the affix wrapper declared, so a `Select` keeps its own width in a flex row.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **Field family — unified anatomy + Select trigger affixes + TextArea counter (2026-06-24).** A cross-system audit (component.gallery: Material 3, Polaris, Carbon, Spectrum, Fluent, Atlassian) confirmed the **shared-chrome** contract: the **label row** (`Field.Label`: label · info · end-slot) and the **support area** (`Field.Description` ⇄ `Field.Message`, message replaces helper) are identical across `TextField`/`Select`/`TextArea` — only the **main input content** differs. **Select trigger affixes:** the trigger composes `[leading icon] · value/placeholder · [clear ✕] · [caret]` — `icon` on `Select.Trigger` (a non-interactive identification glyph), and `clearable` on the root (a clear ✕ that is **persistent while a value is set**, sits left of the caret, is **excluded from the tab order**, and resets to the placeholder). Both are **overlays** (Radix `Select.Trigger` has no slots) positioned in `components.css`; the value-gap is reserved via the inner box's `margin-right` (not trigger padding — that would push Radix's caret inward). The affixed trigger is forced `width:100%` (the wrapper breaks Radix's flex-stretch). **No inset loader** — it's a searchable-combobox/autocomplete affordance, not shared input chrome; only TextField's search keeps a transient spinner. **TextArea character counter:** `showCount` + `maxLength` renders a live `current/max` counter **bottom-right of the support row** (the dominant convention — M3/Polaris/Ant; the label-row end-slot stays for generic notes). The counter is `aria-hidden` (the native `maxLength` conveys the limit). **Surfaced gaps (deferred):** a first-class TextField text **prefix/suffix affix** (Material/Polaris), a shared **counter on TextField**, and a **required/optional marking** convention (Spectrum `necessityIndicator`).

### select-selected-row

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`, `COLOUR`. **Ruled.** 2026-06-26.

**A selected row in the open `Select` panel takes Radix's solid accent fill with no check mark, and weight 600 is its non-colour cue.**

**What you see.**

- The selected row takes `--ds-fill-selected` (accent-9), white `--on-accent` text and weight 600, with the gutter check mark hidden. It stays the solid fill whether or not it is also the active row.
- A non-selected active row takes the neutral `--ds-fill-hover`.
- Rows and group labels take symmetric logical padding that matches the trigger's inline padding at each size. The group label reads `--ds-text-weak` and the separator `--ds-stroke-weak`.
- A disabled current value keeps Radix's dimmed treatment.

**Accessibility.** Weight 600 is the WCAG 1.4.1 non-colour cue the check mark left behind, asserted on the rendered weight. The selected label is gated as `--on-accent` on the opaque accent-9 fill at 4.5:1 or more.

**Scope.** The rules use the compound selector `.radix-themes.rt-SelectContent`, because the portaled content node itself carries `.radix-themes` and a descendant selector never matches it. The re-skin is scoped `:where(:not(.rt-high-contrast))`, so a high-contrast `Select` keeps Radix's native check mark and accent-12 highlight.

**Keyboard.** Radix supplies the open keys, the arrow keys, Home and End, type-ahead jump, the skip over disabled rows, and Escape. With the closed trigger focused, Backspace or Delete resets a clearable value to the placeholder, the keyboard equivalent of the clear button, which sits outside the tab order (WCAG 2.1.1). A `Select.Empty` part renders a muted no-options line.

**Not covered.** Type-to-filter, async loading and multiple values. A static single-select listbox stays a listbox, and multiple values belong to `MultiSelect` ([multi-select-component](#multi-select-component)).

**Changed from.** The first cut, on 2026-06-26, marked the selected row with a stronger accent tint, `--ds-fill-selected-strong` (accent-a8), and weight 600, with a contrast helper and a distinctness gate against the hover fill. The correction of 2026-06-27 removed the token, the helper and the gate, because a solid accent fill is unmistakable against a gray hover.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-06-26, and corrected 2026-06-27.

- [multi-select-component](#multi-select-component) ships multiple values as the separate `MultiSelect` component, which this ruling first deferred.
- [toggle-button](#toggle-button) extends the weight-600 cue to the pressed `ToggleButton`.
- [focus-ring](#focus-ring) gives the active row the system focus ring as its edge.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **Select open-panel — selected row = Radix's solid fill, no checkmark (2026-06-26; corrected 2026-06-27).** **Corrected (2026-06-27):** the selected row is **Radix's own default solid selected styling — `--ds-fill-selected` (accent-9) + white `--on-accent` text + weight 600 — with the gutter checkmark hidden**; nothing invented. The selected row stays the solid accent fill whether or not it is also the active row; only *non-selected* rows take the neutral `--ds-fill-hover`. The invented `--ds-fill-selected-strong` (accent-a8) token, the `assertPairingOver` legibility helper, and the `deltaEOK` selected-vs-hover distinctness gate (`MIN_SELECTED_HOVER_DELTA_E`) are **removed** — a solid accent fill is unmistakable against a gray hover, so the distinctness math is moot. Kept: the hidden checkmark, symmetric logical padding, group-label/separator token binding, the disabled carve-out, the high-contrast carve-out. Weight 600 remains the non-colour WCAG 1.4.1 cue the checkmark left behind (asserted on the *rendered* weight); selected-label legibility is now gated as `--on-accent` on the opaque accent-9 fill ≥ 4.5. The original 2026-06-26 re-skin narrative (superseded) follows. — The open menu marks the **selected** option with a **stronger accent fill** (`--ds-fill-selected-strong` = accent-a8) + a **semibold (600) label**, dropping Radix's left-gutter checkmark; the active-descendant **highlight** is a neutral `--ds-fill-hover` (gray-a4), so persistent *selection* and transient *focus* read as two distinct layers (the selected+active row layers a4 over a8 via a same-colour gradient, staying accent-aware; dark `--ds-text-strong` stays legible on the composite). **Calibration:** the first cut used a faint `accent-a5` tint, which collapsed against the gray hover (both near-white). A cross-system audit (Atlassian, Ant, Material, Spectrum, Carbon, Primer, Radix, Polaris, Fluent) showed **no system separates selected from hover by a faint tint alone**; the no-checkmark systems carry the accent *hue* (text or a real fill). After comparing accent-text vs fill-strength, the **a8 fill** was chosen (selected-vs-hover ΔE-OK ~0.23 vs ~0.05 at a5). The gutter is dropped for **symmetric logical padding** matching the trigger's inline padding per size; the group label binds to `--ds-text-weak`, the separator to `--ds-stroke-weak`. **Weight 600 is the non-colour WCAG 1.4.1 cue** (asserted on the *rendered* weight); selected-label legibility is gated via `assertPairingOver` (text-strong on the flattened a8 fill = 6.7:1 ≥ 4.5), and selected-vs-hover distinctness via a `deltaEOK` floor (`MIN_SELECTED_HOVER_DELTA_E = 0.015`) swept across all 27 accents — a8 clears it by a wide margin everywhere. Scoped `.radix-themes.rt-SelectContent…` (the portaled Content *is* the `.radix-themes` node → **compound** selector, not descendant; no `!important`); **one new token** (`--ds-fill-selected-strong`). The whole re-skin is scoped `:where(:not(.rt-high-contrast))` — Radix's high-contrast variant keeps its native checkmark + accent-12 highlight. **Completeness pass (full single-select definition):** the keyboard contract (open keys, ↑/↓·Home/End, type-ahead *jump*, disabled-skip, Esc — all free from the Radix primitive) is now documented; the clearable ✕ gains a **keyboard equivalent** — Backspace/Delete on the focused closed trigger resets to the placeholder (WCAG 2.1.1), since the ✕ is `tabIndex=-1`; a `Select.Empty` part renders a muted no-options line; and the story now carries the full **menu anatomy diagram**, a **Properties** reference, and a **Keyboard** section. **Out of scope by ruling:** type-to-filter (→ a future `Combobox`), async loading, and multi-tags (→ `MultiSelect`/[multi-select-component](#multi-select-component)) — a static single-select listbox stays a listbox. **Multi-select ([multi-select-component](#multi-select-component)) deferred to v2** (separate `MultiSelect` component).

### multi-select-component

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`. **Ruled.** 2026-06-27.

**Multi-select is its own `MultiSelect` component, a sibling of `Select`, and not a `multiple` prop on `Select`.**

**Why.** Radix Select holds one value only (`value: string`), so a multi-select needs a listbox of its own whatever its name. A `multiple` prop would present the two as interchangeable where the goal is to tell them apart, and Carbon, Mantine, Polaris and Spectrum keep them apart for the same reason.

**Shared with Select.** Imported, never copied:

- the `Field` shell, with its label, its description or message, and its ARIA wiring
- the trigger chrome, the caret, the focus ring and the validation paint, through the `.rt-SelectTrigger` class
- the control size scale, through `useResolvedSize("control")`
- the clear button, with Backspace and Delete parity
- the neutral grey hover, the disabled dimming and every token, with no new token

**What differs.**

| | `Select` | `MultiSelect` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Menu row | A solid accent row marks the choice. | A checkbox per row, and a bold label with no fill on a selected row. |
| Trigger | The chosen value. | A count: the placeholder at 0, the item label at 1, "N selected" at 2 or more. |
| Clear button | Clears the value. | Clears every value. |
| Picking | Commits and closes. | Commits each toggle at once to `value: string[]` and keeps the panel open. |

The row checkbox is `CheckboxVisual`, extracted from `Checkbox`: Radix's checkbox skin on a non-interactive `aria-hidden` span. Chips and tags stay deferred, because the count never overflows the fixed trigger height.

**Accessibility and keyboard.** The multi-selectable listbox of the ARIA Authoring Practices Guide (APG). A trigger `<button aria-haspopup="listbox" aria-expanded>`, one tab stop, opens `role="listbox" aria-multiselectable="true"` with `role="option"` children, and `aria-selected` is the source of truth. A row never holds a real `Checkbox`, because an option must not contain an interactive widget. The whole row is the toggle target, and Enter never submits a surrounding form. `@radix-ui/react-popover` positions the panel, and a roving tabindex written for this component handles arrows, Home and End, type-ahead, Space or Enter to toggle, Shift with an arrow to extend a range, Ctrl or Cmd with A to select all, and Escape, Tab or a click outside to close with no revert.

**Select all.** An opt-in `selectAll` prop, off by default, adds a header above the list and outside `role="listbox"`: Select all (N) or Deselect all (N), a live "N of M selected" `role="status"`, and a lighter Clear shown only when a value is selected. Ctrl or Cmd with A works with or without the prop. The trigger's clear button acts on the committed value and select all acts on the option list, which is why they sit apart.

**Changed from.** [select-selected-row](#select-selected-row) left multiple values out of `Select` and deferred them to a separate component, so no component let a user pick more than one option.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-06-27.

- [input-focus-ring-offset](#input-focus-ring-offset) moves the trigger's focus ring to 2px outside its edge.
- [focus-ring](#focus-ring) replaces the dual-tone focus ring the trigger shared with Select by the 2px accent focus ring.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **MultiSelect — a separate component, not a `multiple` prop (2026-06-27).** Multi-select ships as its own **`MultiSelect`** component, NOT a flag on `Select`. Radix Select is single-value only (`value: string`), so the multi engine is a from-scratch custom listbox regardless of naming — and a `multiple` prop would advertise interchangeability at the exact moment the product goal is to tell the two apart (the enterprise camp — Carbon, Mantine, Polaris, Spectrum — splits them for the same reason). **They read as siblings; only the multiplicity signals diverge.** **Shared substrate (imported, never copied):** the `Field` shell (label · description ⇄ message · aria), the surface trigger chrome + caret + **dual-tone focus ring** + accent-aware `[data-validation]` paint (the trigger reuses the `.rt-SelectTrigger` class, so the dual-tone ring and validation come free — **no new `FOCUS_PAIRING` entry needed**), the `useResolvedSize("control")` size scale, the clear ✕ + Backspace/Delete keyboard parity (reuses the `.rt-ds-select-affix`/`.rt-ds-select-clear` overlay), the neutral gray hover layer, the disabled dimming, and all tokens (no new tokens). The presentational checkbox is **extracted** from `Checkbox` as `CheckboxVisual` — Radix's BaseCheckbox skin on a non-interactive `aria-hidden <span>`. **Distinct signals:** menu rows carry a **checkbox per row** (bold label, NO fill on selected — many checked rows stay quiet; the gray hover is reused verbatim for the active-descendant) vs the single-select's solid accent row; the trigger shows an **adaptive count** (0 → placeholder · 1 → the item label · 2+ → "N selected") vs the chosen value; clear ✕ = clear-all; picking **stays open** (live-apply — each toggle commits to `value: string[]` immediately so the count stays live) vs commit-and-close. **A11y — APG multi-selectable listbox:** trigger `<button aria-haspopup="listbox" aria-expanded>` (one tab stop) opens `role="listbox" aria-multiselectable="true"` with `role="option" aria-selected` children; the checkbox is `aria-hidden` and `aria-selected` is the source of truth — **the real interactive `Checkbox` is never mounted in a row** (a `role=option` must not contain an interactive widget — the #1 trap); the full row is the toggle target; **Enter `preventDefault`s** so it never submits a surrounding form. **Engine:** `@radix-ui/react-popover` (positioning/portal/outside-dismiss; pre-bundled in Storybook `viteFinal` + `vitest` so the primitive shares one React instance; the portal is wrapped in `<Theme>` so the token scales resolve outside the app root) + a **hand-rolled roving-tabindex keyboard** (↑/↓·Home/End·type-ahead jump·Space/Enter toggle·Shift+↑/↓ range-extend·Ctrl/Cmd+A select-all·Esc/Tab/outside close, no revert). The roving keyboard was **hand-rolled** rather than built on `@radix-ui/react-roving-focus`, because the custom contract (range-extend + type-ahead + select-all interleaved with arrow nav) is cleaner in one unified handler than layered onto the primitive — the roving-tabindex *pattern* is preserved; no new dependency. **Select-all (2026-06-27, confirmed after a cross-system survey):** an **opt-in `selectAll`** prop (off by default) adds a header ABOVE the list, OUTSIDE `role=listbox`, with **Select all (N) ⇄ Deselect all (N)**, a live **"N of M selected"** `role=status`, and a lighter **Clear** (hidden when empty). Grounded in research — only **2 of 9** surveyed systems ship a visible select-all in the dropdown (IBM Carbon's `isSelectAll` row, GitHub Primer's `showSelectAll` header toggle); 7 omit it; APG makes `Ctrl/Cmd+A` optional but recommends visible Select-all/Unselect-all buttons *outside* the listbox for a11y. The asymmetry "clear on the trigger, select-all in the panel" is deliberate: the trigger ✕ acts on the committed value (like a TextField clear), select-all manipulates the option list. `Ctrl/Cmd+A` works regardless of the prop. Chips/tags remain deferred (the fixed-height count never overflows).

### type-and-target-density

**Tags.** `TYPOGRAPHY`, `ACCESSIBILITY`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-02.

**Type uses three weights, body line heights snap to the size tokens, and the pointer target floor is 24×24.**

**Weights.** Three, a constrained pick from Inter's nine, because a regular and bold pair cannot cover the UI voice without reading shouty at 700 or flat at 400. Radix does not ship 600, so `--ds-font-weight-strong` holds it ([type-ramp](#type-ramp)).

- 400 Base.
- 600 Strong, the UI workhorse for buttons, labels, table and column headers and menu selection.
- 700 Strongest.

**Line height.** Body line heights follow the size tokens: Small is 14/20 (1.43) and Medium is 16/24 (1.5). They do not chase a fixed 1.5 ratio with off-scale values, because 1.5 is a floor for reading prose, and prose uses Medium or larger.

**Target size.** The 24×24 floor of WCAG 2.5.8 (AA) is the target for this pointer-first system. The 44 to 48px guideline of WCAG 2.5.5 (AAA), Apple HIG and Material is a touch guideline for touch-first displays.

**Related.** The serif `<Em>` and `<Quote>` ([serif-em-and-quote](#serif-em-and-quote)) stay the one intentional contrast of typeface. Invisible 44×44 hit areas under `pointer: coarse` are a deferred accommodation that [ui-polish-ruleset](#ui-polish-ruleset) lists, and nothing ships them yet. `docs/GUIDELINES.md` sections 3 and 9 carry these rules.

**Changed from.** No earlier ruling covered this.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-02. No later ruling amends it.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **Typography & target-size density rulings (2026-07-02).** **(a) Three font-weights, not two** — 400 Base / 600 Strong / 700 Strongest; 600 is the UI workhorse (buttons, labels, table/column headers, menu selection) the common "regular + bold" pair can't cover without reading shouty (700) or flat (400). The three are a constrained pick from Inter's nine. **(b) Body line-height stays token-aligned** — Small 14/20 = 1.43, Medium 16/24 = 1.5; snap to the size tokens rather than chase a fixed 1.5 ratio with off-scale line-heights (1.5 is a floor for *reading* prose, which uses Medium+). **(c) Target size 24×24 is the cursor target** — the AA 2.5.8 floor; the larger 44–48px (AAA 2.5.5 / Apple HIG / Material) is a physical-touch guideline for touch-first displays, not this pointer-first system. The serif `<Em>`/`<Quote>` ([serif-em-and-quote](#serif-em-and-quote)) remains the one intentional typeface contrast. See GUIDELINES §3/§9.

### destructive-tone

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`, `COLOUR`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-08.

**A destructive action takes `tone="danger"`, an axis apart from priority, and never Radix's `color` prop.**

**What you see.** `Button` and `IconButton` take `tone?: "danger"`. Priority grades emphasis and tone grades valence, so every emphasis grade has a destructive form, painted from the accent-aware error family.

| Variant | Use | Paint |
|---|---|---|
| Danger solid | The confirm moment | `--ds-fill-error` with `--on-error`. Hover and press lay `--ds-fill-error-hover` over the rest fill. |
| Danger surface | A destructive action in context | `--ds-fill-error-weak` with an inset `--ds-stroke-error` edge. Hover takes `--error-a4`. |
| Danger ghost | A destructive action in context | `--ds-text-error`. Hover takes `--ds-fill-error-weak`, and press takes `--error-a4`. |

**Not Radix's `color`.** The `color` prop scopes a local `data-accent-color` that the brand collision layer never reaches, so `color="red"` stays red while the error family shifts, to oxblood under a red-adjacent brand for one. Stories never guide destructive intent to `color`.

**Focus.** A danger button takes the same focus ring as every control. The ring answers whether the control has focus, and the fill answers what the action does.

**Priority.** A danger solid does not count against the one solid primary of [button-priority](#button-priority). A safe `primary` and a danger solid may share a dialog, as the exception in `GUIDELINES.md` section 5 allows.

**Scope.**

- `tone` holds one value by design, and a further tone needs a new ruling.
- Menu items take the same axis.
- A destructive label names a verb and an object, such as "Delete project", never "OK" or "Confirm".

**Mechanism.** `data-tone="danger"` with same-element compound selectors in `components.css`, gated on `:not([data-disabled])`, the disabled marker Radix sets on a native button, on `asChild` and on `loading` alike. Hover sits under `@media (hover: hover)`, and the ghost press rule keeps Radix's brand ghost press from painting on a keyboard press.

**Changed from.** The stories guided destructive actions to Radix's `color="red"`, and no emphasis grade had a destructive form of its own.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-08.

- [error-hover-fill](#error-hover-fill) adds `--ds-fill-error-hover` for the danger solid.
- [floating-surface-wraps](#floating-surface-wraps) records `tone="danger"` on the menu items.
- [text-on-solid-fill-contrast](#text-on-solid-fill-contrast) moves the danger solid to its own text fill, with an alpha overlay on hover and press, so its label reaches 4.5:1.
- [focus-ring](#focus-ring) replaces the neutral focus hairline with the stacked accent ring on every control.
- [part-colour-parity](#part-colour-parity) lets a part take its own colour, and `tone` still wins over it.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **Destructive actions — `tone="danger"`, orthogonal to priority (2026-07-08).** Button/IconButton gain `tone?: "danger"`: priority grades emphasis, tone grades valence, and the two compose — danger-solid for the confirm moment, danger-surface / danger-ghost for in-context destructive actions — so every emphasis grade has a destructive expression instead of a single flat "destructive" variant. Paint comes from the accent-aware error family: solid = `--ds-fill-error` / `--ds-fill-error-hover` / `--on-error`; surface = inset `--ds-stroke-error` + `--ds-fill-error-weak`, hover `--error-a4`; ghost = `--ds-text-error`, hover `--ds-fill-error-weak`, press `--error-a4` (the ghost press step is load-bearing — ghost carries no base fill, so it blocks Radix's brand ghost-active from leaking on keyboard press; solid/surface need no press override, their base rule already out-specifies Radix's active). Mechanism: `data-tone="danger"` + same-element compound selectors in `components.css` (the `[data-validation]` pattern), gated on `:not([data-disabled])` — Radix's own disabled marker, set on native + `asChild` + `loading` alike, so it wins where `:disabled` can't match an `asChild` non-button — with hover under `@media (hover: hover)` for touch parity. **Radix's `color` prop is banned for destructive intent:** it scopes a local `data-accent-color` that the collision layer ([brand-collision-shift-table](#brand-collision-shift-table)/[oxblood-preset](#oxblood-preset)/[brand-status-collision-gate](#brand-status-collision-gate)) never reaches, so `color="red"` stays literal red while the system's error family shifts (e.g. to oxblood under a red-adjacent brand) — prior `color="red"` guidance in the stories is superseded by this entry. The focus ring stays the neutral focus hairline (the ring answers "is this focused"; the fill answers "what will this do"). A danger solid does not count against the one-solid-primary budget — [button-priority](#button-priority) constrains the brand-accent channel, and GUIDELINES §5's destructive+safe exception stands: a safe accent `primary` and a danger solid may share a dialog (deliberately keeping the safe action solid rather than demoting it). `tone` is single-valued by design; further tones require a new ruling. Menu items adopt the same axis when the System menu wrappers ship. Copy: destructive buttons carry verb + object ("Delete project"), never "OK"/"Confirm".

### validation-focus-paint

**Tags.** `ACCESSIBILITY`, `COMPONENTS`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-08.

**A validation state recolours only the border of a focused input, and no halo surrounds the box.**

**What you see.** A focused input in a validation state keeps the system ring of [focus-ring](#focus-ring) and changes only its border to the family colour, `box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px var(--ds-stroke-{fam})`. The resting border, the tint, the status glyph and the message carry the family colour, so colour is never the only signal (WCAG 1.4.1).

**Applies to.** `TextField`, `TextArea`, the `Select` trigger and the `@supports` fallback for `TextField` in `src/tokens/components.css`. `Typeahead` follows, because its input is a `TextField.Root`.

**Why.** A solid `--ds-fill-{fam}` glow hugged the box with no gap and read as a heavy band, the subject of repeated complaints.

**Changed from.** The first neutral focus ring, a ruling no longer in this ledger, kept a 4px family halo, `0 0 0 4px var(--ds-fill-{fam})`, around a focused input in a validation state, under a 1px `gray-12` hairline at a 4px offset.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-08.

- [input-focus-ring-offset](#input-focus-ring-offset) moves the ring from 4px to 2px outside the edge, and corrects the claim of this ruling that the 4px offset matched the Radix default. Radix Themes 3.3 rings these inputs at `-1px`.
- [focus-ring](#focus-ring) replaces the 1px `gray-12` hairline with the stacked accent ring, 2px wide.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **Focus ring — validation recolors the border stroke only; NO halo (2026-07-08, ruled).** Supersedes the "kept family halo" of the first neutral focus ring. The input focus ring is the single neutral `gray-12` hairline (`--ds-stroke-focus-hairline`, 1px, `outline-offset: 4px`) — matching Radix's default focus geometry (an offset ring with a gap) and carrying the W3C Technique C40 ≥3:1 guarantee. A validation state changes **only the border stroke** to the family (`box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px var(--ds-stroke-{fam})`); the `0 0 0 4px var(--ds-fill-{fam})` **halo is removed** from TextField/TextArea/Select-trigger + the `@supports` fallback in `tokens/components.css`. The family colour is carried entirely by the resting border + tint + status glyph + message (colour-not-alone, 1.4.1) — never a solid `--ds-fill` glow hugging the box, which rendered as a heavy solid band with no offset (the recurring complaint that the kept halo caused). The neutral-hairline 1.4.11 guarantee (`FocusRingContrast`) is retained; the TextField/TextArea validation-focus plays now assert the family **stroke**, not the fill glow. Applies to Typeahead for free (its input IS a `TextField.Root`). **[Update 2026-09-25 ([focus-ring](#focus-ring)): validation still recolours only the border. The ring is [focus-ring](#focus-ring)'s stacked accent at 2px, 2px out ([input-focus-ring-offset](#input-focus-ring-offset)), not a 1px gray-12 hairline.]**

### toggle-button

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-09.

**ToggleButton composes the Radix Toggle primitive over a ghost Button, so it reuses the whole Button chrome.**

**Composition.** `@radix-ui/react-toggle` wraps the system `Button` at `priority="tertiary"` through `asChild`. Size, focus ring and disabled state come from Button, and nothing is re-skinned.

**Pressed state.** A pressed toggle reads three ways ([select-selected-row](#select-selected-row), [soft-variant-scope](#soft-variant-scope)):

- the accent-aware fill `--ds-fill-selected-subtle`
- a 1px inset edge in `--ds-stroke-accent-weak`, the edge the pressed `Token` paints, so a pressed toggle never shows the flat soft look
- a label in `--ds-text-strong` at weight 600, the cue that needs no colour

**Width.** A hidden, always-bold copy of the label reserves the pressed width, so a press never reflows the row.

**API.** Controlled through `pressed` and `onPressedChange`, or uncontrolled through `defaultPressed`, a deliberate addition over the controlled-only Toggle of Astryx. An icon-only toggle requires `label`, which becomes its `aria-label`. Astryx documents a tooltip from `label` that its source does not contain, so the IconButton rule applies.
