**Paint.** `[data-state="on"]` in `src/tokens/components.css`, gated on `:not([data-disabled])`, scoped to `.radix-themes`, with no `!important`.

**Deferred.** The async `pressedChangeAction` and the event `preventDefault` opt-out for an optimistic update.

**Changed from.** No earlier ruling covered this. Before the revision of 2026-10-02, a pressed toggle showed the tint and the bold label with no edge.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-09.

- An amendment of 2026-07-31 in this entry paints the pressed label in `--ds-text-strong`, where it inherited the ghost `--accent-a11` and failed AA on 17 of 54 accent and appearance pairs.
- [control-box-per-step](#control-box-per-step) stamps `data-icon-only` on an icon-only toggle and gives it the square IconButton box.
- [published-aschild-props](#published-aschild-props) refuses `asChild` on ToggleButton, which rendered no `button` element with it.
- Revised on 2026-10-02: the pressed state carries a 1px edge, because a bare tint on a control is the soft look that [soft-variant-scope](#soft-variant-scope) rules out.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **ToggleButton — Toggle composed over Button ghost (2026-07-09).** `@radix-ui/react-toggle` composed `asChild` over our **Button** at `priority="tertiary"` (ghost), so it reuses the whole Button chrome — size, focus ring, disabled — rather than re-skinning it. The pressed state reads two ways: an accent-aware `--ds-fill-selected-subtle` fill (accent-a5) **and** a weight-600 label — the non-colour cue (extends [select-selected-row](#select-selected-row)), with Astryx's hidden always-bold duplicate label reserving the width so pressing never reflows. Controlled (`pressed`/`onPressedChange`) **and** uncontrolled (`defaultPressed`) — a deliberate capability add over Astryx's controlled-only Toggle. An icon-only toggle **requires** `label` → `aria-label` (Astryx's docs claim an auto-tooltip from `label`; their source has none — false, so the IconButton rule applies). The async `pressedChangeAction` / event-arg `preventDefault` optimistic-update opt-out is a named deferral. Paint is `[data-state="on"]` in `tokens/components.css`, gated on `:not([data-disabled])`, `.radix-themes`-scoped, no `!important`. **Amended 2026-07-31 — the rule now paints the INK too.** It set the fill and the weight but never the label colour, so a pressed toggle inherited ghost `--accent-a11` — accent ink on an accent tint of the same hue, and 17 of 54 accent×appearance pairs failed AA (worst light/orange 3.13:1; lightening the fill was measured and cannot work — a4 still fails 17, a3 still fails 10). Pressed ink is `--ds-text-strong`, the pairing this fill's family already uses (Select's checked row, DateRangeInput's active preset, Pagination's current page) — 0 of 54 fail after, worst 8.84:1, guarded by a 108-reading rasterized sweep play.
>
> The Pressed state part before the revision of 2026-10-02:
>
> **Pressed state.** A pressed toggle reads two ways ([select-selected-row](#select-selected-row)):
>
> - the accent-aware fill `--ds-fill-selected-subtle`
> - a label in `--ds-text-strong` at weight 600, the cue that needs no colour

### toggle-button-group

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-09.

**ToggleButtonGroup composes Radix ToggleGroup over the ghost Button, so the group is one tab stop and its selected item paints as a pressed ToggleButton.**

**Composition.** Built on `@radix-ui/react-toggle-group`. Each item is a `ToggleGroup.Item` with `asChild` over a ghost Button, the composition [toggle-button](#toggle-button) uses.

**Type.**

- `single`: a `radiogroup` with at most one item on.
- `multiple`: a `toolbar` of toggles that carry `aria-pressed`.

**What you see.** A selected item takes the pressed paint of [toggle-button](#toggle-button), the `--ds-fill-selected-subtle` fill, a 1px inset `--ds-stroke-accent-weak` edge and a `--ds-text-strong` label at weight 600, from that component's rule. The group adds no paint rule of its own.

**Keyboard.** The roving tabindex of Radix makes the whole group one tab stop, and Arrow, Home and End move focus between items. Button forwards its ref, so the roving focus can move focus by DOM node.

**State.** Controlled through `value`, or uncontrolled through `defaultValue`. Each item takes its own `disabled`.

**Changed from.** In the Astryx catalog every button in a toggle group is its own tab stop.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-09.

- [toggle-group-box](#toggle-group-box) gives the group one control box per size step, with its members one step smaller inside it.
- Revised on 2026-10-02: the What you see part lists the 1px edge and the label ink, the pressed paint the group inherits from [toggle-button](#toggle-button).

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **ToggleButtonGroup — ToggleGroup composed over Button ghost (2026-07-09).** `@radix-ui/react-toggle-group`; `type` `single` (a `radiogroup`, at most one on) / `multiple` (a `toolbar` of aria-pressed toggles). Each item composes `ToggleGroup.Item` `asChild` over Button ghost — the same composition as [toggle-button](#toggle-button) — so the selected item inherits [toggle-button](#toggle-button)'s pressed paint (`--ds-fill-selected-subtle` + weight-600 label) for free, with **no new CSS**. Radix's roving tabindex makes the whole group **one tab stop** with Arrow/Home/End navigation between items — an a11y upgrade over Astryx's per-button tab stops (which is why Button now forwards its ref, so the roving-focus collection can move focus by DOM node). Controlled (`value`) **and** uncontrolled (`defaultValue`); per-item `disabled`.
>
> The What you see part before the revision of 2026-10-02:
>
> **What you see.** A selected item takes the pressed paint of [toggle-button](#toggle-button), `--ds-fill-selected-subtle` with a weight 600 label, from that component's rule. The group adds no paint rule of its own.

### toolbar-slots

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-09.

**Toolbar is Radix Toolbar under a start, center and end slot layout, and it composes only the system's own controls.**

**What you see.** With a `center` slot the layout is a `1fr auto 1fr` grid, so the center is truly centred. Without one, `justify-content: space-between` places `start` and `end` at the two ends. `dividers` places a `Toolbar.Separator` between the groups in each slot.

**Behaviour.** `@radix-ui/react-toolbar` provides the `toolbar` role, the roving focus and the orientation.

**Children.**

- `Button` and `IconButton`, through `Toolbar.Button asChild`.
- A nested `ToggleButtonGroup`, which keeps its own roving scope.

**Refs.** `Button` and `IconButton` forward their ref. Roving focus moves focus by DOM node, so a composed control without a ref breaks arrow navigation onto that item.

**Not covered.** Toolbar does not adopt the any-focusable focus engine of Astryx, `useListFocus`, or its `useKeyboardHint`. The constrained children remove most of the problem that engine solves.

**Changed from.** No earlier ruling covered this.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-09.

- [choice-controls](#choice-controls) ports `SegmentedControl`, which this ruling recorded as missing.
- [aschild-or-type-error](#aschild-or-type-error) gives `Toolbar.Root` a working `asChild` through `Slottable`, where the prop crashed before.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **Toolbar — Radix Toolbar under a start/center/end slot layer (2026-07-09).** `@radix-ui/react-toolbar` (role, roving focus, orientation) under our start/center/end slot layout — a CSS grid `1fr auto 1fr` when a center slot is present (truly centered), else `justify-content: space-between`. Children are CONSTRAINED to the System controls that exist — Button/IconButton via `Toolbar.Button asChild`, plus a nested `ToggleButtonGroup` (which keeps its own roving sub-scope) — composed through the Radix item wrappers; `dividers` maps to `Toolbar.Separator`. **Button + IconButton gained `forwardRef`** — pure-additive but load-bearing: the roving-focus collection moves focus by DOM node, so a composed control that dropped its ref silently breaks arrow-nav onto that item. Named deferrals: Astryx's `useListFocus` any-focusable DOM-query engine (the constrained-children model makes its caret-guard problem largely evaporate) and `useKeyboardHint`; SegmentedControl is not yet ported (agent-gap — use `ToggleButtonGroup` `type="single"` or raw Radix `SegmentedControl` under conventions until it lands).

### collapsible-and-accordion

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`, `MOTION`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-09.

**`Collapsible` is a single disclosure and `CollapsibleGroup` an accordion, both closed by default, with an animated height.**

**Built on.** `@radix-ui/react-collapsible` for `Collapsible` and `@radix-ui/react-accordion` for `CollapsibleGroup`. The primitives supply `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`.

**Behaviour.**

- Closed by default, the platform convention.
- A `disabled` flag on each.
- In single mode `CollapsibleGroup` forces `collapsible` to true, so every item can close. Radix defaults it to false.
- `dividers` takes `between`, `all` or `none`, drawn by the system CSS.

**Motion.** The content height animates from `--radix-collapsible-content-height` or `--radix-accordion-content-height`, and the chevron rotates.

- Expand: `--ds-duration-moderate` with `--ds-ease-entry`.
- Collapse: `--ds-duration-emphasis` with `--ds-ease-standard`.

Reduced motion needs no rule of its own, because `motion.css` clamps the duration tokens to near zero.

**Not ported.** Astryx's `useCollapsible` dispatch-order bug. Radix's lifecycle is correct as it stands.

**Changed from.** No earlier ruling covered this. The Astryx original it follows opens by default, has no `disabled` flag, toggles `display: none` with no height animation, and omits `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-09.

- [motion-retiming](#motion-retiming) retimes the collapse to `--ds-duration-emphasis` with `--ds-ease-standard`, in place of `--ds-duration-fast` with `--ds-ease-exit`.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **Collapsible + CollapsibleGroup — disclosure + accordion (2026-07-09).** `@radix-ui/react-collapsible` (single disclosure) + `@radix-ui/react-accordion` (the group). **Default closed** — the platform convention, a deliberate divergence from Astryx (which defaults open); adds a `disabled` flag Astryx lacks; `aria-expanded`/`aria-controls` come free from the primitive (Astryx omits them — a closed gap). The content **height animates** via `--radix-collapsible-content-height` / `--radix-accordion-content-height` on the motion ladder — expand `--ds-duration-moderate` + `--ds-ease-entry`, collapse `--ds-duration-fast` + `--ds-ease-exit`, plus a chevron rotation (Astryx has no height animation — a `display:none` toggle); reduced motion is free (motion.css clamps the duration tokens to ~0). `CollapsibleGroup` forces `collapsible=true` for single mode (a single-mode item is always closable to none; Radix defaults it false, which would silently regress Astryx); `dividers` `between`/`all`/`none` drawn by our CSS. Astryx's `useCollapsible` dispatch-order bug is NOT ported (Radix's lifecycle is correct). Content is inline, so the CSS uses descendant `.radix-themes` selectors. **[Update 2026-07-28 ([motion-retiming](#motion-retiming)): the collapse exit is retimed — `--ds-duration-emphasis` + `--ds-ease-standard`, no longer fast + ease-exit.]**

### toast-feedback-tier

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-09.

**Toast is the system's transient feedback, built on `@radix-ui/react-toast`, in four tones, with the queue manager the primitive does not ship.**

**Tones.** Each tone paints a `--ds-fill-*-weak` tint, a `--ds-stroke-*` border and `--ds-text-*` over the opaque `--ds-bg-overlay` base ([floating-surface-fill](#floating-surface-fill)).

| Tone | Dismissal | Announcement |
|---|---|---|
| `info` (default), `success`, `warning` | Hides after 5000ms | `type="background"`, polite |
| `error` | Stays until dismissed | `type="foreground"`, assertive |

The primitive sets the live region, so the system never sets `role` or `aria-live` by hand.

**Queue.** The queue manager carries the [catalog-as-specification](#catalog-as-specification) attribution notice.

- Windowing: only the newest `maxVisible` toasts render, 5 by default.
- Deduplication by `uniqueID` and `collisionBehavior`.
- A timer that pauses on hover, focus and window blur, and resumes with at least 1000ms left.
- On dismiss, focus moves to the next toast, then the previous one, then returns to its earlier place.

**Actions.** One action and a required dismiss sit in a `ButtonGroup`, so `buttonOrder` governs their order. The action is `priority="secondary"`, which keeps the message the main element and matches the overlaid actions of `Overlay`, and `Toast.Action` requires `altText`. Both buttons take `size="1"`, fixed transient chrome outside the `uiSize` lane.

**Motion.** A toast enters at `--ds-duration-moderate` with `--ds-ease-entry` and exits at `--ds-duration-expressive` with `--ds-ease-standard`. Swipe dismissal keeps `--ds-duration-fast` with `--ds-ease-exit`.

**Mounting.** The consumer mounts `ToastProvider` under the system `Provider`. Without it, `useToast` throws, and no singleton fallback exists for server rendering.

**Gap.** A focused toast that windowing evicts can drop focus to `<body>`. The guarantee that focus never lands on `<body>` covers dismissal only, and this case is a named deferral.

**Changed from.** No earlier ruling covered this. The action first shipped as a solid `primary` button and moved to `secondary` on the day of the ruling.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-09.

- [motion-retiming](#motion-retiming) retimes the toast enter and exit to the values above.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **Toast — the full transient-feedback tier (2026-07-09).** The `@radix-ui/react-toast` subsystem. Four accent-aware tone families — `info` (default) · `success` · `warning` · `error` — painted from `--ds-fill/stroke/text-{fam}` as a tint over an opaque `--ds-bg-overlay` base ([floating-surface-fill](#floating-surface-fill)). `error` persists + `type="foreground"` (assertive); the rest auto-hide at 5000ms + `type="background"` (the primitive announces — we never hand-set `role`/`aria-live`). The lifted queue manager Radix deliberately doesn't ship carries the [catalog-as-specification](#catalog-as-specification) attribution notice: windowing (`slice(-maxVisible)`, default 5), `uniqueID` + `collisionBehavior` dedup, a pause-aware timer (hover/focus + window-blur pause, 1000ms resume clamp), and focus handoff on dismiss (next → previous → restore). The action + mandatory dismiss ride a `ButtonGroup` (buttonOrder governs the cluster); the **action is `priority="secondary"`** (ruled 2026-07-09 — a quiet accent surface chip keeps the tone message the hero and aligns with Overlay's overlaid actions, superseding the initial solid `primary`); `Toast.Action` requires `altText`. Motion: enter `--ds-duration-emphasis` + `--ds-ease-entry`, exit fast. Buttons pin `size="1"` — fixed transient chrome, a deliberate opt-out of the `uiSize` lane. Consumer-mounts under the system `Provider`; SSR / no-provider **throws** (Astryx's `createRoot` singleton fallback is not ported). **Known limitation:** a focused toast evicted by windowing can drop focus to `<body>` — the never-body focus guarantee covers dismissal only; a named deferral. **[Update 2026-07-28 ([motion-retiming](#motion-retiming)): toast motion retimed — enter `--ds-duration-moderate` + entry, exit `--ds-duration-expressive` + standard; the swipe-dismiss gestures keep `--ds-duration-fast` + `--ds-ease-exit`.]**

### overlay-hover-scrim

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-09.

**`Overlay` lays a scrim over media and shows it on hover or focus, and it is not a portal layer.**

**What you see.** `Overlay` wraps the media in a `position: relative` container with an absolute-inset scrim over it, and its `position` prop places the content at `fill`, `bottom` or `top`. Anchored floating content belongs to `Popover`, `HoverCard` and `Dialog`.

**Scrim.** `scrim="dark"` paints `--ds-scrim` for light media. `scrim="light"` paints `--ds-scrim-light` ([light-scrim](#light-scrim)) for dark media, where a black scrim would vanish.

**Reveal.** `showOn` takes `hover`, `focus`, `always` or `hover-or-focus`. On a device that matches `(hover: none)`, a tap on the media toggles the scrim, a behaviour ported from Astryx's `useOverlay`.

**Keyboard.** The reveal is opacity, and `:focus-within` shows the scrim in every mode, so inner actions stay in the tab order and the accessibility tree (WCAG 2.4.7). The scrim never hides with `display: none` or `visibility: hidden`, because both remove the actions from the tab order and the accessibility tree.

**Changed from.** No earlier ruling covered this.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-09. No later ruling amends it.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **Overlay — a media hover-scrim (2026-07-09).** Overlay is NOT a portal layer (anchored floating content is Popover/HoverCard/Dialog territory). It ships as a small fully-custom lite widget: a `position: relative` container wrapping your media + an absolute-inset scrim from `--ds-scrim` (dark, for light media) / `--ds-scrim-light` (light — [light-scrim](#light-scrim) — for dark media where a black scrim would vanish), with content slots `fill`/`bottom`/`top`. `showOn` `hover`/`focus`/`always`/`hover-or-focus`, plus a `matchMedia("(hover: none)")` tap-toggle ported from Astryx's `useOverlay`. The reveal is opacity + `:focus-within` (in **every** mode) so inner actions stay keyboard-reachable — never `display:none`/`visibility:hidden`, which drop actions from the tab order + a11y tree (WCAG 2.4.7).

### calendar-grid

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`, `ACCESSIBILITY`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-10.

**`Calendar` gives selection, focus and today one visual channel each, rings a focused day inside its cell, and paints a range as a ramp of existing roles.**

**Channels.**

- Selection takes the fill: `--ds-fill-selected` under an `--on-accent` numeral at weight 600, the Select selected row of [select-selected-row](#select-selected-row).
- Focus takes the outline.
- Today takes a 2px bar under the numeral in `--accent-indicator`, with `aria-current="date"`. The bar turns `--on-accent` on a selected day or an endpoint so it stays visible on the fill. It is never a ring, which would collide with focus, and as a shape it keeps colour from being the only signal (WCAG 1.4.1).

**Focus.** The focus ring is the 2px system ring of [focus-ring](#focus-ring), drawn inside the day at a -2px offset. The cells are flush, so an outset ring would be clipped by its neighbours, and the inset ring follows the full-width Collapsible header.

**Range.**

| Part | Paint |
|---|---|
| Preview band | `--ds-fill-accent-weak` (a3) |
| Committed band | `--ds-fill-selected-subtle` (a5) under a `--ds-text-strong` numeral |
| Endpoints | `--ds-fill-selected` (a9) under an `--on-accent` numeral at weight 600 |

Cells are flush so a band runs unbroken, and only the outer corners and the corners at a break in the run round, on logical radius properties that mirror under right-to-left text. The calendar adds no token, and the flush grid with its corner rounding is its only new design.

**Disabled days.**

- A day the constraints exclude takes `--ds-text-disabled` and `aria-disabled`, and keyboard focus skips it.
- A day outside the month takes `--ds-text-weak` and stays navigable, and a click on it moves to its month.

**Interface.**

- The date math comes from the Astryx engine in `src/dates/` and `src/hooks/useGridFocus.ts` under [catalog-as-specification](#catalog-as-specification). The markup and paint are this system's own.
- `mode` selects single or range, values are ISO date strings, and `onValueChange` takes one argument.
- `isDateDisabled(iso)` returns true to disable a date. The calendar inverts it at the boundary into the engine constraint, which takes a native `Date` and returns true to allow.
- Each day carries a full localized `aria-label`, `aria-selected` on its `role="gridcell"`, and `data-date="YYYY-MM-DD"` for navigation, so no code parses the human label.
- Arrow keys and the navigation chevrons mirror under right-to-left text.

**Changed from.** No earlier ruling covered this.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-10.

- [focus-ring](#focus-ring) replaces the 1px neutral inset hairline with the 2px accent ring, drawn as inset layers on the day's `::after`.
- [textless-part-fills](#textless-part-fills) paints the today bar in `--accent-indicator` in place of `--ds-fill-accent`.
- [indicator-mark-edges](#indicator-mark-edges) adds a 1px edge to the today bar where it paints the accent.
- [mark-on-tint-edge](#mark-on-tint-edge) gives the today bar inside a range an edge step of its own.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **Calendar — three visual channels, an inset focus ring, and the range ramp (2026-07-10).** A from-scratch single + range date grid: the date math is the lifted Astryx engine (DECISIONS [catalog-as-specification](#catalog-as-specification) @ commit 88c95e4 — `src/dates/*`, `src/hooks/useGridFocus`), the UI is this system's own markup + `--ds-*` paint (no Astryx StyleX/Button/Icon). **(1) The today-marker is a third channel.** Selection already owns the **fill** channel (`--ds-fill-selected` = accent-9 + `--on-accent` + weight 600, identical to the Select selected row, [select-selected-row](#select-selected-row)) and focus owns the **outline** channel ([validation-focus-paint](#validation-focus-paint)), so "today" needs a *third*: a **2px accent underline/bar** under the numeral from `--ds-fill-accent`, which **flips to `--on-accent`** when the day is also selected/an endpoint (so it survives the fill), plus `aria-current="date"`. Deliberately **not a ring** (collides with focus) — the bar is the WCAG 1.4.1 non-colour cue (colour is never the only signal). **(2) Grid-cell focus is INSET** (`outline: 1px var(--ds-stroke-focus-hairline); outline-offset: -2px`), a deliberate divergence from the input `+4px` outset ring ([validation-focus-paint](#validation-focus-paint)): the cells are painted **flush** (zero gap, for a continuous range band) so there is no gutter for an outset ring — it would be clipped by neighbours. Cites the **Collapsible** full-width-header precedent (`components.css`, the `rt-ds-collapsible-trigger:focus-visible` inset rule). Documented here so a later reviewer doesn't "fix" it back to +4px and clip it. (Contrast note: the gray-12 hairline resolves to ~3:1 against the accent-9 selected chip at the default accent — meets WCAG 1.4.11 non-text — but a very dark brand `accent-9` could dip below 3:1 on the focused-selected cell, so dark-accent brands should spot-check that state; a future min-contrast guard is the follow-on if it proves insufficient.) **(3) The range is an intensity ramp** across **existing** roles, no new token: preview band `--ds-fill-accent-weak` (a3) · committed band `--ds-fill-selected-subtle` (a5, numeral `--ds-text-strong`) · the two endpoints `--ds-fill-selected` (a9) + `--on-accent` + 600. Cells are flush so the band is continuous; **only outer + run-boundary corners round** — via `computeRangeRounding`/`computePreviewRounding` (endpoints, row edges, and neighbour discontinuity from `computeDayNeighborContinuity`, so an adjacent-month or disabled day caps the run) mapped to **logical** radius props (`border-start-start-radius` …) so rounding auto-mirrors under RTL. **Two disabled tiers:** constraint-disabled = `--ds-text-disabled` (gray-a8) + `aria-disabled` + unfocusable (skipped by the roving `isCellFocusable`); out-of-month = `--ds-text-weak` (gray-11), navigable (click flips the month). **Layout structure — the flush 7-col grid + selective logical-corner rounding — is the only earned net-new** (geometric, reusing `--ds-radius-*`; zero net-new tokens). **API normalization:** discriminated single/range union, ISO strings on the wire, `onValueChange` drops Astryx's second native-`Date` arg; the public `isDateDisabled(iso) => true=disabled` is **double-flipped** into the lifted `useCalendarConstraints` (whose `dateConstraints` take a native `Date` and return true = ALLOWED) at the boundary. **(4) A11y provenance:** `aria-current="date"` on today is a **genuine upgrade** (absent upstream); RTL arrow-nav is an **integration** upgrade (the swap mechanism pre-exists and is tested in `useGridFocus`'s `isRtl` — Calendar never passed it, now it does + the nav chevrons visually mirror); `aria-selected` on the `role="gridcell"` is a **faithful port** (upstream already carries it — not claimed as ours). Full localized `aria-label` per day + a machine-readable `data-date="YYYY-MM-DD"` for navigation (never parse the human label — fr-FR/ja-JP break). No `!important`; `.radix-themes`-scoped.

### disabled-reason

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`, `ACCESSIBILITY`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-10.

**A disabled field control with a non-empty `disabledReason` stays focusable, and its reason reaches the reader.**

**Why.** A natively disabled control leaves the accessibility tree and takes no hover and no focus, so it can carry no reason a reader can perceive.

**What you see.** When `disabled` and a non-empty `disabledReason` are both present:

- The control takes `aria-disabled="true"` and `readOnly`, never native `disabled`, so it stays in the tab order.
- The system `Tooltip` wraps the control's container and opens on hover and on keyboard focus.
- A visually hidden node holds the reason and backs `aria-describedby`, so assistive technology reads the reason before the tooltip opens.
- A quiet `Info` glyph, regular weight in `--ds-icon-neutral`, marks the field and is `aria-hidden`, so the reason is read once.
- The field keeps the Radix disabled skin, because Radix paints `:read-only` the same as `:disabled`. The `[data-disabled-reason]` wrapper adds a `not-allowed` cursor, scoped to that wrapper and never to a bare `[aria-disabled]`.

**Not an error.** The control never takes `aria-invalid`. A reason is guidance, and the error paint and `role="alert"` belong to validation ([field-shell](#field-shell)).

**Without a reason.** `disabled` alone keeps native `disabled`, because nothing remains to perceive.

**Applies to.** Every input on the shared `Field` shell, such as DateInput, TimeInput, NumberInput, FileInput and Tokenizer, through `useDisabledReason`, `DisabledReasonTooltip` and `DisabledReasonGlyph` in `Field.tsx`. Each input returns early from its edit, keydown, focus, step, paste and open handlers while the control is soft-disabled. The affordance adds no token.

**Changed from.** No earlier ruling covered this.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-10.

- [date-range-input](#date-range-input) applies the soft-disable to a button trigger with `aria-disabled` alone, because `readOnly` means nothing on a button.
- [tooltip-wrap](#tooltip-wrap) replaces the raw Radix tooltip with the system `Tooltip`.
- [disabled-label-ink](#disabled-label-ink) keeps the label of a soft-disabled control at full strength, so only the control takes the disabled skin.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **`disabledReason` — soft-disable-with-reason on the shared Field family (2026-07-10).** Built ONCE on the compositional `Field` (`useDisabledReason` + `DisabledReasonTooltip` + `DisabledReasonGlyph` in `Field.tsx`) so every Field-riding input (DateInput / TimeInput / NumberInput / FileInput / Tokenizer) inherits it identically. **The problem:** a natively-`disabled` control drops out of the accessibility tree and receives **no hover and no focus**, so it can never carry a *perceivable* reason for being off — the explanation and the mechanism that would surface it are mutually exclusive. **So soft-disable when — and only when — `disabled` AND a non-empty `disabledReason` are both present:** the control gets **`aria-disabled="true"` + `readOnly`** (NOT native `disabled`), so it **stays focusable/tabbable**; its control-CONTAINER (not the input) is wrapped in a **raw Radix Themes `<Tooltip content={reason}>`** (Tooltip is still a `planned` System wrap — raw primitive per the agent-gap rule [component-registry](#component-registry), the same precedent as TextField's `InfoAffordance`), which opens on hover AND on keyboard focus (focusin bubbles from the inner input to the wrapper trigger); a **persistent, visually-hidden reason node** (`VisuallyHidden`, `id = reasonId`) backs **`aria-describedby`** so AT reads the reason **even before the tooltip opens** (Radix wires describedby only while open — a stable one is added for parity); and a **quiet, `aria-hidden` trailing `Info` glyph** (Phosphor `weight="regular"`, `--ds-icon-neutral`) is the *visual* "there's a reason here" cue — `aria-hidden` because the reason already travels via `aria-describedby`, so the glyph must not double-announce. It is deliberately **NOT `aria-invalid`** — a reason is **guidance, not an error**, and must not borrow the error vocabulary (which owns the accent-aware family paint + `role="alert"`, [field-shell](#field-shell)/the validation blocks). **`disabled` WITHOUT a reason keeps native `disabled`** (nothing to perceive — the cheapest correct treatment). **The dimming is REUSED, not re-declared:** Radix folds `:read-only` into its own `:disabled` skin (same gray-a2 fill, gray-a6 border, gray-a11 text — the sanctioned "reuse a Radix component's own skin" exception), so a `readOnly` field already looks **identical to a hard-disabled** one for free. **The only earned net-new is the selector hook** — a `.radix-themes [data-disabled-reason] { cursor: not-allowed }` rule (Radix leaves `cursor: text` on a readOnly input; the descendant `input`/`textarea`/`button` rule at (0,3,0) beats Radix's `.rt-TextFieldInput:where(:disabled, :read-only)` at (0,1,0)) — scoped to the wrapper attribute, NEVER a bare `[aria-disabled]` (Calendar days / MultiSelect options carry that too). **Zero net-new tokens.** **Consumer contract:** the input owns EARLY-RETURNING its edit / keydown / focus side-effect handlers while soft (readOnly stops native typing, but a custom control's click / step / paste / open handlers must bail on `dr.soft`). No `!important`; `.radix-themes`-scoped. **[Update 2026-07-21 ([tooltip-wrap](#tooltip-wrap)): Tooltip is now ported; `useDisabledReason`'s `DisabledReasonTooltip` composes the System Tooltip wrap (`Field.tsx`) — this "planned System wrap / raw primitive per [component-registry](#component-registry) agent-gap" note is historical.]**

### date-input

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-10.

**DateInput is a free-text date field with a calendar popover, and its feedback runs on two channels that never cross.**

**Build.** DateInput is a sibling of Typeahead on the shared `Field` shell. The input is Radix `TextField.Root`, so it reuses the validation paint, the focus ring and the affix slots ([field-shell](#field-shell), [field-shell-adoption](#field-shell-adoption), [validation-focus-paint](#validation-focus-paint)). Parsing is the lifted `parseDateInput` in `src/dates/`, the popover body is the ported `Calendar`, and `disabledReason` is the [disabled-reason](#disabled-reason) affordance. The control body renders inside its own `Field.Root`, so `useOptionalFieldControl` reads the field's aria wiring.

**Typing and commit.**

- Typed text that resolves to an allowed date, different from the value, fires `onValueChange` at once and moves the calendar to that month.
- On blur or Enter, empty text clears the value to `undefined`, and a resolved new date fires `onValueChange`.
- After a commit the field shows the formatted value again, such as "May 21, 2026", so text it cannot read reverts to that value.

**Feedback.**

| Channel | When | How |
|---|---|---|
| Ephemeral | Typed text that does not resolve and reverts | An assertive announcement through `useAnnounce`, and `aria-invalid="true"` only while the text stays unresolved. It never enters `Field.validation`. |
| Standing | A committed value outside `min` or `max`, or a caller's `validation` | `validation` with `tone: "error"`, and a synthesised message such as "Choose a date on or after …" |

The field otherwise rests in its neutral state. A red border on a field that reverted to a valid value would be false.

**Popover.** The input is a combobox with a dialog popup: `role="combobox"`, `aria-haspopup="dialog"`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`, `aria-autocomplete="none"` and `autoComplete="off"`. The popover keeps Radix's `role="dialog"`, named "Choose date", the deliberate opposite of Typeahead's listbox, because a calendar is a picking dialog. `ArrowDown`, `Alt+ArrowDown` or the calendar button opens it and moves focus into the grid's roving day, since a grid with focus left in the input fails WCAG 2.1.1. Escape and a day choice return focus to the input.

**Tab order.** The calendar button, an `IconButton inset` with `CalendarBlank` and `aria-label="Choose date"`, is a real tab stop, because it opens a whole picking surface. The optional `hasClear` control stays at `tabIndex=-1` ([field-family-anatomy](#field-family-anatomy)).

**API.** `value?: ISODateString`, a required `onValueChange(value | undefined)`, no `null`, ISO strings on the wire, and `isDateDisabled(iso)` passed straight to `Calendar`. The only new CSS is the panel class `.radix-themes.rt-ds-dateinput-panel` on the shared overlay tokens ([floating-surface-fill](#floating-surface-fill)), with no new tokens.

**Not covered.** The `changeAction` async optimistic layer with `isLoading` and a Spinner, and composition with `InputGroup`, are deferred.

**Changed from.** No earlier ruling covered this.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-10. No later ruling amends it.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **DateInput — free-text date field + calendar-dialog popover, two-channel feedback (2026-07-10).** A **Typeahead sibling** on the shared `Field` shell: the input **rides Radix `TextField.Root`** (so the accent-aware `[data-validation]` paint + the dual-tone focus ring + affix slots are **REUSED, not re-built** — [field-shell](#field-shell)/[field-shell-adoption](#field-shell-adoption)/[validation-focus-paint](#validation-focus-paint)), and the control body renders **INSIDE its self-owned `Field.Root`** so it can read the field aria via `useOptionalFieldControl` (the gotcha: at the top level it reads the null outer context and the wiring never reaches the input). **Parsing is the lifted `parseDateInput`** (`src/dates/*`, DECISIONS [catalog-as-specification](#catalog-as-specification) @ `88c95e4`) — never re-implemented; the popover body is the ported `Calendar`; `disabledReason` is the [disabled-reason](#disabled-reason) affordance. **(1) The parse/commit model.** A `pendingInput: string | null` (null ⇒ show the FORMATTED committed value, `plainDateFormat(…, DATE_FORMAT_LONG)` → "May 21, 2026"). On change: keep the raw text, eagerly `parseDateInput`; if it resolves to an **allowed** (in min/max, not `isDateDisabled`) date that **differs**, fire `onValueChange` **immediately** AND drive the popover Calendar's controlled `focusDate` to that month (our Calendar has no imperative `navigateTo`). On blur/Enter (commit): empty ⇒ clear to `undefined`; resolves+differs ⇒ fire; THEN `pendingInput = null` **unconditionally** — so unrecognized text **silently reverts** to the last formatted value. **(2) TWO feedback channels that never cross.** An **ephemeral** parse failure that reverts is announced **assertively** via the singleton `useAnnounce` (`"Didn't recognize that date — kept May 21, 2026."`) and flags `aria-invalid="true"` **ONLY while the pending text is unresolved** (clears on revert) — it **NEVER** enters `Field.validation` (a red border on a reverted-to-valid field would lie). The real `validation={{tone:"error",…}}` channel is reserved for **STANDING** problems: a committed value out of min/max (DateInput **synthesizes** a corrective message — "Choose a date on or after …") or a caller-supplied `validation`. The field sits at **neutral rest** otherwise. **(3) The popover is a combobox-with-DIALOG.** The input is `role="combobox"` + `aria-haspopup="dialog"` + `aria-expanded`/`aria-controls` + `aria-autocomplete="none"` + `autoComplete="off"`. **It KEEPS Radix's hardcoded `role="dialog"`** (named `aria-label="Choose date"`) — the **deliberate OPPOSITE** of Typeahead's `role="listbox"` override (a calendar is genuinely a picking *dialog*, not a list of the input's completions); stated so nobody normalizes it back. `<Theme>`-wrapped `Popover.Content` with the **COMPOUND** `.radix-themes.rt-ds-dateinput-panel` selector on the pre-bundled `@radix-ui/react-popover` (the same overlay surface as the Typeahead/Select menus — opaque `--ds-bg-overlay` ([floating-surface-fill](#floating-surface-fill)), `--ds-shadow-overlay`, `--ds-radius-3`; **no** min-width:trigger-width, since the calendar sizes to its own grid). `ArrowDown`/`Alt+ArrowDown` (or the calendar button) opens AND **moves focus INTO the grid's roving day** (`onOpenAutoFocus` focuses the seed cell) — the Calendar uses real roving-tabindex focus, so keeping focus in the input would leave the grid keyboard-**INOPERABLE** (WCAG 2.1.1); Escape + day-select return focus to the input (`onCloseAutoFocus` prevented). *(A green axe run cannot detect this focus-order gap, so it never proves the grid is keyboard-reachable.)* **(4) The calendar button is a REAL tab stop** — the trailing `IconButton inset` (`CalendarBlank`, `--ds-icon-neutral`, `aria-label="Choose date"`) is **tabbable**, a **divergence** from the Select/Typeahead clear ✕ at `tabIndex=-1`: it opens a whole picking surface, so it earns a place in the tab order. The optional `hasClear` ✕ stays `tabIndex=-1` ([field-family-anatomy](#field-family-anatomy)). **(5) API normalization:** `value?: ISODateString`, a *required* `onValueChange(v | undefined)` (drops Astryx's optional/second-arg), `null`-free (`undefined` = empty), ISO strings on the wire, `PlainDate` internal; `isDateDisabled(iso) => true=disabled` forwarded straight to Calendar (which bridges the polarity). **DEFERRED (named, not built):** the `changeAction` async-optimistic layer + `isLoading`/Spinner (react-server-action optimistic UI — beyond the port boundary), and InputGroup composition (InputGroup not ported). **The only earned net-new CSS is the panel-surface class** (`.radix-themes.rt-ds-dateinput-panel`, geometric — reuses the overlay tokens); **zero net-new tokens.** No `!important`; `.radix-themes`-scoped.

### time-input

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-10.

**TimeInput is a free-text time field with arrow-key increment and no popover, built on the DateInput model.**

**Shared with DateInput.** TimeInput takes the [date-input](#date-input) model whole:

- The input is Radix `TextField.Root`, so it reuses the accent-aware `[data-validation]` paint, the focus ring and the affix slots ([field-shell](#field-shell), [field-shell-adoption](#field-shell-adoption)).
- The body renders inside its own `Field.Root` and reads the field's ARIA through `useOptionalFieldControl`.
- Text parses on change and commits on blur or Enter, and unrecognised text reverts with no message.
- Two feedback channels never cross. An unparseable entry gets an assertive announcement and `aria-invalid` while pending, and never `Field.validation`. A committed value outside `min` or `max` gets a standing message such as "Choose a time at or after …", or the caller's `validation`.
- `disabledReason` soft-disables the field, and the edit, keydown and step handlers return early while it holds ([disabled-reason](#disabled-reason)).
- The API: `value?: ISOTimeString`, a required `onValueChange(v | undefined)`, no `null`, and ISO `HH:MM[:SS]` on the wire.
- Parsing is `parseTimeInput` and the increment is `adjustTime`, both from `src/dates/timeParser.ts`, lifted from the catalog under [catalog-as-specification](#catalog-as-specification). The component implements no time arithmetic of its own.
- An unparseable commit gets the same invalid feedback as DateInput, a deliberate divergence from the upstream TimeInput, which only greys invalid text.

**Arrow keys.** ArrowUp and ArrowDown step the value by `increment` minutes, default 1, with a wrap at midnight. An empty field steps from the current wall-clock time, read in the component and never inside `adjustTime`, and a step that would leave the `min` to `max` range does nothing. Each step is announced politely, apart from the assertive channel for parse failures.

**What you see.** A plain text input that takes free text such as "3pm", "15:00" or "3:00 PM". `hourFormat` (`"12h"` by default, or `"24h"`) and `hasSeconds` change display and precision only, and the wire value is always ISO 24-hour. A leading `Clock` glyph in `--ds-icon-neutral`, `aria-hidden`, marks the field, and the optional `hasClear` control stays at `tabIndex=-1` ([field-family-anatomy](#field-family-anatomy)). `hasAutoFocus` is documented. The field reuses the TextField chrome whole and adds no CSS and no token.

**Rejected.**

- `role="spinbutton"`, which implies a constrained numeric or segmented widget. With no popover, the field also carries no `role="combobox"` or `aria-haspopup`.
- Visible plus and minus stepper buttons. [number-input](#number-input) makes the same call, and a stepper for TimeInput alone would fragment the system.

**Not covered.** Three named deferrals: a shared touch-friendly stepper primitive, together with NumberInput ([number-input](#number-input)), the `changeAction` async optimistic layer with `isLoading` and a Spinner, and InputGroup composition.

**Changed from.** No earlier ruling covered this.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-10.

- [focus-ring](#focus-ring) replaces the two-colour focus ring the field took from TextField with the accent focus ring.
- [input-focus-ring-offset](#input-focus-ring-offset) moves the field's focus ring to 2px outside its edge.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **TimeInput — free-text time field + keyboard increment, no popover (2026-07-10).** A **DateInput sibling MINUS the popover**: it **SHARES [date-input](#date-input)'s model wholesale** — the input **rides Radix `TextField.Root`** (accent-aware `[data-validation]` paint + dual-tone focus ring + affix slots **REUSED**, [field-shell](#field-shell)/[field-shell-adoption](#field-shell-adoption)/[validation-focus-paint](#validation-focus-paint)), the body renders **INSIDE its self-owned `Field.Root`** (reads field aria via `useOptionalFieldControl` — the null-outer-context gotcha), the `pendingInput: string | null` **parse-on-change / commit-on-blur-or-Enter / silent-revert**, the **TWO feedback channels that never cross** (ephemeral parse failure → **assertive** `useAnnounce` + `aria-invalid`-only-while-pending, **never** `Field.validation`; a STANDING committed value out of min/max **synthesizes** a corrective message — "Choose a time at or after …" — or a caller `validation`), the **[disabled-reason](#disabled-reason)** `disabledReason` soft-disable (edit/keydown/**step** handlers early-return while soft), and the **[date-input](#date-input)** API normalization (`value?: ISOTimeString`, *required* `onValueChange(v | undefined)`, `null`-free, ISO `HH:MM[:SS]` on the wire). **Parsing is the lifted `parseTimeInput`** and the increment is the lifted **`adjustTime`** (O(1) double-modulo midnight wrap, non-finite-guarded — `src/dates/timeParser.ts`, DECISIONS [catalog-as-specification](#catalog-as-specification) @ `88c95e4`); zero time math re-implemented. **What's particular to TimeInput:** **(1) ↑ / ↓ in-place increment.** `ArrowUp`/`ArrowDown` (keydown, `preventDefault`) step by `increment` minutes (default 1) via `adjustTime` — `base = value ?? formatISOTime(<now>)`, i.e. an **empty field seeds from the current wall-clock time** (a `new Date()` read **in the component**, never inside `adjustTime`); the step fires **only if** `isTimeInRange(next, min, max)` (**clamped at the bound** — a step that would leave the range is a no-op); midnight wrap comes from `adjustTime`. **(2) Announce every step POLITELY.** An arrow silently mutating a plain text input is invisible to a screen reader, so each successful step announces `formatDisplayTime…(next)` at `"polite"` — distinct from the assertive parse-failure channel. **(3) It stays a PLAIN text input — deliberately NOT `role="spinbutton"`.** TimeInput is **free-text-first** ("3pm", "15:00", "3:00 PM"); spinbutton implies a constrained numeric/segmented widget we didn't adopt (so, unlike DateInput, there is **no `role="combobox"`/`aria-haspopup`** either — there is no popover). **(4) NO visible +/- stepper buttons (reuse gate).** The same call **[number-input](#number-input)** made for NumberInput (upstream ships no custom stepper); a **TimeInput-only** stepper would fragment the system, so a shared touch-friendly stepper primitive is a **named deferral**. **(5) PARITY UPGRADE over Astryx.** Upstream's TimeInput only **greys** invalid text — **no announcement, no `aria-invalid`**; ours gives it the **same** invalid feedback DateInput has (assertive announce on an unparseable commit + `aria-invalid` while pending) — a **deliberate divergence for parity**, framed as ours. `hourFormat` (`"12h"` default / `"24h"`) and `hasSeconds` are **display/precision** only — the wire value is always ISO 24-hour; `hasAutoFocus` (undocumented upstream) is documented. A **leading `Clock` glyph** (`--ds-icon-neutral`, `aria-hidden`) identifies the field; the optional `hasClear` ✕ stays `tabIndex=-1` ([field-family-anatomy](#field-family-anatomy)). **DEFERRED (named, not built):** the shared/touch-friendly stepper primitive (with NumberInput, [number-input](#number-input)), the `changeAction` async-optimistic layer + `isLoading`/Spinner, and InputGroup composition. **The field reuses TextField chrome wholesale — ZERO net-new CSS and ZERO net-new tokens** (no popover means no panel class, unlike [date-input](#date-input)). No `!important`; `.radix-themes`-scoped.

### date-time-input

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-10.

**DateTimeInput takes a date and a time under one group label, as a FieldGroup composite of the shipped DateInput and TimeInput.**

**Composition.** It embeds `DateInput` ([date-input](#date-input)) and `TimeInput` ([time-input](#time-input)) in their bare mode inside a `FieldGroup.Root`. Parsing, formatting, range checks, the ephemeral feedback and the soft disable of [disabled-reason](#disabled-reason) all come from the two children and the shared engine in `src/dates/`. The only new logic is `splitDateTime` and `combineDateTime`, a split of the string at the `T`, and the only new CSS is the row layout.

**Names and focus.** `FieldGroup.Label` names a `role="group"` through `aria-labelledby`, the shell CheckboxGroup and RadioGroup use. Each bare child carries its own `aria-label`, "Date" and the `timeLabel`, so the two inputs have distinct names and no shared field id. The group is not a focus stop, and tab order runs from the date input to its calendar button to the time input.

**Value.**

- `value` is an `ISODateTimeString`, `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM[:SS]`, split at the `T`. A string with no `T` is a bare date.
- The component emits a combined value only when both halves are present, and `undefined` otherwise.
- The time input's `min` and `max` apply only when the selected date equals the boundary date. Between the bounds, time is free.
- A date change snaps the current time into the window of the new date, silently and never as an error.
- A date picked over an empty time takes the current wall-clock time, so a date selection always combines with a time.
- A date-only bound limits the calendar and leaves time free on the boundary day.

**Feedback.**

- Each embedded input keeps its own local ephemeral channel. The composite error never reaches a child as a `validation` prop, which would render it twice.
- A standing problem of the composite, a caller `validation` or a combined value out of range, shows once in `FieldGroup.Message` with `role="alert"`, and the group carries `aria-invalid`. Two fields are few enough for one group-level signal, unlike the many items of CheckboxGroup and RadioGroup.
- On a boundary date, a hint of the available times shows in `FieldGroup.Description` as guidance, and never sets `aria-invalid`.

**Layout.** The row is a flex row under `rt-ds-datetimeinput-*` with a `--space-3` gap. The date grows, the time keeps its own width, and a container query stacks the two below 22rem of group width. No token is new.

**Not covered.** The group message wired into the `aria-describedby` of each subfield, an asynchronous optimistic layer of `changeAction` and `isLoading`, and InputGroup composition.

**Changed from.** No earlier ruling covered this.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-10. No later ruling amends it.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **DateTimeInput — a date AND a time under one group label, a FieldGroup composite (2026-07-10).** A **composite (a GROUP of two sub-controls), NOT a single Field**: it **EMBEDS the shipped `DateInput` ([date-input](#date-input)) + `TimeInput` ([time-input](#time-input))** in their **bare** mode inside a `FieldGroup.Root` — it **re-implements ZERO date/time math** (parsing, formatting, range/compare, the ephemeral two-channel feedback, and [disabled-reason](#disabled-reason) soft-disable all come from the two children and the lifted `src/dates/*` engine, DECISIONS [catalog-as-specification](#catalog-as-specification) @ `88c95e4`); the only new logic is `splitDateTime` / `combineDateTime`, a string split at the `T`. **(1) Why a FieldGroup composite, not a single Field.** Two sub-controls means the name is a group **LABEL** (`FieldGroup.Label` → `aria-labelledby` on a `role="group"`, the same shell as CheckboxGroup/RadioGroup), **not** a `<label htmlFor>` targeting one control; each bare child carries its **own** `aria-label` ("Date" / the `timeLabel`), so the two inner inputs have DISTINCT accessible names. **The duplicate-id trap is dodged structurally:** a bare child renders its body at the top level (no self-owned `Field.Root`) and `useOptionalFieldControl` reads `FieldCtx` — under a `FieldGroupCtx` there is **NO** `FieldCtx`, so it returns `null` and neither bare input is stamped with a shared `${base}-control` field id (verified in the behavior suite: zero duplicate ids in the composite, each input named solely by its aria-label). The group is **not** a focus stop; tab order is date input → the date's calendar button → time input. **(2) The combined ISODateTime value.** `value?: ISODateTimeString` (a branded `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM[:SS]` string) is split at the `T` into `{date, time}` internally (a `T`-less string is a bare date, `time: undefined`); it emits a combined value only when **both** halves are present, else `undefined` (`null`-free). **(3) The conditional time-clamp + snap + auto-seed (the crux).** The embedded TimeInput's effective `min`/`max` apply **ONLY when the selected date equals the boundary date** (`timeMin = minTime` iff `selectedDate === minDate`; same for `timeMax`/`maxDate`) — strictly between the bounds, time is **unconstrained**. On a date change the current time **snaps** into the new date's window (up onto `minTime` landing on minDate, down onto `maxTime` landing on maxDate — a **silent snap, not an error**), and picking a date onto an **empty** time **auto-seeds the current wall-clock time** (`formatISOTime(<new Date()>)`) so a date selection **always** combines with a time (never emits date-only). A date-only bound (no time half) constrains the calendar but leaves time free on the boundary day. **(4) Two-tier feedback that never crosses.** Each embedded input keeps its OWN **LOCAL** ephemeral channel (assertive revert + `aria-invalid`-while-pending — [date-input](#date-input)/[time-input](#time-input)); the composite error is **NEVER** passed down as a sub-field `validation` prop (it would double-render). The **COMPOSITE STANDING** problem (a caller `validation`, or a combined value out of range) surfaces **ONCE** via `FieldGroup.Message` (`role="alert"` on appearance) + the group's **composite `aria-invalid`** (deliberately set here — a two-field composite is small enough that a single group-level invalid is the minimal correct signal, unlike CheckboxGroup/RadioGroup where it over-announces on N items). The proactive time-window **HINT** on a boundary date ("On Jul 3, times from 9:00 AM are available." / "On Jul 3, 9:00 AM–5:00 PM." when min-date == max-date) rides `FieldGroup.Description` as weak-neutral **GUIDANCE** — it never trips `aria-invalid` or the validation channel ([disabled-reason](#disabled-reason) guidance-not-error). **DEFERRED (named, not built):** the fuller **FieldGroup-message-`describedby`-INTO-subfields** wiring (ships the minimal `role="alert"` + composite `aria-invalid` path); the `changeAction`/`isLoading` async-optimistic layer; InputGroup composition. **The only earned net-new CSS is the `role="group"` flex-row layout** (`rt-ds-datetimeinput-*` — date grows / time intrinsic, a container query stacks to two rows below 22rem of group width; geometric, reuses `--space-3`); **zero net-new tokens.** No `!important`; `.radix-themes`-scoped.

### date-range-input

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-10.

**DateRangeInput picks a date range through a Select-style trigger that opens a dialog with a preset sidebar and a range calendar.**

**Trigger.**

- One button with the `.rt-SelectTrigger` surface chrome, not a text field, because a user picks a range rather than typing one.
- A leading `CalendarBlank` glyph, `aria-haspopup="dialog"`, and no caret, because a caret signals a dropdown and this trigger opens a dialog.
- One tab stop. The clear button sits outside the tab order, and Backspace or Delete on the focused trigger clears the value ([field-family-anatomy](#field-family-anatomy)).
- `disabled` with a non-empty `disabledReason` sets `aria-disabled` alone, so the trigger stays focusable, and the shared `[data-disabled-reason]` hook reapplies the Radix disabled skin ([disabled-reason](#disabled-reason)).

**Dialog.** The panel follows [date-input](#date-input): a `Popover.Content` on the raw `@radix-ui/react-popover`, painted as the opaque overlay surface ([floating-surface-fill](#floating-surface-fill)), with Radix's `role="dialog"` kept and named "Choose date range". On open, focus moves into the roving day of the calendar, which shows two months by default, because a grid with roving focus is not operable by keyboard while focus sits outside it (WCAG 2.1.1).

**Presets.** A `role="group"` of tertiary `Button`s in the normal tab order, not a listbox, because a preset is a shortcut and not the selection. The preset whose range equals the value carries `aria-current="true"` and paints `--ds-fill-selected-subtle` with `--ds-text-strong`, the committed band of [calendar-grid](#calendar-grid), because the stronger `--ds-fill-selected` would compete with the range endpoints in the calendar. A preset click sets the value, shows the range in the grid and leaves the dialog open. "Done", Escape or a click outside closes it.

**Value and display.**

- `value` is a `DateRange` of ISO strings, `{ start, end }`, and the required `onValueChange` receives `undefined` for an empty value.
- The trigger formats the range with `Intl.DateTimeFormat` and `formatRange`: the year drops when both ends share it, stays when they do not, and a one-day range shows one date. A visually hidden full form, such as "July 3 to July 10, 2026", gives a screen reader the range without the dash.
- The calendar commits both ends at once, so the trigger never shows half a range. An empty trigger shows the placeholder "Select dates" in `--ds-text-weak`.

**Not built.** Asynchronous apply with a loading state, a partial range shown in the trigger during a pick, InputGroup composition, and two `DateInput`s in a `FieldGroup` as a typed exact-date alternative. The component adds no token.

**Changed from.** No earlier ruling covered this.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-10.

- [published-aschild-props](#published-aschild-props) repairs `Popover.Anchor`, which anchored nothing for this component before.
- [focus-ring](#focus-ring) replaces the trigger's focus ring with the 2px accent ring of every control.
- [input-focus-ring-offset](#input-focus-ring-offset) moves the trigger's ring to 2px outside its edge, the Select trigger rule.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **DateRangeInput — a range picker: MultiSelect-trigger chrome + a preset sidebar + a range-calendar dialog (2026-07-10).** The **range sibling of DateInput** ([date-input](#date-input)), but a **different shape at both ends** — it composes three already-shipped surfaces and adds almost no new logic. **(1) The trigger is the MultiSelect/Select `.rt-SelectTrigger` chrome, NOT a free-text field.** A range is entered by **picking**, so the trigger is a single `<button className="rt-reset rt-SelectTrigger rt-variant-surface">` reusing the surface fill + border + the **[validation-focus-paint](#validation-focus-paint) dual-tone focus ring** + the `.rt-ds-select-affix`/`-lead`/`-clear` scaffolding **for free**. It carries a leading `CalendarBlank` glyph (`--ds-icon-neutral`), `aria-haspopup="dialog"` (**NOT** `listbox`), `aria-expanded`/`aria-controls`, and **deliberately NO caret** — a caret signals a *dropdown*, but this opens a picking **dialog**; stated so nobody adds one back. It is **ONE tab stop / one Field control**; the optional clear ✕ stays `tabIndex=-1` with **Backspace/Delete parity** on the focused trigger ([field-family-anatomy](#field-family-anatomy)). The keyboard-first *exact-date* range-entry alternative is **two `DateInput`s in a `FieldGroup`** — a named deferral, **not** a bespoke range text-parser. **(2) The popover is DateInput's mechanism verbatim.** `<Theme>`-wrapped `Popover.Content asChild` with the **COMPOUND** `.radix-themes.rt-ds-daterange-panel` selector on the pre-bundled `@radix-ui/react-popover` (the same opaque overlay surface as the DateInput/Typeahead/Select menus — `--ds-bg-overlay` ([floating-surface-fill](#floating-surface-fill)), `--ds-shadow-overlay`, `--ds-radius-3`); Radix's hardcoded **`role="dialog"` is KEPT** (named `aria-label="Choose date range"`), `onInteractOutside` exempts the anchor, and **`onOpenAutoFocus` moves focus INTO the range grid's roving day** (queries `button.rt-ds-calendar-day[tabindex="0"]` in the dialog) — the Calendar uses **real roving-tabindex focus**, so keeping focus outside would leave the grid keyboard-**INOPERABLE** (WCAG 2.1.1). Inside, a flex row: the **preset sidebar** (logical-start) beside `<Calendar mode="range" numberOfMonths={2}>`. **(3) The preset sidebar is a `role="group"` of Tab-order ghost `Button`s — NOT a listbox** (presets are *shortcuts*, not the selection surface, so no `aria-selected`/roving). The **ACTIVE** preset — its `getRange()` equals the committed value (an `isRangeEqual` helper) — carries **`aria-current="true"`** (the string `"true"`, **NOT** `"date"`) and paints from **`--ds-fill-selected-subtle` (a5, the [calendar-grid](#calendar-grid) committed-BAND tier) + `--ds-text-strong`**, deliberately **NOT `--ds-fill-selected` (a9)**: a9 would fight the calendar's OWN a9 range endpoints inside the same dialog, and the a5 band tier ties the preset to the *range it produces*; hover stays `--ds-fill-accent-weak` (a3, the ghost Button's own skin, reused). Clicking a preset fires `onValueChange(range)`, drives the Calendar's controlled `value` + `focusDate` (so the grid **shows** the range) and **KEEPS THE DIALOG OPEN** — a **deliberate divergence** from DateInput's day-select-closes: a range benefits from confirm/refine; a trailing **"Done"** button, Escape, or outside-click close it (a committed two-click calendar range also keeps the dialog open, same reason). **(4) Value + display.** `value?: DateRange` (`{start,end}` ISO), a *required* `onValueChange(v | undefined)` (`undefined` = empty — the `null` upstream carries is normalized to `undefined` at **this** boundary only), ISO strings on the wire. The trigger shows a **smart format** — `Intl.DateTimeFormat(undefined, …).formatRange(start, end)` (native, locale-correct part-dropping): **same-year drops the year, cross-year keeps it, `start==end` collapses to a single date**, separator a **spaced en dash (– U+2013)** — with a **`VisuallyHidden` full form** ("July 3 to July 10, 2026") so the dash is never mis-announced. **No partial state is flickered into the trigger** — the Calendar commits `{start,end}` **atomically** (in-progress range lives in the grid preview, [calendar-grid](#calendar-grid)). Empty → a `--ds-text-weak` placeholder ("Select dates") via `data-placeholder`. **(5) Soft-disable ([disabled-reason](#disabled-reason)) on a button trigger.** `disabled` + a non-empty `disabledReason` soft-disables via **`aria-disabled` alone** (readOnly is meaningless on a `<button>`) so it stays focusable — and since Radix greys `.rt-SelectTrigger` only on `:disabled`, its **own disabled skin values are re-applied** via the shared `[data-disabled-reason]` wrapper hook (the sanctioned reuse-a-Radix-skin exception, exactly as [disabled-reason](#disabled-reason)). **DEFERRED (named, not built):** the `changeAction`/`isLoading` async-optimistic layer; a live-partial-range echoed into the trigger while picking (would need exposing Calendar's internal anchor — a net-new Calendar affordance); InputGroup composition; and the two-`DateInput`-in-a-`FieldGroup` reuse-alternative. **The only earned net-new is the panel + preset-column + active-preset + no-caret-clear-offset + soft-disable-trigger CSS** (geometric / reusing overlay + `--ds-fill-*`/`--ds-text-*` roles + Radix's own disabled skin), `isRangeEqual`, and the `Intl.formatRange` formatter; **zero net-new tokens.** No `!important`; `.radix-themes`-scoped. Ported under [catalog-as-specification](#catalog-as-specification).

### number-input

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-10.

**NumberInput is a native `type="number"` field that rejects an out-of-range value and never clamps it, announces a failed entry through the shared assertive announcer, and speaks its units through `aria-describedby`.**

**Model.** NumberInput shares the model of [date-input](#date-input) and [time-input](#time-input): it renders on Radix `TextField.Root` inside its own `Field.Root`, parses on change, commits on blur or Enter, and reverts silently when the text fails. It reuses the TextField validation paint, focus ring and affix slots whole ([field-shell](#field-shell), [field-shell-adoption](#field-shell-adoption), [validation-focus-paint](#validation-focus-paint)), with no new CSS and no new token.

**Reject, never clamp.** The browser's native spinner supplies the increment, and native `min`, `max` and `step` give `role="spinbutton"` with `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax` and `aria-valuenow`, so NumberInput has no increment handler and no custom stepper. `parseNumberInput` (`src/utils/parseNumberInput.ts`) parses the raw pending text, never `valueAsNumber`, and rejects an out-of-range or malformed number: typing `99` into a field capped at `10` reverts to the last valid value and never becomes `10`.

**Feedback.** Two channels that never cross:

- A failed parse or range check is ephemeral. It goes to the shared assertive announcer that DateInput and TimeInput use, sets `aria-invalid` only while the text is pending, tells a non-number apart from a number out of range, and always names the kept value.
- `Field.validation` is the standing channel, reserved for a caller's `validation` or a controlled `value` the parent forces out of range. Typing cannot trigger it.

**API.** `value?: number` and a required `onValueChange`, discriminated on `clearable`: a clearable field reports `number | undefined` and shows a clear button at `tabIndex=-1` ([field-family-anatomy](#field-family-anatomy)), and any other field reports `number` only and reverts when emptied. The other props are `min`, `max`, `step` (default 1, with `inputMode` `numeric`, or `decimal` for a fractional step), `isIntegerOnly`, `placeholder`, `disabledReason` ([disabled-reason](#disabled-reason)) and `units`, a decorative `aria-hidden` suffix in `--ds-text-weak` that a persistent `VisuallyHidden` node folds into `aria-describedby`, so a screen reader hears the unit after the value and the label stays the accessible name ([field-shell](#field-shell)).

**Not covered.** Each of these is a named deferral:

- A custom stepper, shared with TimeInput, and `Intl.NumberFormat` display.
- A separately spoken `unitsLabel`.
- The `changeAction` and `isLoading` layer, and InputGroup composition.
- A guard against the scroll wheel changing a focused field, which belongs on a shared primitive.

The paired input of `Slider` clamps instead, a divergence that [slider-composition](#slider-composition) records as pending the maintainer's ratification.

**Changed from.** The Astryx `NumberInput` this port follows ([catalog-as-specification](#catalog-as-specification)) showed a local, generic invalid-number string and parsed with an inline helper that had no tests.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-10. No later ruling amends it.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **NumberInput — native `type=number` field, reject-not-clamp, two-channel parity announce, units-via-describedby (2026-07-10).** **TimeInput's TWIN ([time-input](#time-input))**: it **SHARES [date-input](#date-input)/[time-input](#time-input)'s model wholesale** — the input **rides Radix `TextField.Root`** (accent-aware `[data-validation]` paint + dual-tone focus ring + affix slots **REUSED**, [field-shell](#field-shell)/[field-shell-adoption](#field-shell-adoption)/[validation-focus-paint](#validation-focus-paint)), the body renders **INSIDE its self-owned `Field.Root`** (reads field aria via `useOptionalFieldControl` — the null-outer-context gotcha), the `pendingInput: string | null` **parse-on-change / commit-on-blur-or-Enter / silent-revert**, the **TWO feedback channels that never cross** (ephemeral parse/range failure → **assertive** `useAnnounce` + `aria-invalid`-only-while-pending, **never** `Field.validation`), the **[disabled-reason](#disabled-reason)** `disabledReason` soft-disable (edit/keydown handlers early-return while soft), and the `null`-free API normalization. **The ONE structural difference from TimeInput:** the increment comes from the **browser's native `type="number"` spinner**, not the lifted `adjustTime` — so there is **NO increment handler and NO custom stepper here**. **(1) Native spinner, reject-not-clamp.** `type="number"` + native `min`/`max`/`step` attributes give **`role="spinbutton"` + `aria-valuemin`/`-max`/`-now` for FREE** (the doc's phantom "Spinner" is this native one); `inputMode` is `numeric`, or `decimal` when `step` is fractional. Parsing is the **lifted `parseNumberInput`** (`src/utils/parseNumberInput.ts` — extracted from Astryx's INLINE `NumberInput.tsx` helper @ `88c95e4`, DECISIONS [catalog-as-specification](#catalog-as-specification), with **net-new node-lane logic coverage** — `parseNumberInput.logic.test.ts` — since upstream ships none) which **REJECTS, never clamps**, an out-of-range/malformed number: **typing `99` into a field capped at `10` reverts to the last valid value; it never becomes `10`.** We parse the **RAW pending string**, NOT `input.valueAsNumber` — a native `type=number` reports `NaN`/`""` for intermediate `"-"`/`"1."`/`"1e"`, and the pending-string model avoids those spurious rejects while typing. **(2) The standing channel is parent-only.** `Field.validation` is reserved for a caller-supplied `validation` **or a *controlled* `value` the parent forces out of range** — the **user cannot cause it** (reject-revert governs typing), mirroring TimeInput's `outOfRange` guard. **(3) NO custom stepper, NO `Intl.NumberFormat` (the reuse gate).** Upstream ships no custom stepper and a NumberInput-only one would fragment the system; a shared, touch-friendly stepper primitive is a **named deferral** (shared with TimeInput's), as is locale/grouped-thousands display (it fights raw-value editing). **(4) `units` via `aria-describedby`.** The `units` suffix is a **decorative, `aria-hidden`** trailing `<Text --ds-text-weak>` (size matching the input) — but a **persistent `VisuallyHidden` node** (the **[disabled-reason](#disabled-reason) reasonId mechanism**) folds it into `aria-describedby`, so AT hears "Weight, spin button, 5, kg" **without the caller duplicating the unit into the label**; the label stays the accessible **NAME** ([field-shell](#field-shell)). A separately-**spoken** `unitsLabel` is a named deferral (not built). **(5) PARITY UPGRADE over Astryx.** Upstream surfaces a **local, generic** "Invalid number" string; ours routes **honest, range-aware** copy through the **SHARED** assertive announcer (the same live region DateInput/TimeInput use) — distinguishing "That isn't a number." from "Enter a number from 1 to 10." and **always naming the kept value** — a deliberate divergence for parity across the Field family. **API:** `value?: number` + a *required* `onValueChange`, **discriminated on `clearable`** (`clearable` → `onValueChange(number | undefined)` + a trailing ✕; else `number`-only and an emptied field **reverts**), `null`-free; `min`/`max`/`step` (default 1)/`isIntegerOnly`/`units`/`placeholder`. The optional `clearable` ✕ stays `tabIndex=-1` ([field-family-anatomy](#field-family-anatomy)). **DEFERRED (named, not built):** the custom +/- stepper + `Intl.NumberFormat` display, the spoken `unitsLabel`, the `changeAction`/`isLoading` async-optimistic layer, InputGroup composition, and the scroll-wheel-mutate guard (a known native `type=number` wart — a shared wheel guard belongs on the primitive, not here). **The field reuses TextField chrome wholesale — ZERO net-new CSS and ZERO net-new tokens.** No `!important`; `.radix-themes`-scoped. Ported under [catalog-as-specification](#catalog-as-specification).

### file-input

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-10.

**FileInput is a file picker whose native input is the control, and its drop surface is its one piece of new UI.**

**Control.** The native `<input type="file">` is the operable control, hidden with the clip technique and never with `display: none` or `visibility: hidden`. In the default `mode="dropzone"` the input is the tab stop inside a `<label>` drop surface, and in `mode="input"` a system `Button` is the tab stop and the input sits at `tabIndex={-1}`.

**Name.** The accessible name comes from `Field.Label` alone. All visible content of the drop surface is `aria-hidden`, and the browse cue is styled accent text, never a nested `<button>`, which would open the picker twice.

**Drop surface.** A dashed `--ds-stroke-weak` border over `--ds-bg-subtle`, `--ds-fill-hover` on hover, a Phosphor `UploadSimple` glyph in `--ds-icon-neutral`, a prompt, and a `--ds-text-weak` line that states the limits from `accept`, `maxSize` and `maxFiles`. Drag-over reuses the accent preview tier, `--ds-fill-accent-weak` with a `--ds-stroke-accent` dash, and a drag is a pointer enhancement only, so keyboard users reach every function through the same input. No token is new.

**Feedback.**

| Surface | When | Paint |
|---|---|---|
| Shared `useAnnounce`, polite | A selection with no rejection | Announcement only |
| Local `role="status"`, polite and visible | A rejection or a partial acceptance | A `Warning` glyph and text in the warning family |
| `Field.validation`, `role="alert"` | The caller passes `validation` | The field's own error |

On a partial acceptance the accepted files commit and the rejection shows on the status region alone, never announced twice.

**Selection.** Every pick or drop replaces the value, and the input's value resets to `''` so the same file can fire again. One clear-all control, an `IconButton inset` named `Remove all files`, is neutral and not `tone="danger"`, and it is a real tab stop, because it is the only way to clear.

**API.** `value` (`File | File[] | undefined`, never `null`), a required `onValueChange`, `accept`, `isMultiple`, `maxSize`, `maxFiles`, `mode`, `placeholder`, `size`, `isRequired`, a required `label`, `description`, `validation`, `width` and `disabledReason`. With `disabledReason` the input is `aria-disabled` rather than `disabled`, and neither the picker nor a drop responds ([disabled-reason](#disabled-reason)). `formatFileSize` and `validateFiles` live in `src/utils`.

**Changed from.** No earlier ruling covered this. The Astryx source makes a `role="button"` div the control and defaults to `mode="input"`, and this port departs from both ([catalog-as-specification](#catalog-as-specification)).

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-10.

- [focus-ring](#focus-ring) replaces the neutral focus hairline on the drop surface with the accent focus ring.
- [drop-target-dash](#drop-target-dash) lays a second dash over the step 7 drag-over dash, so the edge holds 3:1.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **FileInput — a dropzone file picker: the native-`<input type=file>`-as-control model, the earned drop surface, three feedback surfaces (2026-07-10).** FileInput earns **genuinely net-new UI** — a visual **drop surface** — with the net-new **confined to that surface** and everything else **assembled from shipped parts** (the shared `Field` shell, [disabled-reason](#disabled-reason) soft-disable, `IconButton` clear, `Button`, the singleton `useAnnounce`, the accent **preview** tier). **(1) The native `<input type="file">` is the operable control AND the tab stop** (dropzone mode) — a **deliberate divergence** from Astryx's hand-rolled `role="button"` **div**: the native input ships **Enter/Space/focus/disabled/label-association for free** (matching React Aria's `FileTrigger` + GOV.UK progressive enhancement), so a div re-implementing all of that is pure risk. It is hidden with the **CLIP technique** (the `useAnnounce` visually-hidden idiom) — **never** `display:none`/`visibility:hidden`, which would drop it from the **tab order + a11y tree** — takes its `id`/`aria-describedby`/`aria-invalid` from the Field via `useOptionalFieldControl` (the Field label's `htmlFor` **NAMES** it), and the drop surface is **wrapped in a `<label>`** so a pointer click anywhere opens the picker and the input's focus lights the zone's ring via **`:focus-within`** (the **[field-shell-adoption](#field-shell-adoption)/TextArea** override pattern, NOT a parallel focus class). **The wrapping label never pollutes the accessible name:** all of the dropzone's visible content is `aria-hidden`, so the name comes **solely** from `Field.Label`; and the visible "browse" cue is **styled non-interactive accent text**, never a nested `<button>` (which would double-activate the picker). **(2) `mode="dropzone"` is the DEFAULT** — a **stated divergence** from Astryx's `'input'` default that aligns our default with **Astryx's OWN doc guidance** (which pushes the dropzone). `mode="input"` is the **compact Button row** — a real System `Button` ("Choose file") calling `input.click()` with the input at `tabIndex={-1}`: the **focus-mechanism delta** is input-is-tab-stop in dropzone vs **Button**-is-tab-stop in compact. **(3) Drag-and-drop is a POINTER-ONLY enhancement.** `dragenter/over/leave/drop` toggle a `data-drop-target` attribute; keyboard users are **fully served by the same input**, so there is **no second tab stop** (WCAG 2.1.1). **(4) The earned net-new visual — the drop surface only.** A large **dashed** target (`--ds-stroke-weak`) over `--ds-bg-subtle` with `--ds-fill-hover` on hover, a centered Phosphor `UploadSimple` (`--ds-icon-neutral`), a primary prompt, and a `--ds-text-weak` **constraints line stated up front** ("PNG or JPG, up to 5 MB", derived from `accept`/`maxSize`/`maxFiles` and also folded into `aria-describedby`). **Drag-over REUSES the accent PREVIEW tier** — `--ds-fill-accent-weak` (a3, the **same** preview role Calendar uses, [calendar-grid](#calendar-grid)) + `--ds-stroke-accent` dashed border — accent-aware, **NOT a new colour**. Focus is the neutral `--ds-stroke-focus-hairline` ([validation-focus-paint](#validation-focus-paint)). **(5) THREE feedback surfaces that never cross (FileInput needs three, not the inputs' two).** **Surface 1 — clean selection** → the shared **POLITE** `useAnnounce` ("Added report.pdf, 2.4 MB" / "N files selected"), fired **only when there are no rejections**. **Surface 2 — rejections + PARTIAL acceptance** → a **component-local `role="status" aria-live="polite"` that is ALSO VISIBLE text** below the control (**status, NOT alert** — partial acceptance isn't a blocking failure; the user must **SEE** which files were dropped), colour-not-alone (a `Warning` glyph + text in the **warning** family — a heads-up, **not** the red error vocabulary), always mounted **empty** so a later-populated status announces reliably (the `useAnnounce` "born-with-content" lesson) and collapses to zero height when idle. Copy is **honest and categorized** — wrong-type "PNG or JPG only — 'cat.gif' wasn't added.", too-big "Each file must be under 5 MB — 'video.mov' (82 MB) wasn't added.", too-many "You can add up to 5 files — 3 weren't added.", **partial leads with the win** "Added 2 files. 'cat.gif' … weren't added — PNG or JPG only." **Surface 3 — standing whole-field invalid** → `Field.validation` (`role="alert"`), reserved for a **caller** `validation` (a form owns submit-time required-empty; **no error is painted at rest**). **On a partial accept: COMMIT the accepted subset AND surface the rejection on Surface 2 — NEVER double-announce** (the local region self-announces; `useAnnounce` owns **only** clean-success + clear-all). **(6) Replace-never-append + a single clear-all.** Every selection/drop **REPLACES** value; the native input's `.value` is **reset to `''`** after each pick so re-selecting the same file re-fires.
