Per-file remove is a **named deferral**; the single clear-all ✕ (`IconButton inset`, `aria-label="Remove all files"`) is **NEUTRAL — not `tone="danger"`** (clearing an **un-uploaded** selection is trivially reversible, so it must not borrow the destructive vocabulary) and a **REAL tab stop** (tabbable — it is the **only** way to clear, so, unlike the [field-family-anatomy](#field-family-anatomy) date/time ✕ at `tabIndex=-1`, it earns the tab order — the same logic **[date-input](#date-input) §4** used for DateInput's calendar button). **(7) Lifted helpers.** `formatFileSize` (binary 1024, 1-decimal KB/MB) + `validateFiles` (PARTIAL acceptance — filters progressively on accept-token/oversize/maxFiles-slice, returns the **surviving subset PLUS** per-file error strings) are extracted to `src/utils/*` **byte-faithful** (Astryx [catalog-as-specification](#catalog-as-specification) @ `88c95e4`) with **net-new node-lane logic coverage** upstream ships none of — including the **MIXED partial-acceptance** case (some pass + some rejected). **(8) API:** `value?: File | File[]` (`undefined` = empty — **null-free**, normalized from upstream's `null`), a *required* `onValueChange(File | File[] | undefined)`, **controlled**; `accept`/`isMultiple`/`maxSize`/`maxFiles`/`mode`/`placeholder`/`size`/`isRequired`/`label`(required)+`description`/`validation`/`width`. **`disabledReason` soft-disable ([disabled-reason](#disabled-reason)):** the operable control + the drag handlers **early-return** while soft; the input is `aria-disabled` (**not** native `disabled`, so the reason stays perceivable), and its `onClick` is `preventDefault`'d so the native picker never opens. **The earned net-new is the drop-surface + accent-preview-drag-over + `:focus-within`-ring + the visible status region CSS (`rt-ds-fileinput-*`, geometric + existing `--ds-*` roles); ZERO net-new tokens.** No `!important`; `.radix-themes`-scoped. Ported under [catalog-as-specification](#catalog-as-specification).

### token-chip

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-10.

**Use Token for a chip with a clickable or linked body, and Badge for a chip that only labels.**

**Body.** One mode per chip, chosen by props:

- `href`: a link. The chip opens a page.
- `onClick`: a button. The chip runs an action, or with `pressed` it toggles ([token-pressed-state](#token-pressed-state)).
- Neither: plain text. The chip is a removable label.

**Remove.** `onRemove` adds a remove control beside the body, never inside it, so a clickable or linked chip can also be removable and the markup stays valid. Its accessible name is `Remove {label}` unless `removeLabel` replaces it.

**Keyboard.** A clickable or linked body and its remove control are two tab stops. Backspace or Delete on a focused body removes the chip.

**Props.** `children` or `label`, `color`, `size`, `leadingIcon`, `onRemove`, `removeLabel`, `disabled`, either `href` or `onClick`, and `pressed` beside `onClick` only ([token-pressed-state](#token-pressed-state)). Token takes no `tone` prop, and `asChild` is a type error.

**Changed from.** Badge was the only chip component. It took a clickable body through `asChild` or a remove control through `onRemove`, and never both, because a remove control inside a link or a button is invalid HTML.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-10.

- [badge-scope](#badge-scope) narrows Badge to labels, so every clickable, linked or removable chip is a Token.
- [focus-ring](#focus-ring) replaces the neutral focus hairline with the accent focus ring.
- [aschild-or-type-error](#aschild-or-type-error) refuses `asChild` as a type error instead of a crash.
- [token-pressed-state](#token-pressed-state) adds `pressed` to the clickable body, so a Token can be a toggle that keeps one width whether it is pressed or not.

**Evidence.** The entry as first written:

> **Token — the interactive chip: an invisible-button body + a sibling remove ✕, reskinning nothing (2026-07-10).** The **interactive sibling of Badge**. **The boundary test:** *does the body do something?* **Yes → Token** (a chip whose body clicks or navigates), **No → Badge** (a display/labeling chip). Token is the one case Badge **structurally forbids** — an interactive body that **COEXISTS** with a remove ✕: Badge's compile-time invariant bans `onRemove` + `asChild` because a ✕ nested inside an interactive `<button>`/`<a>` is **invalid HTML** (nested interactives). **(1) Reskin NOTHING — the ONLY net-new is the sibling invisible-button body.** Token is a **separate component**, not a Badge extension, yet its container **IS a `.rt-Badge`** (`variant="surface"` + the categorical `color` pass-through), so the **Badge chip skin, the `[data-interactive]` paint (the 24px pointer floor lives on the chip's real targets — the body and the ✕, grown on cancelling negative margins — not on the container's box, `--ds-fill-hover`/`--ds-fill-press` gradient-over-color hover/press, the gray-12 hairline focus ring, [the first neutral focus ring]/[validation-focus-paint]), and the inset-✕ CSS (`.rt-Badge .rt-IconButton[data-inset]` — the already-solved extended 24×24 hit area) all apply VERBATIM**. The remove ✕ reuses Badge's `IconButton inset size="1"` + the `Remove {label}` default name + the icon-only-needs-`aria-label` DEV warning. The net-new is exactly: a container span + an **`all:unset` inner body** + a **SIBLING** remove ✕ (never nested) + the focus ring **HOISTED** to the container via `:has(.rt-ds-token-body:focus-visible)` (because the body is `all:unset` with `outline:none`, `:focus-visible` never matches the container) + `stopPropagation` on remove. **Zero net-new tokens.** **(2) The sibling-remove structure for ALL modes fixes an upstream bug.** Astryx nests the remove `<button>` **INSIDE** the `<a>` for the link case (button-in-anchor = **invalid HTML, untested**). OUR port renders the ✕ as a **SIBLING** of the `<a>` body inside the container span in **every** mode, so removal coexists with a link cleanly — a stated **divergence-fixing-an-upstream-bug**. **(3) Three modes, resolved by props, NO visual split.** `href` → **link** body (`<a>`); `onClick` → **clickable** body (`<button>`); else → **static** body (`<span>`, no affordance) — a compile-time XOR so `onClick`/`href` can't combine (precedence `href` → link). **Static reads PIXEL-IDENTICAL to Badge's removable chip** (same surface, same inset ✕, no `cursor:pointer`, no body hover/focus — it must not become a second drifting display-chip skin). **Link + clickable are visually IDENTICAL** — both take the `[data-interactive]` paint, with **NO link/clickable distinction and NO text underline** (`all:unset` strips it): the bounded surface + hover-deepen **IS** the affordance, like every other interactive surface; link vs clickable differ only in semantics (`<a>` vs `<button>`). **(4) A11y — two separate focusables, not one tab stop.** The body and the ✕ are **TWO** focusable controls (a bare removable-interactive Token is up to **2** tab stops — single-tab-stop/roving is a **container** concern for the future `Tokenizer`, out of scope here); the two are **valid-HTML siblings, never nested** (asserted: exactly 2 buttons, none containing another; the href mode renders an `<a>` with the ✕ a sibling — no button-in-anchor). The ✕ is named `Remove {label}` (Badge's default); the body is named by its content (or `aria-label` when icon-only). **Keyboard removal:** the ✕ removes on click/Enter/Space, and **additionally Backspace/Delete while the BODY is focused removes** the chip (guarded to no-op when not removable or disabled). **`disabled` mirrors to BOTH inner controls** (native `disabled` on the button body + the ✕; `aria-disabled` + `preventDefault` on the `<a>`, which can't be natively disabled) and dims the chip by **reusing Radix's OWN button-disabled skin** (gray-a8 text over gray-a3 fill — the sanctioned reuse-a-Radix-skin exception, since Radix Badge ships no disabled state); Token does **NOT** use the Field `disabledReason` machinery (it's a leaf chip — a consumer wraps it in a Tooltip if a reason is needed). **(5) NO `tone` axis.** [destructive-tone] is a **destructive-action** ban, not a chip concern — semantics ride the categorical `color` (Badge's hues); [destructive-tone] stays intact. **API (LITE):** `children` (or `label`) · `color?` · `onRemove?(e)` · `onClick?` XOR `href?` · `disabled?` · `size?` (via `useResolvedSize("text")`) · `leadingIcon?` · `ref` (→ the container). **Dropped as named deferrals:** `isLabelHidden` / `endContent` / `description` / the Astryx `InteractiveRoleContext` / polymorphic-Link. All scoped `.radix-themes`, no `!important`, no raw scales beyond the reused Radix disabled skin.

### overflow-list

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-10.

**`OverflowList` measures its width and folds the items that do not fit into one `+N` indicator, so a row stays on one line.**

**What you see.** A horizontal row of chips, tags or actions keeps the items that fit and shows `+N` for the rest. The default indicator is a neutral, non-interactive gray `Badge` with the accessible name `N more`. Revealing the hidden items, for example with a clickable `Token` that opens a `DropdownMenu`, is the consumer's job through `overflowRenderer`, which receives each hidden item with its original index.

**Accessibility.** Collapsed items leave the accessibility tree, because they move into the indicator. This is deliberate and differs from [overlay-hover-scrim](#overlay-hover-scrim), which keeps hidden content reachable. The measurement copy is `aria-hidden` and `inert`, and the visible set is a `role="group"` named by `label`, default `"List"`, the `AvatarGroup` idiom.

**Props.**

- `children`
- `gap`: a spacing step from 0 to 9 on `--ds-space-*`, default `2`, which also feeds the fit arithmetic.
- `minVisibleItems`: default `0`.
- `collapseFrom`: `'end'`, the default, keeps the leading items with `+N` last, and `'start'` keeps the trailing items with `+N` first. The default departs from Blueprint's `'start'` and matches `AvatarGroup`.
- `behavior`: `'observeSelf'`, the default, or `'observeParent'`, which sets the visible container to `width: 100%` while it overflows so the list regains width when its parent widens.
- `label`, `overflowRenderer` and `ref`.

**Mechanism.**

- The engine is lifted whole from Astryx ([catalog-as-specification](#catalog-as-specification)). One shared `ResizeObserver` in `src/utils/sharedResizeObserver.ts` serves every instance and fires each callback once when it registers.
- `src/hooks/useOverflow.ts` reads the widths and calls the pure reducer in `src/utils/computeVisibleCount.ts`, which the node lane tests directly.
- A hidden copy holds every child plus the indicator at its widest, so the list measures without a flicker. The indicator is the last measured child, identified by position, because upstream's `data-overflow-indicator` attribute never exists on the rendered node.
- Cleanup runs in the callback ref on unmount, not in an effect return, so a rewrite to `useRef` and `useEffect` would drop it.
- The CSS is layout only, with zero new tokens, no `!important` and `.radix-themes` scope.

**Gap.** The pixel mirror of the gap assumes the default `<Theme scaling>` of 1, so another scaling would drift the measured gap from the rendered one. Reading the resolved gap from the DOM is the fix if a non-default scaling ships.

**Changed from.** No earlier ruling covered this.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-10. No later ruling amends it.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **OverflowList — the lifted collapse-to-"+N" MEASUREMENT ENGINE, not an indicator (2026-07-10).** A horizontal list that measures its width and folds overflowing items into a single **+N**, so a row of chips/tags/actions stays one line responsively. The value is **responsive layout**; the indicator + reveal are **defaulted but consumer-overridable**. **(1) The engine is lifted whole (Astryx [catalog-as-specification](#catalog-as-specification) @ `88c95e4`).** Three lifted pieces: **`src/utils/sharedResizeObserver.ts`** — a lazily-created **singleton** `ResizeObserver` + a `Map<Element, cb>` so N components share ONE observer (one dispatch/frame); `observeResize` registers + observes + **fires the cb synchronously once** (synthetic `{target}` entry) so callers need no separate initial-measure path; `unobserveResize` disconnects + **NULLS the singleton when the map empties** (a later observe re-creates it). **`src/hooks/useOverflow.ts`** — the DOM wrapper: reads `offsetWidth`/`clientWidth`, wires the shared observer, calls the reducer; reuses our `useIsomorphicLayoutEffect`. **`src/components/ui/OverflowList.tsx`** — the component. **(2) The pure reducer is EXTRACTED for the node lane.** `src/utils/computeVisibleCount.ts` is the greedy-fit math pulled out of upstream's `calculate` closure: reverse widths for `collapseFrom:'start'`; greedily accumulate `itemWidth + gap`, reserving `indicatorWidth + gap` for every **non-last** item; break when `candidate + reserved > available && count >= minVisibleItems`; clamp to `[minVisibleItems, itemCount]`. Upstream only tested it **through** the hook (mocking elements as `{offsetWidth}`) — i.e. it was testing this reducer — so it is now **pure + node-lane logic-tested** (`computeVisibleCount.logic.test.ts` ports those arithmetic cases as direct assertions; `sharedResizeObserver.logic.test.ts` ports the 6 observer cases). **(3) Dual-render measurement.** A hidden `<div aria-hidden inert style="position:absolute;visibility:hidden;height:0">` holds **ALL** children **plus the indicator rendered at MAX width**, and a visible container holds the first `visibleCount` items + the **live** indicator. Measuring a twin avoids render-then-shrink flicker. **(4) The indicator is identified by POSITION, not an attribute.** The engine slices `hasIndicator = allChildren.length > itemCount` and takes the **last** measured child as the indicator — the upstream `data-overflow-indicator` attribute is **FICTIONAL** (it never exists on the rendered node); relying on it would silently no-op. **(5) Default `overflowRenderer` = a neutral, NON-interactive Badge "+N"** (`<Badge color="gray">+N</Badge>` — AvatarGroup's stronger-neutral "reads as a count" treatment) with a **hidden `"N more"` accessible name** (`aria-label`). It is **overridable**: the **reveal** of the hidden items (a menu/popover — e.g. a clickable **`Token`** opening the consumer's `DropdownMenu`, each `overflowItem` carrying its original `index`) is the **CONSUMER's** job, not the engine's. **(6) Collapsed items LEAVE the a11y tree — this is NOT [overlay-hover-scrim](#overlay-hover-scrim).** [overlay-hover-scrim](#overlay-hover-scrim)'s reveal idiom keeps hover-revealed content **reachable**; here the folded items are genuinely **relocated** into the indicator, so they are gone from the a11y tree. The **measurement copy is `aria-hidden` + `inert`** so the duplicated children never double-announce, and the **visible set is wrapped in a named `role="group"`** (`label`, default `"List"`) — reusing the **AvatarGroup group-naming idiom** so a screen reader hears one unit, not N items + a stray counter. Flagged in History so no reviewer "fixes" it toward [overlay-hover-scrim](#overlay-hover-scrim). **(7) `collapseFrom='end'` default — a STATED divergence from Blueprint's `'start'`**, matching AvatarGroup's end-collapse house idiom and every token/avatar list. `'end'` keeps leading items, "+N" trails; `'start'` keeps trailing items, "+N" leads. **(8) The cleanup is CALLBACK-REF based, not a `useEffect` return.** React calls `containerRef(null)` on unmount and **that** is where `unobserveResize` runs — there is **deliberately no effect-return teardown** upstream; a naive `useRef` + `useEffect` rewrite would **drop** the observer cleanup. The callback refs are load-bearing (preserved verbatim). **API (LITE):** `children` · `gap?` (0–9 spacing step → `--ds-space-*`, default `2`, also feeds the fit math via a px mirror of the Radix `--space` scale) · `minVisibleItems?` (default `0`) · `collapseFrom?` (default `'end'`) · `behavior?` (`'observeSelf'` default / `'observeParent'` sets the visible container `width:100%` while overflowing for grow-back) · `label?` · `overflowRenderer?` · `ref`. **CSS is layout-only** (`rt-ds-overflowlist` flex row + `overflow:hidden`/`white-space:nowrap`/`min-width:0`, the absolutely-positioned measurement copy, gap steps from `--ds-space-*`); **ZERO net-new tokens**, no `!important`, `.radix-themes`-scoped. **Known limitation:** the gap px mirror assumes the default `<Theme scaling>` (1) — a themed scaling would drift the arithmetic gap from the rendered gap (the same assumption `_size.stories.tsx` documents); a DOM-read of the resolved gap is the future fix if a non-default scaling ships. Ported under [catalog-as-specification](#catalog-as-specification).

### tokenizer-input

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-10.

**Tokenizer is a multi-value input whose tokens come only from its dropdown, built from the `Field` shell, Token chips and an embedded Typeahead.**

**Creation.**

- A token is created only by picking a row in the dropdown. No Enter, comma, paste split or blur commits free text.
- With `creatable`, default `false`, a `Create "{query}"` row sits at the bottom of the list with a `+` glyph and the quoted query.
- That row takes no highlight while real matches exist, so Enter picks the match. With no real match it becomes the first row, so Enter on a new value commits it.

**Why.** Users expect Enter to tag, and the system pays that cost on purpose: a token made from the dropdown is real, deduplicated and open to validation.

**Build.**

- `value` and `onValueChange(items, change)` are required, and `change.type` is `add`, `create` or `remove`. `source` takes the same `TypeaheadSource` that Typeahead reads.
- Typeahead takes an `embedded` mode. Its input renders with no border, fill or ring of its own, a selection fires the host's `onValueChange` and clears the query while `value` stays null, and the popover anchors to the whole Tokenizer surface. Standalone Typeahead does not change.
- The one new surface is a wrapping `role="group"` chip row that reuses the TextField skin, `--color-surface` with a `--gray-a7` hairline and `--ds-radius-2`, and carries the focus ring on the row while its input holds keyboard focus. It adds no tokens.
- The chips come first in source order, then the input as the last flex child. A click anywhere focuses the input, and the placeholder names the mechanism, "Search to add…", never "press Enter".

**Keyboard.**

- The field is one forward tab stop, the input.
- Shift+Tab from the input reaches the chips, and Arrow Left, Arrow Right, Home and End move between them. Each chip is one stop, and its remove control is a pointer target only.
- Backspace or Delete on a focused chip removes it, and focus moves to the next chip, else the previous one, else the input.
- Backspace in the empty input removes the last chip.

**States.**

- Three layers keep tokens unique: a selected item never appears in the menu, no `Create` row appears for a value already selected or matching a result label, and a guard runs at commit.
- `maxEntries` collapses the input to a focusable read-only sliver, never hidden or disabled, so Backspace still removes the last chip. The dropdown closes, a calm "Maximum {n} tags" hint shows in the field description as guidance and not an error ([disabled-reason](#disabled-reason)), and the cap is announced once, politely.
- `tokenOverflowBehavior="unfocusedInline"` folds trailing chips into OverflowList's "+N" while the field is blurred and shows every row on focus. The default is `"none"`.
- `htmlName` renders one hidden input per token for form submission, and a natively disabled field submits none.
- `disabled` with `disabledReason` soft-disables the field ([disabled-reason](#disabled-reason)): the input is `aria-disabled` and read-only, chip removal does nothing, and the reason shows in a tooltip beside a glyph. `aria-disabled` on the group marks the dimmed chip text as inactive, which WCAG 1.4.3 exempts.
- "Added {label}", "Removed {label}, {n} remaining" and the cap are announced politely. The assertive channel stays reserved for errors ([date-input](#date-input)).

**Not covered.** Free-text commit, the `unfocusedLayer` overflow, which needs a top-layer primitive the system lacks, `isLabelHidden`, `startIcon`, `endContent`, `renderToken`, `handleRef`, and an edit mode for chips, so chips stay removable only and Enter on a chip does nothing. The upstream `'reorder'` change type, declared and never emitted upstream, is dropped, and the full shared extraction of the Typeahead engine waits for [command-palette](#command-palette).

**Changed from.** No earlier ruling covered a multi-token input. The component follows the Astryx catalog entry under [catalog-as-specification](#catalog-as-specification).

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-10.

- [focus-ring](#focus-ring) replaces the neutral focus ring of [validation-focus-paint](#validation-focus-paint), which the chip row first carried, with the accent focus ring.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **Tokenizer — the dropdown-only multi-token input on the embedded Typeahead engine (2026-07-10).** A multi-value input — committed **Token** chips + a transient type-to-search combobox — on the shared **Field** shell, assembled almost entirely from shipped parts. **(1) The model is dropdown-only — a deliberate, safe divergence.** Tokens are created **ONLY** by picking from the dropdown; with `creatable` (default **FALSE** — the safe DS default, no accidental junk tokens) a `Create "{query}"` row is synthesized (an id-prefixed sentinel) and committed by **picking** it. There is **NO** free-text Enter/comma/paste-split/blur commit — those are **named deferrals**, stated in History. The tradeoff is real and paid on purpose (users expect Enter-to-tag) — dropdown-only creation buys tokens that are **real, deduped, and validatable**. The `Create` row is visually distinct (a `+` glyph + the quoted query), placed at the **BOTTOM**, and **NOT auto-highlighted while real matches exist** (so Enter picks the match, not Create); with **zero real matches it becomes index 0**, so Enter-on-a-new-value commits it (the intuitive path). **(2) It reuses the Typeahead engine via an additive EMBEDDED/transient mode — behavior-preserving.** The flagship Typeahead gained a minimal `embedded` capability: the input renders **chrome-less** (no own border/fill/ring — the host paints the surface + ring), selection is **TRANSIENT** (`value` stays null — on select it fires the host's `onValueChange` and **resets the query to empty**, never syncing to a label), and the popover anchors to an **external** `anchorRef` (the whole Tokenizer surface, via a Popover `virtualRef`) so the dropdown spans the field. Standalone Typeahead is untouched (its ~200-assertion play suite stayed **100% green** before/after). The full shared-util extraction is **deferred to CommandPalette ([command-palette](#command-palette))**. **(3) The one earned net-new surface** is a wrapping `role="group"` chip-row that **REUSES the TextField surface skin** (`--color-surface` fill + `--gray-a7` hairline border + `--ds-radius-2`) and **hoists the [validation-focus-paint](#validation-focus-paint) dual-tone focus ring to the container via `:has(input:focus-visible)`** (Token's [token-chip](#token-chip) idiom, NOT a parallel focus class): the chips (`Token`, source order, `flex-wrap`) then the chrome-less input as the last flex child (`flex:1 1 ~10ch`, min-width so it's always clickable). Click-anywhere focuses the input; the placeholder **NAMES THE MECHANISM** ("Search to add…", never "press Enter"). **Zero net-new tokens.** **(4) Chip roving is owned by Tokenizer (Token stays composable).** The field is **ONE forward tab stop = the input** (a Tab capture-redirect lands focus on the input from outside). Chips are **OUT of the linear Tab sequence** — reached via **Shift+Tab** from the input, then **Arrow Left/Right / Home/End** rove chip-to-chip (one roving stop per chip; the ✕ is swept to `tabindex=-1`, a pointer target only). Backspace/Delete on a focused chip removes it; **post-removal focus goes next → previous → the input** (guarded so the programmatic re-focus after a removal, whose relatedTarget is `<body>`, is NOT bounced back to the input by the capture-redirect). Backspace on the **empty input** removes the last chip + refocuses the input. **(5) Three-layer dedupe** — selected items never appear in the menu; no `Create` row for a value already selected or matching a result label; a commit-time guard. **(6) `maxEntries`** collapses the input to a **focusable sliver** (readOnly, NOT `display:none`/disabled — Backspace still removes the last chip), swaps in an empty source (dropdown suppressed), shows a calm "Maximum {n} tags" hint in the **Field description** (guidance, **not** validation/error — [disabled-reason](#disabled-reason)) folded into `aria-describedby`, and **announces the cap once, politely**. **(7) Overflow** (`tokenOverflowBehavior: 'none' | 'unfocusedInline'`, default `'none'`): `unfocusedInline` collapses trailing chips into **OverflowList**'s "+N" while BLURRED (`collapseFrom="end"`, `behavior="observeParent"`) and expands to full wrapping rows on FOCUS. **`unfocusedLayer` is DEFERRED** — it needs a Layer/top-layer-popover primitive we don't have (named). **(8) `htmlName`** renders a hidden `<input type="hidden" name value={item.id}>` per token for form participation (hard-disabled ones excluded from FormData, mirroring native `disabled`). **(9) Soft-disable ([disabled-reason](#disabled-reason))** — `disabled` + a reason keeps the input `aria-disabled`+`readOnly` (edits/keydown early-return, chip removal inert), with the reason tooltip + glyph; `aria-disabled` on the `role="group"` also marks the dimmed chip text as **inactive-component text** (WCAG 1.4.3 exempt), so axe doesn't misread the intentional dim as a contrast failure. **(10) Parity announce** — the singleton `useAnnounce` speaks adds ("Added {label}") + removes ("Removed {label}, {n} remaining") + the cap, all **politely** (an upgrade over upstream, which announces nothing; the assertive channel stays reserved for errors, [date-input](#date-input)§2). **(11) The phantom `'reorder'`** change type (upstream declares + documents it but never emits it) is **dropped** — the change union is `{item, type: 'add'|'create'|'remove'}`. **API:** `value: T[]` + required `onValueChange(items, change)` · `source: TypeaheadSource<T>` (reused) · `creatable?` (false) · `maxEntries?` · `tokenOverflowBehavior?` (`'none'`) · `htmlName?` · `label`+`description?`+`validation?` · `disabled?`/`disabledReason?` · `placeholder?` ("Search to add…") · `size?`/`width?`/`debounceMs?` · `ref`. **Dropped as named deferrals:** `isLabelHidden`/`startIcon`/`endContent`/`renderToken`/`handleRef`, and the token-chip **EDIT** mode (chips stay removable-only, Enter-on-chip unbound). All `.radix-themes`-scoped, no `!important`, no raw scales beyond the reused Radix disabled/surface skins. Ported under [catalog-as-specification](#catalog-as-specification).

### command-palette

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-11.

**CommandPalette is a search-to-act and search-to-pick modal, built on the combobox engine lifted out of Typeahead and composed over the raw Radix Themes `Dialog`.**

**Engine.** Typeahead's async search and its listbox navigation moved, with no change in behaviour, into `src/components/ui/useComboboxEngine.ts` as `useAsyncSearch` and `useListboxNavigation`, and Typeahead calls them. Two options default off, so Typeahead is unchanged, and the palette enables both: `optimisticNarrow` filters the shown rows by the new query while the source resolves, and `commitQueryWithResults` makes the "No commands match" line name the committed query, so the line holds steady while a search with no results is pending. The engine has no letter-jump path.

**Shell.** The palette composes the raw Radix Themes `Dialog` and inherits modal motion from the shared `.rt-BaseDialogContent` and `.rt-BaseDialogOverlay` bindings ([toast-feedback-tier](#toast-feedback-tier)), with no motion of its own. The Dialog's own overlay is the backdrop. The panel sits 12vh from the top through `align="start"` and a `:has(> .rt-ds-commandpalette)` padding rule, is at most `min(640px, calc(100vw - 2rem))` wide, paints the opaque overlay surface of [floating-surface-fill](#floating-surface-fill), scrolls its results list inside, and adds no token.

**Listbox.**

- One `groupItems` call (`src/components/ui/groupItems.ts`) produces both the flat order the arrow keys walk and the render tree.
- Group headings are `role="group"` labels, never options, so the arrow keys cross group boundaries with no stop.
- The active row paints `--ds-fill-hover` through `data-highlighted`, and when it enters a new group, that group's heading scrolls into view.
- A `mouseenter` with no pointer move since the last keydown leaves the active row where it is.
- The trailing spinner mounts only after 150ms, so a fast search never flashes it.
- Escape closes the palette through the Dialog's own `onOpenChange`. The footer of key hints, `showFooter`, defaults to true and is `aria-hidden`.

**Modes.**

- Launcher, with no `value`: no option carries `aria-selected`, and the palette opens with nothing highlighted.
- Picker, with `value` and `onValueChange`: the matching option carries `aria-selected`, paints `--ds-fill-selected-subtle`, and is highlighted on open.
- `isInline`: a plain `div` that mirrors the surface for docs pages, with no dialog, backdrop, focus trap, Escape, scroll lock, autofocus or mount scroll. Its docs specimens disable axe's `scrollable-region-focusable` rule, a false positive for the combobox pattern of the ARIA Authoring Practices Guide (APG), whose input arrow keys scroll the list.

**Not covered.** A global ⌘K hotkey, since the consumer opens the palette through `open` and `onOpenChange`, frecency ranking, and nested command pages.

**Changed from.** The system had no palette. Typeahead held its async search and listbox navigation inline, and [tokenizer-input](#tokenizer-input) deferred their extraction to this build, a port under [catalog-as-specification](#catalog-as-specification).

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-11.

- [standard-dialog](#standard-dialog) ships the System `Dialog` and records that the palette keeps the raw Radix Themes `Dialog` on purpose.
- [box-law-scope](#box-law-scope) puts the palette's input row on the control box ladder, 24, 32 and 40px.
- [focus-return-on-close](#focus-return-on-close) returns focus to the opener when the palette closes, because a palette driven from `open` registers no trigger.
- [selected-row-cue](#selected-row-cue) sets the picked option label at `--ds-font-weight-strong` in `--ds-text-strong` and draws its icon solid.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **CommandPalette — the ⌘K surface on an engine EXTRACTED from the Typeahead flagship, over a raw Radix Dialog (2026-07-11).** A search-to-act / search-to-pick modal — a chrome-less search input over a grouped, keyboard-navigable listbox. Built by first extracting the flagship's combobox brain, then composing on it. **(1) The engine extraction (behavior-preserving).** Typeahead's async pipeline and its roving aria-activedescendant machine moved into `src/components/ui/useComboboxEngine.ts` — **`useAsyncSearch`** (the monotonic generation guard `searchGen`/`resultsGen`, the debounce, the loading/error/empty derivation, keep-prior-content-on-refine, the DISTINCT retryable error, and the `useAnnounce` parity announcements) and **`useListboxNavigation`** (highlightedIndex, the Arrow/Home/End wrap-around movers, the active-row `scrollIntoView`, and the `getItemId`/aria-activedescendant id scheme). The refactor is a pure MOVE — Typeahead now CALLS the hooks with the SAME closures/deps/refs/timing (a small render-time ref bridges the two-way dep: `useAsyncSearch` moves the cursor via `useListboxNavigation`'s stable setter, which needs the result COUNT from `useAsyncSearch`). **There is NO letter-jump / type-ahead-to-item path** (Typeahead never had one) — so CommandPalette's upstream `hasSearch` wart is gone **by construction**. **Verified preserved:** Typeahead's full play suite (`_typeahead.stories.tsx` — AriaSelection/Validation/Keyboard/States, incl. the select-vs-search + search-vs-search race guards) and Tokenizer's embedded-mode suite (`_tokenizer.stories.tsx`, 9 plays) stayed **100% green** before/after. **(2) Two opt-in engine deltas, DEFAULTING OFF (so Typeahead is unchanged), turned ON by CommandPalette:** **optimistic narrowing** (`optimisticNarrow` — client-filter the shown rows by the new query substring while the async source resolves; OFF = Typeahead's keep-prior-content-untouched) and **committed-query empty text** (`commitQueryWithResults` — track a `committedQuery` that advances only WITH results, so the "No commands match {query}" line echoes the committed query and holds steady while a no-result search is pending, never flipping to the live query mid-search). **(3) The shell is the RAW Radix Themes `Dialog` ([component-registry](#component-registry) agent-gap rule).** The System `Dialog` wrapper is `status:"planned"` in the registry, so — rather than improvise a `System/Dialog` — CommandPalette composes the raw Radix Themes Dialog thinly (like `AlertDialog.tsx` wraps raw AlertDialog); **the Dialog gap is surfaced** (registry stays `planned`). Modal enter/exit motion ([toast-feedback-tier](#toast-feedback-tier)) is **INHERITED** from the existing `.rt-BaseDialogContent`/`.rt-BaseDialogOverlay` bindings — **NO per-component motion override** (it would double-animate); the Dialog's **own overlay scrim** is the backdrop (NOT the separate `--ds-scrim`/Overlay). **Top-anchored ~12vh** (net-new, justified — Radix centers vertically, wrong for a palette): `align="start"` disables the vertical centering, then a `:has(> .rt-ds-commandpalette)` override sets the scroll-padding's top padding to 12vh; **fixed** `max-width: min(640px, calc(100vw - 2rem))`; the compound `.radix-themes .rt-ds-commandpalette` (0,2,0) beats Radix's `.rt-BaseDialogContent` to repaint the **opaque overlay surface** ([floating-surface-fill](#floating-surface-fill): `--ds-bg-overlay`/`--ds-shadow-overlay`/`--ds-radius-3`) and strip the dialog's inner padding, with the results list the **internal scroll container**. **(4) Grouping from ONE `groupItems` call.** The lifted `src/components/ui/groupItems.ts` (Astryx [catalog-as-specification](#catalog-as-specification)) is called ONCE; BOTH the **flat activedescendant order** AND the **render tree** derive from it — killing the upstream fragile dual-invariant (two inline group passes that had to agree). Group headings are `role="group"` + `aria-labelledby` a quiet weak heading (MultiSelect's group-label token binding) — **visual only, NEVER options** — so arrows flow **continuously across group boundaries**. The active row paints `--ds-fill-hover` via `data-highlighted` (the Select/MultiSelect neutral highlight vocabulary). **(5) Launcher vs. picker.** A launcher (no `value`) sets `aria-selected` on **NO** option (no persistent selection); the optional picker (`value?: string` + `onValueChange?`) marks the matching option `aria-selected` with a muted `--ds-fill-selected-subtle` (a5) paint (listed BEFORE the highlight rule so an active-selected row still shows the neutral cursor). Bootstrap highlights the preselected value in picker mode, else opens with nothing highlighted. **(6) A 150ms delayed-spinner grace** (net-new, justified): the busy flag is immediate for logic, but the visible trailing-slot Spinner is **MOUNTED only after ~150ms**, cancelled on resolve — a sub-150ms async resolve never flashes it. **(7) Two `_internal` polish behaviors:** the active row's **group HEADER scrolls into view** when the active index crosses into a new group (not just the row); and a **pointer-vs-keyboard guard** ignores a `mouseenter` that isn't preceded by a real pointer move since the last keydown (so a keyboard scroll under a stationary cursor can't steal the active row). **(8) `isInline` docs mode** renders a plain `<div>` mirroring the surface — no `<dialog>`/backdrop/focus-trap/Escape/scroll-lock, no autofocus, no mount-scroll — so docs stories stay static/calm on view. **Escape** closes via the Dialog's own `onOpenChange` (no duplicate handler); the aria-hidden Kbd-hint footer (`showFooter`, default true) is redundant for AT (the combobox roles + announcer carry operability). **Zero net-new tokens; `.radix-themes`-scoped; no `!important`.** The one documented axe carve-out: `scrollable-region-focusable` is scoped off for the live-listbox docs specimens (a FALSE positive for the APG combobox — the input's arrow keys provide keyboard scroll access). **Deferred (named):** a global ⌘K hotkey (opening stays consumer-controlled via `open`/`onOpenChange`), frecency ranking, and nested/sub-command pages. Ported under [catalog-as-specification](#catalog-as-specification).

### item-row-primitive

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-11.

**`Item` is one internal row primitive that List, ListItem and TreeList rows share, and `List` is a passive semantic list built on it.**

**Item.** `src/components/ui/Item.tsx` is internal, like `Field.tsx`: it has no `registry.json` entry and the package does not export it. Its slots are `marker`, `startContent`, `label` (required) with `description`, and `endContent`, and its props are `as` (`div`, `li` or `span`), `align`, `density` (block padding of `--ds-space-4`, `--ds-space-8` or `--ds-space-12`), `labelLines`, `descriptionLines`, `isHighlighted`, `isSelected`, `isDisabled`, `onClick` and `href`.

**Interactivity.** One guard keeps a row free of nested interactive elements.

- A row with `onClick` or `href` and no `role` from its parent puts the label and description inside an invisible `<button>` or plain `<a>` (`.rt-ds-item-body`), so the whole row is one keyboard control, and draws the focus ring on the root through `:has(.rt-ds-item-body:focus-visible)`.
- A row with a parent `role` such as `menuitem` or `treeitem` renders no invisible body, because the parent owns keyboard and focus, and its `onClick` sits on the root.
- In both cases the root's click handler extends the hit area to the padding and slots, and ignores a click on the body or on any nested `button`, `a`, `input`, `select` or `textarea`, so nothing fires twice.

**Paint and state.** Paint comes from shipped `--ds-*` tokens on the Select menu vocabulary: `--ds-fill-hover` for hover and `isHighlighted`, `--ds-fill-press` for press, and `--ds-fill-selected-subtle` for `isSelected`, with no hover tint on a selected row. `aria-selected` appears only when a `role` is present, because it is not a global ARIA attribute, and a disabled row carries `aria-disabled` on the root, dims its content to 0.5 opacity, and disables its body.

**List.** `List` renders a passive `<ul>`, or an `<ol>` when `listStyle="decimal"`, and passes density, dividers and marker style to `ListItem` through a context. `ListItem` draws a custom marker in `--ds-text-strong`, aligned to the first line (a 6px dot, a 6px ring, or a CSS counter number), and renders the rest as `Item as="li"`.

**Semantics.** A marker-less `<ul>` restores `role="list"`, because `list-style: none` strips list semantics in Safari, `header` names the list through `aria-labelledby`, and `<ol start>` appears only for a start other than 1. List carries no menu roles and no roving focus: menus are `DropdownMenu`, and trees are `TreeList`.

**Changed from.** The Astryx `Item` and `List` family this port follows ([catalog-as-specification](#catalog-as-specification)) put a raw `onClick` on the root of a row with a parent role, which fired twice on a nested control, and emitted `aria-selected` on every selected row.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-11.

- [tree-list](#tree-list) adds `ariaSelected` for a selection tri-state, `bodyTabIndex` to render the real body under a parent `role`, and a root `tabIndex`.
- [link-and-link-provider](#link-and-link-provider) routes the `href` body through `useLinkComponent`, so a row can render a router link.
- [focus-ring](#focus-ring) replaces the neutral focus hairline with the accent focus ring.
- [selected-row-cue](#selected-row-cue) sets a selected row's label at 600 in strong ink and turns its start icon solid.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **Item (a net-new `_internal` row primitive) + List/ListItem — the passive semantic list (2026-07-11).** The shared row-anatomy primitive that List/ListItem and the `TreeList` rows all consume, built **once** (like `Field`) so the row anatomy and its interactivity guard aren't duplicated three ways. **(1) `Item` is `_internal`, NOT a registry `System` component** — `src/components/ui/Item.tsx`, treated exactly as `Field.tsx` (a shared building block with no `registry.json` entry; only `List` flips to `ported`). Slots: `marker` · `startContent` · `label` (required) `+ description` · `endContent`; props `as?('div'|'li'|'span')`, `align?('center'|'start')`, `density?('compact'|'balanced'|'spacious')` (block padding ~4/8/12px → `--ds-space-4/8/12`; spacious also widens inline), `labelLines`/`descriptionLines` (1 = ellipsis, >1 = webkit line-clamp; a **string** label single-line-truncates by default), `isHighlighted`/`isSelected`/`isDisabled`, `onClick`/`href`. **(2) THE INTERACTIVITY DUAL-MODEL is the whole point** — the enforcement of "no nested interactives". **Interactive (`onClick`/`href`) AND the parent passed NO explicit `role`:** the label/description live inside an **invisible `<button>`/`<a>`** (`.rt-ds-item-body`, `all:unset` + `outline:none`, a plain `<a>` NOT Radix Link so its skin can't fight the reset — Token's [token-chip](#token-chip) idiom), so the whole row is **one keyboard-operable control**; the focus ring is **HOISTED** to the root via `:has(.rt-ds-item-body:focus-visible)` → `--ds-stroke-focus-hairline` (longhands — the `outline:` shorthand `var()` CSSOM-serialization trap the Token/Badge blocks document), and the root ALSO carries a container-click handler that gives the **extended hit area** (padding/marker/slots activate the row) while **IGNORING clicks that land on the body or ANY nested `button,a,input,select,textarea`** (no double-fire). **Interactive AND the parent DID pass a `role`** (`menuitem`/`treeitem`/…): **NO invisible wrapper** (the parent owns keyboard + focus for its role — a plain content span renders); `onClick` rides the **root** through the **SAME** ignoring container-click handler, so a click on a nested action control never double-fires the row. *(This unifies both cases on one guard — a deliberate refinement over Astryx, whose parent-role branch put a RAW `onClick` on the root that would double-fire on nested interactives.)* **(3) Paint reuses shipped `--ds-*` only** — hover/press/highlight/selected on the **Select/MultiSelect menu vocabulary** (`--ds-fill-hover` for hover + `isHighlighted`, `--ds-fill-press` for `:active`, `--ds-fill-selected-subtle` for `isSelected`; a selected row is NOT re-tinted on hover), hover transition `--ds-duration-fast` + `--ds-ease-standard`, label `--ds-text-strong`/`--font-size-2`, description `--ds-text-weak`/`--font-size-1`, radius `--ds-radius-2`. **`aria-selected` is emitted ONLY when a `role` is present** (it is NOT a global ARIA attribute — valid only on a selection-supporting role like `option`/`treeitem`/`row`, which the parent collection supplies; a role-less selected row conveys selection **visually via the tint alone**, axe-clean — a fix over Astryx's unconditional `aria-selected`). **Disabled** = `aria-disabled` on the root (exempts the 0.5-opacity content dim from contrast — inactive-component text, WCAG 1.4.3) + native `disabled` on a button body / `aria-disabled`+`tabIndex=-1`+`preventDefault` on an anchor body; `pointer-events:none` only in the non-parent-role case. **(4) `List` = a passive `<ul>`** (or **`<ol>` when `listStyle='decimal'`**) that pushes `{density, hasDividers, listStyle}` through a `ListContext`; **`ListItem`** consumes it, builds the **custom marker** (disc = a 6px filled dot span, circle = a 6px hollow-circle span, decimal = a `.rt-ds-list-number` whose `::before` is `counter(ds-list) "."`), and delegates the rest to **`Item as="li"`**. Markers are custom-rendered (NOT native `list-style-type`) so they align to the first text line and paint from `--ds-text-strong`. Per-item concerns (counter-increment, dividers) are keyed off the List's `data-*` + the child combinator — **no per-item classes**. **(5) The Safari fix is KEPT:** a **marker-less `<ul>` re-adds `role="list"`** (`list-style:none` strips list semantics in Safari) — a marker `<ul>` and any `<ol>` keep native semantics and get no forced role; `header` is wired via `aria-labelledby`; **`<ol start>` is emitted ONLY when `start != null && start !== 1`**, and the CSS counter is seeded `start - 1` (via an inline `counter-reset: ds-list <start-1>`) so the first increment lands on `start`. **(6) Passive, not a menu** — List carries no menu roles/roving focus; menus are `DropdownMenu`, trees are `TreeList` (stated so List isn't overused for those). **Normalized from Astryx `Item`/`List`/`ListItem`/`ListContext` ([catalog-as-specification](#catalog-as-specification) @ `88c95e4`):** StyleX `*Vars` → `--ds-*` (a `.radix-themes`-scoped block in `tokens/components.css`), `useLinkComponent`/`LinkComponent` → a plain `<a>`, `mergeProps`/`themeProps` dropped, the CSS counter renamed `ds-list`. Both `Item` and `ListItem` `forwardRef` to their root (the [toggle-button-group](#toggle-button-group)/[toolbar-slots](#toolbar-slots) roving-collection convention — `TreeList` ([tree-list](#tree-list)) needs it). **Zero net-new tokens, no `!important`, `.radix-themes`-scoped.** Behavioral plays live in `_internal/Item` (`_item.stories.tsx`) + `_internal/List behavior` (`_list.stories.tsx`); docs are `System/List` (full spine — History · Anatomy · Usage incl. the live token spec · Props). Ported under [catalog-as-specification](#catalog-as-specification).

### tree-list

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-11.

**TreeList is the data-driven tree that follows the Web Accessibility Initiative (WAI) ARIA tree pattern, built on the `useTreeFocus` keyboard hook, the shared `Item` row and optional controlled expansion.**

**Structure.** A `<ul role="tree">` of `<li role="treeitem">` rows. Each row composes the `_internal` `Item` primitive ([item-row-primitive](#item-row-primitive)), so the row anatomy and the guard against nested interactive elements are reused. Visible rows render flat as direct children of the tree, with depth carried by `aria-level` and an indent of `--ds-space-8` plus `--ds-space-16` per level, read from a private inline `--ds-tree-depth`. Three additive `Item` props serve the tree and change nothing for List or menus: `ariaSelected`, `bodyTabIndex` and `tabIndex`.

**Keyboard.** `src/hooks/useTreeFocus.ts` holds the model:

- ArrowUp, ArrowDown, Home and End move over the visible rows and skip disabled ones.
- ArrowRight expands a collapsed parent, moves to the first child of an expanded one and does nothing on a leaf.
- ArrowLeft collapses an expanded parent, or else moves to the parent.
- Enter and Space run the focused row's own link or button, never a descendant row's, and toggle a parent that has no action.
- Typeahead matches row text with a 500ms buffer.
- One row holds `tabindex="0"`, repaired when rows mount, leave or become disabled.

The chevron is a real `<button aria-label="Toggle children" tabIndex={-1}>`, so a parent expands from the keyboard without an inner action while the row keeps the tab stop.

**Expansion and selection.** `expanded` and `onExpandedChange` make expansion controlled. Without them, the tree seeds expansion from `isExpanded` in the data. A row whose data carries `isSelected` is selectable and reports `aria-selected="true"` or `"false"`. A row without it is navigation only and carries no `aria-selected`.

**Paint and motion.** The focus ring sits inset at `-2px`, because a full-width row has no gutter for an outset ring. The chevron rotates 90° on the fast tier. A newly mounted child row fades and rises on the moderate tier, root rows never animate, and collapse is instant because collapsed rows unmount and leave the tab order. TreeList adds no new tokens.

**Not built.** The connector lines between levels, `TreeListBranches` in the catalog, are deferred as pure decoration. Indentation and `aria-level` carry the hierarchy.

**Changed from.** The catalog's tree ([catalog-as-specification](#catalog-as-specification)) supported uncontrolled expansion only and emitted `aria-selected` only on a selected row.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-11.

- [focus-ring](#focus-ring) replaces the neutral `--ds-stroke-focus-hairline` ring with the 2px accent focus ring, still inset.
- [selected-row-cue](#selected-row-cue) gives the selected row a bold label in strong ink and a solid icon.
- [status-dot-edges](#status-dot-edges) gives a selected row's description strong ink.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **TreeList — the data-driven WAI-ARIA tree on a lifted `useTreeFocus` + controlled expansion (2026-07-11).** A `<ul role="tree">` of `<li role="treeitem">` rows, each **composing the `_internal` `Item` primitive** ([item-row-primitive](#item-row-primitive)) `as="li" role="treeitem"` — so the row anatomy (chevron `marker` · `startContent` · `label`+`description` · `endContent`) and the no-nested-interactives guard are reused, not re-written — with TreeList adding the full APG wiring and the keyboard model. Ported under [catalog-as-specification](#catalog-as-specification). **(1) The `useTreeFocus` lift (the flagship — `src/hooks/useTreeFocus.ts`, [catalog-as-specification](#catalog-as-specification) @ `88c95e4`).** The tree analogue of the sibling `useGridFocus` (a tree is NOT a linear list, so it gets its own hook): linear **ArrowUp/Down/Home/End** over the **VISIBLE** treeitems (collapsed subtrees are unrendered → naturally excluded; disabled skipped via `data-tree-disabled`/`aria-disabled`), **ArrowRight** (collapsed parent → expand, expanded → first child, leaf → no-op), **ArrowLeft** (expanded → collapse, else → parent by an upward **level-scan** on `aria-level`), **Enter/Space** (`onActivate` — clicks the row's own inner action — falling back to an expand-toggle for a parent), a **500ms typeahead** buffer (`DEFAULT_TYPEAHEAD_RESET_MS`), and opt-in **roving-tabindex ownership** (`hasRovingTabIndex` — a single `tabindex="0"` repaired on mount and on item add/remove/disable via `useIsomorphicLayoutEffect`, preserving a seeded stop; moved with keyboard nav). It is DOM-query based (reads `aria-expanded`/`aria-level`/`data-tree-*`). **PURE-LOGIC / DOM-INTEGRATION split:** the decisions are extracted to exported pure helpers — `collectExpandedKeys`, `findInitialTabbableId`, `findParentIndexByLevel` (ArrowLeft's parent target), and `matchTypeahead` (the wrap-around, disabled-skipping, `startsWith` buffer matcher) — **unit-tested in the node lane** (`useTreeFocus.logic.test.ts`, auto-globbed by `vitest.node.config.ts`); the DOM behaviours (arrow/expand/collapse/tab-stop-repair/typeahead/controlled/aria-selected) are **`_internal` browser plays** (`_treelist.stories.tsx`, `_internal/TreeList behavior`). **(2) VISIBLE rows render FLAT** — every visible treeitem is a **direct child of the tree `<ul>`**, depth carried by `aria-level` + an **absolute per-row indent** (`padding-inline-start: 8px + level×16px`, keyed off an inline `--ds-tree-depth`). This is exactly the "visible items in DOM order" list the hook queries; it makes the indent non-cumulative and keeps each row's selection tint + focus ring scoped to its OWN row (no subtree bleed). **axe-clean:** a treeitem directly under `role="tree"` satisfies the required-parent rule, and `aria-level`/`-posinset`/`-setsize` convey depth + position. **(3) TWO upgrades over Astryx, both built.** **Controlled expansion** — `expanded?: string[]` + `onExpandedChange?` (upstream is **uncontrolled-only**: an internal override-map merged over the `isExpanded`-from-data seed). When `expanded` is provided it is the source of truth and every toggle reports through `onExpandedChange`; absent → the uncontrolled override-map path (seeded from `collectExpandedKeys`). **`aria-selected="false"` on unselected SELECTABLE rows** — upstream emits `aria-selected` only when selected; APG wants the tri-state so AT can announce "not selected". PRESENCE of `isSelected` in a row's data marks it **selectable** (→ `aria-selected="true"|"false"`); its **absence** = a pure-navigation row (**no** `aria-selected` at all). **(4) The `Item` extension (additive).** Item's shipped `aria-selected` was `true|undefined` only. Three additive props, all no-ops for existing callers (List/menus pass none): **`ariaSelected?: boolean`** (explicit tri-state — emits `"true"|"false"`; falls back to the legacy `role && isSelected ? true : undefined` when omitted), **`bodyTabIndex?: number`** (render the real inner `<a>`/`<button>` body even under a parent `role`, at this tabIndex — so an href/onClick tree row has a genuine control for Enter/Space activation + native link semantics while the ROW owns the single tab stop; omitted → a parent-role row keeps its plain content span, the menu contract), and **`tabIndex?: number`** on the root (the row's roving stop). **(5) Activation scoping** — `activateItem` looks up `a[href], button:not([aria-label="Toggle children"])` and requires `candidate.closest('[role="treeitem"]') === current`, so a parent's Enter/Space never fires a descendant row's action. The **chevron is a real `<button aria-label="Toggle children" tabIndex={-1}>`** (the row owns the tab stop) so a parent expands from the keyboard even with no inner action; its `stopPropagation` + Item's container guard mean a chevron click never double-toggles. **(6) Normalization.** StyleX `*Vars` → `--ds-*` (a `.radix-themes`-scoped block in `tokens/components.css`); `getIcon('chevronRight')` → Phosphor **`CaretRight`**; the StyleX `when.ancestor(':focus-visible')` ring → an **INSET `:focus-visible` scoped ring** (`2px --ds-stroke-focus-hairline`, `offset -2px` — a full-width row has no gutter for the [validation-focus-paint](#validation-focus-paint) outset ring; the Calendar [calendar-grid](#calendar-grid) / Collapsible precedent), no `!important`. **`TreeListBranches` (the StyleX guide-line connectors) are DEFERRED as pure decoration** — indentation + `aria-level` carry the hierarchy; the connector lines add nothing semantic and would re-introduce the `ancestorsIsLast`/`isLast` plumbing the flat render drops. **Motion ([collapsible-and-accordion](#collapsible-and-accordion)):** the chevron rotates 90° in-place on the **fast + standard** tier (both directions); a newly-mounted CHILD row (`aria-level > 1`) **fades+rises in on the moderate + entry** expand tier — root rows (level 1) are excluded so a first paint never animates, and **collapse is instant** because rows UNMOUNT (required so collapsed items leave the tab order + a11y tree — the OverflowList [overflow-list](#overflow-list) principle; the "collapse fast+exit" motion has no frame to show); reduced-motion collapses both via the clamped `--ds-duration-*` tokens. **Zero net-new tokens** (`--ds-tree-depth` is a private inline indent multiplier, not a role token, like `--ds-avatar-box`), no `!important`, `.radix-themes`-scoped. `System/TreeList` is the full-spine docs (History · Anatomy · Usage incl. the live token spec · Keyboard · Props); the hook's pure logic is node-lane, its DOM behaviours are `_internal/TreeList behavior`.

### status-dot

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-11.

**StatusDot is an accent-aware status dot, and its colour is a redundant cue beside a required label.**

**What you see.** A round `<span role="img">` dot that sizes on the global text lane, 8px, 10px and 12px at small, medium and large, so it stays in proportion to the label beside it.

**Paint.** Zero new tokens.

- `success`, `warning` and `error` paint `--ds-fill-success`, `--ds-fill-warning` and `--ds-fill-error`, each with a 1px inset edge ([status-dot-edges](#status-dot-edges)).
- `accent` paints `--accent-indicator` with the `--accent-part-edge` inset edge ([textless-part-fills](#textless-part-fills), [part-fill-edge](#part-fill-edge)).
- `neutral` paints the solid `--ds-icon-neutral`, gray-11, which stays clearly visible in both appearances over any surface. The alpha `--ds-fill-medium` was rejected, because an a9 tint can muddy over a coloured backdrop.

The status fills follow the brand's collision shift, as Badge and Callout do, so a grass brand's success reads lime and a red brand's error reads oxblood.

**Accessibility.** `label` is required and is the dot's accessible name (WCAG 1.1.1), so a nameless dot does not compile. The dot is not focusable, and a sighted reader sees it beside a visible label.

**Pulse.** `isPulsing` runs `ds-statusdot-pulse`, opacity 1 to 0.5 to 1, over a literal `2s`, because an ambient loop sits outside the transition ladder, which tops out at 400ms and serves state changes. Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` the animation stops.

**Props.** `variant` (required), `label` (required), `isPulsing`, `tooltip`, `ref` to the span, and native span props. `tooltip` wraps the dot in the system Tooltip ([tooltip-wrap](#tooltip-wrap)). The Astryx module augmentation that adds variants is not carried, because no consumer needs it.

**Changed from.** No earlier ruling covered this.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-11.

- An update dated 2026-07-22, recorded in this entry, replaced the fixed 8px with the text lane, because a fixed 8px read too small beside large text.
- [tooltip-wrap](#tooltip-wrap): from 2026-07-21 the optional `tooltip` composes the system Tooltip in place of a raw Radix Tooltip.
- [textless-part-fills](#textless-part-fills) moves the accent dot from `--ds-fill-accent` to `--accent-indicator`.
- [part-fill-edge](#part-fill-edge) stacks `--accent-part-edge` on the accent dot.
- [status-dot-edges](#status-dot-edges) stacks a 1px inset edge on the warning, success and error dots, and records that a standalone dot shows nothing under forced colours.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **StatusDot — the accent-aware 8px status indicator (2026-07-11).** A fixed **8px** `<span role="img">` semantic status dot. Ported under [catalog-as-specification](#catalog-as-specification) @ `88c95e4`. **(1) Accent-aware paint.** The four semantic variants paint from the **accent-aware `--ds-fill-*` family** — `success`/`warning`/`error` take `--ds-fill-success`/`-warning`/`-error` (the `-9` solids), `accent` takes `--ds-fill-accent` — so a dot **follows the brand's collision shift** (a grass brand's success reads lime, a red brand's error reads oxblood), exactly like Badge/Callout, rather than a hardcoded Radix green/red. `neutral` takes the **solid `--ds-icon-neutral`** (gray-11) — a peer-weight neutral that stays clearly visible in **both** modes over any surface (the alpha `--ds-fill-medium` was rejected: an a9 tint can muddy over a coloured backdrop). **Zero net-new tokens.** **(2) Colour is a REDUNDANT cue.** `role="img"` + a **required** `label` is the dot's accessible name (WCAG 1.1.1) — colour alone conveys nothing to a screen reader, so `label` is non-optional and a nameless dot can't compile. The dot is **not focusable** (a decorative indicator, named but not a tab stop); sighted users pair it with a visible label. **(3) Pulse + reduced-motion.** `isPulsing` runs `ds-statusdot-pulse` (opacity 1 → 0.5 → 1) — an **ambient** loop, so its `2s` duration is a deliberate **literal** rather than a value off the intent-named transition ladder (the ladder tops out at 400ms and is for state changes, not decorative breathing); a `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block sets `animation: none`. **(4) Fixed 8px, no size lane.** 8px is a density-independent literal (a status dot is a glyph, not a control) — `width`/`height` sit outside the loose-value spacing scope, so no token is forced. `border-radius: var(--ds-radius-full)` on the 8×8 box renders a circle. An optional `tooltip` wraps the dot in a **raw Radix Themes Tooltip** (the System Tooltip is still `planned` → the [component-registry](#component-registry) agent-gap rule, the same call `Field.tsx` makes for its info tooltip). **API (LITE):** `variant` (required) · `label` (required) · `isPulsing?` · `tooltip?` · `ref` (→ the span) + native span props. Astryx's TS module-augmentation variant-extensibility is **noted, not carried** (no consumer needs it). All scoped `.radix-themes`, no `!important`. `System/StatusDot` is the full-spine docs (History · Anatomy · Usage incl. the live token spec · Props); the role/label + accent-aware-paint + pulse + reduced-motion behaviours are `_internal/StatusDot behavior`. **[Update 2026-07-21 ([tooltip-wrap](#tooltip-wrap)): Tooltip is now ported; StatusDot's optional `tooltip` composes the System Tooltip wrap — this "planned System wrap → [component-registry](#component-registry) agent-gap" note is historical.]** **[Update 2026-07-22: (4)'s "fixed 8px, no size lane" is SUPERSEDED — the dot now tracks the global text lane (8 / 10 / 12px via `useResolvedSize("text")` + a `data-size` width/height ladder) so it stays proportional to the label it sits beside. Fixed-8px read too small next to large-tier text; density-independence was incoherent with the size system.]**

### relative-timestamp

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-11.

**Timestamp renders a moment as text inside a semantic `<time>` element, with relative wording in the reader's locale.**

**What you see.** One `<time dateTime={ISO}>` element, styled as a Radix Text through `asChild`, with no wrapper span. Its numerals are tabular, so a live tick does not reflow the line. The component is ported under [catalog-as-specification](#catalog-as-specification).

**Relative wording.**

- `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat` with `numeric: "auto"` supplies the words, so a Spanish locale reads "hace 2 horas" and "ayer".
- A distance under 10 seconds in either direction reads as the present.
- A future value up to 30 seconds ahead reads as the present as well, because a near-future value almost always comes from clock skew, not a real event.
- With `isLive`, a relative value renders again every second under a minute, every 30 seconds under an hour, every minute under a day, and every 5 minutes beyond, and only while the effective format is relative.

**Formats.**

| Format | Output |
|---|---|
| `relative` | The locale's relative wording |
| `auto`, the default | `relative` while the distance is at most `autoThreshold`, 7 days by default, then `date_time` |
| `date`, `date_time`, `time` | A localized date or time through `Intl.DateTimeFormat` |
| `system_date`, `system_date_time`, `system_time` | A fixed machine string, the same in every locale, so log lines sort |

A numeric `value` under `1e12` reads as Unix seconds, and a larger one as milliseconds.

**Tooltip and name.** In relative mode only, the full absolute date and time is both the hover tooltip and the `aria-label`. An absolute format sets no `aria-label`, because its text is already the full value. The tooltip is the Radix Themes Tooltip, and its trigger is Radix Text, because Radix Text forwards a ref and the system `Text` wrapper does not.

**Props.** `value`, `format`, `autoThreshold`, `hasTooltip` (default true), `isTimezoneShown`, `isLive`, `size`, `color` (default `gray`, a muted supporting tone), `weight`, a `ref` to the `<time>`, and the native `<time>` props. The upstream `type` prop is not ported, because `Text` has no such axis, and `size`, `color` and `weight` cover the need.

**Changed from.** No earlier ruling covered this. The upstream reference built its relative wording from fixed English strings, such as "2 hours ago", in every locale.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-11. No later ruling amends it.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **Timestamp — the semantic `<time>` with a locale-correct relative ladder (2026-07-11).** A moment rendered as human text inside a semantic `<time dateTime={ISO}>` (machine-readable), styled AS a Radix Text via `asChild` — ONE element, no wrapper span. Ported under [catalog-as-specification](#catalog-as-specification) @ `88c95e4`. **(1) The i18n FIX — `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat`, not a hand-rolled English ladder.** Upstream's header *claims* `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat` but its source hand-rolls English strings (`"2 hours ago"`, `"yesterday"`). Ours **actually uses** it (`numeric: "auto"`), so a Spanish locale reads `"hace 2 horas"` / `"ayer"`, not the English words (verified in the logic suite). The concern is split: **`getRelativeParts` is a PURE, locale-INDEPENDENT chooser** that returns the `{value, unit}` to feed Intl (past → negative "ago", future → positive "in"), so the ladder boundaries + skew clamps stay unit-testable; **`formatRelative`** applies the locale-correct words. **(2) The asymmetric clock-skew tolerance is KEPT.** `|diff| < 10s` → "now" (both directions); a **future** value `≤ 30s` ahead → "now" (a `FUTURE_SKEW_TOLERANCE` wider than the past window, because a near-future value is almost always the render clock lagging the real clock, not a genuine event — so it never flashes a confusing "in a few seconds"). "now" is expressed as `{value: 0, unit: "second"}`, which Intl renders as the locale's present word. **(3) The live interval ladder is KEPT + lifted.** `isLive` re-renders relative time on a distance-aware ladder — `getLiveInterval`: **1s** under a minute, **30s** under an hour, **60s** under a day, else **5min** — re-derived each render off the current distance, and ticking ONLY while the effective format is relative. **`font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`** (the sole CSS add) keeps a tick from reflowing. **(4) Formats.** `relative` (Intl relative) · `auto` (relative while `|diff| ≤ autoThreshold`, default 7 days, else `date_time`) · `date`/`date_time`/`time` (localized `Intl.DateTimeFormat`) · `system_date`/`system_date_time`/`system_time` (manual `pad()` machine builders — locale-independent BY DESIGN, sortable log strings); `parseValue`'s `< 1e12` heuristic auto-detects Unix seconds vs ms. **(5) Tooltip + a11y.** In **relative mode only**, the full absolute string (`Intl.DateTimeFormat` long form + `timeZoneName`) is both the hover **tooltip** (a **raw Radix Themes Tooltip** — the System Tooltip is `planned`, the [component-registry](#component-registry) agent-gap rule; Radix Text forwards refs so it's a valid trigger, which our thin non-forwardRef `Text` wrapper is not — hence Radix Text directly + `useResolvedSize` for the lane, the size mechanism our wrapper embodies) **and** the `aria-label`. An absolute format sets **no** aria-label (its text is already the full value). Upstream's **lazy/Suspense tooltip indirection is dropped**; there's no mount announce. **(6) Normalization.** Astryx's `type` (a semantic text-type: `supporting`/…) has **no equivalent** in our Radix-based `Text` (which has no `type` axis) → **dropped**; `size`/`color`/`weight` (Radix Text pass-throughs; `color` defaults to `gray` = a muted supporting tone) cover the need. `mergeProps`/`mergeRefs`/`themeProps`/StyleX → inline. **API (LITE):** `value` (string|number) · `format?` (default `auto`) · `autoThreshold?` · `hasTooltip?` (default true) · `isTimezoneShown?` · `isLive?` · `size?`/`color?`/`weight?` · `ref` (→ the `<time>`) + native `<time>` props. The pure time-math is lifted to `src/utils/timestampFormat.ts` with a node-lane suite (`timestampFormat.logic.test.ts` — parse boundary, skew clamps both directions, the interval ladder, `isAbsoluteFormat`, Intl locale-correctness). All scoped `.radix-themes`, no `!important`, zero net-new tokens. `System/Timestamp` is the full-spine docs (History · Anatomy incl. the live Formats table · Usage incl. the live token spec · Props); format-switching / skew→"now" / the relative aria-label contract / a real live tick are `_internal/Timestamp behavior`.

### inline-citation

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-11.

**Citation is an inline leaf that cites a source, a link when the source has a URL and plain text when it does not, with `doc-noteref` on the link form only.**

**Markup.**

- A `source.url` renders an `<a>` that opens in a new tab with `target="_blank"` and `rel="noopener noreferrer"`. A source with no URL renders a `<span>`.
- `role="doc-noteref"` sits on the link form only, because on a plain `<span>` it fails the axe rule `aria-allowed-role`.
- Both forms take the accessible name `Citation {n}: {title}`, with the number in place of a missing title. A native `title` attribute, set only when a real title exists, shows the full source on hover when the pill truncates.

**Variants.**

| Variant | Shape | Paint | Linked hover |
|---|---|---|---|
| `label`, the default | A bordered pill with an optional favicon disc and a title truncated with an ellipsis at `max-width: 15em` | `--ds-text-weak` text, a 1px `--ds-stroke-weak` border, `--ds-radius-2` | `--ds-fill-hover`, with no underline |
| `number` | A superscript badge, square at its minimum so `--ds-radius-full` draws a circle, and a two-digit number widens it to a stadium | `--ds-text-weak` on `--ds-fill-accent-weak` | `--ds-fill-accent-med` |

**Colour.** The badge fill is accent-aware, so it follows the brand collision shift. The system has no `--ds-text-secondary`, so `--ds-text-weak` serves that role, and the component adds no tokens.

**Props.** `source: { title?, url?, icon? }`, `number`, which is required, `variant`, `ref` to the `<a>` or `<span>`, and native props.

**Not covered.** A hover card that previews the source. Upstream ships no such card, it waits for a design from the maintainer, and if built it composes a Radix HoverCard, since the system HoverCard is not ported.

**Changed from.** No earlier ruling covered a citation. The component follows the Astryx catalog entry at commit `88c95e4` under [catalog-as-specification](#catalog-as-specification).

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-11. No later ruling amends it.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **Citation — the inline source-reference leaf, `doc-noteref` on links only (2026-07-11).** A PURE inline leaf — no floating primitive. Ported under [catalog-as-specification](#catalog-as-specification) @ `88c95e4`. **(1) `<a>` or `<span>`, by the source.** A `source.url` → the citation is a **link** (`<a>`, opens in a new tab with `target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer"`); no url → a plain **`<span>`**. The CSS is element-agnostic (keyed on `data-variant`/`data-linked`), so both forms share one skin. **(2) The a11y polarity trap — PRESERVED (upstream gets it right).** `role="doc-noteref"` is a **reference role valid ONLY on the interactive LINK form** — on a plain unlinked `<span>` it trips axe `aria-allowed-role`, so it's **omitted** there (`noteRole = href ? "doc-noteref" : undefined`). The `aria-label` — `Citation {n}: {title}` (title falling back to the number when absent) — names the citation in **both** forms regardless. A native `title` attribute (set only when a real title exists) surfaces the full source on hover even when the pill ellipsis-truncates. **(3) Two variants.** `label` = a **bordered pill** (`display: inline-flex`, `--ds-stroke-weak` 1px border, `--ds-radius-2`) with an optional **favicon** (a fixed non-shrinking bordered disc holding an `alt="" aria-hidden` `<img>`) + an **ellipsis-truncated title** capped at `max-width: 15em`; a linked pill deepens on hover (`--ds-fill-hover` — the bounded surface is the affordance, no underline, the Token idiom). `number` = a **superscript circle badge** (`vertical-align: super`): `--ds-radius-full` (9999px) renders a **circle** because the box is **square at its minimum** (`min-width == height == --ds-space-16`), and a two-digit number grows past the min via `padding-inline` into a tidy stadium — by design. **(4) Accent-aware, --ds-* only.** Text is `--ds-text-weak` (the "secondary" role — our system has no `--ds-text-secondary`; `--ds-text-weak` = gray-11 is the mapping); the pill border is `--ds-stroke-weak`; the **number badge fills from the accent-aware `--ds-fill-accent-weak`** (accent-a3, the "accent-muted" pill), so it follows the brand collision shift, deepening to `--ds-fill-accent-med` on a linked hover. **Zero net-new tokens.** **(5) Named deferral.** A hover **source-preview card** is net-new (not upstream) → deferred for design input from the maintainer; if built it composes a **raw Radix HoverCard** (System HoverCard unported). The registry `buildingBlock` is **corrected** from the stale "superscript trigger + HoverCard" to the inline-leaf reality. **Normalization:** StyleX `*Vars` → `--ds-*`/Radix `--font-size-1`/`--line-height-1` (the established component-layer precedent); `mergeProps`/`themeProps` → inline. **API (LITE):** `source: {title?, url?, icon?}` · `number` (required) · `variant?` (default `label`) · `ref` (→ the `<a>`/`<span>`) + native props. All scoped `.radix-themes`, no `!important`. `System/Citation` is the full-spine docs (History · Anatomy (label + number) · Usage incl. the live token spec · Props); the linked-vs-unlinked role polarity, the aria-label naming, the ellipsis truncation, and the badge geometry are `_internal/Citation behavior`.

### pagination-control

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-11.

**Pagination is a controlled page navigation built on lifted range logic and a small roving focus hook.**

**What you see.** A `<nav>` with an accessible name holds a previous `IconButton`, an indicator chosen by `variant` and a next `IconButton`, plus an optional page-size `Select` whose trigger is named "Items per page". The previous and next buttons disable at the ends of the range, and each page change is announced politely as `Page N of M` through the shared `useAnnounce` region.

**Props.**

- `page` and `onChange`, 1-based and controlled only.
- One data shape: `totalItems`, `totalPages` or `hasMore`.
- `pageSize`, `pageSizeOptions` and `onPageSizeChange`.
- `variant`: `pages` by default, or `count`, `compact`, `dots` or `none`.
- `siblingCount`, default 1.
- `size`: `sm` or `md`.
- `isDisabled`.
- `label`, default `Pagination`. Give each pager on a page its own label, because two landmarks with one name fail axe `landmark-unique`.

**Empty.** The component renders nothing when `totalItems` or the computed page count is zero or less.

**Range logic.** `generatePageRange(current, total, siblingCount)` and the `coercePageSize` guard are lifted word for word into `src/utils/generatePageRange.ts` ([catalog-as-specification](#catalog-as-specification)). The range holds `5 + 2 × siblingCount` slots, and `coercePageSize` maps `Infinity` and `NaN` to 10 and floors any other value to at least 1.

**Dots.** The `dots` variant is a `role="group"` of buttons with the radio group interaction of the ARIA Authoring Practices: focus selects a page, and the arrow keys move one dot and wrap. Only the current dot takes `tabIndex` 0. `src/hooks/useListFocus.ts` moves focus and nothing else, so the tab stop and the selection stay declarative in the component.

**Rejected.**

- `useGridFocus`, the lifted grid hook. It takes a column count, offers no wrap, and writes the roving `tabIndex` itself, which conflicts with the declarative tab stop.
- A true `role="radiogroup"` with `aria-checked`. The dots also carry `aria-current="page"`, and a radio group with children that are not radios fails axe `aria-required-children`. A true radio set remains a documented alternative.
- The upstream optimistic layer, `useOptimistic`, `useTransition` and `changeAction`. `page` is the one source of truth, and an optimistic advance and an async `changeAction` are named deferrals.

**Paint.** No new tokens.

- The current page number: `--ds-fill-selected-subtle` under `--ds-text-strong`, at the strong weight.
- A rest dot: a 1px ring of `--ds-fill-press` with `--neutral-ring-stack` stacked on it and a clear centre, which `--ds-fill-medium` fills on hover.
- The current dot: a pill `--ds-space-20` long in `--accent-indicator`, edged with `--accent-mark-edge`.
- Focus: the accent focus ring ([focus-ring](#focus-ring)).

`aria-current="page"` marks the current page and the current dot, so colour is never the only cue. The dot sizes are density literals on `width` and `height`, outside the spacing scale, like the 8px StatusDot.

**Changed from.** No earlier ruling covered page navigation.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-11.

- [textless-part-fills](#textless-part-fills) paints the current dot `--accent-indicator` in place of `--ds-fill-accent`.
- [indicator-mark-edges](#indicator-mark-edges) and [mark-on-tint-edge](#mark-on-tint-edge) gave the current dot an edge, which [neutral-part-stacks](#neutral-part-stacks) replaces.
- [neutral-part-stacks](#neutral-part-stacks) makes the current dot a pill edged with `--accent-mark-edge` and rings the rest dots with a stacked alpha.
- [focus-ring](#focus-ring) replaces the neutral focus hairline on the dots with the accent focus ring.
- [control-box-per-step](#control-box-per-step) sizes the page cells from the box of the page button itself.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **Pagination — controlled page nav on lifted range math + a thin roving hook (2026-07-11).** A `<nav aria-label>` holding a prev IconButton, a variant-driven indicator, and a next IconButton, plus an optional page-size Select. Ported under [catalog-as-specification](#catalog-as-specification) @ `88c95e4`. **(1) The lifted pure logic + the coercion guard.** `generatePageRange(current, total, siblingCount)` (publicly exported upstream) + the `pageSize` coercion guard are lifted **verbatim** to `src/utils/generatePageRange.ts` ([catalog-as-specification](#catalog-as-specification)) with a **node-lane** suite (`generatePageRange.logic.test.ts`): slot budget `5 + 2·siblingCount`, the four regimes (fits-all / near-start / near-end / middle) at siblingCount 0/1/2, and `coercePageSize` (Infinity/NaN → default 10; else floor/clamp≥1) which protects the `dots` `Array.from({length})`. **Doc-bug fix (source wins):** upstream's JSDoc near-start example `generatePageRange(1,10,1) → [1,2,3,'...',10]` under-counts the `leftRange = 3 + 2·siblingCount = 5` window the code actually emits (`[1,2,3,4,5,'...',10]`); corrected in the lifted JSDoc + asserted true. **(2) THE dots-focus DECISION — a thin new `useListFocus`, NOT `useGridFocus`.** The `dots` variant is a `role="group"` of buttons implementing the APG radiogroup *interaction* (selection-follows-focus + 1D roving with wrap). It rides a minimal new `src/hooks/useListFocus.ts` (horizontal/vertical, wrap, itemSelector) whose pure index math (`nextFocusIndex`) is node-lane tested. **Why not `useGridFocus` (our lifted 2D grid hook):** it needs a `columns` count, has **no wrap** (its edges fire `onNavigateBefore/After` month-flip callbacks), and **owns the roving tabindex imperatively** (setAttribute in a layout effect) — which would fight the **declarative** per-dot `tabIndex` the radiogroup needs (the active dot renders `tabIndex=0`, the rest `-1`, and the stop moves *with selection*, not via a hook-owned mutation).
