So `useListFocus` only **moves focus**; the tab stop + selection stay declarative in the component (`handleDotsFocus` selects the focused dot's page; Safari `onClick={e => e.currentTarget.focus()}` workaround kept). The `role="group"`-of-buttons (Astryx's own choice) is kept over a true `role="radiogroup"`/`aria-checked` set — the dots also carry `aria-current="page"` navigation semantics, and a radiogroup+non-radio-children mix trips axe `aria-required-children`; a true radio set is a documented alternative. **(3) Accent-aware paint, zero net-new tokens.** Active dot / active page number paint from `--ds-fill-accent` (accent-9) and `--ds-fill-selected-subtle` (accent-a5, the [calendar-grid](#calendar-grid) committed band) + `--ds-text-strong`; rest dots take `--ds-fill-press` (gray-a5), hover `--ds-fill-medium`; the dots' focus-visible ring is the system neutral hairline (`--ds-stroke-focus-hairline`, 2px offset 2px). `aria-current="page"` marks the current page/dot so colour is never the only cue. The 8px/6px dot glyphs are density literals on `width`/`height` (like StatusDot's 8px), outside the spacing scale. **(4) Normalization + the dropped optimistic layer.** StyleX `*Vars` → `--ds-*`; `themeProps`/`mergeProps`/`stylex.props` dropped; Astryx `Button`/`Icon`/`Selector`/`Text` → our `Button`/`IconButton` (ghost = `priority: tertiary`), our compound `Select` (a `Select.Item` per `pageSizeOptions` entry, trigger named "Items per page"), and Radix `Text`; CaretLeft/CaretRight from Phosphor. The `useOptimistic`/`useTransition`/`changeAction` **optimistic in-flight layer is DROPPED** (the deferral pattern shared with the date inputs) — `page` is the single source of truth; optimistic advance + async `changeAction` are named deferrals. The polite `Page N of M` announce rides the shared `useAnnounce` region. **API (LITE, controlled-only):** `page` + `onChange` (1-based) · data via `totalItems | totalPages | hasMore` · `pageSize`/`pageSizeOptions`/`onPageSizeChange` · `variant` (`pages`|`count`|`compact`|`dots`|`none`, default `pages`) · `siblingCount` (default 1) · `size` (`sm`|`md`) · `isDisabled` · `label` (default `Pagination` — make it distinct per pager, `landmark-unique`). Returns `null` on empty (`totalItems <= 0` or computed pages `<= 0`); prev/next disable at the range ends. All scoped `.radix-themes`, no `!important`. `System/Pagination` is the full-spine docs (History · Anatomy · Usage incl. the live paint spec · Props); the generatePageRange render, dots roving + selection-follows-focus + wrap, the page announce, disabled ends, the page-size-Select reset-to-1, and the empty-state null are `_internal/Pagination behavior`.

### breadcrumb-trail

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-11.

**Breadcrumbs is a `nav` trail of list items, and when no crumb is marked current, the content element of the last crumb carries `aria-current="page"`.**

**Structure.** A `<nav aria-label="Breadcrumb">` holds an `<ol>` of `<li>` crumbs, with `Breadcrumbs`, `BreadcrumbItem` and `BreadcrumbContext` in one file. Breadcrumbs takes `children`, `separator`, `variant`, `label` and `ref`, and BreadcrumbItem takes `children`, `href`, `onClick`, `isCurrent`, `startIcon`, `as` and `ref`. `label` names the landmark, so each trail on a page carries a distinct name.

**Current page.** When no item sets `isCurrent`, the last crumb's content element, the link, button or span and never the `<li>`, takes `aria-current="page"`. A scan of the `<ol>` after render places it, so a last crumb that is a link stays navigable and is marked current, whatever structure wraps the children.

**Element forms.**

- `href`: a link, a plain `<a>` or the component passed in `as`, such as a router link.
- `onClick` alone: a reset `<button type="button">` in the link's skin.
- `isCurrent`: a non-interactive `<span aria-current="page">`.
- Neither: a plain `<span>`, still a candidate for the current page.

**Separators.** Each item renders its own leading separator span, `aria-hidden`, which takes any React node and defaults to `/`, and CSS hides it on the first item. Screen readers skip the separators, and the crumbs carry the meaning.

**Skin.** A linked crumb is a plain `<a>` styled from `--ds-*` in `--ds-text-weak`, underlined on hover and ringed by the system focus ring, not the Radix `Link`, whose accent skin clashes with the muted trail. The current crumb is set in `--ds-text-strong` in the `default` variant and `--ds-text-weak` in `supporting`, the two variants sit one step apart on the Radix type scale, `--font-size-2` and `--font-size-1` at the default size, and the trail has no collapse, after the reference catalogue's advice to flatten a hierarchy rather than truncate it.

**Changed from.** The system had no breadcrumb trail. This one ports the reference catalogue's component under [catalog-as-specification](#catalog-as-specification).

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-11.

- [focus-ring](#focus-ring) replaces the neutral hairline focus ring on linked crumbs with the accent ring.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **Breadcrumbs — the nav trail with content-element auto-current (2026-07-11).** A `<nav aria-label="Breadcrumb">` › `<ol>` › `<li>` trail — `Breadcrumbs` + `BreadcrumbItem` + `BreadcrumbContext` in one file. Ported under [catalog-as-specification](#catalog-as-specification) @ `88c95e4`. **(1) THE auto-current a11y fix (navigation-11) — the lifted DOM-scan `useEffect`.** When NO item sets `isCurrent`, the **last** crumb's **content element** (the link/button/span via a `contentRef` — **NEVER** the `<li>`) gets `aria-current="page"`, via a post-render DOM scan of the `<ol>` children (`isLast && !ol.querySelector('[aria-current="page"]')` → `contentRef.current ?? li`). **Polarity preserved:** the marker lands on the actual interactive element — including when the last crumb is a **link** (it stays navigable AND is marked current). **Why a DOM scan, not React-side children introspection:** it needs no `React.Children`/`cloneElement`, is robust to any child structure (fragments, wrappers), and is what correctly targets the content element. A DOM-dependent behavior → its coverage is an `_internal` play, not a node suite. **(2) Leading, decorative separators.** Each item renders its OWN **leading** `aria-hidden` separator span (any `ReactNode` — slash default, a chevron, a dot), hidden on `:first-child` via CSS (`.rt-ds-breadcrumb-item:first-child .rt-ds-breadcrumb-sep { display:none }`) — a real rendered node (not a `::before` `content`) so an arbitrary ReactNode separator works. Screen readers skip them; the crumbs carry the meaning. **(3) Element forms.** `href` → a **link**; `onClick`-only → a reset `<button type="button">` matching the link skin; explicit `isCurrent` → a non-interactive `<span aria-current="page">` (no link); a bare crumb → a plain `<span>` (still an auto-current candidate). **(4) Plain `<a>`, not Radix Link ([component-registry](#component-registry) agent-gap).** System `Link` is `planned`, so linked crumbs render as a **plain `<a>` styled from `--ds-*`** — muted secondary text (`--ds-text-weak` = the "secondary" role; our system has no `--ds-text-secondary`), underline on hover (the bounded row is the affordance, the Token/Citation idiom), a neutral-hairline focus ring (`--ds-stroke-focus-hairline`, 2px offset 2px) — **not** the raw Radix `Link` whose accent skin would fight the muted trail; a caller `as` component (a router Link) overrides. Current text = `--ds-text-strong` (default) / `--ds-text-weak` (supporting). **(5) Two variants, no collapse.** `default` / `supporting` size text off the Radix scale (`--font-size-2`/`-1`, the [inline-citation](#inline-citation) precedent). Astryx ships **no collapse mechanism** (its guidance is to flatten the hierarchy, not truncate) — ported as-is. **Normalization:** StyleX `*Vars` → `--ds-*`; `themeProps`/`mergeProps`/`mergeRefs`/`stylex.props` dropped (inline className merge + a callback ref merging the public ref and `liRef`); `useLinkComponent`/`LinkComponentType` → plain `<a>`/`as`; the Astryx `--separator-display` CSS-var trick → a plain `:first-child` rule. **API (LITE):** Breadcrumbs — `children` · `separator?` (default `/`) · `variant?` (default `default`) · `label?` (default `Breadcrumb` — distinct per trail, `landmark-unique`) · `ref` (→ the `<nav>`); BreadcrumbItem — `children` · `href?` · `onClick?` · `isCurrent?` · `startIcon?` · `as?` · `ref` (→ the `<li>`). All scoped `.radix-themes`, no `!important`, zero net-new tokens. `System/Breadcrumbs` is the full-spine docs (History · Anatomy · Usage incl. the live text spec · Props); the auto-current polarity (content element not `<li>`, even on a link), explicit-current precedence, the leading/first-hidden separators, and the element forms are `_internal/Breadcrumbs behavior`.

### thumbnail-preview

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-11.

**`Thumbnail` is a 64px square preview that shows its placeholder when the image fails to load.**

**What you see.** A fixed 64px square frame on `--ds-fill-weak` shows one of four states: the image, a skeleton while an upload has no URL yet, a spinner over the image while it processes, or a placeholder glyph in `--ds-icon-neutral`. A 1px inset edge in `--ds-stroke-strong` paints over a real image only. The component adds no new token.

**Load error.** A broken `src` shows the placeholder, so a 404 reads as no image rather than a broken page. The error flag resets on every change of `src`, so a new URL gets a fresh attempt.

**Remove ✕.** The optional remove button sits on a `--ds-scrim` disc inside a permanently dark `Theme`, so its glyph reads light from the dark scale in both appearances, with no hardcoded white. A click on it stops propagation.

**Accessibility.**

- The frame is a `role="group"`, named from `label` and `alt` together, from either alone, or as "Thumbnail".
- The remove button carries its own name, "Remove" and the group name.
- With `onClick` the tile is a real `<button>` named "Open" and the group name, and the frame shows its focus ring.
- The remove button and the open button are siblings, never nested, so the markup is valid in every mode.
- The `label` is also the hover tooltip.

**API.** `src`, `alt`, `label`, `onRemove`, `onClick`, `isLoading` (default `false`), `isDisabled` (default `false`), `removeLabel`, and `ref` on the group.

**Rejected.** The per-image luminance sampling and adaptive remove-button contrast of the Astryx source, which this component follows under [catalog-as-specification](#catalog-as-specification). Both cost far more than a scrim disc.

**Changed from.** No earlier ruling covered this. The Astryx source promised a failure placeholder and shipped none, so a broken URL showed the browser's broken-image glyph.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-11.

- [tooltip-wrap](#tooltip-wrap) ports the system `Tooltip`, which ends the reason this ruling had for a raw Radix Tooltip.
- [button-focus-ring-offset](#button-focus-ring-offset) rings the remove button at offset 0, because the frame clips a ring outside its edge.
- [focus-ring](#focus-ring) makes the frame's ring the stacked accent ring, drawn from the root.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **Thumbnail — a 64px preview with the load-error fallback upstream promised (2026-07-11).** A fixed 64px square `role="group"` frame holding a prop-driven state machine, with an optional scrim-backed remove ✕ and an optional keyboard-operable open trigger. Ported under [catalog-as-specification](#catalog-as-specification) @ `88c95e4`. **(1) THE load-error fix — BUILT.** Astryx's docs promise a failure placeholder, but its source ships none: `showPlaceholder = !isLoading && !hasSrc` covers a MISSING `src` only, and the `<img>` has no `onError` — so a broken URL shows the browser's default broken-image glyph. Ours **adds `onError` → an `errored` flag → fall back to the placeholder**, so a 404 reads as "no image", not "broken page". The flag **resets on every `src` change** (a `useEffect` keyed on `src`) so a new URL gets a fresh attempt (a previously-broken tile can recover). The four states derive: `showImage = hasSrc && !errored` · `showSkeleton = isLoading && !hasSrc` · `showUploadOverlay = isLoading && showImage` · `showPlaceholder = !showImage && !showSkeleton` (which covers BOTH no-src-not-loading AND the broken-src fallback). **(2) The scrim-backed remove ✕ — the normalized contrast model.** Upstream samples image luminance (APCA, `useImageMode`) and adapts the remove button's contrast per-image (`MediaTheme`) — heavy. **Both dropped.** The ✕ sits on a `--ds-scrim` disc inside a **permanently-dark `<Theme appearance="dark" hasBackground={false}>`** — the scrim is dark in BOTH app modes (`black-a8` light / `black-a11` dark), so the glyph reads light via the system's own dark-scale `--ds-*` tokens (`--ds-text-strong` = `gray-12` = near-white in the dark scale). No per-image sampling, **no hardcoded white** — the sanctioned "content on a permanently-dark surface" mechanism (semantic.css's contrast-surface note). The scrim approach's sufficiency is the trigger for the deferred APCA sampling. **(3) Structure + a11y.** `role="group"` named by `label && alt ? "{label} — {alt}" : label ?? alt ?? "Thumbnail"`; the remove ✕ carries its OWN name (`Remove {name}`); when `onClick` is set the tile is a real `<button>` ("Open {name}") and the frame **hoists its focus ring** via `:has(.rt-ds-thumbnail-open:focus-visible)` → the neutral focus hairline (Token/Overlay idiom). The remove ✕ and the open `<button>` are **SIBLINGS** inside the frame (never nested → valid HTML in every mode), and `onRemove` calls `stopPropagation`. A 1px inset border (`--ds-stroke-strong`) paints only over a real image. The `label` is the hover **tooltip** via a **raw Radix Tooltip** (System Tooltip `planned` → [component-registry](#component-registry) agent-gap). **(4) Reuse + normalization.** Our `IconButton` + Phosphor `X` (remove) · Radix `Skeleton` / `Spinner` (loading) · a **fixed 64px box**, not `AspectRatio` (the square is a constant, no ratio math). StyleX `*Vars` → `--ds-*`; `mergeProps`/`themeProps`/`stylex.props` → inline; `Icon` → Phosphor `ImageSquare` (placeholder) / `X` (remove). Paints from `--ds-fill-weak` (frame) / `--ds-icon-neutral` (placeholder glyph) / `--ds-stroke-strong` (inset border) / `--ds-scrim` (remove disc + upload overlay). **API (LITE):** `src?` · `alt?` · `label?` · `onRemove?` · `onClick?` · `isLoading?` (default false) · `isDisabled?` (default false) · `removeLabel?` · `ref` (→ the group). All scoped `.radix-themes`, no `!important`, **zero net-new tokens**. `System/Thumbnail` is the full-spine docs (History · Anatomy incl. the four-state matrix · Usage incl. the live token spec · Props); the four states, the broken-src → placeholder fallback, the remove-✕ stopPropagation + sibling structure, the open trigger, and the disabled affordance-drop are `_internal/Thumbnail behavior`.

### carousel-scroller

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-11.

**Carousel is a horizontal scroll container with edge fades and optional prev and next buttons, and never a slideshow.**

**What you see.** A region (`role="region"`, `aria-roledescription="carousel"`, `aria-label`) wraps a horizontal scroll track that takes keyboard focus (`tabIndex=0`), with a fade on each side that overflows and optional prev and next pills. It has no index, no dots and no autoplay, because the source has none.

**Track.** The track scrolls on `overflow-x: auto` with its scrollbar hidden and wraps each child in a slot that does not shrink, and `hasSnap` sets `scroll-snap-type: x mandatory` with `scroll-snap-align: start` per item. `useScrollOverflow` (`src/hooks/useScrollOverflow.ts`) tracks overflow at each end on the shared observer in `src/utils/sharedResizeObserver.ts`, folds the negative axis of right-to-left layout with `Math.abs(scrollLeft)`, and allows 1px of tolerance, so a track that cannot scroll never reads as overflowing.

**Buttons.** Each pill sits absolutely positioned inside the `position: relative` region and is the floating surface (`--ds-bg-overlay` from [floating-surface-fill](#floating-surface-fill), `--ds-shadow-overlay`, `--ds-radius-full`) around a ghost `IconButton` with a Phosphor caret. At an end with nothing to scroll toward, the pill stays mounted, becomes `disabled` and takes `opacity: 0`, because unmounting it would send focus to `<body>`, and a press scrolls by the track width less half an item, instantly under reduced motion.

**Edge fade.** An alpha-only `mask-image` gradient, `--ds-space-16` wide and keyed on `data-fade`, fades the overflowing side and paints no colour. `hasEdgeFade={false}` removes it for full-bleed items a mask would clip.

**API.** `children`, `gap` (0 to 6, default 2), `padding` (0 to 6), `hasButtons` (default true), `hasEdgeFade` (default true), `hasSnap` (default false), `aria-label` (default `"Carousel"`, to replace with a distinct name for each carousel) and `ref`, which reaches the region. The spacing steps map to `--ds-space-*` and have no half steps.

**Changed from.** The Astryx `Carousel` this port follows ([catalog-as-specification](#catalog-as-specification)) rendered its buttons on the top layer with CSS anchor positioning to escape clipping, and took fractional spacing steps such as `0.5` and `1.5`.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-11. No later ruling amends it.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **Carousel — a scroll container (not a slide widget) on the lifted overflow hook (2026-07-11).** A `role="region"` + `aria-roledescription="carousel"` + `aria-label` wrapping a `tabIndex=0` horizontal scroll track, with per-side edge-fade masks and optional prev/next pills. Ported under [catalog-as-specification](#catalog-as-specification) @ `88c95e4`. **(1) It's a scroll container — do NOT invent a slideshow.** No index, dots, or autoplay upstream; ported as-is. The track (`overflow-x: auto`, scrollbar hidden) `Children.map`s each child into a shrink-proof snap slot; `hasSnap` sets `scroll-snap-type: x mandatory` + `scroll-snap-align: start` per item. **(2) `useScrollOverflow` LIFTED + REUSES our shared observer.** Lifted to `src/hooks/useScrollOverflow.ts` ([catalog-as-specification](#catalog-as-specification)); it **reuses `src/utils/sharedResizeObserver.ts` (`observeResize`/`unobserveResize`)** — the exact singleton primitive upstream imports — so N carousels share ONE `ResizeObserver`. The **pure overflow math is extracted to `computeOverflow`** (`Math.abs(scrollLeft)` folds RTL's negative axis; a 1px tolerance so an unscrollable track never reads as overflowing) with a **node-lane suite** (`useScrollOverflow.logic.test.ts` — the four scroll regimes, the RTL fold, the tolerance boundary). **`scrollByViewport`** (also exported) scrolls `clientWidth − 0.5·itemWidth` (a half-item peek) and is **reduced-motion-aware** (`matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)')` → `behavior: "auto"`) — the JS mirror of the CSS `scroll-behavior` override, which itself flips to `auto` under the media query. **(3) Plain absolute buttons — the Layer normalized away.** Upstream renders prev/next on the **top layer** (`useLayer`) via CSS anchor-positioning (`positionArea` / `anchor-size()`) to escape parent clipping. **Dropped** — plain absolutely-positioned pills inside the `position:relative` region (the region is `overflow: visible`; the **track** owns horizontal clipping via `overflow-x`), no top layer needed on our substrate. The nav pill **wrapper IS the floating surface** (opaque `--ds-bg-overlay` [floating-surface-fill](#floating-surface-fill) + `--ds-shadow-overlay` elevation, `--ds-radius-full`); the ghost IconButton inside just holds the Phosphor caret. **(4) Buttons mounted, disabled + hidden at the ends.** Each pill stays **mounted** and becomes `disabled` + `opacity: 0` (out of pointer/tab flow) when its edge has nothing to scroll toward — never unmounted, which would drop focus to `<body>`. The track is `tabIndex=0` so keyboard users scroll it directly. **(5) The per-side edge-fade mask.** A `mask-image` linear-gradient fades whichever side overflows (start / end / both / none), keyed on a `data-fade` attribute; the mask is **alpha-only** (`black`/`transparent` define opacity, not paint) so it's not a `--ds` paint violation. 16px fade width off `--ds-space-16`; `hasEdgeFade={false}` suppresses it for full-bleed-surface items a mask would clip. **(6) Normalization + API.** StyleX `*Vars` → `--ds-*`; `mergeProps`/`mergeRefs`/`themeProps`/`stylex.props` → inline; `HStack`/`Icon` → our `Flex`/`IconButton` + Phosphor `CaretLeft`/`CaretRight`; `useLayer`/`Layer` dropped. `gap`/`padding` accept **integer spacing steps** (0–6) mapping to `--ds-space-*` via inline CSS vars — a **divergence from Astryx's fractional `0.5`/`1.5` steps** (our scaling-aware scale has no half-steps; the useful range is covered). **API (LITE):** `children` · `gap?` (0–6, default 2) · `hasButtons?` (default true) · `hasEdgeFade?` (default true) · `hasSnap?` (default false) · `padding?` (0–6) · `aria-label?` (default `"Carousel"` — make it **distinct** per carousel, `landmark-unique`) · `ref` (→ the region). All scoped `.radix-themes`, no `!important`, **zero net-new tokens**. `System/Carousel` is the full-spine docs (History · Anatomy · Usage incl. the live nav-pill spec · Keyboard · Props); the overflow-driven button enable/hide-at-ends, `scrollByViewport`, the region roledescription, and the reduced-motion scroll-behavior override are `_internal/Carousel behavior`.

### lightbox-viewer

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-11.

**Lightbox is a fullscreen media viewer on the raw Radix Dialog, with the keyboard zoom its Astryx source lacks.**

**What you see.** A single image or a gallery with previous and next controls, a counter, captions, and optional zoom and pan. The controls, counter and caption sit in a dark `Theme`, so they read light on the dark stage in both appearances: the discs paint `--ds-scrim`, and the glyphs and text paint `--ds-text-strong`. The backdrop paints `--ds-scrim` with `blur(2px)`.

**Dialog.** Lightbox composes the raw Radix Themes `Dialog`, which provides the focus trap, scroll lock, Escape and backdrop dismissal, and the shared modal motion with no override. A click on the empty stage closes the viewer, because the full-viewport content covers the Radix overlay.

**Keyboard.**

- Left and Right arrows move through the gallery.
- `+` or `=` zooms in, `-` or `_` zooms out, and `0` resets.

Double-click toggles between 1x and 2x, and a drag pans. Zoom and pan are off for video and reset on every change of index or source.

**Gallery.** Previous and next are `disabled` at the ends of the range but stay mounted, because an unmounted focused control drops focus to `<body>`. The `N / M` counter is `aria-hidden`, and `useAnnounce` politely announces each change of index within an open session, never on mount, open or close, since the dialog's `aria-label` names the current item on open.

**API.** `isOpen`, `onOpenChange`, `media` (one `LightboxMedia` or an array, each `{src, alt, caption?, type?}`), `index`, `defaultIndex` (0), `onIndexChange`, `hasZoom` (false), `hasAutoPlay` (false) and `ref`. The `useLightbox` hook returns `open(i)`, `close`, `isOpen`, `index`, `element`, `triggerProps` and `getTriggerProps(i)`, and the trigger props carry `role="button"`, `tabIndex=0`, `aria-haspopup="dialog"` and Enter and Space activation.

**Changed from.** No earlier ruling covered this. The Astryx source used a native `<dialog>` with `showModal()`, its own scroll lock and focus restore, and zoom by double-click alone, and its docs omitted `defaultIndex` and `hasAutoPlay`.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-11.

- [standard-dialog](#standard-dialog) ships the system `Dialog` and keeps Lightbox on the raw Radix Dialog on purpose, because Lightbox steers its own focus, skins its own content and animates its own tiers.
- [focus-return-on-close](#focus-return-on-close) returns focus to the opener on close, which Radix does not do for a dialog opened from a prop.
- [dragging-movement-gaps](#dragging-movement-gaps) records pan as drag-only, a failure of WCAG 2.5.7 Dragging Movements, recorded and not fixed.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **Lightbox — a fullscreen viewer on the raw Radix Dialog, with keyboard zoom added (2026-07-11).** A fullscreen media viewer — a single image or a gallery with prev/next, a counter, captions, and optional zoom/pan. Ported under [catalog-as-specification](#catalog-as-specification) @ `88c95e4`. **(1) THE swap — native `<dialog>` → raw Radix Dialog.** Upstream uses `<dialog>` + `showModal()`. Ours composes the **raw Radix Themes `Dialog`** (System `Dialog` is `planned` → the [component-registry](#component-registry) agent-gap rule, the `AlertDialog.tsx` thin-wrapper pattern). Radix owns **focus-trap + scroll-lock + Escape + backdrop-dismiss**, so upstream's `useScrollLock` and the manual `triggerElementRef` focus-restore are **dropped** (Radix owns both; Escape routes through the Dialog's own `onOpenChange`, no duplicate handler). Full-viewport chrome-less content: the compound `.radix-themes .rt-ds-lightbox` (0,2,0) beats `.rt-BaseDialogContent` (0,1,0) → `position: fixed; inset: 0`, transparent, no shadow/radius/padding. **Backdrop** repainted to `--ds-scrim` + `blur(2px)` via `.rt-BaseDialogOverlay:has(.rt-ds-lightbox)` (the CommandPalette `:has()` idiom, since the overlay is an ancestor of the content). **Modal enter/exit motion is INHERITED** from the [toast-feedback-tier](#toast-feedback-tier) `.rt-BaseDialogContent`/`.rt-BaseDialogOverlay` bindings — **no per-component override** (it would double-animate). **(2) The permanently-dark control surface.** The viewer content lives in a `<Theme appearance="dark" hasBackground={false}>`, so the controls, counter, and caption re-resolve to **light** on the dark stage in both app modes — the control discs paint `--ds-scrim` and the glyph/counter/caption `--ds-text-strong` (near-white in the dark scale). The same scrim-surface idiom as Thumbnail ([thumbnail-preview](#thumbnail-preview)) — no hardcoded white; `--color-on-dark` → `--ds-text-strong`. **(3) THE keyboard-zoom fix.** Upstream's `handleKeyDown` does ArrowLeft/Right ONLY — zoom is **double-click-only**, a keyboard a11y gap. Ours **adds keyboard zoom**: `+`/`=` zoom in, `-`/`_` zoom out, `0` reset. Double-click still toggles 1↔2×, drag still pans (`scale(z) translate(pan/z)`); zoom/pan is **disabled for `video`** and **resets on every index / src change**. **(4) THE doc-omitted props — documented.** `defaultIndex` (uncontrolled starting index) and `hasAutoPlay` (video autoplay) exist in the source but are **omitted from the upstream doc**; both are documented + wired (controlled `index` OR uncontrolled `defaultIndex`). **(5) Gallery + announcer.** Clamped index; `canPrev`/`canNext` gate the nav; **prev/next are `disabled` at the range ends but stay MOUNTED** — unmounting the focused control would drop focus to `<body>`. The `N / M` counter is `aria-hidden` (silent to AT); navigation is announced **politely** via OUR `useAnnounce` (`"{alt}, N of M"` / `"Image N of M"`), fired **ONLY on an in-session index change** — not on mount, open, or close (the dialog's `aria-label = currentItem.alt || "Media viewer"` already names the current image on open). Clicking the empty **stage** closes (Radix's overlay is fully covered by the full-viewport content, so the backdrop-dismiss is reproduced in JS: `e.target === e.currentTarget → onOpenChange(false)`). **(6) `useLightbox` companion hook** (lifted, swapped onto our Lightbox): `open(i)` / `close` / `isOpen` / `index` / `element` / `triggerProps` / `getTriggerProps(i)` — the trigger props carry `role="button"` + `tabIndex=0` + `aria-haspopup="dialog"` + Enter/Space activation. **Normalization:** StyleX `*Vars` → `--ds-*`; `mergeProps`/`mergeRefs`/`themeProps`/`stylex.props` → inline; `Icon` → Phosphor `X`/`CaretLeft`/`CaretRight`; `useScrollLock`/`useIsomorphicLayoutEffect` open-close machinery → the Radix Dialog. The image zoom `transition` rides `--ds-duration-overlay` · `--ds-ease-standard`, dropped while dragging + under reduced motion. **API (LITE):** `isOpen` · `onOpenChange` · `media: LightboxMedia | LightboxMedia[]` (`{src, alt, caption?, type?}`) · `index?` · `defaultIndex?` (0) · `onIndexChange?` · `hasZoom?` (false) · `hasAutoPlay?` (false) · `ref` (→ the Dialog content). All scoped `.radix-themes`, no `!important`, **zero net-new tokens**. `System/Lightbox` is the full-spine docs (History · Anatomy · Usage incl. the live token spec · Keyboard · Props); open/close + Escape, gallery nav + disabled-not-unmounted ends, the counter, keyboard zoom, and the announce-only-on-index-change are `_internal/Lightbox behavior`.

### power-search

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-11.

**PowerSearch is a structured filter bar on a flat AND model, with a non-dialog edit popover and Radix's Escape stack.**

**What you see.** A field pick opens an editor that builds a filter, and each committed filter becomes a `Token` chip that reads field, operator and a bold value. The component is ported under [catalog-as-specification](#catalog-as-specification).

**Model.** `src/powersearch/` holds the pure, tested model.

- Filters combine with AND only. The `nested` type is deferred, and the evaluator treats it as a passthrough.
- `OperatorValue` is a union of 14 members.
- `createPowerSearchConfig(defs)` returns `config` and `applyFilters`, and `InferData` maps a field key to its type.
- `usePowerSearchSource` is the typeahead source for fields, aliases and quick adds.
- One `formatFilterValue` replaces two renderers that upstream kept in sync by hand. A `date_range` reads as "Jan 25, 2026 – Feb 10, 2026", and a `date_relative` reads as its label, such as "7 days ago".

**Value editors.** Each value type opens a system field.

| Type | Editor |
|---|---|
| `string` | `TextField`, or `Typeahead` with a `searchSource` |
| `string_list`, `entity_list` | `Tokenizer` |
| `integer`, `float` | `NumberInput` |
| `time` | `TimeInput` |
| `date_absolute` | `DateInput` |
| `date_range` | `DateRangeInput` |
| `date_relative`, `enum` | `Select`, which commits and closes on pick |
| `enum_list` | `MultiSelect` |
| `custom` | The consumer's `Editor` |

**Edit popover.** The popover follows Typeahead on `@radix-ui/react-popover`: `Popover.Content role="none"`, automatic focus prevented on open and close, and outside interaction exempt for the anchor. Focus goes to the editor's first field, the field combobox stays live behind it, and a click on another chip swaps the editor and resets its state. The panel is the compound `.radix-themes.rt-ds-powersearch-popover` on the shared opaque overlay ([floating-surface-fill](#floating-surface-fill), [select-selected-row](#select-selected-row)).

**Escape.** Escape works on two levels on Radix's DismissableLayer stack, with no escape stack written by hand. A nested Select closes on the first Escape, and the edit popover closes on the second, resets and returns focus to the field input. Enter to save stays an explicit handler.

**Chips.** The chip row reuses the `.rt-ds-tokenizer` surface and holds `Token` chips ([token-chip](#token-chip)) with an embedded `Typeahead` as the last child. A chip's body opens the editor, and its remove control sits outside the tab order, so each chip is one tab stop. The `Tokenizer` component is not used, because its chips commit on pick and are removable only ([tokenizer-input](#tokenizer-input)).

**API.**

- `components`, a map from value type to `Token` and `Editor`, is the override seam.
- `resultCount` announces politely on change, formatted with `Intl.NumberFormat`.
- `disabledMessage` maps to `disabledReason` ([disabled-reason](#disabled-reason)), and `status` maps to `validation`.
- `menuWidth` and `maxOperatorMenuItems`, never wired upstream, are dropped.
- No new tokens. The only new CSS is the popover panel and its editor layout.

**Changed from.** No earlier ruling covered this.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-11. No later ruling amends it.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **PowerSearch — the structured filter bar on a flat-AND model, a non-dialog edit popover, and Radix's Escape stack (2026-07-11).** A field pick opens an editor that builds a filter; each committed filter is a Token chip (field · operator · **bold value**). Ported under [catalog-as-specification](#catalog-as-specification) @ `88c95e4`. **(1) THE MODEL LAYER (`src/powersearch/`, pure + tested — 107 logic tests).** Flat **AND-only**; the 14-member `OperatorValue` union; `createPowerSearchConfig(defs)` → `{config, applyFilters}` + `InferData` (maps field key → JS type); `usePowerSearchSource` (the field/alias/quick-add typeahead source); and the **ONE** `formatFilterValue` — COLLAPSED from upstream's TWO hand-synced token renderers (which drifted: one returned the literal string `date range`). Two upstream stubs fixed there: `date_range` now renders `{start} – {end}` (a real range → **"Jan 25, 2026 – Feb 10, 2026"**, not the `date range` literal), and `date_relative` maps the machine code back to its label (**"7 days ago"**, not the raw `7d_ago`). `nested` (the only TreeList consumer) is DEFERRED — the evaluator treats it as passthrough — so v1 has no blocking dep on it. **(2) THE 14-TYPE VALUE EDITOR (`PowerSearchValueEditor.tsx`).** Each operator value type routes to OUR Field-shell input: `string`→**TextField** (or **Typeahead** with a `searchSource`); `string_list`→**Tokenizer** (creatable); `integer`/`float`→**NumberInput** (integer-only for integer); `time`→**TimeInput**; `date_absolute`→**DateInput** (marshals unixSeconds ⇄ ISODateString); `date_relative`→**Select** (auto-commit); `date_range`→**DateRangeInput** (marshals ABSOLUTE endpoints ⇄ ISO); `enum`→**Select** (auto-commit); `enum_list`→**MultiSelect**; `entity_list`→**Tokenizer** (`TAux` carries `{photo}`); `custom`→the consumer `Editor`; `nested`→skipped. `enum`/`date_relative` fire `onChange(value, shouldSave=true)` → commit + close on the same tick. Upstream's LOCAL `createStaticSource` copy is eliminated (enum_list → MultiSelect needs none; the shared one still lives in `Typeahead.tsx`). **(3) THE NON-DIALOG EDIT POPOVER (`PowerSearch.tsx`).** Driven on `@radix-ui/react-popover` EXACTLY like our Typeahead: `Popover.Content role="none"` + `onOpenAutoFocus`/`onCloseAutoFocus` prevented + `onInteractOutside` exempting the anchor surface — so focus is ours to place (the editor's first field via a `requestAnimationFrame`), the field combobox stays live behind it, it's not a modal, and a chip re-click SWAPS the editor (keyed by mode+index+field so `useState` resets — the `PowerSearchEditPopover.test.tsx` switch-tokens / delete-then-edit-shifted-index cases). Portaled content wrapped in `<Theme>`; the panel is a COMPOUND `.radix-themes.rt-ds-powersearch-popover` (Theme + Content on the same node, the [select-selected-row](#select-selected-row) trap) painting the shared opaque overlay treatment (`--ds-bg-overlay`/`--ds-radius-3`/`--ds-shadow-overlay`, [floating-surface-fill](#floating-surface-fill)). **(4) THE 2-LEVEL ESCAPE — escapeStack DELETED.** Upstream hand-rolled `!e.defaultPrevented` bookkeeping; ours rests on **Radix's DismissableLayer stack** (the `_internal/EscapeStack` mechanism guard): a nested Select/dropdown is the inner layer (Escape #1 closes just it — verified: `@radix-ui/react-select` IS a DismissableLayer), the edit popover is the outer (Escape #2 → `onEscapeKeyDown`/`onOpenChange(false)` → reset + refocus the field input). **Enter-to-save stays an explicit handler** (Radix doesn't own Enter). **(5) CHIP ASSEMBLY — reuse over reinvention.** The chip row REUSES the `.rt-ds-tokenizer` surface verbatim (fill + `--gray-a7` hairline + the [validation-focus-paint](#validation-focus-paint) dual-tone focus-ring hoist + the `[data-validation]` paint + the disabled skin) holding `Token` chips ([token-chip](#token-chip) — clickable body opens the editor, sibling ✕ removes; the ✕ swept out of the tab order → one stop per chip) + an embedded `Typeahead` as the last flex child. We do NOT drive our `Tokenizer` component: its [tokenizer-input](#tokenizer-input) contract COMMITS a chip on pick and its chips are removable-only, but a PowerSearch pick must OPEN THE EDITOR and its chips are clickable — so `Token` + `Typeahead` are composed directly. A single-entity `entity_list` chip shows the entity photo as the Token **Avatar** leading icon. The `components` map (`Partial<Record<OperatorValue['type'], {Token?, Editor?}>>`) is the LOAD-BEARING override seam. `resultCount` announces politely on change via `useAnnounce` + `Intl.NumberFormat`; `disabledMessage` → our `disabledReason` ([disabled-reason](#disabled-reason)); `status` → `validation`. **(6) THE 7 DOC-OMITTED PROPS documented** (`components`, `startIcon`, `onFocus`, `onBlur`, `tokenOverflowBehavior`) + `menuWidth` and `maxOperatorMenuItems` were DEAD upstream (never wired) and DROPPED, not carried as no-ops. **Normalization:** StyleX `*Vars` → `--ds-*`; Astryx `Selector`→our `Select`, `TextInput`→`TextField`, native `usePopover`→Radix Popover; the two token renderers → one `formatFilterValue`; the local `createStaticSource` → eliminated; dates via `src/dates/*`. `System/PowerSearch` is the FULL-tier spine (History · Anatomy incl. a live token spec · Usage · Keyboard · Properties · Props); the editor matrix, add/edit/remove, the 2-level Escape, and the state-reset cases are `_internal/PowerSearch behavior` (verified over a COLOURED `--accent-3` backdrop). All scoped `.radix-themes`, no `!important`, **zero net-new tokens** (the only net-new CSS is the `.rt-ds-powersearch-popover` panel + its 3-cell editor layout).

### badge-scope

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-11.

**Badge is a display marker only, and every clickable, linked or removable chip is a Token.**

**What you see.** A Badge is a flat `soft` chip: a label with a semantic `tone`, a `leadingIcon` and a `trailingIcon`, and a categorical `color`, `size` and `radius`. It has no interactive mode of any kind.

**Removed from Badge.**

- The `emphasis` prop and its `BadgeEmphasis` type.
- The `asChild` interactive body.
- The `onRemove` and `removeLabel` remove control.

**Why.** A control carries a visible boundary and a label carries none. The surface edge of a Token reads as a control and the flat tint of a Badge reads as a label, so the two never overlap. A chip that only removes is a Token too, because its remove control is a control, and one removable chip skin cannot drift from a second.

**Migration.** No product code used the removed modes, only the Badge stories. A Token with a plain body matches the old removable Badge pixel for pixel ([token-chip](#token-chip)).

**Docs.** The Badge and Token Usage pages both render the shared `CHIPS_COMPARISON` table from `_comparisons.tsx`, with the column of the current component highlighted.

**Changed from.** Badge was the only chip. It took an `emphasis` prop, a clickable body through `asChild` and a remove control through `onRemove`.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-11.

- [aschild-or-type-error](#aschild-or-type-error) makes `asChild` on a Badge a type error, where before the prop arrived through an untyped spread and threw.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **Badge — narrowed to DISPLAY-ONLY; the interactive/removable modes consolidated onto Token (2026-07-11).** Badge is now a **display marker only** — a flat `soft`-variant chip (semantic `tone` + `leadingIcon`/`trailingIcon` + categorical `color`/`size`/`radius` + a label) with **no interactivity**. **(1) REMOVED from Badge:** the `emphasis` prop and its `BadgeEmphasis` type, the `asChild` interactive-body mode, and the `onRemove`/`removeLabel` removable-chip mode. A clickable, navigable, or removable chip is now **always a Token** ([token-chip](#token-chip)); its no-body/static mode is pixel-identical to the old removable Badge, so nothing is lost. **(2) The rationale — the surface EDGE is the honest signal.** A control must carry a real boundary; a label must not. Letting Badge own a removable/interactive mode meant a flat `soft` display fill could stand in for a control (and a second removable-chip skin risked drifting from Token's). The line is now drawn at **any** interactivity: **display → Badge** (flat `soft` tint, reads as a label), **interactive → Token** (surface edge, reads as a control) — so the two never overlap. **(3) Remove-only is a Token concern too**, because a ✕ is a control. **(4) Non-breaking.** There were **no in-app consumers** of Badge's interactive/removable modes — only Badge's own stories exercised them — so the removal touches no product code; the stories were reworked to a clean display-only doc. The docs teach the split via the shared **Badge vs. Token** comparison table (`_comparisons.tsx`, `CHIPS_COMPARISON`), rendered on **both** the Badge and Token Usage stories with the current component's column highlighted.

### tooltip-wrap

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-17.

**Tooltip is a thin system wrap over the Radix Themes Tooltip, and the disabled-reason tooltip composes it.**

**What it adds.**

- a `delayDuration` default of 400ms
- the solid panel of [floating-surface-fill](#floating-surface-fill)
- the hint-tier motion of [motion-retiming](#motion-retiming), 120ms in and 180ms out

**Skin.** Radix's tooltip skin, unchanged and with no token of its own. The docs page reads the rendered panel live through `RenderedRow`.

**Disabled reason.** `DisabledReasonTooltip` in `Field.tsx` composes this wrap, where it used a raw Radix `<Tooltip>` under the gap rule of [component-registry](#component-registry). Its plays did not change.

**Docs.** A lite page whose docs story is named `Usage`. The open and close behaviour sits in `_internal/Tooltip behavior`.

**Changed from.** Tooltip was a planned component, so `DisabledReasonTooltip` used a raw Radix Themes `<Tooltip>` under the gap rule of [component-registry](#component-registry).

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-17.

- [docs-page-spine](#docs-page-spine) renames the docs story of a lite page from `Overview` to `Usage`, on 2026-07-30.
- [motion-retiming](#motion-retiming) gives the tooltip its own motion pair, 120ms in and 180ms out, in place of the popper-tier motion it inherited.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **Tooltip — the System wrap over Radix's Tooltip; [disabled-reason](#disabled-reason)'s disabled-reason now composes it (2026-07-17).** A thin wrap over Radix Themes' `Tooltip`: a friendlier `delayDuration` default (400ms), the [floating-surface-fill](#floating-surface-fill) solid panel, and the [collapsible-and-accordion](#collapsible-and-accordion) popper-tier motion inherited from the `.rt-TooltipContent` binding — no per-component motion override. It **reuses Radix's tooltip skin verbatim** (tokenless), so the lite-spine token spec reads the rendered panel live via `RenderedRow` (dark `#1c2024` bg / `#fcfcfd` text / `--ds-radius-2`). Zero net-new tokens, zero new CSS. **The [disabled-reason](#disabled-reason) disabled-reason swap:** `useDisabledReason`'s `DisabledReasonTooltip` was a raw Radix `<Tooltip>` under the [component-registry](#component-registry) agent-gap rule; now that Tooltip is `ported` it composes the System wrap (`Field.tsx` import + JSX), its plays unchanged. `System/Tooltip` is the lite spine, its single docs story named `Usage` (renamed from `Overview` by [docs-page-spine](#docs-page-spine)'s 2026-07-30 amendment, which gave both tiers one grammar); open/close driving lives in `_internal/Tooltip behavior`.

### separator-wrap

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-17.

**`Separator` is a thin wrap over the Radix Themes `Separator` that keeps its skin and adds `aria-orientation` to a semantic vertical rule.**

**What you see.** The Radix rule paints `--gray-a6`, the value `--ds-stroke-weak` aliases, so a bare divider matches the system with no override, no new token and no new CSS.

**Accessibility.** A semantic rule, `decorative={false}`, with `orientation="vertical"` carries `aria-orientation="vertical"`, because the Radix Themes `Separator` is its own component, not the `@radix-ui/react-separator` primitive, and emits none. A decorative rule carries no role.

**Docs.** The wrap declares no token of its own, so its docs page measures the rendered rule live. It opened the Layout category of the navigation.

**Changed from.** No earlier ruling covered this.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-17. No later ruling amends it.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **Separator — the System wrap over Radix's Separator, with an aria-orientation a11y fill (2026-07-17).** A thin wrap over Radix Themes' `Separator`, reusing its skin (its default `--gray-a6` rule = what `--ds-stroke-weak` aliases, so a bare divider matches the system with no override). Tokenless → the lite-spine spec reads the rendered rule live via `RenderedRow` (`#00002f26`, 1px). **One a11y upgrade:** a semantic (`decorative={false}`) *vertical* rule gets `aria-orientation="vertical"` — Radix Themes' hand-rolled Separator emits none (it is NOT the `@radix-ui/react-separator` primitive; a decorative separator carries no role). Seeds the new **`System/Layout`** nav category. Zero net-new tokens/CSS.

### link-and-link-provider

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-17.

**The system `Link` underlines by default, and `LinkProvider` routes every system link through the framework link of the app.**

**What you see.** `Link` wraps the Radix Themes `Link` and keeps its skin, the accent step 11 that `--ds-text-link` names. `underline` defaults to `always`, and focus draws the system focus ring ([focus-ring](#focus-ring)).

**Why.** The Radix default, `auto`, underlines only on hover, so an inline link reads about 2.5:1 against the text around it, under the 3:1 that link-in-text-block asks.

**Router adapter.** `LinkProvider` takes a `component`, and `useLinkComponent()` returns it, or the native `"a"` tag when no provider is present. The component receives `href` and the anchor attributes.

**Item.** This ruling amends [item-row-primitive](#item-row-primitive). An `Item` with `href` renders `linkComponent ?? useLinkComponent()`, so a nav row routes through a framework `<Link>` and still composes `Item`. With no provider the output is identical to the old output, so List, TreeList and Token do not change.

**Not covered.** The ruling left the adoption by Breadcrumbs and Outline to a named later change.

**Changed from.** `Item` rendered its `href` body as a plain `<a>`, and the system offered no link wrapper and no router seam.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-17.

- [focus-ring](#focus-ring) replaces the neutral focus hairline of [validation-focus-paint](#validation-focus-paint) with the accent focus ring.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **Link + LinkProvider, and the Item pluggable-link amendment (2026-07-17).** **System `Link`** wraps Radix Themes' `Link`, reusing its accent-11 skin (= `--ds-text-link`, confirmed live) with `underline="always"` the default (Radix's `auto` only underlines on hover, so an inline link fails link-in-text-block contrast at ~2.5:1 < 3:1) and the [validation-focus-paint](#validation-focus-paint) neutral focus hairline overriding Radix's accent-8 ring (the same non-text-contrast fix the system applies to every other control). **`LinkProvider` / `useLinkComponent`** are a router adapter: `useLinkComponent()` returns the provided `component` (`{href}` + anchor attrs), defaulting to the string `"a"`. **Item amendment (amends [item-row-primitive](#item-row-primitive)):** `Item.tsx` restores the dropped `useLinkComponent` — its `href` body renders `linkComponent ?? useLinkComponent()` (default `"a"`), so nav rows route through a framework `<Link>` while still composing `Item`, and every existing consumer (List/TreeList/Token) is byte-for-byte unchanged (default identical). Breadcrumbs/Outline retro-adoption is a named follow-up.

### layout-primitive

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`, `LAYOUT`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-17.

**`Layout` composes a page shell from header, footer, panel and content slots, draws the dividers between them, and emits a landmark only on request.**

**Parts.** `Layout` with `LayoutHeader`, `LayoutFooter`, `LayoutPanel` and `LayoutContent`, also reachable as `Layout.Header` and its siblings. Its docs page is the full page of [docs-page-spine](#docs-page-spine), led by a page-anatomy diagram, and it adds no token.

**Dividers and padding.** `Layout` scans its children for slots and, with `defaultHasDividers`, draws a system `Separator` between adjacent areas, and a slot's `hasDivider` overrides that for its own edge. `padding` applies per slot, and `contentWidth` caps and centres the content.

**Landmarks.** Slots render plain `<div>` elements. The boolean `landmark` prop gives a slot its role: `banner` for the header, `contentinfo` for the footer and `complementary` for a panel. `Layout` never emits `main`, which belongs to `AppShell`.

**Props.** `contentWidth`, `padding` and `defaultHasDividers` are documented, and other props and `data-testid` reach the root element. A prop the type accepts is never discarded.

**Resizing.** A `resizable` `LayoutPanel` reads the [resize-handle](#resize-handle) engine, `useResizable` and `ResizeHandle`, from a subcomponent, so the hook never runs conditionally or inside a `.map()`.

**Changed from.** The system had no page-shell primitive. The source it was ported from hid `contentWidth`, `padding` and `defaultHasDividers` from its documentation and dropped other props and `data-testid`.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-17.

- [seam-ownership](#seam-ownership) has `Layout` skip its own divider on either side of a resizable panel, whose `ResizeHandle` draws that seam.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **Layout — the page-shell composition primitive with resolved dividers and opt-in landmarks (2026-07-17).** `Layout` + `LayoutHeader`/`LayoutFooter`/`LayoutPanel`/`LayoutContent` (also a `Layout.Header` namespace). A **slot-context architecture** (a static slot marker + `LayoutContext` + a synchronous children-scan) resolves which dividers to draw between adjacent areas (`defaultHasDividers` + per-slot overrides, drawn with the System `Separator`) and applies slot-aware padding. The real-but-hidden `contentWidth`/`padding` API is **documented**; `...rest`/`data-testid` are **forwarded** (upstream silently drops them — forward honestly or omit from the type, never accept-and-discard). **Landmarks are opt-in** via a boolean `landmark` prop emitting the slot's canonical role (`banner`/`contentinfo`/`complementary`) — slots render generic `<div>`s (an implicit `<header>` in divs would be an auto-banner), and `main` is NOT emitted here (AppShell owns it). A `resizable` `LayoutPanel` reads the [resize-handle](#resize-handle) engine (`useResizable` + `ResizeHandle`), the hook isolated in a subcomponent so it is never conditional/in a `.map()`. FULL spine; a page-anatomy diagram is the centerpiece. Zero net-new tokens.

### app-shell

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`, `LAYOUT`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-17.

**AppShell composes one Layout, owns the responsive swap to a mobile drawer, and provides the app shell contexts.**

**Composition.** One `Layout`, with `topNav` in the header, `sideNav` in the panel, `children` in the guaranteed `main` and `footer` in the footer. `main` takes its padding from `gutter` ([app-shell-gutter](#app-shell-gutter)).

**Mode swap.** Below the breakpoint the side and top navigation re-render into the `MobileNav` drawer through the render-mode contexts, a swap of modes rather than a CSS collapse. The desktop tree stays mounted under the `hidden` attribute, not the experimental `React.Activity`.

- The `breakpoint` in `mobileNav` takes `sm`, `md`, `lg` or `none`, or a number of pixels.
- The media query runs on `useMediaQuery` and `useIsMobile`, safe under server-side rendering (SSR), with `useSyncExternalStore` over `matchMedia`, and `defaultIsMobile` seeds the server snapshot so a mobile client shows no layout flash.
- `mobileNav` takes `false`, a `MobileNavConfig` or a `ReactNode`.
- Tests force the mode through config rather than a viewport resize.

**Contexts.** `AppShellMobileProvider` publishes `{isMobile, open, setOpen, drawerId, toggleId}`, beside `SideNavRenderProvider` and `TopNavRenderProvider`. No parallel context exists.

**Landmarks.** `main` is the only landmark AppShell emits. A skip link, hidden until focused, targets it, and `main` takes `tabIndex={-1}` so focus lands there in every browser, where the upstream relied on fragment navigation alone.

**Header height.** The shell publishes the header's height as the runtime custom property `--ds-appshell-header-height` through the shared `sharedResizeObserver`, with no new observer, and consumers read `var(--ds-appshell-header-height, 0px)`. It is a runtime value, not a design token, and it is the only new piece the shell adds.

**Changed from.** No earlier ruling covered this.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-17.

- [stacking-ladder](#stacking-ladder) gives the skip link `--ds-z-skip-link`, above the app chrome.
- [focus-criterion-numbers](#focus-criterion-numbers) asks a consumer who makes the header sticky to pair `--ds-appshell-header-height` with `scroll-padding-top`.
- [app-shell-gutter](#app-shell-gutter) adds `gutter`, default `"5"`, the 24px that `main` carried as a fixed pad.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **AppShell — the responsive page shell that owns the mode-swap and provides the app-shell contexts (2026-07-17).** Composes one `Layout` (topNav→Header, sideNav→Panel, children→the guaranteed `main`, footer→Footer) and owns the responsive behavior. **Breakpoint mode-swap** via the lifted SSR-safe `useMediaQuery`/`useIsMobile` (`useSyncExternalStore` over `matchMedia`, seeded by a `defaultIsMobile` server snapshot so a mobile client does not layout-flash; `breakpoint` accepts a named `sm|md|lg|none` OR a numeric px threshold): below it, sideNav/topNav **re-render into the MobileNav drawer** via the render-mode contexts (a mode-swap, NOT a CSS collapse), the desktop tree kept mounted-but-`hidden` (the `hidden` attribute, not the experimental `React.Activity`). **Provides the committed `appShellContext` providers** (`AppShellMobileProvider` publishing `{isMobile, open, setOpen, drawerId, toggleId}`, `SideNavRenderProvider`, `TopNavRenderProvider`) — no parallel contexts. **Skip link** (visually-hidden-until-focus) targets `#main`, which gets `tabIndex={-1}` so focus lands deterministically (the fix — upstream relied on fragment nav alone); `main` is the only auto-emitted landmark. **Header-height** is published as the runtime CSS var `--ds-appshell-header-height` via the shared `sharedResizeObserver` (no new observer; consumers read `var(…, 0px)`). Tri-modal `mobileNav` = `false | MobileNavConfig | ReactNode`. FULL spine with a full-page anatomy; the mode-swap is tested by FORCED config, not viewport resize. Only net-new is the runtime header-height var (not a design token).

### form-layout

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`, `LAYOUT`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-17.

**FormLayout sets the label direction for the Fields inside it and stacks them in a grid, and it renders a `<div>`, never a `<form>`.**

**What it does.**

- Publishes `direction`, `"vertical"` or `"horizontal"`, to descendant Fields through a context, read with `useFormLayoutDirection()`.
- Stacks the fields in a grid that never wraps, one field per row.
- In the horizontal direction, owns the label and control tracks, so every horizontal Field inside it aligns its control to one edge ([horizontal-field-labels](#horizontal-field-labels)).

**Why a div.** The consumer owns the form element, so a FormLayout nests inside any form, route or dialog.

**Rejected.** A wrapping flex row, which the source specification described.

**Tokens.** The component adds no token.

**Changed from.** No earlier ruling covered this.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-17.

- [horizontal-field-labels](#horizontal-field-labels) carries the horizontal direction into `Field.Root`, and its update of 2026-07-22 gives a horizontal FormLayout the two tracks that its Fields share through `subgrid`.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **FormLayout — a direction context for Field-riding forms (2026-07-17).** Publishes a `{direction: "vertical" | "horizontal"}` context (`useFormLayoutDirection()`) to descendant Fields and renders a **`<div>`, not a `<form>`** (composition — the consumer owns the form element, so FormLayout nests inside any form/route) as a **non-wrapping grid stack** (upstream's "flex wrapping" is fiction). LITE spine. Its horizontal effect is realized by the Field amendment ([horizontal-field-labels](#horizontal-field-labels)). Zero net-new tokens.

### horizontal-field-labels

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`, `LAYOUT`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-17.

**`Field.Root` takes a `direction`, and a horizontal Field sets its label beside the control.**

**Resolution.** `direction` resolves from the explicit prop, then the ambient `FormLayout`, then `"vertical"`, and reaches the root as `data-direction`. Every input on the Field shell inherits the mode.

**Horizontal.** Label and control sit in a CSS grid, `grid-template-columns: auto minmax(0,1fr)`, with the label in its own `auto` track and the control in the rest. At `480px` and below a `@media` query stacks them in one column, in CSS alone.

**Aligned rows.** A horizontal `FormLayout` owns the two-track grid, and each horizontal `Field.Root` inside it takes `grid-template-columns: subgrid`, so every control in the form starts at one left edge. A horizontal Field with no `FormLayout` parent keeps its own `auto` track.

**Vertical.** The default renders exactly as before, because no grid rule matches `data-direction="vertical"`.

**Tokens.** The amendment adds no token.

**Changed from.** Every Field stacked its label above the control ([field-shell](#field-shell)). Until 2026-07-22 each horizontal Field held its own label track, so the start of each control moved with the length of its label.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-17, and updated in this entry on 2026-07-22 with the aligned label column. It amends [field-shell](#field-shell) with the `direction` mode. No later ruling amends it.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **Field horizontal-labels — a layout amendment to the shared Field shell (2026-07-17).** Amends [field-shell](#field-shell). `Field.Root` gains `direction` (resolution: explicit prop → the ambient `FormLayout` context → `"vertical"`), threaded as `data-direction`. **Horizontal** lays label + control as a CSS grid `grid-template-columns: auto minmax(0,1fr)` (the label its own auto track, the control filling the rest), collapsing to a single stacked column at `≤480px` via a `@media` query — **CSS only, not JS**. Vertical (the default) is **byte-identical** to before (an inert `data-direction="vertical"`, `display:flex`, no grid rule matches). Every Field-riding input (TextField/Select/…) inherits the mode for free. **Known limitation:** each Field is its own `auto` label track, so control start-x varies with label length across rows — a shared/aligned label column would be a subgrid/JS follow-up beyond the pinned spec. Zero net-new tokens. **[Update 2026-07-22: the "known limitation" is CLOSED. A horizontal FormLayout owns the two-track `auto minmax(0,1fr)` grid and each horizontal `Field.Root` inside it flips to `grid-template-columns: subgrid` (the "[horizontal-field-labels](#horizontal-field-labels) subgrid alignment" block in `components.css`), so every row's control aligns to one left edge; a horizontal Field with NO FormLayout parent keeps its own `auto` track, and the ≤480px collapse drops the subgrid back to a single stacked column. Still CSS-only.]**

### resize-handle

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`, `LAYOUT`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-17.

**ResizeHandle is the presentational grab handle, and the `useResizable` engine implements the window splitter of the Web Accessibility Initiative (WAI) ARIA practices.**

**Handle.** `ResizeHandle` takes its `separatorProps` and `onDragStart` from `useResizable`, which its owner calls. It is the 1px seam, and its grab zone is an overlay that reaches `--space-1` past the track ([resize-handle-seam](#resize-handle-seam)). It paints `--ds-stroke-weak` for the track and `--ds-fill-hover` for a grab pill that strengthens to `--ds-fill-medium` on hover and focus, and focus draws the system ring around the grab zone ([focus-ring](#focus-ring)). The cursor is `col-resize` or `row-resize` by orientation. Zero new tokens.

**Engine.** `useResizable`, with the pure `resizableMath` tested on the `.logic.test.ts` lane, implements the splitter contract:

- `role="separator"`, `aria-valuenow` (0 when collapsed), `aria-valuemin`, and `aria-valuemax`, omitted when the maximum is `Infinity`.
- An arrow key moves 10px, Shift with an arrow 50px, and Home and End reach the bounds.
- Enter and a double-click collapse the pane, and a pointer drag resizes it.
- The size persists in `localStorage` under a `ds-` prefix.

**Fixes carried.** The port omits four upstream bugs:

- Expanding by keyboard or double-click restores the remembered `preCollapseSize`, where upstream lands on `minSizePx`.
- The dead `shrinkOrder` field is gone.
- Several regions take a fixed number of hooks, never hooks inside `.map()`.
- The drag listeners are removed on unmount in the middle of a drag.

**Gap.** `useResizable` is not exported, so a consumer has no supported way to drive `ResizeHandle` outside `Layout` and `SideNav` ([internal-hooks](#internal-hooks)). The drag is the only pointer route to a size, a WCAG 2.5.7 failure ([dragging-movement-gaps](#dragging-movement-gaps)).

**Changed from.** No earlier ruling covered this.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-17.

- [dragging-movement-gaps](#dragging-movement-gaps) records the drag as the only pointer route to a size, a WCAG 2.5.7 failure.
- [seam-ownership](#seam-ownership) makes the handle the one part that draws the seam at a resizable panel.
- [resize-handle-seam](#resize-handle-seam) makes the handle the 1px hairline itself, with the grab zone as a `::before` overlay that takes no layout.
- [focus-ring](#focus-ring) replaces the inset focus hairline with the accent focus ring around the grab zone.
- [internal-hooks](#internal-hooks) records that `useResizable` is not exported.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **ResizeHandle and the useResizable engine — the WAI window-splitter (2026-07-17).** `ResizeHandle` is the presentational grab handle: the consumer owns `useResizable` and hands the handle its `separatorProps` + `onDragStart`; a grab pill strengthens on hover/focus, `col-resize`/`row-resize` by orientation, an inset focus hairline, painting only `--ds-stroke-weak`/`--ds-fill-hover`/`--ds-fill-medium`. **The lifted engine** (`useResizable` + pure `resizableMath` on the `.logic.test.ts` lane) implements the WAI splitter contract — `role="separator"`, `aria-valuenow` (0 when collapsed) / `aria-valuemin` / `aria-valuemax` (omitted when `Infinity`), Arrow ±10 / Shift+Arrow ±50 / Home/End, Enter + double-click collapse, pointer drag, `localStorage` under a `ds-` prefix. **Fixes carried, not the upstream bugs:** keyboard/double-click **expand restores the remembered `preCollapseSize`** (upstream lands on `minSizePx`), the dead `shrinkOrder` field is dropped, multi-region is fixed-arity (never hooks-in-`.map()`), the drag-listener cleanup runs on unmount mid-drag. Zero net-new tokens.

### mobile-nav

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-17.

**`MobileNav` is a navigation drawer that slides from a screen edge, and it uses the raw Radix Dialog.**

**Parts.** `MobileNav` and `MobileNavToggle`. Like [command-palette](#command-palette) and [lightbox-viewer](#lightbox-viewer), the drawer uses the raw Radix Dialog, which supplies the focus trap, scroll lock, Escape and the backdrop.

**State.** Inside `AppShell`, the drawer reads the open state that `AppShell` owns from `useAppShellMobile()`. A standalone drawer manages its own state, and an explicit `id` gives the toggle's `aria-controls` its target.

**What you see.**

- `side="auto"`, the default, reads the trigger's position at open from `document.activeElement` and slides from the nearer edge. Radix has no equivalent.
- The width is `min(100vw, width)`. The 85vw cap that the upstream docs describe does not exist.
- The panel is the opaque `--ds-bg-overlay` surface ([floating-surface-fill](#floating-surface-fill)) over the `--ds-scrim` backdrop.
- The drawer slides on the modal tier: in at `--ds-duration-moderate` with `--ds-ease-entry`, and out at `--ds-duration-expressive` with `--ds-ease-standard`. Only the slide keyframes are new.
- Nav rows use a real `href` and `aria-current="page"`. The drawer adds zero new tokens.

**Accessibility.** Initial focus lands on the panel through `onOpenAutoFocus`. `MobileNavToggle` adds `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`, which upstream lacks, and swaps a hamburger glyph for an X when the drawer opens.

**Changed from.** No earlier ruling covered this.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-17.

- [motion-retiming](#motion-retiming) retimes the slide from emphasis in and fast out on the exit curve to moderate in and expressive out on the standard curve.
- [focus-return-on-close](#focus-return-on-close) returns focus to the opener when the drawer closes.
- [published-aschild-props](#published-aschild-props) refuses `asChild` on `MobileNavToggle` as a type error.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **MobileNav — a slide-in drawer on raw Radix Dialog (2026-07-17).** Rides the [command-palette](#command-palette)/[lightbox-viewer](#lightbox-viewer) raw-Dialog precedent. `MobileNav` + `MobileNavToggle`. Consumes the committed `appShellContext` mobile seam (`useAppShellMobile()` — AppShell owns the open state; a standalone drawer manages its own via an explicit `id` for the toggle's `aria-controls`). `side="auto"` reads `document.activeElement`'s rect at open to slide from the edge nearest the trigger (no Radix analog — lifted). Honest width `min(100vw, width)` (upstream's "85vw cap" is fiction). **Emphasis-tier slide motion** (`ds-mobilenav-in/out-{start,end}` keyframes, enter emphasis/entry, exit fast/exit; only the transform path is net-new — Radix's inherited modal motion is scale+fade). `onOpenAutoFocus` steers initial focus to the panel; Radix owns focus-trap/scroll-lock/Escape/backdrop. The panel is the **opaque [floating-surface-fill](#floating-surface-fill) `--ds-bg-overlay`** surface over the `--ds-scrim` backdrop (verified opaque over coloured content). **`MobileNavToggle` gains `aria-expanded` + `aria-controls`** (upstream has neither) and swaps a hamburger↔X glyph. Nav rows use real `href` + `aria-current="page"`. LITE spine. Zero net-new tokens.

### side-nav

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-17.

**SideNav is a labelled navigation rail of links that collapses on the reader's command, with three ways to render an item.**

**Parts.** `SideNav` with `SideNavItem`, `SideNavSection`, `SideNavHeading` and `SideNavCollapseButton`, and its rows compose `Item` ([item-row-primitive](#item-row-primitive)). Its docs page is the lite page and carries the `NAV_SURFACES_COMPARISON` table, and it adds no token.

**Semantics.** A labelled `<nav>` of links, never `role="menu"`, and the current destination carries `aria-current="page"`.

**Item regimes.**

- Expanded: a parent opens a nested `role="group"` that animates on the [collapsible-and-accordion](#collapsible-and-accordion) `ds-collapsible-*` keyframes with a measured height, and stays mounted but `inert` while closed, so its rows leave the tab order.
- Collapsed rail: an icon with a system `Tooltip`.
- Collapsed with children: an opaque popover flyout, built as MultiSelect builds its popover, which provides the expanded rows again.

**Collapse.** The reader or the app state collapses the rail, never a breakpoint. A narrow viewport swaps the rail for the drawer instead, which SideNav reads from `useSideNavRenderMode()`. The rail resizes on the [resize-handle](#resize-handle) engine, and `SideNavCollapseButton` carries `aria-expanded`.

**Keyboard.** A parent is one disclosure control with `aria-expanded` and no split navigate-and-toggle chevron, so leaves navigate and parents disclose. Arrow keys rove over the visible rows with the pure `nextFocusIndex` of `useListFocus`, which skips inert rows, because `useTreeFocus` hardcodes `role="treeitem"`.

**Changed from.** The source it was ported from built the rail as `role="menu"` link lists, gave its collapse button no `aria-expanded`, and carried a `collapsible.buttonLabel` sub-prop that did nothing, now dropped.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-17.

- [nav-row-ladder](#nav-row-ladder) puts every SideNav row on the Item ladder, 32, 36 and 40px at small, medium and large, and the collapsed rail measures what the expanded rows measure.
- [side-nav-section-divider](#side-nav-section-divider) adds the opt-in `divided` prop to `SideNav.Section`.
- [selected-row-cue](#selected-row-cue) gives the selected row a bold label and a solid icon.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **SideNav — a collapsible rail with three item regimes, render-mode aware (2026-07-17).** `SideNav` + `SideNavItem`/`SideNavSection`/`SideNavHeading`/`SideNavCollapseButton`. A labelled **`<nav>` of links** with `aria-current="page"` (nav+links, NOT `role="menu"`); rows **compose `Item`** (never re-anatomized). **Three regimes:** expanded (a nested `role="group"` that animates via the [collapsible-and-accordion](#collapsible-and-accordion) `ds-collapsible-*` keyframes fed a self-measured height, and is **`inert`-but-mounted** while collapsed so the subtree survives the toggle and drops out of the tab order); collapsed rail (icon + a System **Tooltip**); collapsed-with-children (an **opaque popover flyout** — the MultiSelect recipe — re-providing the expanded context). Collapse is **user/state-driven, never breakpoint-driven** (breakpoints swap to the drawer — a different axis). **No split-action chevron:** a parent is a **single disclosure control** (`aria-expanded`; leaves navigate, parents disclose) — composing `Item` yields one clean disclosure button, the honest a11y. Roving uses `useListFocus`'s pure `nextFocusIndex` (skipping inert rows) — `useTreeFocus` hardcodes `role="treeitem"`, incompatible with nav+links. Resizable via the [resize-handle](#resize-handle) engine; render-mode swap via `useSideNavRenderMode()`; `SideNavCollapseButton` gains `aria-expanded`, the dead `collapsible.buttonLabel` dropped. Adds `NAV_SURFACES_COMPARISON`. LITE spine. Zero net-new tokens.

### top-nav

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-17.

**`TopNav` is a bar whose menus are hover-intent popovers of links and whose mega panel spans the bar, built on the popover primitive and not on the navigation-menu primitive.**

**Parts.** `TopNav`, `TopNavItem`, `TopNavHeading`, `TopNavMenu`, `TopNavMegaMenu`, `TopNavMegaMenuItem` and `TopNavMegaMenuFeaturedCard`. `useTopNavRenderMode()` swaps the render mode.

**Menus.** Each menu composes `@radix-ui/react-popover` with `useMenuHover`, so every menu is an independent popover in the top layer. A panel is a labelled `nav` region of links, with `aria-current="page"` on the current link and never `role="menu"`. The arrow keys rove the links of every panel, the mega panel included, through `useListFocus`.

**Opening.** Hover intent shows a menu after 150ms and hides it after 200ms, only where `(hover: hover)` matches, and a click latches the menu. The trigger is a `Popover.Anchor`, exempt from outside dismissal, and opening never moves focus. ArrowDown moves focus into the panel. Menu and mega triggers carry `aria-controls`.

**Mega panel.** The mega panel spans the full width of the bar, anchored in script to the measured rectangle of the bar. `TopNavMegaMenuFeaturedCard` is presentational and ends in a Phosphor `ArrowRight`.

**Rejected.** The navigation-menu primitive, `@radix-ui/react-navigation-menu`, because the menus of the reference catalog ([catalog-as-specification](#catalog-as-specification)) open independently as top-layer popovers.

**Not covered.** Deferred by name:

- one menu open at a time, because the reference catalog has no such rule and enforcing one would invent it
- a More menu for overflow, which the reference catalog documents and never shipped
- CSS anchor positioning for the mega panel

**Docs.** A lite page, which compares the menu surfaces in `MENU_SURFACES_COMPARISON`. The menu, mega and featured card registry entries are documented on the `TopNav` page. No new tokens, and one new exit keyframe, `ds-overlay-out`.

**Changed from.** The registry named `@radix-ui/react-navigation-menu` as the building block of the bar.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-17.

- [top-nav-bar-height](#top-nav-bar-height) makes the bar height follow the size tier, at 56, 60 or 64px.
- [selected-row-cue](#selected-row-cue) adds a stronger label and icon weight to the selected row of the bar and its menus.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **TopNav — a bar with hover-intent popover menus and a full-width mega, NOT the navigation-menu primitive (2026-07-17).** `TopNav` + `TopNavItem`/`TopNavHeading`/`TopNavMenu`/`TopNavMegaMenu`/`TopNavMegaMenuItem`/`TopNavMegaMenuFeaturedCard`. **The navigation-menu primitive was evaluated and REJECTED** — Astryx's menus are focus-trapped, independently-open, top-layer popovers, so ours compose on `@radix-ui/react-popover` + the lifted `useMenuHover` (the registry `buildingBlock` is **corrected off `@radix-ui/react-navigation-menu`**). Panels are labelled **`<nav>` regions of links** with `aria-current="page"` (NOT `role="menu"`) — *including* arrow-key roving via `useListFocus`, which Astryx's mega lacks. **Hover-intent** = 150ms show / 200ms hide, `(hover:hover)`-gated, with a click-latch; the trigger is a `Popover.Anchor` (owns opening, exempts itself from outside-dismiss) and `onOpenAutoFocus` is prevented (no focus-steal; ArrowDown enters — no hand focus trap). The **mega panel is full-width, anchored to the measured bar rect** (JS measurement; CSS anchor-positioning is a named deferral); mega/menu triggers gain `aria-controls`. **Single-open coordination is deliberately NOT added** (menus open independently — a named deferral, since enforcing it would be invention); the documented "More menu overflow" is **upstream vaporware and not ported** (a named deferral on `useOverflow`). `FeaturedCard` is presentational, its hard-appended glyph replaced with a Phosphor `ArrowRight`. Render-mode swap via `useTopNavRenderMode()`. Adds `MENU_SURFACES_COMPARISON`. LITE spine; TopNavMenu/MegaMenu/FeaturedCard are documented-in-sibling registry entries. Zero net-new tokens (adds the `ds-overlay-out` exit keyframe).

### outline-scrollspy

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-17.

**Outline is a table of contents whose active entry follows the scroll position, read by a passive scroll listener and `requestAnimationFrame`.**

**Structure.** A labelled `<nav>` holding a `<ul>` of links. Entries are flat, and level shows as indentation only. Each entry renders through the pluggable `Link`, an in-page `#anchor` by default. The documentation page follows the lite spine.

**Sources.** Pass `items`, or pass `containerRef` and `useOutlineFromDOM` builds the list from the `h1` to `h6` headings in the container and rescans them on a `MutationObserver`.

**Scroll spy.** `useScrollSpy` reads a passive scroll listener on each animation frame, and it does not use `IntersectionObserver`.

- The active entry is the last heading whose top passed its activation line, with guards at the bottom of the page and above the first heading.
- A click pins its entry active until `scrollend`, or for 1200ms when that event never fires.
- A controlled `activeId` disables the spy.

**What you see.** The active entry carries `aria-current="location"`. A sliding bar marks it, positioned in JavaScript from the box of the active entry. CSS anchor positioning is a named deferral. Outline adds no new tokens.

**Changed from.** The catalog's Outline ([catalog-as-specification](#catalog-as-specification)) marked the active entry with the nonstandard `aria-current="true"`, and it rested on an `IntersectionObserver` assumption that testing proved false.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-17.

- [per-component-line-budget](#per-component-line-budget) adds `labelLines`, so an entry truncates to one line by default.
- [textless-part-fills](#textless-part-fills) paints the bar in `--accent-indicator`.
- [mark-on-tint-edge](#mark-on-tint-edge) rings the bar with `--accent-mark-edge`, in place of the [indicator-mark-edges](#indicator-mark-edges) edge.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **Outline — a rAF scrollspy table-of-contents on the lifted engines (2026-07-17).** A labelled `<nav> > <ul>` of TOC links. Consumes the lifted **`useScrollSpy`** (a passive scroll listener + rAF; active = the LAST heading whose top passed its activation line, with `atBottom`/top-edge guards; a click suppresses the spy via `lockActiveId` until `scrollend`/1200ms; a controlled `activeId` disables the spy) and **`useOutlineFromDOM`** (an `h1`–`h6` scan + `MutationObserver` — the DOM-driven mode), with the pluggable **`Link`** for entries (default in-page `#anchor`). The falsified IntersectionObserver assumption is not carried. The sliding indicator is **JS-measured** (reads the active entry's box, positions the bar — NOT CSS anchor-positioning, a named deferral). Active entries carry **`aria-current="location"`** (the upgrade from Astryx's nonstandard `"true"`). Flat items; level = indentation only. LITE spine. Zero net-new tokens.

### standard-dialog

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`, `SIZING`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-23.

**Dialog is the standard modal, a thin wrapper on the Radix Themes Dialog that sizes on a container lane.**

**Parts.** `Root`, `Trigger`, `Content`, `Title`, `Description` and `Close` come from Radix Themes, and a system `Dialog.Footer` renders a `ButtonGroup` wired to the global `buttonOrder`. A dialog holds one solid primary ([button-priority](#button-priority)), and Dialog takes no `tone`, because a destructive confirm belongs to AlertDialog.

**Size.** `Content` rides the `container` lane, new in `SizeContext`: small takes step 2, medium step 3 and large step 4, one step above the control lane. AlertDialog stays on the control lane on purpose, small at step 1, because a content dialog reads roomier than a short confirm. Card shares the container lane ([surface-wraps](#surface-wraps)).

**What you see.** The panel is opaque and raised, with no translucent variant ([floating-surface-fill](#floating-surface-fill)). Modal motion and the scrim fade come from the shared `.rt-BaseDialogContent` and `.rt-BaseDialogOverlay` classes, so Dialog adds no motion CSS. The docs page carries the full docs.

**Not swapped.** CommandPalette ([command-palette](#command-palette)), Lightbox ([lightbox-viewer](#lightbox-viewer)) and MobileNav ([mobile-nav](#mobile-nav)) keep the raw Radix Themes Dialog on purpose, because each steers its own focus, skins its own content and animates its own tiers.
