**Changed from.** The system had no Dialog. The registry listed it as planned, so a modal composed the raw Radix Themes Dialog.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-23.

- [motion-retiming](#motion-retiming) retimes the modal tier to a moderate entrance and an expressive exit on the standard curve.
- [focus-return-on-close](#focus-return-on-close) gives `Content` a default that returns focus to the opener when the consumer holds `open`.
- [button-cluster](#button-cluster) gives `Dialog.Footer` the cluster's flat gap and the alignment that follows its solid primary.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **Dialog — the standard modal, on a new container size lane (2026-07-23).** Wraps Radix Themes' compound Dialog (`Root/Trigger/Content/Title/Description/Close`) + a System `Dialog.Footer` that renders a `ButtonGroup` wired to the global `buttonOrder` (a wrapper wires EVERY system-parameterized behavior — the AlertDialog primary-first precedent); one solid primary per dialog ([button-priority](#button-priority)); `tone` is NOT exposed (destructive confirms stay AlertDialog's job — the Usage cross-links the pair). Content is the opaque, elevated panel ([floating-surface-fill](#floating-surface-fill), no translucent variant) and **rides a NET-NEW `container` size lane** added to `SizeContext` (`small→2 / medium→3 / large→4`) — a step above the control lane, shared by Card + (adapted) ScrollArea. **Deliberate divergence:** Dialog is container-scale (small→2) while AlertDialog stays control-scale (small→1) — a standard content dialog reads roomier than a terse confirm. Modal-tier motion (emphasis-in / fast-out **[Update 2026-07-28 ([motion-retiming](#motion-retiming)): now moderate-in / expressive-out, standard curve]** + the scrim fade) is inherited from the shared `.rt-BaseDialogContent`/`.rt-BaseDialogOverlay` base classes — ZERO new motion CSS. **The non-swap:** the three specialized raw-Dialog consumers (CommandPalette [command-palette](#command-palette), Lightbox [lightbox-viewer](#lightbox-viewer), MobileNav [mobile-nav](#mobile-nav)) deliberately KEEP the raw Radix Themes Dialog (they steer their own focus, skin their own content, animate their own tiers) — recorded so it never reads as an oversight. FULL spine.

### floating-surface-wraps

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-23.

**Popover, HoverCard, ContextMenu and MoreMenu are thin wraps over Radix, and Tabs is one name over panel tabs and link tabs.**

**Motion.** Each popper surface takes its motion from the shared `.rt-PopperContent` rule and adds no motion CSS. The timing is the one in [motion-retiming](#motion-retiming).

**Surfaces.**

- Popover: a click-opened panel with `role="dialog"`, on the control size lane.
- HoverCard: a supplementary preview only, on the control lane. It never shows on touch, so its trigger must itself navigate to the full content.
- ContextMenu: matches DropdownMenu, with the solid Content of [floating-surface-fill](#floating-surface-fill), the control lane and `Item tone="danger"`. The danger paint reuses the shared `.rt-BaseMenuItem[data-tone="danger"]` rule.
- MoreMenu: a ghost three-dots IconButton, named by a required `label`, over a DropdownMenu. It holds secondary and overflow actions only, never the primary action.
- Tabs: `Root`, `List`, `Trigger` and `Content` switch panels in place. `Nav.Root` and `Nav.Link` hold link tabs that navigate through `useLinkComponent` ([link-and-link-provider](#link-and-link-provider)) and mark the current tab `aria-current="page"`.

**Tabs size.** Radix tab lists accept only steps `1` and `2`, and `extractProps` swaps an out-of-range step for the prop's own default. The wrap clamps the size lane to `TabsSize`, `"1" | "2"`: small and medium map to `1` (32px) and large to `2` (40px). The label follows the text lane, 12, 14 and 16px, so at medium and large the tab row matches the control row in box and type.

**Docs.** A Tooltip, Popover and HoverCard comparison, `FLOATING_INFO_COMPARISON`, shows on all three pages and answers which floating surface carries information. ContextMenu adds a column to `MENU_SURFACES_COMPARISON`. MoreMenu appears as a cross-link on the DropdownMenu page, and Tabs and SegmentedControl cross-link as view switcher and value picker.

**Changed from.** No earlier ruling covered this.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-23.

- [motion-retiming](#motion-retiming) retimes the popper motion to the overlay duration in and the emphasis duration out, on the standard curve.
- An update of 2026-07-31 moved the Tabs map from 32, 40 and 40px to 32, 32 and 40px, and moved the tab label onto the text lane.
- [tabs-open-on-navigation](#tabs-open-on-navigation) gives Tabs its own activation. `Tabs.Root` holds the value and runs Radix in manual mode, and a tab opens on a navigation key, Enter, Space or a click, never on focus alone.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **Floating surfaces — Popover / HoverCard / ContextMenu / MoreMenu / Tabs (2026-07-23).** Thin wraps whose popper-tier **motion is inherited for free** from the shared `.rt-PopperContent` base class (moderate-in / fast-out **[Update 2026-07-28 ([motion-retiming](#motion-retiming)): now overlay-in / emphasis-out, standard curve]**) — verified per surface, ZERO new motion CSS. **Popover** (control lane, `role=dialog`) + **HoverCard** (control lane; a supplementary preview ONLY, invisible on touch, whose trigger must itself navigate to the full content) render a new **`FLOATING_INFO`** comparison (Tooltip · Popover · HoverCard — "which floating surface carries information?"), shown on all three pages incl. the existing Tooltip. **ContextMenu** mirrors System DropdownMenu exactly (solid Content [floating-surface-fill](#floating-surface-fill), control lane, `Item tone="danger"` → `data-tone`); the danger paint reuses the shared `.rt-BaseMenuItem[data-tone="danger"]` rule with ZERO new CSS; it adds a ContextMenu column to `MENU_SURFACES`. **MoreMenu** is a composition — a ghost IconButton (three-dots, REQUIRED `aria-label`) + DropdownMenu passthrough — for secondary/overflow actions only (never the primary action); it appears as a cross-link on the DropdownMenu page, not a comparison column. **Tabs** is a DUAL surface under one name: `Root/List/Trigger/Content` (panel tabs, content-in-place) + `Nav={Root,Link}` (link tabs that navigate via `useLinkComponent`/[link-and-link-provider](#link-and-link-provider) + `aria-current="page"`); its size is a documented **2-size clamp** (`small→1 / medium→2 / large→2`, since Radix tab lists accept only 1|2 — the raw control lane's "3" is out of range). **The clamp's real reason (corrected 2026-07-27):** an out-of-range enum is NOT dropped — `extractProps` (`@radix-ui/themes/dist/esm/helpers/extract-props.js`) substitutes the prop's own `default`, so an unclamped `large` would land on the tab list's default `"2"` — a step nobody asked for, chosen by the vendor rather than by the lane. Clamping makes that landing ours, explicit, and type-checked (`TabsSize = "1" | "2"`, so an invalid step can't be passed in the first place). Reciprocal do/don't vs SegmentedControl (view-switcher vs value-picker). LITE spines. **[Update 2026-07-31 (remap): the clamp stands — the vendor still ships two tab steps and the narrowed `TabsSize` type still stops the silent vendor default — but the mapping moved to `small→1 / medium→1 / large→2` (32/32/40). Each vendor step now lands on the tier whose CONTROL box it equals, so the tab row matches the control row's height at medium AND large, and the visible size change lands at medium→large. The vendor pairs each tab box with a label one step below what the control lane pairs with that box — so the pairing was not taken: the BOX rides the clamp and the TYPE rides the ordinary text lane (12/14/16px), restated on the tab list from a step the wrap stamps off the tier. The tab row therefore matches the control row on BOTH axes at medium (32+14) and large (40+16). Guarded twice: the class-step map in _internal/Size COVERAGE, and box AND type on both surfaces in _internal/Tabs behavior.]** **[Update 2026-09-28 ([tabs-open-on-navigation](#tabs-open-on-navigation)): what opens a tab is the wrap's own. Tabs.Root holds the value and runs Radix in manual mode, and Tabs.Trigger opens a tab on a navigation key, Enter, Space or a click, never on a bare focus.]**

### choice-controls

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-23.

**Switch, Slider, SegmentedControl, CheckboxCards and RadioCards ride the control size lane, and the two card pickers share one selected treatment.**

**What you see.**

- Switch shows Radix's on track, Slider its range, and SegmentedControl a neutral raised tile. The three reuse Radix's accent-aware skins and declare no `--ds-*` colour role.
- Slider passes its accessible name to any thumb without one, because Radix leaves a single-thumb slider's `role="slider"` nameless.

**Card pickers.** A selected card in CheckboxCards or RadioCards takes a slight `--ds-fill-accent-weak` wash, layered as a background image over Radix's own surface, and a 2px accent band at its edge in `--accent-indicator`. Radix alone gives a selected RadioCards card an outline and no fill, and a selected CheckboxCards card nothing at card level, so the two pickers read as different components.

**Why a3.** The a5 tint of a selected row, `--ds-fill-selected-subtle`, drops the card's `--ds-text-weak` description to 4.43:1 in light, under AA 4.5:1. The a3 wash holds 5.29:1 in light and 7.63:1 in dark, and it reads as a slight wash where a5 reads as a filled block.

**State precedence.**

- Disabled: Radix's gray wash wins, and no selected paint shows.
- Focus: the fill stays, so a selected card never reads as unselected under keyboard focus. The focus ring paints at 4px where the band paints at rest.
- Hover: Radix's border and shadow step, a separate channel from the fill, so a hovered card and a selected one read apart.

**Scope.** Both card pickers hand `variant` to Radix unchanged. The rules are scoped to `.radix-themes`, use no `!important` and add no token.

**Changed from.** No earlier ruling covered these controls. A selected card showed only Radix's own state, which differed between the two pickers.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-23. The card-picker selected state was ruled again and built on 2026-07-26.

- [textless-part-fills](#textless-part-fills) paints the CheckboxCards outline in `--accent-indicator` in place of `--ds-fill-accent`, so the card and its checkbox share one shade.
- [part-fill-edge](#part-fill-edge) and [radio-cards-band-edge](#radio-cards-band-edge) stack a 1px edge on the selected band of each picker, and move the RadioCards band to an inset ring.
- [focus-ring](#focus-ring) replaces Radix's focus ring on these controls with the system accent ring.
- [card-picker-focus-width](#card-picker-focus-width) widens the focus ring of both card pickers to 4px, selected or not.
- [neutral-part-stacks](#neutral-part-stacks) stacks a Radix alpha on the Slider thumb and on the selected SegmentedControl segment.
- [colour-prop-and-high-contrast](#colour-prop-and-high-contrast) removes `soft` from Switch and Slider and carries the contrast fixes to a part given `color` or `highContrast`.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **Choice controls — Switch / Slider / SegmentedControl / CheckboxCards / RadioCards (2026-07-23; the card-picker selected state re-ruled and BUILT 2026-07-26).** All ride the CONTROL size lane. **Switch** (the Progress-style ON track), **Slider** (the range) and **SegmentedControl** (the **neutral** raised tile — documented accurately, NOT a false accent claim) reuse Radix's own accent-aware skins and declare **no `--ds-*` roles**. **A11y upgrade (Slider):** Radix leaves a single-thumb slider's `role="slider"` nameless — the wrap forwards the accessible name to any unnamed thumb (the Separator `aria-orientation` precedent). **The two card pickers share ONE selected treatment, and it IS net-new CSS**. What Radix 3.3 ships: a checked **RadioCards** card gets an accent outline and nothing else; a checked **CheckboxCards** card gets NO card-level treatment at all (only the inner checkbox fills), so at a glance a picked card is indistinguishable from an unpicked one and the two pickers read as different components. `components.css` (`Card pickers · the selected state`) adds the missing paint: a checked card in **either** picker takes a slight **`--ds-fill-accent-weak`** (accent-a3) wash, layered as a background-IMAGE over Radix's own `::before` surface so it composites on top instead of replacing it; **CheckboxCards** additionally takes the 2px **`--ds-fill-accent`** `::after` outline RadioCards gets for free (accent-9 is the exact value `--accent-indicator` resolves to, so both pickers' outlines are the same hex on every brand and both follow the collision shift). **So the card pickers DO declare one `--ds-*` role** — the selected fill — the only choice controls that do; every other role on the card is still Radix's. **Why a3, not the a5 `--ds-fill-selected-subtle` a selected *row* takes:** measured on the rendered plan-picker specimen, compositing page → card surface → tint, the a5 tint drops the card's `--ds-text-weak` description line to **4.43:1** in light mode — under AA 4.5 for body text — while a3 holds **5.29:1** (dark: 7.63:1 vs 5.74:1); a5 also reads as a filled block rather than the slight wash the ruling calls for. **State precedence:** every selector carries a disabled guard (Radix's gray wash wins), each outline rule steps aside for `:focus-visible` — the fill STAYS (a selected card must not read unselected the moment you tab to it) while the keyboard ring is handed back to Radix untouched — and hover is a different channel (border/shadow), so a hovered card and a selected one still read apart. Scoped `.radix-themes`, out-specifying Radix's `:where()`-wrapped rules on source order: **no `!important`, zero net-new tokens**. `variant` passes through on both card pickers. Comparisons: `BOOLEAN_CHOICE` += Switch; `PICK_FROM_SET` += a combined `RadioCards / CheckboxCards` column + SegmentedControl. Each ships an `_internal` behavior play. LITE spines.

### surface-wraps

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-23.

**Card, ClickableCard and ScrollArea are wraps with rules of their own, and Grid, Section, AspectRatio and VisuallyHidden ship as documented re-exports.**

**Card.** Card rides the container lane, where small resolves to step 2 ([standard-dialog](#standard-dialog)). Its variants are ruled in [card-variants](#card-variants).

**ClickableCard.**

- An overlay link around the heading text carries an `::after` that covers the whole card (`.rt-ds-clickable-card` in `components.css`). A click anywhere on the card navigates, with one tab stop and one accessible name, the heading.
- The link is the component that `useLinkComponent()` returns ([link-and-link-provider](#link-and-link-provider)).
- Hover paints `--ds-fill-hover`. Focus draws the accent focus ring on the card box, 2px inside its edge, and the link draws no ring of its own.
- A nested interactive control sits above the overlay with the exported `interactiveLayer`.
- The overlay blocks text selection, so ClickableCard serves navigation only.

**ScrollArea.** The scrollbar rides the control lane, a documented deviation from the container surface around it. ScrollArea's `size` runs from 1 to 3, and Radix's `extractProps` replaces an out-of-range value with the prop's default, `"1"`, so a container-lane `large` would render the thinnest scrollbar.

**Pass-through wraps.** Grid, Section, AspectRatio and VisuallyHidden paint nothing and ride no size lane, so a re-export with documentation is the whole wrap. Section's `size` is a vertical padding scale and reaches Radix untouched.

**Docs.** Each pass-through wrap has a full docs spine, with History, Usage and Props pages. Its Usage page carries worked specimens, a live Tokens spec, a Props reference and a pair of do and do-not specimens. A wrap with no paint is documented by when to choose it, which takes prose and specimens.

**Changed from.** No earlier ruling covered these components.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-23. Corrected on 2026-07-27 within this entry: the true reason for the ScrollArea deviation, and the full docs pages of the four pass-through wraps.

- [card-variants](#card-variants) replaces Radix's `surface`, `classic` and `ghost` card skins with `outlined`, `elevated` and `filled`.
- [focus-ring](#focus-ring) replaces the neutral focus hairline on the ClickableCard box with the accent focus ring, drawn 2px inside the card edge.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **Surfaces & pass-through wraps — Card / ClickableCard / ScrollArea + Grid / Section / AspectRatio / VisuallyHidden (2026-07-23).** **Card** rides the container lane ([standard-dialog](#standard-dialog), small→2), reusing the surface/classic/ghost skins. **ClickableCard** layers the stretched-link pattern on Card: an overlay link wrapping the heading text carries an `::after` covering the whole card (`.rt-ds-clickable-card` in components.css) — a pointer click anywhere navigates, with a SINGLE tab stop and one accessible name (heading, name-from-content); the link routes through `useLinkComponent()` ([link-and-link-provider](#link-and-link-provider)); hover = `--ds-fill-hover`, focus = the neutral focus hairline drawn on the CARD box (the link's own ring suppressed); nested interactives opt above the overlay (the exported `interactiveLayer`); NAMED CONSTRAINT — the overlay eats text selection, so it is navigation-only. **ScrollArea** — its scrollbar rides the CONTROL lane, a **documented deviation** from the container surface it lives on: ScrollArea's `size` range is 1–3, so the container lane's `large→4` is out of range. **The deviation's real reason (corrected 2026-07-27):** an out-of-range enum is NOT dropped — `extractProps` (`@radix-ui/themes/dist/esm/helpers/extract-props.js`) substitutes the prop's own `default`, which for ScrollArea is `"1"`, so a container-lane `large` would silently render the **thinnest** scrollbar, the exact opposite of what it asked for. **Pass-through wraps** (Grid, Section, AspectRatio, VisuallyHidden) ship as documented **re-exports** (nothing to override — pure layout / a11y plumbing, no paint, no size lane; Section's `size` is a vertical-padding scale passed through untouched). **Their docs pages are NOT stubs (corrected 2026-07-27):** all four ship the full spine — History (Decisions + Changelog), Usage, Props — each Usage carrying worked specimens, a live Tokens spec, a Props reference, and a do/don't **pair** — roughly 360 (Grid) to 650 (VisuallyHidden) lines apiece. The pages earn the length because a pass-through wrap's whole documentation value is *when to reach for it* — which is prose and specimens, since there is no paint to document. LITE spines.

### content-typography

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`, `TYPOGRAPHY`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-23.

**Code, Blockquote and DataList reuse the skins of Radix and declare no `--ds-*` roles of their own.**

**Code.** An inline chip on the text size lane. It keeps the accent-tinted `soft` skin of Radix by default. Docs tables set some chips to gray, a documented exception in the story kit.

**Blockquote.** A documented re-export of the Radix quote skin, whose left rule is accent step `a6`, the value `--ds-stroke-accent-weak` also names. Its `size` is scaled to the prose and reaches Radix unchanged, outside the type lane. Its usage cards cross-link Callout.

**DataList.** A compound wrap of the Radix `<dl>` metadata pairs on the control lane, for the details of one entity. Its usage cards cross-link Table.

**Docs.** The token specs read each colour live from the rendered page.

**Changed from.** No earlier ruling covered this.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-23.

- [data-list-overflow](#data-list-overflow) gives DataList one overflow policy for every value in a list.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **Content typography — Code / Blockquote / DataList (2026-07-23).** **Code** — an inline chip riding the TEXT lane, keeping Radix's accent-tinted `soft` skin (the default keeps the tint; comparison tables neutralize their chips to gray, a documented storyKit exception). **Blockquote** — a documented re-export reusing Radix's quote skin (an accent-a6 left rule = `--ds-stroke-accent-weak`); its `size` is prose-scaled, passed through untouched (NOT the type lane); do/don't cross-links Callout. **DataList** — a compound wrap (control lane) of Radix's `<dl>` metadata pairs, for the details of ONE entity (do/don't cross-links Table). All reuse Radix skins (no `--ds-*` roles); token specs read colours live. LITE spines.

### feedback-set

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`, `MOTION`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-23.

**`Progress`, `Spinner`, `Skeleton` and `EmptyState` form the feedback set, and the three loading loops stop under reduced motion.**

**Progress and Spinner.** Both ride the control size lane and reuse Radix's accent-aware skins. `Button`'s `loading` state renders the same spinner.

**Skeleton.** `Skeleton` is a re-export that sizes to its children.

**Reduced motion.** The spinner leaf fade, the indeterminate progress sweep and the skeleton pulse run outside the `--ds-duration` ladder, the [status-dot](#status-dot) precedent, and Radix ships them with no `prefers-reduced-motion` guard, so the `motion.css` clamp never reaches them. One `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block in `components.css` stops all three, and `Progress` also takes `transform: none` so a stopped indeterminate bar stays visible.

**Exception.** The Skeleton rule is `animation: none !important`, the one `!important` in `components.css`. Radix declares its pulse `!important` on a bare `.rt-Skeleton`, so no `.radix-themes` selector can outrank it, and a reduced-motion guarantee for accessibility lies outside the reasoning behind the ban on `!important`.

**EmptyState.** A centred column, capped in width, holds a regular-weight `--ds-icon-neutral` icon, a `Heading` title, a weak `Text` description and a `ButtonGroup` of actions with at most one solid primary ([button-priority](#button-priority)). Its copy states the empty state, such as "No projects yet", and never blames the reader.

**Changed from.** No earlier ruling covered this.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-23. No later ruling amends it.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **Feedback set + EmptyState — Progress / Skeleton / Spinner / EmptyState (2026-07-23).** Progress/Spinner ride the control lane and reuse Radix's accent-aware fill / leaf-ring skins (Button's own `loading` renders the same spinner — no fork); Skeleton is a re-export that sizes to its children. **Ambient-loop reduced-motion:** the spinner leaf fade, the progress indeterminate sweep, and the skeleton pulse are ambient loops OUTSIDE the `--ds-duration` ladder (the StatusDot [status-dot](#status-dot) precedent), which Radix ships with NO `prefers-reduced-motion` guard, so `motion.css`'s clamp never reaches them; a central `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block in components.css silences all three (Progress also pins `transform:none` so a silenced indeterminate bar stays visible). **SANCTIONED `!important` exception (by ruling):** the Skeleton line needs `animation: none !important` because Radix declares its pulse `!important` on a bare `.rt-Skeleton` (not a `:where()` rule), so the no-`!important` cascade mechanism — a `.radix-themes` selector out-specifying Radix's `:where()` — is structurally unable to reach it; overriding a vendor `!important` for a reduced-motion a11y guarantee is the case the no-`!important` ruling's rationale did not contemplate. It is the ONE `!important` in the file, clearly commented, surfaced for ratification. **EmptyState** is a net-new lite composition (no Radix equivalent): a centered, max-width-capped column of a regular-weight `--ds-icon-neutral` icon · a Heading title · a weak Text description · a `ButtonGroup` of actions (buttonOrder, ≤1 solid primary [button-priority](#button-priority)); no blame copy ("No projects yet", never "You haven't…"). LITE spines.

### static-table

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-23.

**Table is a styling wrap for simple, static tables, with three system conventions and no behaviour props.**

**Conventions.**

- Body rows wash on hover with `--ds-fill-hover`. The header never washes and carries no sort affordance, because a header that reads as interactive and is not is a control that misleads.
- Column headers sit at weight 600, the strong step, in place of the 700 of Radix.
- A numeric column takes `numeric`, which stamps `data-numeric`, aligns the column right and sets `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`. Figures align by column, and digits stay in place as values change.

**Not covered.** Sorting, selection, virtualization and column resizing. A data grid belongs to a dedicated grid library.

**Defaults.** The `surface` variant, with cell text on the control size lane. Status specimens use the system Badge with its accent-aware `tone`, never a raw Radix scale.

**Adopters.** The ledger keeps no roster of tabular-figure sites. The roster is `TABULAR_SITES` in `src/components/ui/_tabular-figures.stories.tsx`, and the suite fails when a registered site loses its declaration or a new site ships unregistered.

**Changed from.** No earlier ruling covered this.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-23.

- [ui-polish-ruleset](#ui-polish-ruleset) deleted the hand-kept roster of tabular-figure sites from this ruling and made `TABULAR_SITES` the roster.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **Table — a styling wrap for simple/static tables ONLY (2026-07-23).** A thin compound wrap over Radix's Table with three system conventions and **no behaviour props at all** (no sorting, selection, virtualization, or column resizing — for a data grid, reach for a dedicated grid library): (1) body rows wash on hover with `--ds-fill-hover` (the HEADER never washes and carries no sort affordance — a header that reads interactive but isn't is a control that lies); (2) the column header at weight 600 (the strong ramp step, retuned from Radix's bold/700); (3) numeric columns carry `numeric` → `data-numeric`, which right-aligns them AND carries `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`, so figures line up column-wise and digits don't jitter as values change. **A hand-kept roster in the ledger needs editing on every future adoption, so it is not kept here at all: the adopter list is `TABULAR_SITES` in `src/components/ui/_tabular-figures.stories.tsx`, which fails the suite both when a registered site loses its declaration and when a new one ships unregistered.** Measured before: `$1,240.00` 65.91px vs `$4,010.00` 65.58px at equal character count; after, both exactly 70.98px. The story's play now asserts both the declaration and painted-width parity (drift ≤ 0.05px), so the treatment can't quietly lapse. Surface variant default; cell text on the control lane. **A11y notes:** status specimens use the System Badge (accent-aware `tone`, never a raw Radix scale); Radix's Table.Root wraps content in a viewport with `overflow-x: scroll` UNCONDITIONALLY, so axe's `scrollable-region-focusable` false-fires on a fitting table — scoped off in the stories, with genuine overflow keyboard-access flagged as a component follow-up. LITE spine.

### card-variants

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-23.

**Card exposes three variants that differ by how the card meets the page: `outlined`, `elevated` and `filled`.**

**Why.** Radix's `surface`, `classic` and `ghost` are a generic skin vocabulary shared across components. On a card, `surface` and `classic` differ only by border alpha and a faint drop, so they look the same, and `ghost` removes the border and cancels the padding, so it does not read as a card. The wrap does not expose them.

**Variants.** All three build on Radix's `surface` variant, so radius, padding and size lane never differ between them. Only the boundary changes.

| Variant | Edge | Fill | Shadow |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `outlined`, the default | 1px edge | the translucent panel fill | none |
| `elevated` | 1px edge | the translucent panel fill | `--ds-shadow-2`, the Raised step of [elevation-model](#elevation-model) |
| `filled` | none | `--ds-fill-weak`, a tonal alpha | none |

**Filled.** The fill alone separates a filled card, so a border would encode the same thing twice. `--ds-fill-weak` is an alpha step, so it darkens a light page and lightens a dark one, and the card reads apart in both appearances. An opaque `--ds-bg-*` step separates in one appearance and matches the page in the other. `--ds-fill-hover` is the hover role, and a resting card does not paint it.

**Use.**

- Elevation carries meaning. Reserve `elevated` for a card that floats, dragged or over a busy canvas, because a wall of elevated cards is noise.
- The anatomy is container, media, header, body and footer actions, each optional, in a fixed order.
- A card is not for tabular rows (use Table), a lone call to action (use Button), a single ungrouped block, or decoration. A card that needs an override to remove its border or padding was never a card.
- The `CARD_SURFACES` comparison tells Card, ClickableCard, RadioCards and CheckboxCards apart: a container, a link and two form pickers.

**Gap.** Radix's `Inset`, the flush media slot, is absent from the registry.

**Changed from.** Card reused Radix's `surface`, `classic` and `ghost` skins ([surface-wraps](#surface-wraps)).

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-23. Amended on 2026-07-26 within this entry: the `filled` fill moved from the opaque `--ds-bg-subtle` to the alpha `--ds-fill-weak`, because in dark `filled` and `outlined` painted the same interior. No later ruling amends it.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **Card variants — three that are actually tellable apart (2026-07-23).** Radix's surface and classic cards look exactly the same, and ghost does not read as a card at all. Verified at the source: Radix's `surface | classic | ghost` is a **generic cross-component skin vocabulary** (the same three words appear on Badge, Callout, Select, Switch, Table — Radix's own docs define variants only as "visual variations… used to create visual hierarchies", with no card-specific meaning), and in `card.css` `surface` vs `classic` differ **only** by border alpha (`--gray-a5` ≈12% vs `--gray-a3` ≈6% black) plus a ~5% drop — the same box twice; `ghost` is `--card-border-width: 0` plus negative margins cancelling its own padding, an optical-alignment device, a card with the card removed. **So the wrap does not expose them.** It exposes the industry-standard trio (Material's elevated / filled / outlined; echoed by Chakra, Fluent, MUI, Ant, Web Awesome), which differ by **how the card meets the page** — the axis that actually makes them distinguishable: `outlined` (default — a 1px edge on the translucent panel fill) · `elevated` (that same edge and fill + **the [elevation-model](#elevation-model) Raised step, `--ds-shadow-2`** — reuse of the existing elevation ladder, no new shadow) · `filled` (a **tonal `--ds-fill-weak`** fill with the **edge removed** — the fill is what separates it, so a border would double-encode; dropping it is also what makes the trio readable at a glance). **Amended 2026-07-26 — the original clause named an opaque `--ds-bg-subtle` fill, and it failed this ruling's own test.** Measured from rendered pixels in dark mode, `filled` and `outlined` painted the **identical** interior (`rgb(24,25,27)`, 1.000:1), separated only by whether the edge was drawn — the exact "same box twice" defect this ruling was written to eliminate, reintroduced by its own implementation clause. The fix is the **alpha** step: `--ds-fill-weak` (the existing *component background (normal)* role) darkens a light page and lightens a dark one, so ONE token separates in both appearances, where every opaque `--ds-bg-*` step separates in one and collapses in the other (`--ds-bg-subtle` = 1.026:1 in light; `--ds-bg-sunken` = 1.048:1 in dark). `--ds-fill-hover` (a4) was rejected despite being stronger — it is the hover-state role, and a resting card wearing it is a semantic lie. After: filled-vs-page **1.139 light / 1.186 dark**, filled-vs-outlined **1.158 / 1.106**, invariant across nine accents. Guarded by `_internal/Card variants`, which was falsified against the old token before landing.. All three are built on ONE Radix variant (`surface`), so the BOX — radius, padding, size lane — never drifts between them; only the boundary treatment changes. **Elevation is a meaning, not decoration**: reserve it for a card that genuinely floats — dragged, or over a busy canvas; a wall of elevated cards is noise. Card is promoted to a FULL spine because a Card page's value is its RULES, not its box: anatomy (container · media · header · body · footer-actions — all optional, order fixed), **when NOT to use it** (not tabular rows → Table; not a lone CTA → Button; not a single ungrouped block; never as decoration — "if you'd have to override the border or padding away, it was never a card"), and the new **`CARD_SURFACES` comparison** across Card / ClickableCard / RadioCards / CheckboxCards (a container vs a link vs two form pickers) — the disambiguation nothing previously provided. Known gap surfaced, not closed: Radix's `Inset` (the flush media slot) is absent from the registry.

### modal-dismissal

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`, `ACCESSIBILITY`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-23.

**A modal has exactly one labelled dismissal, judged by what a button does and not by its label.**

**The rule.**

- A Footer button whose whole job is to close the dialog, such as Cancel, Got it, OK, Done or Dismiss, is the dismissal, and the dialog carries no header X.
- A header X is required only when nothing else dismisses the dialog: every Footer button commits, such as Save, Submit or Apply, or the dialog has no Footer.
- `AlertDialog` never has an X. Radix Themes exposes no `Close` part on it, only `Action` and `Cancel`, and it focuses Cancel on open.
- Escape and the scrim always close a modal, and Escape is never the only exit.

**Why.** Two controls with identical behaviour is the configuration to avoid. Showing both is defensible only where their outcomes differ, as when OK records an acknowledgement and the X does not, and this system has no such case. The rule costs no component surface, because Radix ships no X part, and actions stay in `Dialog.Footer`, which applies `buttonOrder` and the one solid primary of [button-priority](#button-priority).

**Research.** A survey of about twenty design systems found:

- Alert, decision and destructive dialogs omit the X almost everywhere, and Radix, React Spectrum and shadcn expose no close part on an alert dialog at all.
- Standard task modals split between systems that show both an X and a Cancel and systems that allow one or the other.
- For an acknowledgement dialog, eight systems omit the X with a stated reason. Atlassian and Primer require it with no reason given, and the ruling records them as dissent.
- For a dialog with no Footer, Carbon, Spectrum and Primer all show the X, which meets the ARIA Authoring Practices call for one visible close control.

**Gap.** No unsaved-changes check on the X, Escape or the scrim, and no forced-action mode that blocks dismissal. Both are recorded gaps.

**Changed from.** The first version of this ruling, on 2026-07-23, made the word Cancel the test: a dialog with a Cancel had no X, and a dialog without one required an X. It misclassified the acknowledgement dialog, so the read-only release notes specimen showed an X beside its Got it button.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-23 and revised 2026-07-26. No later ruling amends it.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **One labelled dismissal per modal — keyed on whether a footer button DISMISSES, not on whether it is spelled "Cancel" (2026-07-23; re-ruled 2026-07-26).** Research across ~20 systems found no universal law, but three clear tiers: **(tier 1, near-unanimous)** a decision/alert/destructive dialog omits the X and the user leaves through a labelled action — stated by Fluent (*"Alert dialogs can only be dismissed by selecting one of the available buttons in the footer"*), Base Web (*"alert modals have no close 'X', nor do they allow for out of bounds dismissal"*), Gestalt (warning/error), SLDS Prompt, USWDS forced-action and Ant's `Modal.confirm`, and enforced structurally by Radix, React Spectrum and shadcn, none of which expose a close part on AlertDialog at all (counter-examples exist and are noted: eBay MIND's confirm and Carbon's danger modal keep an X); **(tier 2, genuinely contested)** the standard task modal splits into an "always both" camp (Carbon, Atlassian, Polaris, Primer, USWDS, Paste, Ant's base `Modal`) and an "either/or, never both" camp (Fluent — *"Don't use the 'X' button in combination with a Close button"*; Spectrum — a dismissable Dialog *"forgoes its ButtonGroup in favor of rendering a close button at the top right of the Dialog"*; Material — the X belongs to full-screen dialogs); **(tier 3)** where both ship, the defensible versions give them **different outcomes** (Carbon: Cancel *"undoes all applied changes"* vs X *"close the modal without submitting any data"*; NN/g argues FOR both, but explicitly as X = close-and-save vs Cancel = abandon, and only where intermediate work exists to save or abandon — it also concedes that *"in some cases, the distinction between cancel and close doesn't matter"*). **THE FIRST RULING WAS WRONG (2026-07-26).** It keyed on the literal word **Cancel** — *"a Dialog whose Footer contains a Cancel carries no header X; a Dialog with NO Cancel requires an X"* — and so mis-classified the **acknowledgement** dialog, whose only footer button is an OK / Got it / Done / Dismiss. Our own specimen for that arm was a read-only "What's new" panel shipping an X **beside** a "Got it": precisely the redundancy the rule exists to eliminate, because "Got it" is a labelled dismissal wearing a different label. Systems with a *named* acknowledgement pattern overwhelmingly omit the X: **SLDS Prompt** is the most explicit (*"Prompts do not have a close (×) button. To dismiss a prompt, the user needs to hit the action button inside of the prompt"*; *"There is no requirement for a close button, as the confirmation button should be used to dismiss the prompt, along with the usual Esc key dismissal"*, with `closeButton: false` baked into the blueprint); **Ant** flips `closable` to **false** for `Modal.info/success/error/warning` while its base `Modal` defaults it to **true**; **Material** permits a lone action *"only if it's an acknowledgement"* and lists a close affordance exclusively in full-screen dialog anatomy, never in the basic dialog's; **Apple** alerts carry no X ever, and a single-button alert gets a *Done*; **Gestalt**'s own single-action acknowledgement example renders no dismiss icon; and **Fluent** groups *Done, Finish, Close, Got it, Dismiss* together as buttons that end a task, then forbids pairing the X with one. The dissent is real and is not manufactured away: **Atlassian** (*"Close button is required (except rare cases—consult a11y team)"*, enforced by its own lint rule) and **Primer** (*"The close button is required and may not be visually hidden"*) apply a blanket accessibility requirement with no acknowledgement carve-out — **recorded as dissent, not as a live alternative**: eight systems omit the X with a stated mechanism, two require it with no reasoning offered, so the evidence settles this rather than leaving it a judgment call; **Polaris** is effectively silent (its Modal doc is deprecated and the replacement API documents no close-button convention); and **NN/g** never addresses the acknowledgement case at all. **Carbon** keeps the X on its named Acknowledgment modal — but Carbon *confirms* the revised rule rather than contradicting it, because there the two controls do different things: OK records the acknowledgement, while the X *"will close the modal without submitting the user's acknowledgement"*. A button that commits a recorded acknowledgement is a COMMIT, not a dismissal. **THE RULING (revised):** a modal gets **exactly one labelled dismissal**, and the test is what a button *does*, not what it is *called*. If any Footer button's whole job is to close — `Cancel`, but equally *Got it*, *OK*, *Done*, *Dismiss* — that button **is** the dismissal and the Dialog carries **no header X**. A header X is **required** only when **nothing** in the dialog dismisses it: every Footer button **commits** (Save, Submit, Apply, or Carbon's recorded acknowledgement), or **there is no Footer at all**. That last arm is the one point of near-unanimity in the whole sweep — Carbon's passive modal (*"It contains no actions for the user to take"*; *"Passive dialogs only contain a close button (X), so that takes focus"*), Spectrum's `isDismissable` Dialog (whose documented example is a footerless status panel), and Primer all put the X there — and it is what satisfies the APG's *"a visible element with role button that closes the dialog, such as a close icon or cancel button"* (the APG treats the two as interchangeable: one is required, and it never asks for more than one). **`AlertDialog` never has an X** — it already cannot: Radix Themes' AlertDialog exposes no `Close` part, only `Action` + `Cancel`, and focuses Cancel on open. Escape and the scrim always close; Escape is never the sole exit. Rationale, sharpened: two controls with **identical** behaviour is the configuration to avoid, and the "both" camp is defensible only where the outcomes genuinely diverge (Carbon's recorded acknowledgement, NN/g's save-vs-abandon) — divergences we neither have nor plan; the rule costs **zero** component surface (Radix ships no X, so "both" is the option that would require adding a `Dialog.CloseIcon` part); and actions already route through `Dialog.Footer`, which wires `buttonOrder` + the one-solid-primary rule ([button-priority](#button-priority)), while an X bypasses that channel with an unlabelled control. **Named deferrals:** no unsaved-changes intercept on X/Escape/scrim, and no forced-action (non-dismissible) mode — both are real gaps, recorded rather than silently missing.

### slider-composition

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-23.

**Slider composes Radix's raw slider primitive under Radix Themes' own slider classes, and adds detents, a paired numeric input and ranges.**

**Architecture.** Radix Themes' `Slider` takes no children, so marks, ARIA per thumb and affixes cannot pass through it. The wrapper composes `Slider.Root`, `Slider.Track`, `Slider.Range` and `Slider.Thumb` from `radix-ui` and gives them `rt-SliderRoot`, `rt-SliderTrack`, `rt-SliderRange`, `rt-SliderThumb`, `rt-r-size-N` and `rt-variant-*`, the precedent `CheckboxVisual` set. The accent fill and the focus ring use the same CSS as the stock slider, with no new token.

**Features.**

- `marks`, an array of detents with ticks and labels, placed with Radix's own `getThumbInBoundsOffset` so the end ticks sit under the thumb centre, up to 500 marks.
- `step={null}`, which snaps to the marks.
- `showInput`, a paired numeric input beside the track and never below it, at `inputPosition` `flank` or `end`. It is absent when `step` is `null`, when the slider is vertical, and above two thumbs.
- `aria-valuetext`, which Radix does not emit.
- A name per thumb, referenced ahead of the field label, so a thumb reads as "Minimum, Price".
- `aria-valuemin` and `aria-valuemax` per thumb, bounded by the neighbouring thumb, as the APG multi-thumb pattern requires.
- `minStepsBetweenThumbs`, documented as blocking: Radix stops the thumb and does not push its neighbour.

`Field` gains `labelId`, because `htmlFor` on a `role="slider"` span names nothing. The `size="1"` thumb has a 30 by 30px pointer target, above the 24px floor, with no added CSS.

**Exception.** The paired input clamps an out-of-range value to the bound and reverts an unparseable one, and announces each assertively ("150 was corrected to 100%"). This diverges from [number-input](#number-input), which rejects and never clamps. A slider's bounds are visible, a drag past the end already yields `max`, and clamping is the common convention for an input paired with a slider. Neither case raises `Field.validation`, which serves standing problems ([date-input](#date-input)). The divergence was recorded on 2026-07-23 as pending the maintainer's ratification, and no later ruling records that ratification.

**Input width.** The box sizes from a hidden stand-in rendered inside its own `TextField.Root`, so it inherits the font, size and letter spacing of the `<input>`, and the width is measured again on resize and once fonts load. The stand-in holds both bounds and one same-length shape per digit, so the box fits the widest value with or without tabular figures, with `1px` of headroom. A character count times `1ch` and canvas `measureText` are rejected, because each under-counts a digit.

**Not covered.** A value tooltip, `dots`, `included={false}`, a vertical slider with an input, generated marks, non-linear scales, and design guidance for three or more thumbs. `minStepsBetweenThumbs` has no effect under `step={null}`, and `inverted` with marks is correct by construction but untested in a browser.

**Changed from.** The Slider wrapped Radix Themes' `Slider`, which takes no children, so it offered no marks, no paired input and no name per thumb.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-23.

- An amendment of 2026-07-26 inside this entry measures the input's width in place of counting characters.
- [colour-prop-and-high-contrast](#colour-prop-and-high-contrast) removes `soft` from the Slider's `variant` type.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **Slider — the primitive + skin-reuse rebuild: detents, a paired numeric input, and a range (2026-07-23).** The slider carries a paired numeric input that both reports the value and lets the user modify it, plus detents and ranges. **The architecture:** Radix Themes' `Slider` accepts **no children**, so marks, per-thumb ARIA and affixes are impossible through it; the wrap therefore composes the **raw `radix-ui` `Slider.Root/Track/Range/Thumb` while wearing Radix Themes' own `rt-SliderRoot/Track/Range/Thumb` + `rt-r-size-N` / `rt-variant-*` classes** — the established `CheckboxVisual` precedent ("the skin is sourced from the same CSS and can never drift"), so the accent-aware fill and the system focus ring come free with zero net-new tokens. **Shipped:** `marks` (array shape — object-keyed marks stringify their keys and can't be honestly typed) with tick + label rendering positioned by Radix's own `getThumbInBoundsOffset` maths (naive `left:%` drifts half a thumb at each end — measured: thumb centre 435.000 vs last tick 434.992 at max, 45.000 vs 45.000 at min), a 500-mark cap; `step={null}` snap-to-marks; an optional **paired numeric input** (`showInput`, `inputPosition` flank|end — beside the track, never below), suppressed when `step===null` / vertical / >2 thumbs; `aria-valuetext` (Radix emits NONE); per-thumb names via hidden name nodes referenced **ahead** of the field label (`aria-labelledby="<nameId> <labelId>"` → "Minimum, Price" — a bare `aria-label` + `aria-labelledby` would lose the distinguisher, since labelledby wins the accname computation); per-thumb `aria-valuemin`/`aria-valuemax` **constrained by neighbours** (the APG multi-thumb requirement Radix violates by reporting the global bounds on every thumb); `minStepsBetweenThumbs` documented as **BLOCKING, not pushing** (Radix returns the previous values rather than pushing the neighbour). `Field` gained a **`labelId`** because `htmlFor` pointed at a `role="slider"` span is a silent no-op (a span is not a labelable element). **Measured, not assumed:** the `size="1"` thumb's effective pointer target is **30×30px** — Radix's `::before` at `3 × thumb-size` DOES receive events despite `z-index:-1` — verified by a real drag grabbing 12.4px below the thumb centre; clears the 24px floor with no CSS. **⚠️ DIVERGENCE FROM [number-input](#number-input), PENDING RATIFICATION BY THE MAINTAINER:** the paired input **CLAMPS** an out-of-range value to the bound (and reverts an unparseable one), each announced assertively ("150 was corrected to 100%"), where [number-input](#number-input) rules that `NumberInput` *rejects and never clamps*. The justification: a slider's bounds are **visible** — the track physically ends, and dragging past the end already yields `max`, so typing past the end should do what dragging does; a bare NumberInput has no visible bound, which is exactly why reject-revert is right there. Clamping is also the near-universal convention for slider-paired inputs. Neither case raises `Field.validation` (that channel is for standing problems, [date-input](#date-input)). **Named deferrals:** value tooltip/bubble (the input IS the readout, and a tooltip belongs only on a slider with no input), `dots`, `included={false}`, vertical+input, auto-generated marks, non-linear scales, and 3+ thumb design guidance; `minStepsBetweenThumbs` is inert under `step={null}`, and `inverted` + marks is correct by construction but not browser-verified. **[Amendment 2026-07-26 — the input's width is MEASURED, not counted.]** The first build sized the box from a character count times `1ch` plus a hand-tuned `0.03em`, because `1ch` is the *proportional* zero and under-counts a `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` digit. That produced zero slack — every case landed at `scrollWidth === clientWidth` — so any font, size or letter-spacing change clipped the value and tripped the regression test rather than degrading. A constant tuned against one font IS the defect; the test only exposed it. The box now sizes from a hidden stand-in rendered INSIDE its own `TextField.Root`, so family / size / letter-spacing reach it by the same inheritance path as the `<input>`; a layout effect writes the measured width and a `ResizeObserver` plus `document.fonts.ready` re-read it on any change. The stand-in carries both bounds AND one same-length all-one-digit shape per digit, because without tabular figures three characters span 14.7px ("111") to 23.4px ("444") and only the widest is a safe bound — correct by construction whether or not tabular figures are in play. Canvas `measureText` was rejected: a 2D context has no `font-variant-numeric`, so it would measure proportional figures and reintroduce the same under-count. One type-INDEPENDENT `+1px` of headroom remains for border-box/pixel-snapping arithmetic; measured slack is 1.0-1.9px across 40 boxes (6 scales x 3 size lanes, plus serif / monospace / 110%-scaled variants and both range positions). Proven by swapping the family to Courier and to Georgia with a letter-spacing retune: the box followed every time, while the OLD formula's budget went negative by 1.75-2.33px on the same change. The `InputFitsItsBound` behaviour play now guards BOTH directions -- clipping and dead space -- and was falsified in both.

### token-row-shape

**Tags.** `DOCUMENTATION`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-26.

**A token row names its token, and the resolved value is a muted footnote after the name.**

**The rule.** The token name leads the row. The value comes after it in muted ink, and the verdict takes a cell of its own and never joins the value. `NoteRow` and a `RenderedRow` with no token stay prose rows, for lengths, keywords and layout facts.

**Why.** A hex identifies nothing. It cannot be searched for, reused in a second component, compared against the token file or checked for drift. It is only evidence that the named token resolved.

**Vendor skins.** A wrap that reuses another component's skin still names a token: the Radix token the skin paints from, such as `--color-panel-solid`, `--accent-a11` or `--gray-a3`. Where the vendor hardcodes a keyword and no token exists, the row states that literal, such as the `white` face of the Radix slider thumb.

**Enforced.** The props of `RenderedRow` in `_storyKit.tsx` are a discriminated union, so a row that passes `swatch` without `token` does not compile. `src/foundations/token-rows.node-check.ts` rejects a hand-typed hex in any row.

**Colour wall.** The Foundations colour wall renders through the shared `TokenRow` shell at a second density, `SWATCH_GRID`, with a 40px specimen chip. It shares one column rhythm with the component tables and carries the same `data-token-row` marker.

**Changed from.** [docs-page-spine](#docs-page-spine) already required values read live from the CSS, but no ruling fixed the shape of a row. Some rows showed a swatch with no token named, and many led with the hex and set the token inside the value.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-26.

- [measured-token-rows](#measured-token-rows) replaces the columns and the primitives: the cells are part, token, value and verdict under a header row, the Radix alias column is gone, `MeasuredRow` reads the value off the element that paints it, and `RoleRow` and `RenderedRow` are legacy. It keeps this ruling's core, that the name outranks the value.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **The token row NAMES its token; the value is the footnote (2026-07-26).** [docs-page-spine](#docs-page-spine) already rules that a token spec is read live from the CSS and never hand-typed, and every table obeys it — zero hand-typed hexes across 82 story files. What was never written down is the row's **shape**, and that gap let 32 files drift: 10 rendered a swatch with **no token named at all** (Kbd's "Text colour · ▪ #1c2024" — a colour with no source), and 21 more led with the hex and buried the token inside it ("▪ #5b5bd6 — = --ds-fill-accent ✓"), where the hex was painted in `--ds-text-link`, taking the emphasis the token name is supposed to own. **The ruling — one canonical row, four columns:** *part · swatch + token (`--ds-*` role, link ink) · Radix alias or verdict · resolved value (muted, right-aligned, last)*. **The name outranks the value** because a hex identifies nothing: it cannot be searched for, reused in a second component, diffed against the token file, or checked for drift — it is only *evidence* that the named token resolved, which is why it is a trailing footnote and why it is muted. The verdict ("=" bound / "≠ (--other)") gets its **own slot**; concatenating it into the value was how the token name ended up inside the value string in the first place. **Which primitive:** `RoleRow` when the component declares a `--ds-*` role (the default — it takes the role and resolves the alias + hex itself); `RenderedRow` when a wrap reuses another component's skin and declares no role of its own, so the value must be read off the rendered element. **Reusing a vendor skin is not a licence for a nameless row** — the answer to "which colour is this?" is then the **Radix** token the skin paints from (`--color-panel-solid`, `--accent-a11`, `--gray-a3`), or, where the vendor hardcodes a keyword and there is genuinely no token (Radix's slider thumb face is `background-color: white`), that literal, stated. `NoteRow` and a tokenless `RenderedRow` stay prose rows for lengths, keywords and layout facts. **Enforced two ways, because each catches what the other cannot.** (1) `RenderedRow`'s props are a **discriminated union**: a row that passes `swatch` without `token` does not compile (`_storyKit.tsx`) — a rule you cannot type wrong beats a rule you are told about later. (2) `src/foundations/token-rows.node-check.ts` parses every story with the TypeScript compiler API — **not** a line regex, which cannot tell `` `${v.panel} — ${v.panelToken}` `` (correct: the name arrives through a variable) from a literal, and false-fires on it — and asserts: **R1** every user-facing story has a token surface at all (floor: 0 violations), **R2** swatch implies token (still reachable past the type for `swatch={undefined}`), **R3** a colour row's `value` carries no `--` literal and no `=`/`≠`/`✓`, **R4** no hand-typed hex in a row ([docs-page-spine](#docs-page-spine) at row level). (3) `assertTokenRowShape` (`foundations/_assert.ts`, called from a `play` — the reference call is Button's Anatomy) closes the gap **neither static check can reach: that the named token is what actually paints.** It measures each `[data-token-row="colour"]` as rendered — name present, name before value, value in `--ds-text-weak` and not `--ds-text-link` — and sets nothing it then reads back. **Also folded:** the Foundations colour wall was hand-reimplementing the same four columns; it now renders through the shared `TokenRow` shell at a second named density (`SWATCH_GRID` — a 40px specimen chip instead of a 14px swatch, since a chip dropped into a 1.2fr track floats in dead space), so both surfaces carry the `data-token-row` marker the runtime check keys on and the column rhythm has one definition. R3's 76 remaining hits across 18 files are the conversion work-list, deliberately left failing.

### measured-token-rows

**Tags.** `DOCUMENTATION`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-28.

**A token row measures the element that paints the part, and prints a verdict that can disagree with the token it claims.**

**The four cells.** A measured table carries a header row, and the Radix alias is prose rather than a column.

| Cell | Holds |
|---|---|
| Part | What is painted, in the component's own vocabulary |
| Token | The rule the row claims, the one searchable and reusable cell |
| Value | The property measured on the rendered element, never on a probe the story painted |
| Verdict | Whether that measurement equals what the claimed token resolves to on its own |

**When it cannot measure.** The row prints "not measured" with the reason, such as no element that matches, no rule that declares the property for that state, or an animation with no frame named. It never resolves its token in place of a measurement.

**Hard cases.**

- A portaled surface is force-mounted into the table's hidden measurement host, where it computes full styles and paints nothing.
- A pseudo-state such as `:hover` or `:focus-visible` reads the declaration that the component's own matched stylesheet rule paints for that state, with media and supports conditions honoured.
- An animated value names a frame. The primitive pauses that element's animation there, reads it and restores the clock.

**Mechanism.** `MeasuredRow` takes `select`, `prop` and the claimed token, and computes the value, the swatch and the verdict itself. Its `value`, `swatch` and `verdict` props are typed as unsatisfiable strings, so a row that passes one fails to compile with the fix in the message, and `src/foundations/token-rows.node-check.ts` and `assertMeasuredRows` in `src/foundations/_assert.ts` reject a row that reads its answer from the node it painted.

**Why.** A row that painted a probe with its token and read the probe back agreed by construction, which proved that the token layer resolves and nothing about the component. A row that quietly resolves a token while it looks like evidence is worse than a row that admits its limit.

**Changed from.** [docs-page-spine](#docs-page-spine) required a live read and [token-row-shape](#token-row-shape) set the columns, but a row could resolve the very token it named, the Radix alias was a peer column, and `RoleRow` and `RenderedRow` were the two sanctioned primitives. This ruling replaces the row shape of [token-row-shape](#token-row-shape), keeps its core that the name outranks the value, and extends [docs-page-spine](#docs-page-spine).

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-28.

- [modal-measurement-lifecycle](#modal-measurement-lifecycle) measures a modal surface by mounting it, reading it and unmounting it, and replaces the check that the measured node is connected when the assertion runs with a check that it was connected at the read.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **The token row MEASURES the component; it may not resolve the token it claims (2026-07-28).** **What the table is for:** a reader uses it as a point of reference *and* as the evidence that the system is operating by its own rules. Both jobs need one property — the row must be able to **disagree** with the component. It could not. [docs-page-spine](#docs-page-spine) rules that the spec is read live from the CSS and never hand-typed, and [token-row-shape](#token-row-shape) ruled the row's column order, but neither stopped a row from *resolving the very token it names*: the story painted a hidden probe with `var(--ds-fill-accent)`, read that probe back, and printed the hex. That agrees by construction. It proves the token layer resolves, which nobody doubted, and proves nothing about what the component paints. Two components shipped the extreme version — HoverCard and Popover each painted a span `--color-panel-solid` and read that same span back under the label "Panel background". **The stricter rule: read the value off the ELEMENT THAT PAINTS IT, and print the verdict.** **The four cells, and what each asserts:** *part* — what is painted, named in the component's own vocabulary; *token* — the rule being claimed, and the only searchable, reusable, drift-checkable thing in the row; *value* — the property as measured off the rendered element, never a probe the story painted; *verdict* — whether that measurement equals what the claimed token independently resolves to. Only the verdict is new, and it is the whole point: it is the cell that can say *no*. **The Radix alias is demoted** from a peer column to prose. It was explanatory, not evidential, and as a column it carried **nine different meanings** across the tree — Radix alias, a bare `=`, a component name, a CSS class, a WCAG criterion number, free prose, an em-dash placeholder — with **no header on any table** saying which. Measured tables now carry a header row. **What a row does when it cannot measure:** it says so — *"not measured · <reason>"* — and never falls back to resolving its token. The story cannot request that shape; it is what a failed measurement produces (no element matched the selector; no rule declares that property for that state; an animation is running and no frame was named). **A row that quietly resolves a token while looking like evidence is worse than a row that admits its limit.** **The hard cases, solved rather than skipped** — they are exactly the rows nobody had ever verified. A *portaled* surface (menu, popover panel) is `forceMount`ed and `container`-portaled into the row table's own `visibility: hidden` measurement host, so it exists, computes full styles, paints nothing, holds no focus and is skipped by axe. A *pseudo-state* value (`:hover`, `:focus-visible`) cannot be forced from a render effect — no script can synthesise a real hover — so the row reads the declaration the component's **own matched stylesheet rule** will paint for that state (media/supports conditions honoured, so a hover fill inside `@media (hover: hover)` is reported honestly) and resolves it on the element; the row still compares two independently-sourced expressions and can still disagree. An *animated* value has no resting state, so a row must name a **frame**: the primitive pauses that element's own animation there, reads, and restores the clock — and a row with no frame named stays unproven rather than printing a number that is true for a few milliseconds. **The architecture is the enforcement.** `MeasuredRow` takes no `value`, `swatch` or `verdict`; a story supplies *which element* (`select`) and *which property* (`prop`) plus the token it claims, and the primitive does the reading, the independent resolution, the comparison and all four cells. The three forbidden props are *declared* as unsatisfiable literal string types rather than merely omitted, so the compiler prints the fix: passing `value="#fcfcfd"` fails with *‘Type "#fcfcfd" is not assignable to type "MEASURED ROWS READ THE VALUE — drop `value`, and give `select` + `prop` instead"’* (the [token-row-shape](#token-row-shape) idiom that turned 52 bad rows into 52 compile errors). **Three layers, each catching what the others cannot.** (1) The **type** makes a handed-in value unrepresentable. (2) `src/foundations/token-rows.node-check.ts` parses every story with the TypeScript compiler API and asserts **R1** the file documents its tokens at all (floor: zero — and the old `/spec/i` title test was widened to a word-bounded `/\b(tokens?|roles?|spec)\b/i`, because unbounded it matched “Specimen” and R1 had therefore never been able to fire), **R2** a token row is a `MeasuredRow` (`RoleRow`/`RenderedRow` take the value from the story), **R3** no row is handed `value`/`swatch`/`verdict`, **R4** no inline `style` inside a measurement root paints a token a row in that same root claims — the static half of “a row must not resolve the token it claims” — and **R5** no hand-typed hex in a row ([docs-page-spine](#docs-page-spine) at row level). (3) `assertMeasuredRows` (`foundations/_assert.ts`, called from a `play`) closes what no static check can reach: that the row actually measured something. It reads the evidence each row records — the measured node is real and connected, is not a probe, carries **no inline paint** for the property read, the claim resolved somewhere else, and the two agree — and **the specific defect it exists to kill is `probeNode === measuredNode`**, the row that reads its answer off the node it asked the question of. Every rule was proven to fail against real shipping code, not a fixture: R1/R4/R5 and the runtime circular, inline-paint and false-claim checks each fired with their message captured. **Supersedes [token-row-shape](#token-row-shape)** where [token-row-shape](#token-row-shape) blessed the current shape — the four columns are now *part · token · value · verdict* with a header, the Radix-alias column is gone, and `RoleRow`/`RenderedRow` are legacy rather than the two sanctioned primitives. [token-row-shape](#token-row-shape)'s surviving core is unchanged and re-affirmed: **the name outranks the value**, because a hex identifies nothing. **Extends [docs-page-spine](#docs-page-spine)** rather than replacing it: read-it-live is still the floor; measure-the-painting-element is the ceiling. **Landed:** the primitive, the guard, the runtime assertion, and four converted components covering all four hard cases — Popover and HoverCard (portaled), Collapsible (`:hover` + `:focus-visible`), Skeleton (animated endpoints). R2/R3 are left **failing** on the remaining **368 rows across 78 files**, because the list of unverified rows is more useful checked in than deleted. The first converted table found a live doc-lie on its first render: Collapsible's trigger label claimed `--ds-text-strong` and measured `#60646c`, the component having moved to `--ds-text-weak` — a mismatch the resolving row could not have seen.

### disabled-label-ink

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`, `ACCESSIBILITY`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-28.

**A natively disabled control dims its label, and a soft-disabled control keeps its label at full strength.**

**Why.** A natively `disabled` control is inert: it leaves the accessibility tree, takes no hover or focus and offers no reason, so its name dims with it. A soft-disabled control stays focusable so its reason stays perceivable ([disabled-reason](#disabled-reason)), and a reason such as "Only workspace owners can change this" needs a readable name beside it.

**Measured.** `--ds-text-disabled` is exempt from the contrast floor and reads 1.91:1 in light and 3.01:1 in dark. A soft-disabled label keeps `--ds-text-strong`, at 15.98:1 in light and 16.25:1 in dark, the same as the enabled state.

**Rule.** The field label, the group label and the group item label in `src/tokens/components.css` dim on `:disabled` only, and a soft-disabled control never sets `:disabled`. The rule keys on the pseudo-class and not on `aria-disabled`, because Tokenizer and PowerSearch mark their surface `aria-disabled` in both states.

**Groups.**

- A group name dims only when every control in it is `:disabled`, so a soft-disabled member keeps the name strong. A soft-disabled `DateTimeInput` keeps "Appointment" readable, and the same composite hard-disabled dims its name.
- One natively disabled item in a CheckboxGroup or RadioGroup dims its own label and supporting line, and nothing else.
- One soft-disabled item dims nothing: its title stays strong and its description stays weak, the pair a live option shows.

**Unchanged.** A soft-disabled control still reads as unavailable through the disabled skin of [disabled-reason](#disabled-reason), with its `not-allowed` cursor, `aria-disabled`, glyph and reason tooltip. Only the label differs.

**Changed from.** No earlier ruling covered the label. [disabled-reason](#disabled-reason) ruled how a soft-disabled control is wired and that its chrome reuses the disabled skin, and this ruling extends it.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-28. No later ruling amends it.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **Native `disabled` dims the label; soft-disable does not (2026-07-28).** The ruling: a soft-disabled label is not dimmed. **The two states are not the same thing, and the label is where the difference has to show.** A natively-`disabled` control is simply inert — it is out of the accessibility tree, takes no hover and no focus, and offers no explanation; nothing about it is there to be read, so its **name goes off with it**. A soft-disabled control is the opposite case by construction: `aria-disabled` + `readOnly` and never native `disabled`, specifically so the control stays focusable and its **reason stays perceivable** ([disabled-reason](#disabled-reason), the soft-disable-with-reason ruling — the tooltip, the persistent hidden reason node, the `aria-describedby` that points at it). It is chosen when the user must be able to find out *why* the control is off. Dimming its name defeats the pattern at exactly the moment it is meant to work: the reason says "Only workspace owners can change this," and the word identifying **which** thing they cannot change is the faintest ink on the field. **Measured, both appearances:** the disabled role is `--ds-text-disabled`, deliberately low-contrast and one of only two roles exempt from the contrast floor — **1.91:1** in light (`#b7b9c4` on `#fcfcfd`) and **3.01:1** in dark (`#5a6169` on `#111113`). That is enough to read *"this is off"* and not enough to read a name you are being asked to reason about, which is the whole argument: the exemption is legitimate for an inert control and illegitimate for one that is explaining itself. A soft-disabled label therefore holds `--ds-text-strong` — **15.98:1** light, **16.25:1** dark, identical to the enabled state. **Nothing else about soft-disable moves.** The control itself still reads as unavailable (Radix folds `:read-only` into its own disabled skin, per [disabled-reason](#disabled-reason) — that dimming is untouched), the `not-allowed` cursor stays, `aria-disabled` stays, the glyph and the reason tooltip stay. Only the label changes. **The rule is one selector, three places, and the split falls out of the DOM rather than needing a carve-out** (`tokens/components.css`, the Field-label block): the field label, the group label and the group-item label all match `:disabled` **only**, and a soft-disabled control never sets `:disabled`. Verified across all fifteen controls that ride the shared Field shell — every one puts a real `:disabled` inside its `Field.Root` when hard-disabled, and none does when soft-disabled. **Keying on the pseudo-class rather than the attribute is what makes that clean:** Tokenizer and PowerSearch mark their own surface `aria-disabled` in **both** states (deliberately — it lets AT treat the dimmed chip text as inactive-component text), so a rule that read the attribute could not tell their two states apart at all. **The group cases follow the same logic.** A group's name dims only when **every** control in it is `:disabled`, so a soft-disabled member still counts as live and the name stays strong: a `DateTimeInput` soft-disabled with a reason keeps "Appointment" readable while both sub-fields read as unavailable; the same composite hard-disabled dims its name, correctly, because nothing in it is reachable and nothing explains why. One natively-disabled **item** in a CheckboxGroup/RadioGroup dims that item's label (and its supporting line, which travels with it) and nothing else; one soft-disabled item dims **nothing** — its title stays strong and its description stays weak, the same pair a live option shows. **Extends [disabled-reason](#disabled-reason)** rather than amending it: [disabled-reason](#disabled-reason) ruled how a soft-disabled control is wired and that its *chrome* reuses the disabled skin; this rules that the *label is not part of that skin*. **How it was verified:** the label colour rasterised through a 1×1 sRGB canvas (the `_assert.ts` method — `getComputedStyle` returns `color(display-p3 …)` on a wide-gamut display) and composited over the real ancestor background, for enabled / native-disabled / soft-disabled / group-soft-disabled, in both appearances, on all fifteen controls. The natively-disabled CheckboxGroup specimen renders **byte-identical** before and after. **Both halves are now guarded** in `_internal/Field`: the soft story asserts the label is `--ds-text-strong` and *not* the disabled ink, the native story asserts it *is* — each read off the rendered label and compared against the token resolved in the same tree, never a value the story painted. The guard was proven able to fail: putting `[aria-disabled="true"]` into the selector fires it in both appearance lanes.

### modal-measurement-lifecycle

**Tags.** `DOCUMENTATION`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-28.

**A token row on a modal surface reads a transient instance that mounts, measures and unmounts, and the row records whether its node was connected at the moment of the read.**

**Why.** Radix Themes hardcodes `modal: true` on `Dialog.Root` and `AlertDialog.Root`, so a mounted modal locks page scroll and hides most body children from assistive technology. A modal surface cannot stay mounted on a docs page, so [measured-token-rows](#measured-token-rows) could not reach twelve rows.

**Lifecycle.** `MeasuredSpec transient` mounts the instance, lets every row beneath it read, and unmounts it.

- Barrier: the host unmounts only after every joined row releases, with four frames of grace for a late row and a 4s cap so a row that never releases cannot leave the page locked.
- Annex: a body child that appears during the cycle, such as a portaled modal Content, joins the measurement scope and stays hidden before the browser paints.
- Re-run: the cycle restarts on every appearance and accent change, so the values resolve again.

**Connectivity.** A row stamps `connectedAtRead` from `isConnected` inside `measure()`, and `assertMeasuredRows` checks that stamp in place of `node.isConnected` at assert time. A node built in a detached fragment still fails, and no story prop can set the stamp.

**Smaller rules.**

- A row waits for a finite animation to end, such as the enter transition of a modal panel, and refuses only an endless one.
- A flyout that a component opens from its own trigger is measured through `OpenedByClick`, which clicks that real trigger inside the measurement host.
- `awaitMeasuredRows` waits for any mount cycle to close and, given the row count a story declares, for the table to exist. On timeout it names the frames waited and the rows still silent.

**Rejected.** `Dialog.Root modal={false}`. It needs the raw primitive in place of the System `Dialog.Root`, and MobileNav, Lightbox and the AppShell drawer build their own `Dialog.Root` and expose no `modal`.

**Changed from.** Twelve rows on modal and flyout surfaces could not be measured, and `assertMeasuredRows` asked whether a node was connected when the assertion ran. [measured-token-rows](#measured-token-rows) stands except for that clause, which this ruling supersedes.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-28. No later ruling amends it.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **A modal surface is measured by mounting it, reading it, and taking it down again; the connectivity check changes tense with it (2026-07-28).** [measured-token-rows](#measured-token-rows) rules that a token row reads the value off the element that paints it. Twelve rows could not obey it, and all twelve failed on the same thing: **the surface cannot be left mounted.** Radix Themes hardcodes `modal: true` on `Dialog.Root` and `AlertDialog.Root` *after* the prop spread (`Root = (p) => createElement(Primitive.Root, {...p, modal: true})`, and `DialogRootProps` omits `modal` from the type outright), so no caller can opt out; a mounted modal puts `data-scroll-locked` on `<body>` and `aria-hidden` on **9 of 12** body children. Measured on the Dialog docs page with the panel force-mounted, a real 600px wheel moved `scrollTop` **0 → 0** — the page could not be scrolled at all. **The lifecycle: `MeasuredSpec transient` — mount · measure · unmount.** The instance goes up, every row beneath it reads, and it comes down; the lock exists for the few frames of the reading. Three parts make that safe. **(1) A barrier.** Rows `join()` in their layout effect and release when they have recorded evidence; children's effects run before the parent's, so by the time the host's own effect runs the participant count is final, and it will not unmount until every joined row has released (plus four frames of grace for a row rendered behind a conditional, and a 4s hard cap so a row that never releases cannot leave the page locked). Unmounting early is worse than not measuring: the rows would read a torn-down tree and print it as a fact about the component. **(2) An annex.** A modal Content portals to `document.body`, not into its React parent, so it lands outside the measurement host; Radix's portal is `asChild`, so the node that lands there *is* the overlay rather than a wrapper around it. Every body child that appears while the instance is mounted is therefore taken into the measurement scope (the root itself is matched, not only its descendants) and hidden. Radix's portal primitive renders null on its first pass and opens the portal from its own layout effect — a commit later than the host's — so the hiding is done by a body watcher whose callback is a microtask, which still lands before the browser paints. Sampled in the pre-paint animation frame, every portaled surface reads `visibility: hidden`: the reader never sees a flash. **(3) A re-run.** The cycle restarts on every appearance/accent flip, so a transient table re-resolves like every other one (Dialog panel `#ffffff` → `#18191b` on a live flip, with the page unlocked again afterwards). **The connectivity check changes tense, and does not weaken.** `assertMeasuredRows` asked `node.isConnected` — *is it in the document now* — which is the wrong question for a surface that is torn down on purpose: it would reject every honest modal row. The row now stamps `connectedAtRead` inside `measure()`, from `isConnected`, at the instant of the read, and the assert checks that instead. A node built in a detached fragment reads `false` there and is still rejected; there is no prop a story can pass to set it.
