Proven in the Dialog play, which takes the kit's own evidence, points it at a never-rendered element and captures the refusal, then shows the same evidence with the stamp intact being accepted. **Two smaller rules fall out.** An *enter transition* is not an animation with no resting value: a modal panel plays one on mount, and for its ~200ms the element is 'animated' even though the surface colour being read is a plain resting declaration the transition never touches. A row now waits out a **finite** animation and refuses only an endless one — the pulse/sweep rule is unchanged. And a *flyout* is not a prop: a collapsed rail's panel and a nav menu's panel are opened by a trigger the component owns, so `OpenedByClick` clicks that real control inside the measurement host rather than a story rebuilding the panel's markup and measuring itself. **The waiting lives in one place, and is bounded.** `awaitMeasuredRows` now also waits for any mount cycle to close (so a play cannot assert on scrolling, focus or 'nothing is portaled' against a page mid-measurement) and, given the row count a story declares, waits for the table to *exist* — a table gated on something asynchronous has no rows at the instant the story renders, and a check that only asks 'does every row I can see have evidence?' is trivially satisfied by an empty one. On timeout it names the frames waited and the rows still silent, so it fails loudly instead of hanging. Thirteen plays that hand-rolled a copy of that poll now call it; Calendar, which called the synchronous form with no wait at all, was failing in both appearance lanes and is fixed by the same move. **Landed:** the twelve rows are measured — Dialog panel/elevation/scrim, MobileNav ×3, Lightbox ×2, AppShell drawer scrim, SideNav flyout, TopNav menu panel, CommandPalette selected row (a picker seats its cursor on the preselected row, where the neutral highlight wins, so the selected tint is read after one real ArrowDown). Every converted page was checked with a real 600px wheel: `scrollTop` **0 → 600** with `data-scroll-locked` absent and **zero** aria-hidden body children. **The cheaper route was evaluated and rejected:** `Dialog.Root modal={false}` would need the raw dialog primitive in place of the System `Dialog.Root`, which measures a hand-assembled stand-in rather than the component being documented — and it is unavailable outright for MobileNav, Lightbox and the AppShell drawer, which construct their own `Dialog.Root` internally and expose no `modal`. **Extends [measured-token-rows](#measured-token-rows)**; supersedes only its clause that the measured node must be connected when the assertion runs.

### motion-retiming

**Tags.** `MOTION`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-28.

**Surfaces enter faster than they exit, and a closing surface leaves on the standard curve.**

**What you see.** A surface answers intent promptly and leaves at a readable pace. Token values do not change, only the roles they serve.

**Bindings.**

| Tier | Selector | In | Out |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Popper | `.rt-PopperContent` | `--ds-duration-overlay` (150ms) with `--ds-ease-entry` | `--ds-duration-emphasis` (260ms) with `--ds-ease-standard` |
| Modal | `.rt-BaseDialogContent` and `.rt-BaseDialogOverlay` | `--ds-duration-moderate` (180ms) with `--ds-ease-entry` | `--ds-duration-expressive` (320ms) with `--ds-ease-standard` |
| Tooltip | `.rt-TooltipContent` | `--ds-duration-fast` (120ms) with `--ds-ease-entry` | `--ds-duration-moderate` (180ms) with `--ds-ease-standard` |

The modal scrim stays linear. `--ds-duration-overlay` is the popper entry step ([overlay-entry-duration](#overlay-entry-duration)). The tooltip carries per-side `animation-name` rules, because Radix ships no animation name on tooltip content and a bare duration had no effect.

**Exit curve.** A closing surface runs `--ds-ease-standard`, not `--ds-ease-exit`, because an accelerating exit read as bailing and the standard curve reads as a deliberate departure. `--ds-ease-exit` serves only dismissal gestures the user makes, such as the toast swipe-out and snap-back.

**Applies to.** The shared bindings above and the nav surfaces: the `SideNav` flyout, the `TopNav` menus and the `MobileNav` drawer. The comments in `motion.css` are the operational record, and section 7 of `docs/GUIDELINES.md` mirrors them.

**Changed from.** Exits ran shorter than entrances on `--ds-ease-exit`, the accelerate-out doctrine of [motion-duration-ladder](#motion-duration-ladder). The popper tier ran moderate in and fast out, the modal tier emphasis in and fast out, and [collapsible-and-accordion](#collapsible-and-accordion) and [toast-feedback-tier](#toast-feedback-tier) timed their exits the same way. Each of those rulings carries an update note.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-28.

- [select-anchoring](#select-anchoring) excludes the `Select` listbox from the popper tier, so it opens and closes with no motion.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **Motion retiming — fast in, slow out; standard-curve departures (2026-07-28).** Records the ruled reversal of the shared motion bindings: entrances are QUICKER than their exits — a surface answers intent promptly, then leaves readably rather than fleeing. The shared bindings now read: **popper tier** (`.rt-PopperContent`) in `--ds-duration-overlay` (150ms, [overlay-entry-duration](#overlay-entry-duration)) + `--ds-ease-entry`, out `--ds-duration-emphasis` (260ms) + `--ds-ease-standard`; **modal tier** (`.rt-BaseDialogContent`/`Overlay`) in `--ds-duration-moderate` (180ms) + entry (scrim stays linear), out `--ds-duration-expressive` (320ms) + standard; **tooltip** its own pair — in `--ds-duration-fast` (120ms), out `--ds-duration-moderate` (180ms) — via per-side `animation-name` rules (Radix ships no animation-name on tooltip content, so a bare duration was dead CSS; the named keyframes make the tier real). **The closed-state curve is `--ds-ease-standard`, not `--ds-ease-exit`** — accelerate-out read as bailing; standard-out reads as a deliberate departure. `--ds-ease-exit` is retained ONLY for user-initiated dismissal gestures (toast swipe-out / snap-back and kin). Token VALUES are unchanged; the intent roles were re-assigned (`motion.css` comments are the operational truth, GUIDELINES §7 mirrors them). Supersedes the timing claims inside [motion-duration-ladder](#motion-duration-ladder) (the "accelerate-out exits" doctrine), [collapsible-and-accordion](#collapsible-and-accordion) (the collapse exit), and [toast-feedback-tier](#toast-feedback-tier) (toast enter/exit) — each carries its own update note. The nav surfaces (SideNav flyout, TopNav menus, MobileNav drawer) ride this ladder too.

### chat-family

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-29.

**The chat set ships as seven components, with the bubble part of `ChatMessage` and two sub-parts documented in their host.**

**Components.**

| Component | Tier |
|---|---|
| `ChatLayout` | Full |
| `ChatMessageList` | Full |
| `ChatMessage` | Full |
| `ChatToolCalls` | Full |
| `ChatComposer` | Full |
| `ChatMessageMetadata` | Lite |
| `ChatSystemMessage` | Lite |

`ChatMessageList` is an entry of its own, because it owns the labelled log region, the streaming busy state and the context its siblings read. The two lite entries are single-purpose presentational rows, where a full page would pad rather than teach.

**Bubble.** The bubble is set through the `variant` and `group` props of `ChatMessage` and ships no component of its own, because a bubble with no message around it has no meaning.

**Sub-parts.** `ChatLayoutScrollButton` and `ChatSendButton` have no registry entry and no story page, and each is named in the registry entry of its host. The reference's other two helpers are not named, because the composer's input is part of the field shell and the attachments drawer is deferred.

**Category.** Chat sits between Action and Choice in the category map and in the sort order.

**Tokens.** The family adds no design token. Its one custom property is a component-local input, not a role.

**Changed from.** No earlier ruling covered this. The reference shipped the bubble as a separate component, because its message frame rendered none.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-29. No later ruling amends it.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **The chat family — seven entries, a folded bubble, and sub-parts documented in their host (2026-07-29).** The chat set ships as **seven** components. `ChatMessageList` owns load-bearing behaviour — the labelled log region, the streaming busy state, and the context its siblings read — so it is an entry, not an implementation detail. The **bubble folds INTO `ChatMessage`** as `variant`/`group` props rather than shipping as its own component: a bubble with no message around it has no meaning, and the reference's separate bubble existed only because its message frame rendered none. **Tiers:** `ChatMessageMetadata` and `ChatSystemMessage` ship **lite** — single-purpose presentational rows, where a full spine would pad rather than teach. The other five are full. **Four helper exports become internal sub-parts** with no entries and no story pages, each named in its host's registry note — the nav-family precedent, not the first-class-entry-without-a-page precedent. Only the **two that actually ship** are named (`ChatLayoutScrollButton`, `ChatSendButton`); the composer's input folds into the field shell and the attachments drawer is deferred, so naming either would document something that does not exist. Category **Chat** is inserted between Action and Choice in both the category map and the sort literal, whose key AND member order are asserted against each other. Registry closes at **96 ported / 0 planned / 3 out-of-scope**. **Zero net-new design tokens**, so no K entry: the one custom property minted is a component-local input (the Item block-padding shape), not a role.

### chat-log-scroller

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`, `ACCESSIBILITY`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-29.

**`ChatMessageList` puts the log role, the accessible name, the tab stop and the busy state on the one node that scrolls.**

**What you see.** `ChatMessageList` renders the system scroll area and passes `role="log"`, `aria-label`, `tabIndex={0}` and `aria-busy` to its viewport. The vendor wrapper sends rest props to the viewport and `className` and `style` to the root, so a style for the viewport needs a descendant selector.

**Rejected.** A focusable log that wraps a separate scroller, which yields a region that announces but cannot move and a scroller that moves but is not announced.

**Name.** The `label` prop is required in the type, and a development warning fires when it is empty, because a focusable region with no name fails WCAG 4.1.2.

**Announcements.**

- `role="log"` carries an implicit polite live region, and that is the announcement mechanism. The imperative announce hook serves messages with no place in the DOM.
- `isStreaming` sets `aria-busy`, so assistive technology announces the transcript once on release and does not read it again on every token.
- An assistant turn that streams with no content yet renders a `Spinner` as its body, so the answer has a place to appear and the transcript does not shift when it lands.

**Focus outline.** The browser's own focus outline on the viewport is dropped, because it painted a second ring one pixel outside the system ring, in a colour no theme can reach.

**Changed from.** A stock scroll area had no tab stop, role or name, and no earlier ruling covered a chat log.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-29.

- [scroll-area-keyboard-stop](#scroll-area-keyboard-stop) gives every text-only ScrollArea the tab stop, the role and the name check by default.
- [focus-ring](#focus-ring) drops the browser focus outline on every focusable ScrollArea viewport, where only the chat log dropped it before.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **One node is the scroller and the log (2026-07-29).** `ChatMessageList` renders the system scroll area and stamps `role="log"`, the accessible name, the tab stop and `aria-busy` onto it — all on the single scrolling node. This is possible because the vendor wrap forwards its ref and spreads rest props onto the **viewport** while routing `className`/`style` to the root, verified in its source; the consequence is that the viewport cannot be styled through `className` and needs a descendant selector. The alternative — a separate focusable log wrapping a scroller — produces a region that announces but cannot move, and a scroller that moves but is not announced. **The accessible name is REQUIRED, not optional:** the region is focusable, and a focusable region without a name is a 4.1.2 failure, so the type demands it and a dev warning fires when it is empty. `role="log"` already carries an implicit polite live region — that IS the announcement mechanism, and the imperative announce hook is for messages with no home in the DOM, not for this. **Streaming sets `aria-busy`** so the transcript is announced once on release instead of re-read on every token; the sighted-reader half of that gap closes with reuse rather than invention — an assistant turn that is streaming with no content yet renders a spinner as its body, so the answer has a place to appear instead of shifting the transcript when it lands. **Giving the viewport a tab stop surfaced a latent defect:** the browser's own focus outline painted a second ring one pixel outside ours, in a colour no theme can reach. A stock scroll area has no tab stop, so nothing had ever needed to suppress it.

### chat-bubble

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`, `COLOUR`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-29.

**The bubble is a property of `ChatMessage`: the person's turn is filled and aligned to one side, the assistant's turn is ghost and unboxed, and the filled skin paints `--ds-fill-accent-weak`.**

**Why.** Shape and side carry authorship, where a tint on both sides carries none. The asymmetry survives a narrow column in which side alignment alone collapses, and the unboxed answer keeps its width.

**Measured.** Swept across 27 accents in both appearances, the accent-weak fill holds body text at 11.86:1 or better and small print at 4.73:1 or better. The next step up fails small print on 25 of the 54 combinations, at 3.78:1 worst.

**Width.** The bubble clamps at `min(max(80%, 280px), 100%)` and declares `box-sizing: border-box`. Without it a filled bubble measured 304px in a 320px column, because the substrate ships no universal reset.

**Name.** A message takes the sender's name when one renders, and an overridable sentence otherwise. It never takes the raw sender value, which would put an API token in the accessibility tree.

**Changed from.** No earlier ruling covered this.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-29. No later ruling amends it.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **The bubble is a property of the message, and its fill was chosen by measurement (2026-07-29).** Authorship is carried by **shape and side, not by tint on both sides**: the person's turn is `filled` and side-aligned, the assistant's is `ghost` and unboxed. Asymmetry survives a narrow column where side-alignment alone collapses, and it buys back width for long answers. **The filled skin paints the accent-weak step**, on evidence: swept across 27 accents in both appearances, body text clears at 11.86 worst and small print at 4.73 worst, while the next step up fails small print on 25 of the 54 combinations at 3.78 worst — reproducing an earlier recorded failure at 4.43 almost exactly, which independently validates the sweep. **The clamp is `min(max(80%, 280px), 100%)` and the bubble MUST declare `border-box`:** measured without it, a filled bubble rendered 304px inside a 320px column — one padding-box wider than the clamp computes — because a plain element here is content-box and the substrate ships no universal reset. **The message names itself:** the sender's name when there is one, otherwise an overridable sentence. Never the raw sender enum, which leaks an API token into the accessibility tree.

### delivery-status

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`, `ACCESSIBILITY`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-29.

**A delivery status shows a glyph and its word, and its accessible name never restates the visible text.**

**What you see.** All five states ship, the failed send included, on `ChatMessageMetadata`. Each state reads as a glyph plus its own word, so `delivered` and `read` differ by the word rather than by their shared double check, and no state relies on colour alone.

**Accessible name.** The status row carries no `title` and no `aria-label`, and a test asserts their absence. A title is a hover-only duplicate, and a label that overrides the visible content makes the accessible name and the rendered text disagree.

**Secondary text.** Weight and colour carry secondary text, never a smaller size step. The text lane floors at 12px at the default size, so a smaller step merges the two tiers into one.

**Retry.** The consumer places a retry action, in the footer slot. Whether a failed send may be retried is the product's decision, not the message's.

**Changed from.** No earlier ruling covered this. The reference design distinguished `delivered` from `read` with a hover `title`, and gave the row an `aria-label` that differed from its visible text.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-29. No later ruling amends it.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **Delivery status is a glyph AND its word; the accessible name may not restate the visible text (2026-07-29).** All five states ship, including the **failed send** — a send that can fail and says so is the honest set. Each state reads as a glyph plus its own word, so `delivered` and `read` are told apart by the word rather than by a shared double tick, and nothing is carried by colour alone. **The row carries no `title` and no `aria-label`.** The reference set both: the title is a hover-only duplicate, and the label *overrode* the visible content, so the accessible name and the rendered text disagreed by construction. Dropping both is the fix; their absence is asserted. Secondary text is carried by **weight and colour, never a smaller step** — the text lane already floors at 12px at the default size, so a sub-floor offset collapses the two tiers into one. **The retry affordance belongs to the consumer** and lands in the footer slot: whether a failed send may be retried is the product's decision, not the message's.

### chat-system-line

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-29.

**`ChatSystemMessage` is a centred line a conversation says about itself, with no surface, no tint and no severity, and it is never a `Callout`.**

**Why.** A footnote in a transcript that looks like a warning misleads the reader. Once a reader must act on a notice, it is no longer a system line.

**What you see.** A centred supporting line with an optional glyph. Its text wraps rather than truncating, because a single line cuts off the long notices the documentation recommends.

**Live region.** Inside a message list the log already announces the line, so it takes no role. On its own it takes `role="status"`. It reads its place from an optional context hook, the idiom the field shell uses, and a test asserts both branches.

**Divider.** The `divider` variant composes the system `Separator` with a centred label. Each rule keeps a minimum width from the spacing scale, so a long label never removes the divider.

**Documentation.** The messaging comparison carries `ChatSystemMessage` as a fourth column, on each of the four pages that render it.

**Changed from.** No earlier ruling covered this. The reference the component follows pinned the line to a single line.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-29. No later ruling amends it.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **A line a conversation says about itself is not a Callout (2026-07-29).** `ChatSystemMessage` is a centred supporting line with an optional glyph — **no surface, no tint, no severity** — because a footnote in a transcript that looks like a warning is a lie, and the moment a reader must act on it, it has stopped being a system line. The shipped messaging comparison gains it as a fourth column so that ruling lands where readers actually look, on all four pages that render the dataset. **Its text wraps** rather than truncating: the reference pinned it to a single line, which destroys exactly the long notices its own documentation recommends writing. **Its live-region role depends on where it sits** — inside a message list the log already announces it, so it takes no role; standalone it takes `role="status"`. It reads that through an optional context hook, the same idiom the field shell uses, and both branches are asserted with the assertion proven to fail in each direction. The `divider` variant composes the system separator with a centred label; its rules carry a minimum from the existing spacing scale because a long label otherwise ate the row and the divider silently stopped being one.

### chat-tool-log

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-29.

**`ChatToolCalls` is a record of tool calls, and its four states differ by shape before colour.**

| State | What the row shows |
|---|---|
| Queued | A clock and the word "Queued" |
| Running | A spinner |
| Complete | A check and the call's duration |
| Failed | A cross and the reason as visible text |

**Why.** A lone clock reads as a duration rather than as a call not yet started. A reason in a `title` attribute is invisible to touch and to most assistive technology.

**Disclosure.**

- The collapsed group shows the latest call's state and name, so a failure is visible without opening the log.
- The summary stays the same open and closed, so the line does not jump on toggle.
- The group is closed by default, and closed content unmounts, so a collapsed group holds no focusable descendant and needs no `inert` or forced mount.
- A row with detail is a real `<button>` around the row primitive, because the primitive renders as a span and an expanded state on its root would be an invalid ARIA attribute.

**Built from.** Rows on the internal `Item` primitive at compact density, the disclosure on the system `Collapsible`, and `Badge`, `Spinner` and `Code` for the row's parts. The `Collapsible` is wrapped rather than widened, because its prop type is closed on purpose and other consumers depend on that.

**Dropped.** A label prop nothing read, a render callback that never existed, an orphan data field, and the stacked-card styling.

**Changed from.** No earlier ruling covered this. The reference drew queued and running calls alike, put a failure reason in a `title` attribute, and left closed rows as tab stops at zero height.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-29.

- [ui-polish-ruleset](#ui-polish-ruleset) sets the diff counts in tabular figures.
- [status-glyph-line-box](#status-glyph-line-box) centres the status glyph on the first line of its row at every size.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **A tool log is a record, told apart by shape before colour (2026-07-29).** `ChatToolCalls` is rebuilt on shipped parts — rows on the internal row primitive at compact density, disclosure on the system collapsible, with the badge, spinner and code wraps supplying the row's parts. **Four states, distinguishable without reading colour:** queued is a clock **plus the word**, because a lone clock reads as a duration rather than as *not started*; running is the spinner; complete carries its duration; failed carries **its reason as visible text**, where the reference put it in a `title` attribute that is invisible to touch and to most assistive technology. **The group summary shows the LATEST call's state and name**, so a failure is visible from the collapsed state and nobody must open the log to discover something went wrong; it stays stable across open and closed rather than swapping to a glyph and a count, which made the line jump on toggle. Default closed, and the content **unmounts**, so a collapsed group holds no focusable descendants — the reference's live-tab-stop-at-zero-height defect cannot occur on this substrate, and no `inert` or forced mount is needed. **The row is a real button wrapping the row primitive**, which renders as a span: the primitive's own reset button cannot carry the expanded state, and putting that on its root would be an invalid ARIA attribute. **Dropped as dead:** a label prop nothing read, a render callback that never existed, an orphan data field, and the pile-of-cards styling. Its collapsible is wrapped rather than widened — the shared disclosure's prop type is deliberately closed, and other consumers depend on that.

### chat-composer

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-29.

**The chat composer is a real textarea on the shared field shell.**

**What you see.** The input is the system `TextArea`, so it carries real textbox semantics, a native placeholder and the field focus ring. It grows with its text to eight lines, measured from its own rendered line-height, and then scrolls. It measures again on a size lane change, when fonts load and when its width changes through the shared resize observer, never on a window resize.

**Keyboard.** Enter submits the trimmed value and clears the field. Shift+Enter inserts a new line. Enter on whitespace alone does nothing and still consumes the key, so it never adds a blank line.

**Focus.** The dock is one bordered surface that holds the input and its actions, so the focus ring moves from the textarea to the dock with a `:has()` selector, and the field inside the dock draws no border of its own. Two nested rings would read as two controls.

**Status line.** The message sits under the dock, where every other input in the system puts its message, as colour and a glyph with no fill and no border. An error takes `role="alert"`, and a warning takes `role="status"`, where a field's warning takes no live region.

**Why.** A composer warning can be the only response to a send the reader just attempted, and silence there reads as a send that worked. The send control stays the last element of the dock, and a validation message is never a tinted panel ([field-shell](#field-shell)), so the line cannot sit inside the dock.

**Deferred.** Token chips, mention and slash menus, message history, dictation and the attachments drawer, each with the trigger that would reopen it in [chat-deferrals](#chat-deferrals). None leaves an unused prop.

**Changed from.** The source it was ported from used a content-editable element with a faked placeholder and only a multiline hint for semantics. A first build placed the status line inside the dock, on the ground that a 12px warning read 4.61:1 on the dock's raised surface and 4.50:1 on the page. This ruling placed it under the dock, because warning text already passes below 4.5:1 ([warning-text-tolerance](#warning-text-tolerance)).

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-29.

- [focus-ring](#focus-ring) replaces the neutral hairline the dock first drew with the accent focus ring, 2px wide.
- [input-focus-ring-offset](#input-focus-ring-offset) sets the dock ring at `outline-offset: 2px`, the gap a button takes.
- [chat-layout-assembly](#chat-layout-assembly) routes a session condition above the dock and a sent message's failure to that message, and keeps the composer `status` for the draft.
- [container-size-seeding](#container-size-seeding) publishes the composer's control step to its `actions`, so an unsized button there matches the send control.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **The composer is a real textarea on the shared field shell (2026-07-29).** A deliberate divergence, framed as the upgrade it is: the reference uses a content-editable element with a faked placeholder and only a multiline hint for semantics. Ours gets **real textbox semantics, a native placeholder, and the field ring** for free. **Autogrow measures the rendered line-height**, caps at eight lines, then scrolls — measured at 1, 4, 8 and 12 lines as 16 / 64 / 128 / 128px with overflow turning auto past the cap. It re-measures on a lane change, on fonts settling, and on width through the shared observer — **never on a window resize**. **Enter submits the trimmed value and clears; Shift+Enter inserts a newline; Enter on whitespace does nothing at all** and still swallows the key, so the no-op cannot become a blank line. **The focus ring hoists to the dock** via a `:has()` selector, because the dock is ONE bordered surface holding the input and its actions and two nested rings would read as two controls; the field inside is de-skinned so there is no second border. The ring is the single neutral hairline with no halo, per the focus-ring chain. **A warning here announces where a field's does not, deliberately.** The shared field shell gives an error `role="alert"` and a warning no live region at all; the composer gives a warning `role="status"`. The difference is the surface: a form warning sits beside a control the reader is already looking at, whereas a composer warning can be the only response to a send they just attempted, and silence there reads as the send having worked. **The status line sits UNDER the dock**, where every other input in the system puts its message — colour and a glyph, no fill, no border. It shipped inside the dock on a measured basis (a 12px warning clears at 4.61 on the raised surface but reads 4.50 on the page and 4.39 on the subtle one) and was moved out. The measurement was real but the conclusion was not available: warning text is **already accepted at 4.40** on the ground that the glyph ships with it and status is never colour alone, so 4.50 is better than the ratified figure and the question returns to layout. Layout is decisive — the send control is the input's final anchor and must stay its last element, and the field ruling is explicit that a validation message is colour + glyph and **not a tinted panel**, which rules out a filled shelf too. Token chips, mention and slash menus, message history, dictation and the attachments drawer are named deferrals with triggers, and none leaves a dead prop behind.

### chat-layout-assembly

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-29.

**`ChatLayout` holds the transcript, the docked composer and a scroll control, and each of the three kinds of trouble around a composer has its own place on screen.**

**Scroll engine.** The spring that scrolls the transcript integrates in floating point and writes each frame to the element. It reads the element again only when the two differ by more than rounding explains, which happens when the browser clamps at an edge or the reader scrolls. A spring that wrote whole pixels stalled within about 5px of its target and never arrived.

**Handle.** The imperative handle exposes `scrollToBottom` and nothing more. It returns the transcript to the bottom and pins it there even after the reader left the bottom, because the consumer called it on purpose. The type carries no `scrollToMessage`, not even as a stub.

**Scroll control.** Two elements, one mounted at a time, so the control is one tab stop and causes no layout shift. Its entrance is a keyframe animation, `ds-chat-layout-scroll-in`, because two separate elements leave nothing to interpolate, and no width or height ever animates.

**Dock.**

- The layout holds the dock, not sticky positioning, because the scrolling element is the log's own viewport, and a dock inside it would sit inside the log region and announce typing as conversation.
- The fade above the dock paints `--ds-chat-layout-bg`, a component property that defaults to the page background, so a chat inside a card sets it and paints no page-coloured band.
- The dock carries no blur. Blur belongs to small floating surfaces, and a persistent full-width dock is not one.

**Where a message goes.**

| Message about | Where it sits | Prop |
|---|---|---|
| The session: reconnecting, queued, a model retiring | Above the dock, outside its border | `sessionStatus` on `ChatLayout` |
| A sent message that failed | On that message, in its metadata row beside its retry | The failed state of the message |
| The draft in the composer | Under the dock, where every field puts its message | `status` on `ChatComposer` |

**Why.** Each sentence sits next to the thing it concerns. A session message inside the dock would read as a note on the draft, and in the transcript it would read as an event in the conversation. Research across chat products found composers that differ from form fields by emptying the one message slot and routing each message by type, and no verified source that moves a panel into the box.

**Session line.** The session line stacks above the fade, with `position: relative` and `z-index: 1`, because the fade dissolves transcript into the dock and this line is chrome. Under the fade its ink measured 1.88:1 against a role of 5.79:1, and neither `getComputedStyle` nor axe reported the loss.

**Changed from.** No earlier ruling covered this.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-29. The placement of the three messages was ruled on 2026-07-30.

- [chat-layout-tag](#chat-layout-tag) adds `as`, so the root can render as `main` or `section`.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **The assembly, and a sub-pixel integrator the pure tests could not have caught (2026-07-29).** `ChatLayout` holds the transcript, the docked composer and the scroll affordance. **The engine had a real defect that only a runtime test could see:** a scroll offset is quantised to whole pixels, and the spring's step is about 0.09 of the remaining distance, so within roughly 5px of the target every write rounded to *no movement* — the distance stopped shrinking, the arrival test never fired, and a frame callback ran **forever** with the transcript resting short of its newest message. Measured before the fix: 419 of 422, 375 of 378, 30166 of 30170. The spring now **integrates in floating point and presents each frame** to the element, re-reading it only when the two disagree by more than rounding explains — which is the browser clamping at an edge, or the reader taking over. The engine's 29 pure tests still pass unchanged: the defect lived entirely in the DOM half, which is the general lesson — a hook whose pure math is fully covered can still be wholly broken where it meets the document. **The handle exposes `scrollToBottom` only, and it re-takes the lock even when the reader had scrolled away** — the consumer asked for it deliberately, and a control that silently does nothing is a control that lies; `scrollToMessage` is absent rather than stubbed. **The affordance is two elements with one mounted at a time**, so there is one tab stop and no layout shift, and no width or height is ever animated. **Three ratified deviations:** the dock is held by the layout rather than by sticky positioning, because the scroller is the log's own viewport — a sticky child of the non-scrolling root gets no offset, and a dock inside the viewport would sit inside the log region and announce typing as conversation; the affordance's entrance is a keyframe animation rather than a transition, because two mutually exclusive elements give nothing to interpolate; and the fade's background is an overridable component-local property defaulting to the page role, so a chat inside a card does not paint a page-coloured band. **No blur:** the polish bound already restricts it to small floating surfaces, and a persistent full-width dock is what that excludes. **THREE THINGS GO WRONG, AND THERE ARE THREE PLACES TO SAY SO (2026-07-30, ruled after cross-product research).** A composer does not have one message slot, it has three destinations, and the routing is by WHAT the sentence is about. The SESSION's condition — reconnecting, queued, a model retiring — takes `sessionStatus`, above the dock and outside its border. A SENT MESSAGE's failure goes on that message, where the metadata row already has a failed state and a slot for its retry. Whatever is wrong with the DRAFT still in the box is the composer's own `status`, under the dock, where every field in this system puts its message. Each sentence sits next to the thing it is about, and each of the other two placements would misattribute it: inside the dock claims to be about the draft, in the transcript claims something happened in the conversation. **The research is the reason this is a rule and not a preference:** chat composers genuinely diverge from form fields, but by EMPTYING the single message slot and routing by type — not by pulling a panel into the box, which no verified source does. **A defect this immediately produced, recorded because the class recurs:** the session line was placed in exactly the 48px the dock's fade band occupies, and the band — a `::before` on a positioned dock — painted over it. Declared ink `--ds-text-weak`; rendered pixel `rgb(185,187,191)`, 1.88 : 1 against a role that is 5.79 : 1. `getComputedStyle` reported the correct colour throughout and axe passed the story, because the wash came from a sibling's gradient rather than from any colour the rules declare. The line now carries its own stacking context above the fade: the fade exists to dissolve TRANSCRIPT into the dock, and this line is chrome, not transcript. Its Usage is the family's flagship — the whole set in a page shell holding one real exchange about this system's own accent, including the step that failed.

### scroll-position-animation

**Tags.** `MOTION`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-29.

**A frame-loop animation of a scroll position stands outside the motion rules, because it paints nothing.**

**Why.** The motion rules govern `transition` and `@keyframes` on painted elements and rule out spring and physics tokens. A frame-loop integrator that drives a scroll offset moves a viewport and paints nothing of its own.

**Bounds.**

- Reduced motion replaces the animation with an instant jump.
- No token is minted for the spring constants. They are named module constants, documented where they are used.

**Applies to.** The transcript scroll of `ChatLayout`, in `src/hooks/useChatStreamScroll.ts`. `docs/GUIDELINES.md` section 7 states the exemption in its list of exclusions, so it stands as a stated carve-out rather than a silent exception.

**Changed from.** The motion section ruled out spring and physics tokens and named no exemption for a scroll position.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-29. No later ruling amends it.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **Scroll-position animation is exempt from the motion rules — it paints nothing (2026-07-29).** The motion section rules out spring and physics tokens. A frame-loop integrator driving a scroll offset is **not** what that governs: the rules there constrain transitions and keyframes on painted elements, and moving a scroll position paints nothing of its own. This is a stated carve-out rather than a silent exception, and it is bounded — **reduced motion short-circuits it to an instant jump**, and **no token is minted for the spring constants**, which are named module constants documented where they are used. The guidelines' exclusion list gains one line saying so, so the next reader does not have to rediscover the argument.

### chat-density

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`, `SIZING`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-29.

**The chat components take no density prop, and each reads its size from a global size lane.**

**Why.** The system already has a density vocabulary, on the row primitive and its list consumers, and a second one scoped to chat would be a parallel mechanism with the same name. The tool log passes `density="compact"` to its rows and never exposes it on its own API.

**Lanes.** Each component's token spec names its lane.

| Lane | Components |
|---|---|
| Container | `ChatLayout` and the transcript, `ChatMessageList` |
| Control | `ChatComposer` and its send, stop and scroll controls |
| Text | The bubble body, `ChatMessageMetadata` and `ChatSystemMessage` |

**Changed from.** The source it was ported from exposed compact, balanced and spacious on its chat surfaces through a prop. Its observation of the container width was a leftover, since its density came from the prop throughout.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-29. No later ruling amends it.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **A density prop does not port as chat API (2026-07-29).** The reference exposes compact / balanced / spacious on its chat surfaces. Ours does not — **not because the system lacks a density vocabulary**, but because it already has one on the row primitive and its list consumers, and a second one scoped to chat would be a parallel mechanism with the same name. The tool log passes compact to its rows explicitly and never surfaces it upward. **Lane assignments, each named in its component's token spec:** the layout and the transcript ride **container**; the composer and its send, stop and scroll controls ride **control**; bubble body, metadata and the system line ride **text**. The reference's container-width observation was falsified as a leftover — its density was prop-driven throughout.

### chat-deferrals

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-29.

**Chat leaves eight features out on purpose, and each has a named trigger that would reopen it.**

**Why.** The list lets a later reader tell an omission from a decision.

**Deferred.**

| Feature | What it would take | Trigger |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Token chips and paste as token | A rebuild of the composer input, since chips cannot render inside a textarea | A consumer needs inline entity pills |
| Mention and slash menus | An addition to the textarea, through caret coordinates and the shipped combobox engine | The first consumer with mentions |
| Arrow-key message history | An addition | A console-style consumer |
| Dictation | An addition with its own accessibility pass | A consumer asks for it |
| An attachments drawer | A disclosure composition. The disclosure ships and the drawer does not | The first attachments consumer |
| A distinct typing indicator | Nothing yet, since the spinner in the bubble covers the gap | A product wants a dedicated animated affordance |
| Virtualised history | Nothing ships, and the reference has none either | A real consumer with threads of thousands of messages |
| Deep links to a message | Absent from the message list handle by [chat-layout-assembly](#chat-layout-assembly) | A thread needs addressable messages |

**Not to be restored.** The reference has no markdown, no sanitiser and no raw HTML injection anywhere. Content is nodes the caller supplies, so the parser question stays parked.

**Changed from.** No earlier ruling covered this.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-29. No later ruling amends it.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **What chat deliberately does not ship, and what would re-open each (2026-07-29).** Recorded so a future reader can tell an omission from a decision. **Token chips and paste-as-token** re-open the composer's input decision rather than adding to it — chips cannot render inside a textarea, so this is a rebuild, not a feature; trigger: a consumer needs inline entity pills. **Mention and slash menus** are additive on the textarea via caret coordinates and the shipped combobox engine; trigger: the first consumer with mentions. **Arrow-key message history**, additive; trigger: a console-style consumer. **Dictation**, additive and needs its own accessibility pass; trigger: a consumer asks. **An attachments drawer** is a disclosure composition — the disclosure ships, the drawer is what does not; trigger: the first attachments consumer. **A distinct typing indicator** — the spinner-in-the-bubble covers the gap; trigger: a product wants a dedicated animated affordance. **Virtualised history** — none ships, matching the reference, which was grep-verified to have none; trigger: a real consumer with thousand-message threads. **Deep-linking to a message** — absent from the handle by ruling; trigger: a thread needs addressable messages. Source-verified and not to be restored: there is **no markdown, no sanitiser and no raw-HTML injection** anywhere in the reference — content is caller-supplied nodes, so the parked parser question stays parked.

### press-to-see-demos

**Tags.** `DOCUMENTATION`, `MOTION`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-29.

**A docs page may hold a control that the reader presses to see motion, and nothing on the page moves until the reader presses it.**

**The rule.** Nothing animates when a story opens, and no `play` function drives motion in a docs story. A control the reader presses may sit on a docs page, inert until clicked, with a caption that says so in words.

**First instance.** The ChatLayout Usage page carries a Simulate incoming message button, and the transcript stays static until the reader presses it. The earlier press-to-see precedent, `_internal/PressScale A-B`, was an internal fixture, and this ruling extends the pattern to the docs pages readers see.

**Not covered.** Everything that runs unattended, such as stream sequences, spring assertions and reduced-motion checks, stays in the `_internal/<Name> behavior` suites.

**Conformance.** The entrance keyframe of the ChatLayout scroll control moves from `--ds-ease-standard` to `--ds-ease-entry`, the entry curve that [motion-retiming](#motion-retiming) already sets for every entrance.

**Changed from.** Press-to-see controls existed only in internal fixtures, and no docs page held an interactive motion demo.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-29. No later ruling amends it.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **Press-to-see demos on docs pages (2026-07-29).** **The rule: nothing animates on story view, and no `play` drives motion in a docs story — but a control the USER presses may live on a docs page, inert until clicked.** ChatLayout's Usage page is the first sanctioned instance ("Simulate incoming message": the transcript is static until the reader acts; the caption says so in words). The prior press-to-see precedent (`_internal/PressScale A-B`) was an internal fixture — this ruling is what extends the pattern to user-facing docs. Everything that runs unattended (stream sequences, spring assertions, reduced-motion checks) stays in `_internal/<Name> behavior` suites. Companion conformance note: the scroll control's entrance keyframe ran on `--ds-ease-standard` — the file's only entrance off the entry curve — and is aligned to `--ds-ease-entry` (no new doctrine; the [motion-retiming](#motion-retiming) ladder already said so).

### chat-avatar-size

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`, `SIZING`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-30.

**A chat avatar is pinned at 30px, and only the other party in the conversation shows one.**

**Size.** The slot is pinned to `lg`, 30px or `--ds-text-h3-leading`, and does not follow the message's text lane, because an avatar is an identity object and holds one size while the type moves. A survey of seven messaging and comment systems put the mode at 32px in a band of 28 to 36, and the ladder has no 32, so the slot takes the nearest step.

**Rejected.** `xl`, 40px, leaves 272px in a 320px row, under the 280px that the bubble clamp of [chat-bubble](#chat-bubble) requires. `lg` is the last step that fits.

**Anatomy.** The avatar renders for `assistant` alone, and an avatar passed to `user` or `system` is ignored, as the prop documents. Direction already marks the reader's own messages ([chat-bubble](#chat-bubble)), and no bubble-family pattern in the survey shows a self avatar.

**Portrait ramp.** `useResolvedAvatarSize` carries two ramps: `"inline"`, the beside-text ladder of `xs`, `sm` and `md`, and `"portrait"`, the identity ladder of `md`, `lg` and `xl` at 24, 30 and 40px. `AvatarGroup` rides the portrait ramp and tracks the global size, chat pins `lg` because its header band is fixed geometry, and an explicit size wins over both.

**Mechanism.** The wrapper sets `--ds-avatar-box`, and a `(0,3,0)` child rule makes the avatar inherit it, the `AvatarGroup` idiom, because `Avatar` writes that variable on its own element.

**Changed from.** The chat avatar rode the inline-text avatar ladder, 16px at the default tier, and the reader's own messages carried an avatar that sat 7.28px above its first line of text.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-30, and extended in this entry the same day with the portrait ramp for `AvatarGroup`.

- [chat-avatar-header-row](#chat-avatar-header-row) keeps the 30px pin, makes the header row the avatar's own box and renames the local input to `--chat-avatar-box`. It also meets the condition this ruling set for a later multi-party transcript with faces on both sides, which is not built.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **A chat avatar is pinned at 30px, and only the OTHER party gets one (2026-07-30).** Two findings from a survey of messaging and comment patterns across seven systems, which agreed on both counts. **Size:** the mode is 32px and the whole band is 28–36. Ours was resolving the inline-text avatar ladder — 16px at the default tier, half the mode, a face too small to recognise beside a paragraph. Our ladder has no 32, and the rule here is to take the nearest step rather than invent a value, so the slot is pinned to **lg (30px, `--ds-text-h3-leading`)** and does **not** follow the message's text lane: an avatar is an identity object, not a line of type, and it stays one size while the transcript's type moves. **xl (40px) was measured and rejected on [chat-bubble](#chat-bubble)'s bubble floor** — at a 320px row it leaves 272px, under the 280px the clamp requires; lg lands at exactly 280, the last step that fits. **Anatomy: the reader's own avatar is dropped.** [chat-bubble](#chat-bubble) already committed to direction as the authorship signal, and the filled tint says the same thing a second time; every bubble-family pattern in the survey omits the self avatar. Ours was a graft that contradicted its own ruling, and it had a visible defect to go with it — with a filled bubble and no name row, the avatar top-aligned with the *bubble* while the first line of text sat inside the padding, so the face floated **7.28px above the line it belonged to** (6.78px centre to centre, measured at the default tier). Removing it also returns the avatar's width and its gap to the message column, which the bubble takes up to its own clamp (measured on the flagship: 443 → 462px). The slot now renders for `assistant` alone; passing one to `user` or `system` is ignored, and that is documented on the prop rather than left to be discovered. **The named alternative, for the amendment this will eventually need:** a multi-party transcript — several human participants rather than one reader and one assistant — genuinely wants a face on both sides, because there the side no longer identifies the speaker. The condition on re-opening is that avatars there arrive **with `name`**, so both sides get a header row for the avatar to align to and the misalignment above cannot return. Not built: no consumer has that shape yet. Implementation is AvatarGroup's two-rule idiom (the wrapper sets `--ds-avatar-box`, a `(0,3,0)` child rule makes the avatar `inherit` it), because `Avatar` writes that variable on its own element and a wrapper variable alone loses. **Amended by [chat-avatar-header-row](#chat-avatar-header-row) (2026-07-30), same day:** the 30px pin stands and the size finding is unchanged — what this ruling got wrong is the geometry it left the pinned avatar sitting in. It fixed the *self*-avatar's centre-to-centre defect by deleting that avatar, and left the assistant's avatar top-aligned to a one-line name row, where 30px against a 16px row put the picture's bottom edge 10px down the first line of the body. The header row is now the avatar's own box ([chat-avatar-header-row](#chat-avatar-header-row)); the `--ds-avatar-box` value and the two-rule idiom are unchanged, and the local input is renamed `--chat-avatar-box` because three rules now read it. The re-opening condition recorded here is *satisfied by construction* under [chat-avatar-header-row](#chat-avatar-header-row), which gives an avatar a header row whether or not a name comes with it. **Generalised same day: the category becomes machinery.** The error fixed here for chat — an identity object riding the inline-text avatar ladder — was not chat's alone: `AvatarGroup`, a stack of identities, resolved the same beside-text ladder ambiently and rendered 16px discs at the default tier. `useResolvedAvatarSize` now carries two ramps — `"inline"` (xs/sm/md, the beside-text ladder; standalone `Avatar` unchanged) and `"portrait"` (md/lg/xl → 24/30/40, identity contexts) — and `AvatarGroup` rides portrait. Chat's lg pin is untouched and the distinction is deliberate: chat PINS because its header band is fixed geometry ([chat-avatar-header-row](#chat-avatar-header-row)); a group TRACKS the global size because nothing above it fixes a band. Explicit sizes win, as everywhere.

### chat-avatar-header-row

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`, `LAYOUT`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-30.

**In a chat message the avatar sets the height of the header row, and a run of messages shows its speaker once.**

**With a name.** The row of the name grows to the avatar box through `min-height`, with the name centred in it, so the bottom of the avatar, the bottom of the header and the top of the body share one line at every size.

**Without a name.** The first line of the body is the header. It is lowered by half the difference between the avatar box and the line box, less any inset the bubble already holds above that line, so its centre meets the centre of the avatar.

**Without an avatar.** Nothing aligns to anything: the name keeps its own line and nothing is lowered.

**Runs.** The first message of a run draws the avatar and the name. A `middle` or `last` message draws neither and holds an empty box the width of the avatar, so every body in the run shares one left edge. The caller passes `avatar` and `name` on every message of the run, and the component shows them only on the first.

**Accessible name.** A string `name` stays the accessible name of the later messages, because a reader may reach the third message of a run without its context. An explicit `label` takes precedence over both.

**Rejected.**

- The avatar inline in the header row, as in a comment thread. It aligns only at 16, 20 or 24px, too small to recognise ([chat-avatar-size](#chat-avatar-size)), and at 30px it moves every assistant body 38px left and removes the speaker column.
- The first body line centred on the avatar with the name unmoved. The overlap then depends on the size, and the name leaves the top edge of the message.
- A reserved band with no name. It aligns, but the avatar stands beside an empty row that reads as a hole.

**Tokens.** No new tokens. Three component-local inputs carry the geometry: `--chat-avatar-box`, `--chat-line` and `--chat-body-lead`. The lead is a real `0px` length, because `--ds-space-0` is a unitless `0`, which voids any `calc()` that contains it.

**Changed from.** Under [chat-avatar-size](#chat-avatar-size), a 30px avatar sat top-aligned to a name row one line tall and ended inside the body, 10px into its first line at the small size, 6px at medium and 2px at large. With no name row it reached the second line of the body, and the later messages of a run sat 38px left of the first.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-30. No later ruling amends it.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **The avatar owns the header row, and a run introduces its speaker once (2026-07-30).** Three candidate treatments were built as throwaway variants and measured at all three lanes; the numbers are the argument. **What was wrong:** a 30px avatar top-aligned to a name row one line of the text lane tall (16 / 20 / 24px) ends *inside the body*, and where it ends moves with the lane — measured 10px into the body's first line at small, 6px at medium, 2px at large. The picture was aligned with nothing at any size, and with no name row it ran 14px into the body's SECOND line. **The rule: the avatar shares a vertical centre with the message's first line, and there are two shapes of that.** *Band* — with a name, the name's row is grown to the avatar's own box (`min-height`) and the name is centred in it, so the avatar's bottom edge, the header's bottom edge and the body's top edge are ONE line: measured 0.00px apart at all three lanes, against 10 / 6 / 2px before. The band also carries the slack the column gap used to add (7px under the name at the small lane), so the column now owns no gaps at all and each part carries its own spacing — the header's spacing depends on which shape it is, and a single `gap` cannot express that. *Line* — with no name, the body's first line IS the header and is nudged down half the difference between the two boxes (7 / 5 / 3px), less whatever inset the bubble already holds above that line, so a filled bubble is not counted twice; measured centre-to-centre agreement of 0.00–0.50px (the residual is the ink rect against the line box). Without an avatar there is nothing to align to, so the name keeps its own line and nothing is nudged. **The two rejected candidates, and why:** *avatar inline in the header row at the lane's leading, body at full column width* (the comment-thread shape) aligns perfectly — the avatar IS the line box — but only by shrinking the avatar to 16 / 20 / 24px, which is the exact "too small to recognise" finding [chat-avatar-size](#chat-avatar-size) was minted to fix; at 30px inline the same shape loses the gutter, moves every assistant body 38px left and gives a bubble family no speaker column to scan down. *First body line centred on the avatar with the name left in place* leaves the picture ending 3px into the body's first line at small and 1px past its top at large — tier-dependent by construction, and the name is pushed off the message's top edge. A fourth (reserve the band even with no name) measures the same 0.00px but was rejected on sight: the avatar stands alone beside an empty row, which reads as a hole. **Runs introduce their speaker once.** The message that opens a run draws the avatar and the name; `middle` and `last` draw neither and stand an empty box the avatar's width in its place, so every body in the run keeps one left edge — without the held gutter the run's later messages slid 38px left of its first, which is what the ungrouped-looking run measured before. The contract is that the caller passes `avatar` and `name` on **every** message of the run and the component decides where they show; a caller who never passes an avatar holds nothing and is unaffected. A **string** `name` still becomes the accessible name of the later messages, because a reader may arrive at the third message of a run out of its context; an explicit `label` stays ahead of both. **Zero net-new tokens** — two component-local inputs (`--chat-avatar-box`, `--chat-line`, plus `--chat-body-lead` for the bubble's own inset), the Item block-padding precedent. One trap worth recording: `--ds-space-0` is a **unitless** `0`, which is legal as a padding and poisons any `calc()` it lands in — the whole declaration is thrown away — so the lead is a real `0px` length.

### container-size-seeding

**Tags.** `SIZING`, `COMPONENTS`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-30.

**A container that resolves a size seeds it to its slots, and a row of small print gives its slot the row's own type step.**

**Why.** A container passes its resolved step to the children it renders, while content a consumer passes into a slot resolves the ambient tier, so the two land in one row at different sizes. The call site cannot see what the container resolved, so it cannot fix the mismatch. The sign is a slot whose content can disagree with the container's own children.

**Seeding.** Where the mismatch is about the size tier, the container publishes its resolved step as a `SizeContext` tier. `Toolbar` and `ChatComposer` do this, so an unsized `IconButton` in the composer's `actions` matches the send control beside it. Both read the one step-to-tier map, `CONTROL_STEP_TO_UISIZE` in `SizeContext`. An explicitly sized child still wins, because `useResolvedSize` reads the explicit value before the context, and `size="inherit"` seeds nothing.

**Row constraint.** Where the mismatch is about treatment, seeding cannot help, so the row constrains its slot. The chat message metadata footer carries the row's type step onto its content with a `(0,2,0)` descendant rule that outranks the `(0,1,0)` size class Radix writes. Inside the footer a control's block padding yields, so the [control-box-per-step](#control-box-per-step) floor sets the box while the row sets the type. An action there is a `Link` around a real `<button>`: text in a line of text, at the row's size, in a row one line tall.

**Scope.** In the chat family only `ChatComposer` takes a size apart from the ambient tier. `ChatLayout`, `ChatMessageList`, `ChatMessage`, `ChatMessageMetadata`, `ChatSystemMessage` and `ChatToolCalls` resolve their lane from the ambient tier and take no size prop. [delivery-status](#delivery-status) is unchanged, and the consumer still places the retry.

**Gap.** An inline text action is smaller than the 24px target floor and relies on the WCAG 2.2 inline exception. The 44px hit areas under `pointer: coarse` that would cover it on touch are not built.

**Changed from.** Only `Toolbar` seeded its step. An unsized `IconButton` in the composer measured 24 by 24 at step 1 beside a 40 by 40 send control at step 3, and a control in the metadata footer brought its own type step and its own box.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-30.

- Amended 2026-07-31 to meet [box-law-scope](#box-law-scope): inside the footer a control's block padding yields (`padding-block: 0`), so the box follows the law while the type follows the row.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **A container that resolves a size must seed it to its slots; a row of small print must own its slot's type step (2026-07-30).** One seam, found three times in the chat family, and worth naming as a class: **a slot whose content can disagree with the container's own children is the fingerprint.** A container hands its resolved step to the children it renders itself, while anything a consumer passes into a slot resolves the **ambient** tier — so the two land in the same row at different sizes, and no amount of care at the call site fixes it, because the call site cannot see what the container resolved. **The mechanism, where the disagreement is about the TIER: seed it.** `Toolbar` already did this — it publishes its resolved control step back as a `SizeContext` tier — and `ChatComposer` now does the same, so an unsized `IconButton` in `actions` comes out at the size of the send control beside it: measured 24×24 at step 1 beside a 40×40 step-3 send, now both step 3 with 18px glyphs on one centre line. An explicitly-sized child still wins, because `useResolvedSize` checks the explicit value before it reads the context, and `size="inherit"` seeds nothing (nothing was decided). The step ⇄ tier map moves to `SizeContext` as `CONTROL_STEP_TO_UISIZE` and both containers read it: two private copies of one inverse is how the two drift. **Where the disagreement is about the TREATMENT, seeding does not help, and the row must constrain its slot.** The metadata row is one line of small print on the TEXT lane; a control in its `footer` brought its own type step (a `Button` pinned to step 1 read 12px beside a 16px "Failed" at the large lane) and its own box (24px tall against a 16px line of text at the small lane, stretching the row). The slot now carries the row's own step onto its content — a `(0,2,0)` descendant rule outranks the `(0,1,0)` size class Radix writes, so the disagreement cannot be composed — and the documented treatment for an **action** there is a `Link` wrapped around a real `<button>`: text in a line of text, underlined, at the row's size, in a row that stays one line tall (16 / 20 / 24px at the three lanes, against a flat 24 before). [delivery-status](#delivery-status) is unchanged: the retry is still the consumer's to place. **The audit that goes with the ruling:** the seam only bites where a container can be sized independently of the ambient tier. In this family that is `ChatComposer` alone — `ChatLayout`, `ChatMessageList`, `ChatMessage`, `ChatMessageMetadata`, `ChatSystemMessage` and `ChatToolCalls` all resolve their lane from the ambient tier with no size prop of their own, so seeding there could only re-publish the tier they read. **The follow-on, stated rather than assumed:** an inline text action is smaller than the 24px target floor and rides WCAG 2.2's inline exception (it is constrained by the line-height of the text around it); the touch accommodation this system has already committed to — ≥44px invisible hit areas under `pointer: coarse` — is what covers it on touch, and it is not built yet. **Amended 2026-07-31 — the type rule meets the box law.** The footer's descendant type rule made a boxed control's own block padding inflate its box past the step (a step-1 Retry measured 28/32px under the medium/large lanes — a [box-law-scope](#box-law-scope) violation manufactured by a [container-size-seeding](#container-size-seeding) mechanism). Reconciled rather than won: inside the footer a control's block padding yields (`padding-block: 0`) so the [control-box-per-step](#control-box-per-step) floor governs the box while the type keeps taking the row's step. Type from the row, box from the law. The fixture's boxed-vs-linked contrast now asserts the boxed control never sits SHORTER than the link treatment (the strict inequality encoded the old geometry, not the ruling).

### control-box-per-step

**Tags.** `SIZING`, `COMPONENTS`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-30.

**A size step names one control box, and every button variant honours it.**

**What you see.** Buttons, icon buttons and toggles in one row share one height at each step, 24, 32 or 40px across the three tiers. A ghost control's hover and press paint fill the whole box. An icon-only control at the floor step is 24px, the target size `docs/GUIDELINES.md` section 9 requires.

**Why.** Radix applies `--base-button-height` to every `.rt-BaseButton` variant except ghost, which sizes from its glyph or label. At the medium tier a 22px toggle and a 28px icon button stood beside a 32px button, and no call site could fix the row.

**Mechanism.**

- `.rt-BaseButton` takes `min-height: max(var(--base-button-height), 24px)`, the vendor's own variable with the 24px pointer floor of `docs/GUIDELINES.md` under it, and `box-sizing: border-box`, so the floor is exact and does not add to the padding.
- `.rt-IconButton` takes the same value as `min-width`, so an icon button is square.
- An icon-only toggle carries `data-icon-only`, set by `ToggleButton` when it has a `label` and by a `ToggleButtonGroup.Item` with an `aria-label`. It takes the same square with `padding-inline: 0`.
- The rules sit last in `components.css`, so they win on source order over the ghost rules. `.radix-themes` scoping beats the vendor's `:where()` rules without `!important`.

**Inset affixes.** `[data-inset]`, the badge remove control and the token remove control keep their own step-1 box of 24px. A control with `[data-inset]` counts as declared under [box-law-scope](#box-law-scope), with its reason built into `boxLaw.ts`, and the guard still measures it against step 1.

**Pagination.** A page cell reads `--base-button-height` from the page button itself. The ellipsis is a `<span>` outside that variable's scope, so it takes its height from `align-self: stretch` and its width from a mirror of the vendor ladder, `--ds-space-24`, `--ds-space-32` and `--ds-space-40`, which resolve to the vendor's own `--space-5`, `--space-6` and `--space-7`.

**Changed from.** Ghost controls sized from their content, so one row at one step held three heights. Pagination kept its own `--ds-pagination-square` ladder, 24, 28 and 34px, which this ruling deletes.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-30. Amended within this entry the same day, when icon-only toggles took the square, and on 2026-07-31, when inset affixes became declared.

- [box-law-scope](#box-law-scope) extends the one-box law to every single-row control and guards it.
- [toggle-group-box](#toggle-group-box) makes a ToggleButtonGroup one control in the box, with its members one step down, and a lone ToggleButton keeps the whole box.
- [container-size-seeding](#container-size-seeding) removes a control's block padding inside a footer, so the floor governs its box there.
- [nav-row-ladder](#nav-row-ladder) moves the collapsed SideNav rail from the control box to the nav row ladder.
- [text-spacing-control-box](#text-spacing-control-box) adds `height: auto` beside the floor, so a control grows with its content under text spacing overrides.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **One control box per size step (2026-07-30).** Radix declares `--base-button-height` on **every** `.rt-BaseButton` — 24 / 32 / 40 / 48px against `--scaling` at steps 1–4 — and then applies it as a height to every variant **except ghost**, which it leaves `box-sizing: content-box; height: fit-content` to size from its own label or glyph instead. A row therefore disagreed with itself wherever the two met: measured on the toolbar at the medium tier, a **22px** toggle and a **28px** icon button standing beside a **32px** button — three heights in one row, at one step, and no call site can fix it because none of the three is wrong on its own terms. **The rule: a size step names ONE box, and every variant honours it.** The floor is the vendor's own variable rather than a second ladder of ours — `min-height: var(--base-button-height)` on `.rt-BaseButton`, plus `min-width` on `.rt-IconButton` so an icon button is that same box on both axes — with `box-sizing: border-box`, which is what makes the floor exact instead of additive (a content-box `min-height` stacks the button's own padding on top of the step). `min-*` and not `height`, so a control that legitimately needs to be taller still can be. Declared **last in `components.css`**, because it has to win on source order over the ghost rules above it; `.radix-themes` scoping beats the vendor's `:where()` rules, so no `!important`. Measured after: the toolbar row reads 32 / 32 / 32 at medium, and every affected surface lands on 24 / 32 / 40 across the three tiers. The inset carve-outs are untouched — `[data-inset]`, the badge ✕ and the token ✕ all match at higher specificity — verified by measurement, not by reading the selectors: chips paint the chip ladder (20px at the floor step) with a 24×24 ✕ inside and a ≥24px body target — re-measured 2026-07-31 when the container floor moved to the real targets. **An inset affix DECLARES ITSELF to the box law (amended 2026-07-31).** `IconButton`'s `inset` prop decides the STEP as well as the variant — an in-field or in-chip ✕ is a step-1 24×24 target whatever step the surface around it claims — so every one of these affixes is a *pin* by construction the moment the ambient tier is anything but small, and [box-law-scope](#box-law-scope)'s layer 2 (a pin in a docs page must carry `data-size-lesson`) started failing them: the case that surfaced it was Callout's Anatomy page at the medium tier, where the dismiss ✕ claims step 1 against a step-2 tier and the page would not render. Marking each site by hand would be asking a story to restate a rule the component already enforces, in the same sentence every time. So the rule declares them: a control carrying `[data-inset]` is read as declared, with the reason built into `boxLaw.ts` (*"inset affix — pinned to step 1 by rule, [control-box-per-step](#control-box-per-step) carve-outs"*). The attribute is the hook because it is what the DOM exposes — the badge and token carve-outs are CSS selectors over this same attribute rather than markers of their own, so one test covers the whole family. It is a **declaration, not a suppression**: layer 1 still measures the affix against step 1 and still fails when the box is off it. **Ghost hover and press paint now fill the whole box.** The tint that used to hug a label is a full 40×40 square at the large tier. That is part of the ruling and not a regression: a control that claims a box should show the box it claims when you touch it, and the previous behaviour was the visible symptom of the box being wrong. **An icon-only toggle at the floor step grows 20 → 24px, and that is a FIX rather than a side effect** — GUIDELINES section 9 has required ≥24×24 including compact size-1 all along, and the quiet affordances were precisely the ones sitting under it. **Deferred, named here so it reads as an omission on the record rather than an oversight: true squareness for icon-only toggles.** `ToggleButton` renders `.rt-Button`, not `.rt-IconButton`, so the cross-axis half of the rule cannot reach it — measured 28×24 at small and 30×32 at medium, square at large (40×40) only by coincidence of the glyph. Squaring it needs the component to mark its icon-only shape (a `data-icon-only` attribute for the CSS to hook), which is a component change and not a token-layer one; **trigger: the first row where a toggle's width visibly disagrees with an icon button beside it.** **The one stated residue lives in pagination's ellipsis.** The vendor declares `--base-button-height` **on the button element**, so it resolves only inside a button's own scope, and the ellipsis is a `<span>` standing in a row of buttons — it reads nothing from that variable. Its height comes free from `align-self: stretch` (the flex row's cross size, which the buttons set); its **width** is a hand-kept mirror of the vendor ladder — 24 / 32 / 40, spelled as `--ds-space-24/32/40`, which resolve to the identical `--space-5/6/7` the vendor itself uses, so the two sides track `--scaling` together. Everything that is a button reads the real variable; this span alone carries a copy, and if the vendor's ladder ever moves this is what moves with it. **What the ruling deleted: the `--ds-pagination-square` ladder** — a local 24 / 28 / 34 duplicate of the vendor's box, and a demonstration of exactly the drift a duplicate invites. It had been tuned to agree with the *ghost* boxes beside it, so once those were themselves short the whole pager sat a step under the real control box (28px page cells beside 32px buttons at the medium tier, which is how it was caught). Pagination now reads `--base-button-height` off the page button itself, where the variable is already in scope, so the square is the vendor's own by construction and cannot drift again. **Amended same day: the deferral fired, and it is implemented.** The trigger written above fired in the flagship Toolbar specimen: 28×24 toggles beside 24×24 icon buttons at the small tier, 30×32 beside 32×32 at medium — surfaced by this ruling's own fill change, which paints the box the toggle actually claims. The marker needed no new API: an icon-only toggle already MUST carry its accessible name (`label` on `ToggleButton`, `aria-label` on a `ToggleButtonGroup.Item` — both documented contracts), so both composers stamp that presence as `data-icon-only`, and one rule gives it the IconButton square — `min-width: var(--base-button-height)` with `padding-inline: 0`, the zero side padding being what lets the floor BIND as a square instead of going oblong on glyph + padding. Measured after: toolbar toggles 24×24 / 32×32 / 40×40 beside identical icon buttons; text-bearing toggles are unaffected (no `label`, no stamp — their width stays their content's).

### button-cluster

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`, `LAYOUT`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-30.

**A `ButtonGroup` holds one flat gap between its controls, and its alignment follows the end that the solid action anchors.**

**Gap.** A flat `gap="2"` (8px) at every size tier, which does not scale with the controls. The tiers move the Radix size step of each component and never `--scaling` (`LANE_STEPS` in `SizeContext`), so `--space-2` stays 8px while the controls grow.

**Exception.** `gap="0"` is the one sanctioned override, and the gap follows the fill, not the size. Tertiary controls paint no resting surface, so flush they read as one block, each with its own box and target ([control-box-per-step](#control-box-per-step)). Surface or solid controls set flush let fills and borders touch, which cramps the row or reads as a segmented control.

**Anchor.** The cluster reads `buttonOrder` from `Provider`, `primary-first` by default or `primary-last`, and moves the child with `priority="primary"` to that end. `primary-first` justifies the row to the start and `primary-last` to the end. The reorder is a DOM reorder, so tab order follows the visual order, and fragments are flattened first, so a mapped list of buttons counts as its buttons and not as one child.

**Overrides.**

- a per-cluster `order` overrides the system setting, for a destructive confirm that must read safe action first
- an explicit `justify` overrides the derived alignment
- with no solid child the author's order stays and no alignment is forced, because a row of equal utilities is a list

**Wired in.** `Dialog.Footer` ([standard-dialog](#standard-dialog)), the `EmptyState` action row, the `Toast` action and dismiss pair, and the `DoDont` specimen row of the story kit.

**Not covered.** The cluster resolves no size and seeds none ([container-size-seeding](#container-size-seeding)), so a mixed-size cluster is an authoring mistake. A toolset that acts on one surface is a `Toolbar`, with one tab stop and arrow-key navigation ([toolbar-slots](#toolbar-slots)), where the cluster keeps one tab stop per control.

**Changed from.** Each screen chose its own gap and alignment. The `DoDont` row of the story kit used a gap of `"2"` at small and `"3"` above, deleted on 2026-06-20 when the cluster shipped, because the flat step read well at every size.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-30. The anchor rule dates from 2026-07-09.

- [aschild-or-type-error](#aschild-or-type-error) gives `ButtonGroup` an `asChild` seam that orders the children of the slotted element.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **The cluster owns two decisions — one flat gap, and an anchor the alignment follows (2026-07-30).** `ButtonGroup` is a `Flex` that exists so that no screen re-decides either of them. Both rules are recorded here because a History card that states a rule and cites nothing is indistinguishable from a story's own opinion. **Rule one — the space between controls is a flat `gap="2"` (8px), the same at every size tier, and deliberately does NOT scale with the controls.** The tiers move each component's Radix size *step*, never `--scaling` (`LANE_STEPS` in `SizeContext`), so `--space-2` resolves to the same 8px at small, medium and large while the controls beside it grow. **A size-relative gap was tried and reverted, and the reverted code is the evidence:** the story kit's `DoDont` carried `const specimenGap = useUISize() === "small" ? "2" : "3"` under the comment *"a fixed step reads too loose beside small controls"*, and it was deleted the day the cluster shipped (2026-06-20) on the finding that the flat step read well at every size — the ladder bought nothing and added a second thing to keep in sync.
