Making it a component rather than a number is the point: the value is decided once here instead of retyped per screen. **The one sanctioned override is `gap="0"`, and the rule for reaching for it is that the gap follows the FILL, not the size.** A `priority="tertiary"` control paints no resting surface, so there is nothing for a gap to hold apart and 8px between three ghost glyphs reads as a hole; flush, the three read as one utility block, and each still owns its own box and its own target ([control-box-per-step](#control-box-per-step)). The inverse is the documented don't: surface or solid controls set flush let their fills and borders touch, so the row cramps or reads as a segmented control it is not. **Rule two — the solid action anchors an END of the cluster, and the alignment is DERIVED from that anchor rather than set beside it (ruled 2026-07-09).** The cluster reads the system `buttonOrder` — `primary-first` (the default) or `primary-last`, set once on `Provider` — and moves the child carrying `priority="primary"` to that end; `primary-first` justifies the cluster to the start, `primary-last` to the end. One setting therefore decides both which side the solid sits on and which edge of its container the row hangs from, which is what stops a screen pinning an order and forgetting the alignment. **The reorder is a DOM reorder**, so tab order follows the visual order rather than the authored one. **The anchor search flattens one level of fragments first** — a mapped list of buttons arrives as `<>…</>`, and without the flatten that fragment counts as ONE child: a two-button fragment reports no solid, the cluster silently falls through to author's-order-no-anchor, and a confirm panel renders Cancel-first while every other panel reads primary-first (the observed failure that put the flatten in the component, where it fixes every call site at once). A per-cluster `order` prop overrides the system setting — the case it exists for is a destructive confirm that must read safe-action-first whatever the global says — and an explicit `justify` overrides the derived alignment. **No solid child → no opinion:** the author's order is left untouched and no alignment is forced at all, because a row of equal-weight utilities is a list, and anchoring one of them would be the component inventing a hierarchy the page did not ask for. **Where both rules are already wired**, so those surfaces inherit them instead of re-implementing them: `Dialog.Footer` ([standard-dialog](#standard-dialog)), `EmptyState`'s action row, `Toast`'s action-plus-dismiss pair, and the story kit's own `DoDont` specimen row. **What the cluster is NOT:** it resolves no size and therefore seeds none ([container-size-seeding](#container-size-seeding)) — every control inside reads the ambient control lane directly, which makes a mixed-size cluster possible and an authoring mistake rather than something the component prevents; and it is not a toolbar — a cohesive toolset acting on one surface wants `Toolbar`'s `role="toolbar"`, its single tab stop and its arrow-key navigation ([toolbar-slots](#toolbar-slots)), where the cluster keeps a tab stop per control on purpose, these being actions a keyboard user reaches one at a time.

### box-law-scope

**Tags.** `SIZING`, `COMPONENTS`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-30.

**Every component that presents a single-row control takes one box per size step, 24, 32 or 40px, and a test measures it.**

**The box.** Steps 1, 2 and 3 resolve to 24, 32 and 40px against `--scaling`. These are the vendor's own values: `--base-button-height`, `--text-field-height`, `--select-trigger-height` and the segmented control's height all resolve to `--space-5`, `--space-6` and `--space-7`. A control off this ladder departs from the vendor's ladder, not from a preference of this system.

**Applies to.**

- Buttons and icon buttons ([control-box-per-step](#control-box-per-step)), toggles and toggle group items.
- Text fields, and the trigger and input rows of Select, MultiSelect, Typeahead, DateInput, DateRangeInput, DateTimeInput, TimeInput and NumberInput.
- Segmented controls, tokenizers, search bars and the command palette's input row.
- Every single-row control that ships after this ruling.
- A docs specimen of a control, which renders the real component, never a hand-drawn imitation.

**Composites.** The law binds each inner row of a composite, not the composite. The chat composer's dock is two rows, so each row takes the box and the dock does not. The test is whether the thing presents one row that a user presses or enters text in.

**Not covered.** Multi-line surfaces such as TextArea and the file dropzone, the checkbox, radio and switch glyphs, and the slider track. A control reachable only through a portal stays with its own behaviour suite.

**Guarded.** `_internal/Control box` renders each control unsized at all three tiers and asserts the measured height of the painting element against 24, 32 and 40px exactly. The expected values are local constants, never read from `SizeContext` or the theme, so a moved table fails the test. A new single-row control must join `CONTROL_BOX_MANIFEST` in that file, because a control missing from it is unguarded whether or not it is correct.

**Changed from.** [control-box-per-step](#control-box-per-step) set the box for the button family, so it read as a family rule. Measured on 2026-07-30, a populated Tokenizer and PowerSearch sat at 32, 40 and 48px, the command palette's input row at 40, 44 and 48px, and a hand-drawn Select stand-in on the ToggleButtonGroup page matched no declared height.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-30.

- [toggle-group-box](#toggle-group-box) gives a ToggleButtonGroup the step box for the group as a whole, with its members inside it.
- [nav-row-ladder](#nav-row-ladder) puts navigation rows on the Item family ladder, 32, 36 and 40px, outside this box.
- [control-box-per-step](#control-box-per-step), amended 2026-07-31, reads a control with `[data-inset]` as pinned to step 1 by rule, and the guard still measures it against step 1.
- [container-size-seeding](#container-size-seeding), amended 2026-07-31, removes a control's block padding inside a container footer, so the box holds the step there.
- [text-spacing-control-box](#text-spacing-control-box) makes the box a floor, so a label that wraps under user text spacing grows its control, and the guard measures the box at default text spacing.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **The one-box law is system-wide, and it is guarded (2026-07-30).** [control-box-per-step](#control-box-per-step) unified the *button* family on the vendor's box, and by naming a family it read as a family rule. It is not one. **A size step names ONE box — 24 / 32 / 40px against `--scaling` at steps 1 / 2 / 3 — and EVERY component that presents a single-row control honours it.** The vendor already agrees with itself here, which is what makes the number not ours to pick: `--base-button-height`, `--text-field-height` and `--select-trigger-height` are three separately-declared ladders that resolve the identical `--space-5` / `--space-6` / `--space-7` (verified in the vendor stylesheet, all three, at every step), the segmented control's own `height` is a fourth spelling of the same three spaces, and those spaces are `calc(24px * var(--scaling))`, `32px`, `40px`. A control that lands off 24 / 32 / 40 has therefore left the vendor's own ladder — it has not disagreed with a preference of ours. **In scope:** buttons and icon buttons ([control-box-per-step](#control-box-per-step)), toggles and toggle-group items, text fields, the Select / MultiSelect / Typeahead / DateInput / DateRangeInput / DateTimeInput / TimeInput / NumberInput trigger and input rows, segmented controls, tokenizers, search bars, the palette's input row — **and every single-row control that ships after this entry**, which is the half of the rule that carries the weight, because the deviations found today were in components that were never part of the family [control-box-per-step](#control-box-per-step) named. **Composites are governed at their inner row level, not at their own.** The chat composer's dock is two stacked rows: the law binds each ROW to 24 / 32 / 40 and says nothing about the dock, which is not a row control and has no business measuring like one. The test is whether the thing presents one row a user types into or presses — not whether it happens to be one element tall.
>
> **The deviations, and the cause of each in one line.** *Tokenizer* — `.rt-ds-tokenizer:has([data-tk-chip]) { padding-block: var(--space-1) }` added 4px a side the instant a chip existed, so the POPULATED state (the one every real use is in) sat exactly 8px off a `min-height` that was already the vendor's box: the guard measures **32 / 40 / 48 against 24 / 32 / 40**. The empty state was correct and the state that ships was not, which is why the bar looked right in every static specimen. *PowerSearch* — composes that same tokenizer surface, so it inherited the identical +8 without owning a rule of its own, and measures the same three numbers. *CommandPalette's input row* — a constant `padding: var(--space-3) var(--space-4)` and no box floor at all, so the row's height was its own padding plus whatever line-height the input resolved: **40 / 44 / 48**, a private ladder whose steps are not even evenly spaced, agreeing with the rest of the system only by coincidence. *ToggleButtonGroup's `SelectMock`* — a hand-painted stand-in for a Select on a docs page, drawn to a height nothing declared. **A docs specimen that imitates a control is the same defect in docs form**, and a mock cannot inherit a fix — which is exactly why it was still wrong after [control-box-per-step](#control-box-per-step) corrected every real control beside it. Specimens render the real component.
>
> **The enforcement, which is the reason this is a ruling rather than a restatement of [control-box-per-step](#control-box-per-step).** The law is GUARDED. `_internal/Control box` mounts each single-row control UNSIZED under all three tiers and asserts the measured `getBoundingClientRect().height` of the painting element against 24 / 32 / 40 **exactly**. The expectations are written out in that file as local constants and are deliberately NOT read from `SizeContext` or the theme: a probe that reads the same table the component reads agrees with it by construction and can never catch a table that moved. **A new single-row control MUST be added to that file's `CONTROL_BOX_MANIFEST`** — the manifest is the registration point, is commented as such, and a control missing from it is unguarded whether or not it happens to be correct. Twenty entries are in it at mint, covering every control named above; the palette's row is among them only because `isInline` renders the surface as a plain div, and that is the general condition — **anything that cannot be reached without opening a portal is out**, by rule rather than by oversight, and its open-state geometry stays with its own behavior suite. Also named out, so the boundary is on the record: multi-line surfaces (TextArea, the file dropzone), the checkbox / radio / switch glyph ladder, and the slider track — none of them present a row, so the law does not reach them. From here a deviation is a red test rather than a review discovery — which is the whole difference, [control-box-per-step](#control-box-per-step) having been right and still not stopping the next three.

### toggle-group-box

**Tags.** `SIZING`, `COMPONENTS`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-30.

**A `ToggleButtonGroup` is one control in its row, so the group owns the step box and its members sit one step down inside it.**

**The box.** The group's outer box, chrome included, is the step box: 24, 32 and 40px at steps 1, 2 and 3. A lone `ToggleButton` still claims the whole box ([control-box-per-step](#control-box-per-step)), so a toggle beside a group of three is a 32px control beside a 32px control.

**Members.** The group resolves step N and seeds its members step N-1 through `CONTROL_MEMBER_STEP`, floored at step 1, so a member renders 24, 24 and 32px. A member is a smaller button in glyph, box and pressed paint, centred in the tray, and the smallest target in any group is 24px.

**Tray.** The group paints its own container: `--ds-bg-subtle` with an inset `--ds-stroke-weak` hairline that costs no layout, cornered at `--ds-radius-2`, `--ds-radius-2` and `--ds-radius-3`. The geometry follows `SegmentedControl`, the system's component with the same box model.

**Spacing.** At steps 2 and 3 the members keep a 4px gap and the tray a 4px `padding-inline`. At step 1 both are 0, the members tile the tray, and each end member takes the tray's radius on its outer side and a square corner against its neighbour, as `SegmentedControl` does at its small step.

**Unchanged.** The pressed paint, the weight-600 label cue, the `pressedIcon` face swap, the roving focus and the square icon-only member stay as they were.

**Mechanism.** The step rides on `data-size`, stamped from the size the component resolves, because the vendor declares `--base-button-height` on the button and a `div` cannot read it. `CONTROL_BOX_MANIFEST` measures the group root against the row ladder and a member against its own ladder of 24, 24 and 32px, and the Usage play compares the group's box with a real `Select` on the same page.

**Changed from.** The group was a flex row with a gap, so its box was its members' box. The docs drew a tray by hand that measured 38, 46 and 54px against a `Select` at 24, 32 and 40px.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-30. A correction the same night, before merge, made the members step down a full size, and an amendment in this entry on 2026-07-31 made the small step flush. No later ruling amends it.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **A ToggleButtonGroup is ONE control in its row, so the group owns the box and its members own a part of it (ruled 2026-07-30).** [box-law-scope](#box-law-scope) binds every single-row control to one box per step; it does not say what happens when a control is made of other controls, and the group is the first case where that matters. **The rule: the group's OUTER box — chrome included — is the step box, 24 / 32 / 40px at steps 1 / 2 / 3, and its members render inside it. A LONE `ToggleButton` still claims that whole box for itself ([control-box-per-step](#control-box-per-step)).** Put a single toggle beside a group of three and the toggle is a 32px control while the group is a 32px control — not a 32px toggle beside a 46px cluster, which is what the row read as before. **The group therefore needs a container of its own**, and it had been renting one: `.rt-ds-toggle-group` was `display:flex` plus a gap, so its box was simply its members' box and nothing was left to be the control. The docs drew the missing container by hand — a `Box` with `padding: 6`, `--ds-bg-base`, a `--ds-stroke-weak` hairline and `--ds-radius-3`, in the Specimen, the DO card and the Props. **A story reaching for chrome three times is the component asking for it**; measured, that hand-drawn box was **38 / 46 / 54px** against the real `Select` beside it at **24 / 32 / 40**. It is deleted from all three specimens and the component paints it.
>
> **[Partially superseded the same night, before merge — the SegmentedControl measurements here are accurate and the root-owns-the-step-box model STANDS; only the members-full-height conclusion drawn from them was reversed by the correction at this entry's end: members STEP DOWN a full size.]** **The geometry is the segmented control's, measured rather than picked.** `SegmentedControl` is the system's existing component with exactly this box model, so it is the spec source and not a comparison: measured on all three tiers, its root is `height: var(--space-5 / --space-6 / --space-7)` = **24 / 32 / 40** with **zero** block padding, its items are **FULL-HEIGHT inside that root** (24/24, 32/32, 40/40 root/item), and the entire visual inset is a constant **1px** on the selected paint — its indicator's `inset: 1px`, cornered `max(0.5px, radius - 1px)`, giving 22 / 30 / 38 painted inside 24 / 32 / 40. Its radius ladder is `--radius-2` at steps 1–2 and `--radius-3` at step 3 (4 / 4 / 6), and its label font is the step's own (12 / 14 / 16). The group takes all of it: root `min-height: var(--ds-space-24/32/40)` — the same `--space-5/6/7`, in our spelling — `--ds-radius-2 / --ds-radius-2 / --ds-radius-3`, and members at the group's own resolved step. **The members do NOT seed a step down**, because the vendor does not: a segment renders at the root's step and only its paint is inset, and seeding down would have shrunk the glyphs and the targets to buy an inset that costs neither.
>
> **[Superseded the same night, before merge — see the correction at this entry's end: members STEP DOWN a full size; the paint-inset mechanism described here never shipped.]** **The step-1 target answer is the vendor's own, and it is why the inset is paint and never layout.** A 24px box cannot hold a 24px target if the chrome takes real space, so the chrome takes none: the member keeps its full border box ([control-box-per-step](#control-box-per-step)'s `min-height: var(--base-button-height)` binds unfought — that floor IS the target), and a **1px transparent border plus `background-clip: padding-box`** insets every fill it draws — rest, hover and the [toggle-button](#toggle-button) `[data-state="on"]` pressed tint alike — by exactly the vendor's 1px, with the browser deriving the painted corner by the same subtraction the vendor writes out by hand. Measured after: root **24 / 32 / 40**, member hit box **24×24 / 32×32 / 40×40** (icon-only members still square, `data-icon-only` untouched), member paint **22 / 30 / 38**. **Two second-order effects, both real and both fixed here.** The 1px border lands in the member's height budget, and the vendor Button's 4px block padding plus a 16px line box already totalled exactly 24 at the floor step — so a TEXT member tipped to **26px**, caught on the time-zone specimen. `padding-block: 0` on a member removes the coincidence and lets the floor do the work (intrinsic 18, `min-height` 24); it is also the segmented item label's own shape, which carries side padding and no block padding for the same reason — the root owns the height. And the hairline is an **inset box-shadow, not a border**: a border would eat 2px of the box and push the members under the step, where an inset shadow costs no layout and lands in exactly the 1px the members' paint is inset by. The segmented control needs no such line because its segments tile the whole tray; a gapped group does, so the tray is `--ds-bg-subtle` (the sunken fill — the segmented root's recessed surface in our tokens) plus `inset 0 0 0 1px --ds-stroke-weak`.
>
> **What did NOT change, deliberately.** The 4px gap stays: members are spaced and distinct, not flush, and a flush segmented control remains `SegmentedControl`'s job. `padding-inline` is that same `--space-1` so an end member sits off the tray edge by about what separates it from its neighbour (5px painted at the ends against 6px between). **Amended 2026-07-31 by ruling — the SMALL step goes flush, and the sentence above now holds at steps 2 and 3 only.** The member ladder floors at step 1 (a step-1 tray holds step-1 members; there is no step 0), so at that step the member is exactly as tall as the tray and the block inset is already zero — while the 4px gap and the 4px caps kept the INLINE inset. One axis spaced and the other flush is visible: a horizontal gap with no vertical gap reads as a mistake. At `[data-size="1"]` the gap and `padding-inline` go to **0**, the members tile the tray edge to edge, and a selected fill reaches all four of the tray's edges. The end members then need corners, and the treatment is **matched, not clipped** — the tray's own radius on each end member's outer side, square against its neighbour — which is exactly what `SegmentedControl` does at its own small tier (root radius 4px, first item `4px 0 0 4px`, last `0 4px 4px 0`, middles square); clipping the tray over the members' 3px radius instead would leave a sliver of tray showing inside each end fill. Measured after at small: root 24px tall, members at x = 0 / 24 with the root's full width, first corner `4px 0 0 4px`, last `0 4px 4px 0` — identical to the segmented control beside it. Steps 2 and 3 are untouched, because there the member IS a genuinely smaller button inside a larger tray and the inset is the point. The pressed paint, the weight-600 label cue, the `pressedIcon` face swap, the roving focus and the `data-icon-only` square all survive untouched — the ruling moves boxes, not behaviour. **The step is carried on `data-size`**, stamped from the size the component already resolves, because the vendor declares `--base-button-height` on the BUTTON element and a div cannot read it — the same stamping Calendar, FileInput and Pagination use. **Guarded on both levels**: `CONTROL_BOX_MANIFEST` now measures the group ROOT (the box a Select lines up with) *and* a member inside it (the target the container must not eat), 21 entries; both were proven to go red before being trusted green. The Usage play adds the equality directly — the group's box against a real `Select`'s on the same page, at whatever tier is running — because a control claiming to be one control in a row is a claim about the row, not about a constant. **Corrected same night by ruling, before it ever merged: the members step DOWN a full size.** As shipped now: the group resolves step N and seeds its members step N-1 — a medium tray holds SMALL buttons (24-in-32), a large tray holds medium ones (32-in-40), and the floor step holds itself (24-in-24; no step 0 exists, the same floor collapse every secondary tier in the system uses). A member is a genuinely smaller button — glyph, box, pressed paint, all the lower step's — centred in the tray by the tray, with the root's 4px inline caps. Targets hold: the smallest member anywhere is 24px (the [control-box-per-step](#control-box-per-step) floor is the member's own). The guard's member entry carries its own ladder ({24, 24, 32}) — the one manifest entry that deliberately does not ride the row box, and the distinction is the point: a member is a part of a control, not a control in the row.

### nav-row-ladder

**Tags.** `SIZING`, `COMPONENTS`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-31.

**A navigation row rides the Item family's ladder of 32, 36 and 40px, and the collapsed SideNav rail measures what the expanded rows measure at every tier.**

**Why.** Navigation carries more prominence than a standard control. [box-law-scope](#box-law-scope) binds every single-row control to one box per step, and [toggle-group-box](#toggle-group-box) made an exception for the group member. Navigation is the second family that is not a control standing in a row.

**Derivation.** The ladder is a derivation, not a token. Each rung is `--line-height-N` plus 2 × `--ds-space-8`, which gives 16 + 16, 20 + 16 and 24 + 16 at steps 1, 2 and 3. Both terms carry `--scaling`, and `max(…, 24px)` keeps the absolute 24px pointer floor under the rung, the same shape [control-box-per-step](#control-box-per-step) writes on `.rt-BaseButton`. No 36px literal exists in the implementation.

**Glyph and lane.** The rail glyph inherits the nav's own font size, as the leading icon of an expanded row does, so rail and row glyphs match at every tier: 14, 16 and 18px. `SideNav.tsx` resolves the rail's step on the text lane, the lane `Item` and the collapse button read.

**Guarded.** `src/foundations/boxLaw.ts` judges a SideNav navigation row, collapsed or expanded, on `NAV_LADDER_PX`, written out as local constants. `_internal/SideNav behavior` → `NavLadderTracksBothStates` mounts both states at all three tiers and asserts the ladder, and, with no constant at all, that collapsed equals expanded.

**Not covered.** The ruling covers `SideNav` only. `TopNav` rows keep the sizes they had, and the control box, [control-box-per-step](#control-box-per-step) and [box-law-scope](#box-law-scope) stay unamended.

**Changed from.** An earlier change on 2026-07-31 removed a private 24px floor from the rail so the control box law could reach it. That put the collapsed rail on 24, 32 and 40px beside expanded rows of 32, 36 and 40px. This ruling reverses that change, because the control box was the wrong family for navigation.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-31. No later ruling amends it.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **Navigation carries more prominence than a standard control, so a nav row rides the Item family's ladder — and a collapsed rail rides it too (ruled 2026-07-31).** [box-law-scope](#box-law-scope) binds every single-row control to one box per step and [toggle-group-box](#toggle-group-box) carved out the group member; this is the second family that is not a control standing in a row. **The rule: a navigation row is an ITEM-family row — 32 / 36 / 40px at small / medium / large — and the COLLAPSED SideNav rail measures exactly what the EXPANDED rows measure, in both states, at every tier.**
>
> **The ladder is a DERIVATION, not a token, and the question "is 36 a token?" is answered by that.** 36 is not a value anyone picked and it is not in the space scale — it is what an Item row already computes: the row's own line box plus the Item block padding on both sides, `--line-height-N` + 2 × `--ds-space-8`, which is 16+16 / 20+16 / 24+16 at steps 1 / 2 / 3. The rail is built the same way — `min-height`/`min-width: max(calc(var(--line-height-N) + 2 * var(--ds-space-8)), 24px)` on the rail button, with the base rung at step 2 and steps 1 and 3 stated beside it, the identical shape (and the identical three leadings) as the Item label ladder directly above it in `components.css`, so the two cannot drift apart. **No 36px literal exists anywhere in the implementation.** It is the same mechanism `SideNavCollapseButton` already derived its own height from, which is what made the rail the odd member of its own rail. **It scales by construction:** both terms are `calc(Npx * var(--scaling))`, so the ladder moves with a consumer's scaling knob, and `max(…, 24px)` keeps GUIDELINES §9's absolute pointer floor under it — the same shape [control-box-per-step](#control-box-per-step) writes on `.rt-BaseButton`. **The glyph is the nav's own text**, inherited rather than restated: an expanded row's leading icon is a 1em glyph reading the nav's font-size, and the rail button now reads the same one, so rail and row glyphs are equal by construction at every tier (measured 14 / 16 / 18px) where the vendor's `.rt-IconButton:where(.rt-r-size-N)` type ramp had the rail a step behind the rows it stands in for (12 / 14 / 16). The rail resolves its step on the TEXT lane — the lane `Item` and the collapse button already read — stated in `SideNav.tsx` rather than inherited from `IconButton`'s control-lane default; the two lanes resolve the same step at every tier, so this moves no number and makes the rail read its size from the lane it belongs to.
>
> **This REVERSES the conform of 2026-07-31, and the reason is that the control box was the wrong family for navigation.** That change deleted a private 24px floor from the rail so [control-box-per-step](#control-box-per-step)'s law could reach it, which put the collapsed rail on 24 / 32 / 40 — correct against the control box, and wrong against the rows beside it: a 24px rail row under the small tier's 32px expanded rows, a 32px rail row under 36px rows at medium. The defect was never the floor; it was judging a nav row on the control ladder at all. Measured before: **24 / 32 / 40 collapsed against 32 / 36 / 40 expanded**. After: **32 / 36 / 40 in both states**, glyphs 14 / 16 / 18 in both.
>
> **Guarded on both runners.** `boxLaw.ts` gains a third rule beside `row` and `member`: a `.rt-BaseButton` inside `.rt-ds-sidenav` — collapsed or not — is judged on `NAV_LADDER_PX`, written out there as local constants with the derivation in the comment, for the same reason every other number in that file is typed out rather than read from `SizeContext` (a probe that recomputes the component's own derivation agrees with it by construction and can never catch a derivation that moved). Proven to go red before being trusted green: forcing one rail button back to the control ladder's 32px at the medium tier reports `BROKEN-BOX` against the nav ladder's 36. `_internal/SideNav behavior` gains `NavLadderTracksBothStates`, which mounts both regimes under all three tiers and asserts two separate things — the literal ladder, and (with no constant at all) that collapsed equals expanded, which is the half of the ruling that would survive the whole ladder moving. It too was proven red against the old 24 / 32 / 40.
>
> **Scope: `SideNav` only.** `TopNav`'s bar is under a separate open question and is deliberately untouched by this entry — its rows still ride what they rode. Nothing outside a `.rt-ds-sidenav` changes; the control box is unmoved and [control-box-per-step](#control-box-per-step) / [box-law-scope](#box-law-scope) are unamended.

### docs-page-header

**Tags.** `DOCUMENTATION`. **Ruled.** 2026-07-31.

**Every docs page opens with a `PageHeader` whose title names the component or topic and then the page's role, and whose standfirst is the file's one definition.**

**Title.**

- `<PageHeader>` is the first child of the story's `<Page>`, also when the `Page` sits inside a local wrapper.
- The subject is the component's name as `registry.json` spells it, the same on every story of that component. A file the registry does not know fails.
- On a Foundations page the subject is the topic, the last segment of `meta.title`.
- Every title appends its role after a space, a middle dot (U+00B7) and a space, such as "Button · Usage" and "Carousel · Props".
- A role never stands alone and never leads, and an editorial phrase is never a title.

**Headings.** `PageHeader` renders the h1 and `Section` the h2, so the h1 names the subject and the first `Section` names what the page holds. A nested `Section` stays h2, a heading the content brings takes h3, and a specimen title takes bold `<Text>`.

**Standfirst.** `standfirst` is the file's single `DEFINITION` constant, which every story of the component references. A story with a distinct job may append one sentence after it, never replace it.

**Exceptions.** A story whose role is its subject, such as Changelog or Decisions, keeps the bare name. The guard exempts two stories that are not docs pages: `Index`, whose header names the system, and the `FailLoudProbe` story on Foundations Colors, which renders no `Page`.

**Why.** A page that names its tab tells the reader the one thing it is not. Hand-typed definitions of one component drift into slightly different components.

**Guard.** `src/foundations/page-header.node-check.ts` holds every exported story in each story file under `src/components/ui` and `src/foundations` whose name does not begin with an underscore. It reads the story's render through the compiler API, and an exemption that names a missing story fails too.

**Changed from.** [docs-page-spine](#docs-page-spine) fixed the order of a page's stories and left its opening unspecified. Measured on 2026-07-31, 271 of the 341 component stories opened with no title, and 11 of the 70 titled ones named the story role.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-07-31.

- Amended 2026-07-31 in this entry: the role joins the title as a suffix, the page title takes h1 rank, and the Spacing topic takes the name "Spacing & radius".
- Amended 2026-08-01 in this entry: every page carries its role, and the bare title on a primary page ends.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **A docs page names its subject before it says anything else, and the subject is the COMPONENT — never the story you clicked to reach it (2026-07-31).** [docs-page-spine](#docs-page-spine) fixed the story *spine* (History → content → Props) and left the page *opening* unspecified, so it drifted the way an unspecified thing does. Measured across the 100 user-facing story files the day this was ruled: **271 of the 341 component stories opened with no title at all** — straight into a `<Section>`, a specimen, or a bare diagram — and the 70 that did carry a `<PageHeader>` were split between two conventions that cannot both be right. **57 named the component; 11 named the STORY ROLE** (`title="Props"` on Carousel, MobileNav, SideNav, Thumbnail, TopNav; `title="Usage"` on Lightbox and Tokenizer; PowerSearch doing it four times over, on Anatomy, Usage, Keyboard and Props); **2 named the story's topic editorially** (Slider's `"The value box"` and `"Detents"`). A reader landing on `System/Carousel → Props` was told the page was called "Props", which is the one thing it is not. **The split was tier-shaped, and inverted:** Foundations 14/14 titled, lite components 49/136 (36%), full components 21/205 (10%) — the pages carrying the MOST content were the least likely to say what they were about, because a lite file's single Usage story got the header and a full file's five stories shared none of it. **Amended same night — the rule's own second half crosses to Foundations.** The retitles created heading-identical sibling pages (Motion→Integration and Icons→Gallery each rendered ONE heading, their topic's, indistinguishable from their siblings' — the exact failure this entry was minted to kill, one tier up). Part (3) therefore binds Foundations too: every Foundations story's FIRST Section names what the page holds, so the tree is H1 topic → H2 page-role on every page, single-page topics included.
>
> **The rule, in four parts.** (1) **Every docs story opens with `<PageHeader>` as the FIRST child of its `<Page>`** — not the second, not inside the first `Section`, not tucked under a local wrapper. Token's Usage sits inside a `DemoNav` that mutes its link specimens; the header still goes first inside the `Page`, not first inside the wrapper. (2) **`title` is the component's name, spelled exactly as `registry.json` spells it, and IDENTICAL on every story of that component.** **[Second clause superseded the same night — see the suffix amendment below: the SUBJECT stays identical and registry-spelled on every story; the full title appends · the story’s role on every non-primary page.]** The registry is the authority for what a thing is called ([component-registry](#component-registry)), not the story's own opinion; a page whose file the registry does not know has no authority at all and fails rather than self-certifying off its own filename. (3) **A story role is never a title, and an editorial phrase is never a title.** **[Refined by the suffix amendment below: a role never stands alone as a title and never leads it — it may only FOLLOW the subject, `Name · Role`.]** The role is carried one level down, by the page's first `Section` — History opens on "Decisions", Anatomy on "Anatomy" / "The parts", Keyboard on "Keyboard" — which gives every page the same two-line tree: **h1 names the component, h2 names what this page holds.** That tree is also why the role cannot move up: `PageHeader` renders the h1 and `Section` the h2, so a role in the header would make the tab the document's subject and the component a subsection of it. (The page title outranks everything on its page: a story renders in the preview iframe, its own document, so the manager's hidden "Storybook" h1 is not above it and there is no borrowed root to rank under. A heading the CONTENT brings with it — an EmptyState or ClickableCard rendering its own — takes h3 under a Section, while a nested `Section` stays h2 (Sections are peer bands, not an outline hierarchy); a SPECIMEN title takes bold `<Text>`, because it is content being demonstrated rather than a rung of the outline.) (4) **`standfirst` is the file's single `DEFINITION` constant** — one module-level `const DEFINITION = <>…</>;` per component, referenced by every story on the page. This is the anti-drift mechanism and the reason the rule is worth a ruling: four hand-typed definitions of one component are four things to keep in sync and, in practice, four slightly different components. A story with a genuinely distinct job MAY append ONE sentence after `{DEFINITION}` (the Props's "the row below is the system's one switch shape…"); it may not replace it.
>
> **Foundations pages are titled with their TOPIC** — the last segment of `meta.title`, so `Foundations/Colors` reads "Colors" and every story under one topic shares it, exactly as a component's stories do. **[Suffix amendment: a multi-story topic now suffixes EVERY story — none is primary — while a single-story topic stays bare.]** The editorial titles this replaced were the same defect in the other direction: "Colour roles", "Type scale", "Spacing & radius", "Icon gallery", "Enforced constraints", "Reading measure", "A live Popover on our tokens" and "Elevation — one ladder, two expressions" each named the story rather than the topic, so the sidebar and the page disagreed about what the reader was looking at. The old editorial line is not lost — it opens the standfirst, which is where a page-specific angle belongs.
>
> **Amended 2026-07-31, before merge — three rulings on this standard the night after it was minted: the role joins the title as a suffix, the page title takes document rank as an h1, and the Spacing topic widens.** (1) The identical-titles clause is superseded: **the primary page keeps the bare subject, and every other story titles itself `Subject · Role`** — “Button · Anatomy”, “Carousel · Props” — separator space–MIDDLE DOT–space (U+00B7, byte-verified `20 C2 B7 20`, and the guard builds it from the code point so a look-alike ‧/•/∙ cannot creep in). **[The bare-primary rule in this clause lived one night — superseded by the 2026-08-01 amendment below: every page is labelled.]** A component’s primary page was **Usage** — the one page that carries the definition alone; a Foundations topic keys on its landable-story count — more than one and every story is suffixed, none being primary (“Motion · Durations”, “Motion · Integration”), exactly one and it stays bare (Elevation). The subject half still obeys parts (2)–(3) in full: registry-spelled, never a role, never editorial — a role may follow the subject, never replace or lead it. 258 titles rewritten by one idempotent codemod; the guard’s P3 gained the three named variants listed below, each proven able to go red before being trusted. (2) The heading tree shifted up one rank to what part (3) now describes: `PageHeader` h2→**h1**, `Section` h3→**h2** — the kit’s ONLY two semantic headings — with the corpus swept for deeper ranks (none remain; maximum heading depth anywhere is 3) and specimen titles converted to bold `<Text>`. Measured pixel-neutral: Radix’s `rt-Heading rt-r-size-N` classes fully override the UA heading styles, so only the tag name changes. Two knock-ons caught and fixed — ClickableCard and EmptyState Propss render the live specimen between the h1 and the first Section, so the specimen’s own heading became a rank skip; both pin the specimen heading to h2, EmptyState gaining a `headingAs` prop that mirrors ClickableCard’s exactly. axe `heading-order` + `empty-heading` + `page-has-heading-one`: **685 stories, zero violations, both colour lanes.** (3) The widening ruling reinstated one entry from the replaced-titles list above as a TOPIC NAME: the Spacing topic is now titled **“Spacing & radius”** (meta.title and storySort both), because the page genuinely documents both ladders — a topic rename, not an editorial title.
>
> **Amended 2026-08-01 — the bare-primary exception is dead: EVERY page is labelled.** A title that does not say which page it is reads as a missing label, not as a hierarchy. Usage pages now title `Name · Usage` (90 files, one codemod); the four single-story Foundations topics whose sidebar leaf named something the title never said take their suffix — **Elevation · Levels, Colors · Swatches, Spacing & radius · Scale, Enforcement · Contract**. The ONE carve-out is the degenerate double: a story whose role IS the subject (Changelog, Decisions) keeps the bare name — “Changelog · Changelog” would distinguish nothing, and the bare name already labels the page fully. The guard’s `suffix-on-primary-page` variant died with the exception; `suffix-missing` now binds every page, and both new directions were proven red before being trusted (a bare “Button” reports suffix-missing; “Changelog · Changelog” fails expecting the bare name).
>
> **Guarded by `src/foundations/page-header.node-check.ts`** (node lane, alongside story-order / token-rows / registry), binding every exported story in every non-underscore `*.stories.tsx` under `src/components/ui` and `src/foundations`. Eight rules, each with its own named message: **P1** the story reaches a `<Page>`; **P2** `<PageHeader>` is its first child, the message naming what occupies the slot instead; **P4** — checked BEFORE P3, and reported separately, because it is the regression class that actually shipped — the title’s SUBJECT (everything before any ` · `) is a bare story role (`History | Anatomy | Usage | Keyboard | MenuStates | QueueStates | Props | Overview`), the page naming its tab instead of its subject; **P3** the title is not exactly the standard — the named variant `suffix-missing` (a bare title — the pre-suffix state, which reads as correct in review) plus the plain wrong name; **P5** the standfirst is present and non-empty; **P6** a component story’s standfirst hand-types its definition instead of referencing the file’s `DEFINITION` constant; **U** a story export missing its `Story` annotation — caught by diffing the file’s exports against the scan’s own story list, so an untyped story cannot silently escape the rules; **E** an exemption naming a story that no longer exists. It is a compiler-API scan, not a line regex, because a story's render resolves through three routes — the story's own `render`, `meta.render`, and `meta.component` (which every Foundations page uses: `export const Index: Story = {}` renders `SystemIndex`) — and the `Page` itself can sit under a local wrapper or behind a bare component reference (`render: () => <MeasureDemo />`); a text scan sees none of that. **Exactly two exemptions, each carrying its reason in the file, and both exempt for being not-a-docs-page rather than for being inconvenient:** `Index` (the front door — its header names the system, "Design system", which neither the registry rule nor the topic rule can express) and `Foundations/Colors → FailLoudProbe` (a fail-loud negative probe that renders one deliberately-unmapped swatch and no `<Page>` at all). The set is the audit trail, so it is held true both ways: a story that wants an exemption and is not in it simply fails, and an entry naming a story that no longer exists fails too — a stale exemption is an unguarded page wearing a permission slip. Every rule was proven able to go red before being trusted green, against a conforming file.

### ui-polish-ruleset

**Tags.** `MOTION`, `TYPOGRAPHY`, `CONTRIBUTING`. **Ruled.** 2026-08-01.

**The system adopts a reviewed set of interface-polish rules, and records each adopted rule against the layer that enforces it.**

**Layers.** A guard fails the code, a paint rule sits once in `components.css`, a default reaches every instance with no opt-in, and guidance lives in `docs/GUIDELINES.md` and in review. An adopted rule with no layer named is a preference, not a rule.

**Guard.** `src/foundations/loose-values.node-check.ts` holds two motion rules, across the components and the token, theme and search layers:

- `transition` and `transition-property` never carry the keyword `all`.
- `will-change` names only `transform`, `opacity`, `filter` or `auto`, checked entry by entry, and the CSS-wide keywords pass.

The guard reads CSS without regard to case and TSX with regard to case. It opens `.tsx` and `.css` files only, so a `.ts` file and a value built in a template literal escape it.

**Paint and defaults.** A number that updates in place takes `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`, declared in `components.css` and never inline. Two sites take it as a default: every `.rt-Badge`, which covers the `+N` of `OverflowList`, and every `.rt-TextFieldInput[type="number"]`. `TABULAR_SITES` in `src/components/ui/_tabular-figures.stories.tsx` lists every adopter, and it fails when a site loses its declaration, when another rule outranks it, or when a new site goes unregistered. The rule holds per digit: a value that gains a digit still widens, so reserve space with a `min-width` where that matters.

**In the guidelines.** `docs/GUIDELINES.md` states:

- the Figures rule, where its declaration goes, and the three places an inline `fontVariantNumeric` stays right
- the `transition` and `will-change` rules
- that text smoothing ships on the theme root and takes no second declaration
- a nudge of at most 1px where geometric centring reads off, once a fix to the SVG is ruled out
- that shadows complement a boundary, so a boundary that accessibility needs keeps an opaque `--ds-stroke-*`

**Not built.** Each item stays on the record, so no reader mistakes it for an oversight:

- deferred: a media edge ring, a neutral alpha inset ring on image surfaces, which would add a token
- deferred: text-wrap defaults, `balance` on `Heading` and `pretty` on prose
- deferred: press-scale, an opt-in compress on one consequential button, which would add a ruling and a motion value
- deferred: touch hit-areas of at least 44 by 44 pixels under `pointer: coarse`, with visible geometry unchanged
- open: the enter animation of the clear control of a field, which appears as a cut until the maintainer decides
- open: the scope of `filter` blur in the table of animatable properties, escalated to the maintainer

**Dropped.** The icon cross-fade on `ToggleButton`. The pressed icon swaps instantly, and a reopening needs a new decision. The 24 by 24 pointer floor of [type-and-target-density](#type-and-target-density) stands unchanged.

**Changed from.** The system held no adopted polish ruleset, and [static-table](#static-table) kept a hand-written roster of tabular-figure adopters, which this ruling deleted in favour of `TABULAR_SITES`.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-08-01. No later ruling amends it. A deferred rule that ships extends this entry in place, never a second adoption ruling, and the text-wrap defaults amend this entry when they ship.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **The UI-polish ruleset is adopted, recorded by LAYER — where a rule is enforced is the half that stays useful (2026-08-01).** A reviewed set of interface-polish rules was cross-referenced against the system rule by rule; most were already met and needed nothing. Each adopted rule is recorded below against the layer that actually holds it — a **guard** (a test refuses the code), a **token/paint** rule (declared once in `components.css`), a **default** (every instance carries it without opting in), or **guidance** (GUIDELINES states it and review carries it). "Adopted" with no layer named is a preference rather than a rule, and that is the failure this entry exists to prevent.
>
> **Guard layer — two motion-hygiene rules, deliberately wider than the guard's own scope.** `src/foundations/loose-values.node-check.ts` gains rules 4 and 5 (its header docblock's "three drift vectors" becomes five): `transition` / `transition-property` may not carry the bare token `all` — a wildcard animates whatever happens to change, layout included, and silently absorbs every property a later edit adds to the rule — and `will-change` may name only `transform`, `opacity`, `filter` or `auto` (the reset value), matched per entry of its comma list — the CSS-wide keywords (`inherit` / `initial` / `unset` / `revert` / `revert-layer`) pass too, since they are universal CSS machinery rather than a hint this system has a view on. Both read the CSS spelling and the camelCase TSX one, case-INSENSITIVELY for CSS (where property names and keyword values are case-insensitive per spec, so `TRANSITION: all` is a live declaration) and case-SENSITIVELY for TSX (where an object key is not, so `WILLCHANGE: "top"` sets nothing and reporting it would report a non-defect). **Rules 4-5 scan wider than rules 1-3 on purpose:** the token-file exemption is a claim about palettes and the spacing scale, and neither rationale reaches a transition or a compositor hint, so these two also cover `src/tokens/*.css`, `src/theme/**` and `src/powersearch/**`; the stories / `_storyKit` exemption still applies, and widening rules 1-3 is a named follow-up. **What the widening buys today is zero findings** — `transition: all` has no occurrences anywhere, and `will-change` has exactly one, `will-change: transform` on the Outline indicator's JS-positioned sliding bar, which the allowlist admits. These guards lock a status quo; they clean nothing up, and the file says so rather than implying a cleanup. Two reach limits are stated in the guard's own header instead of being left to be discovered: the scanner opens `.tsx` and `.css` ONLY, so a `.ts` file is invisible to every rule (nine of the ten files in `src/powersearch` are `.ts`), and a value built in a template literal evades the TSX matcher. Both rules register as GUARANTEED rows on `Foundations/Enforcement` carrying that same reach statement — a guard the enforcement page overstates is a fresh doc-lie.
>
> **Token/paint layer, plus two defaults — a number that updates in place is set in tabular figures.** `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`, declared in `components.css` and never inline in a component, on the nine sites the 2026-08-01 census found uncovered: `Pagination`'s info row and its page cells, `MultiSelect`'s panel status and its trigger's selected-count text, the `TextArea` `showCount` counter, `PowerSearch`'s result count, `NumberInput`'s value, `AvatarGroup`'s `+N` counter, `OverflowList`'s `+N`, `ChatToolCalls`' `+N`/`-N` diff counts, and the `ChatMessageMetadata` timestamp SLOT — the last of these carrying the rule on the container, because a slot that accepts arbitrary caller content cannot know what it will hold and `font-variant-numeric` inherits. **Two of the nine landed as DEFAULTS rather than as their own selectors:** `OverflowList`'s `+N` is covered by a blanket on `.rt-Badge` (Badge ships no counter API and its text is short, so the blanket costs nothing and reaches the chip for free), and `NumberInput` is targeted by TYPE — `.rt-TextFieldInput[type="number"]` — so every numeric field gets it, which also subsumed `Slider`'s private copy of the same declaration, since removed. **The adopter list is a manifest, not prose:** `TABULAR_SITES` in `src/components/ui/_tabular-figures.stories.tsx` registers all 19 shipped selectors and fails three ways — a registered site that loses its declaration, a declaration present but outranked (that arm mounts the real components and reads the RESOLVED value), and a new rule that takes the property unregistered. Painted glyph advance is measured at two sites only and the manifest says so: `Pagination`'s same-digit-count flip (the `TabularInfo` play in `_pagination.stories.tsx`, asserting `Range#getBoundingClientRect` width equality) and `Table`'s equal-length column. [static-table](#static-table) was amended in the same commit — its hand-kept adopter roster was wrong on the day it was written, and it is deleted rather than corrected, because a roster in the ledger needs editing on every future adoption. **Exact about what this buys:** the fix is per DIGIT, not per string. A value that gains a digit (9 to 10) still widens, and should; reserve the space with a `min-width` where that jump matters.
>
> **Guidance layer.** GUIDELINES §3 gains the Figures rule plus its two mechanics paragraphs — where the declaration goes (the selector must REACH the painting element; a container it inherits from is legitimate, an ancestor whose descendant resets the property is not), and the exactly three places an inline `fontVariantNumeric` is still right (a specimen or probe whose subject IS the property, a table of measured numbers, and a number a CALLER composes into a slot the system does not own — the last a gap marker that names its missing mechanism at each instance, not a licence). §7 gains the transition and `will-change` lines above. §3, §4 and §8 gain the three notes this ruleset's remaining rules reduce to: antialiasing already ships on the substrate root and is not to be re-solved; a nudge of ≤1px is sanctioned where geometric centering reads off, after fixing the SVG has been considered first; and shadows COMPLEMENT boundaries, so any boundary that must be visible for accessibility keeps an opaque `--ds-stroke-*` — the elevation ring is a single-digit-percent alpha and cannot reach the 3:1 non-text minimum. §7's motion text was corrected against the ledger rather than restated from the ruleset: the ambient-loop count (five loops run in the component layer; two are authored here), `--ds-ease-entry`'s use cell (open / state-change, never mount), the enter-fires-on-open rule with its one shipped deviation named out loud, the stagger claim reduced to the intra-list `--ds-stagger-step` with coarser tiers deliberately undocumented, the `--ds-ease-exit` site census, and the caveat that a keyframed open/close RESTARTS on interruption rather than reversing.
>
> **Deferred, not dropped — four rules, named here so the deferral is on the record rather than remembered.** **Media edge ring:** a pure-neutral alpha inset ring on image-rendering surfaces (Thumbnail, Avatar in image mode, Lightbox media, Carousel media), which would mint a token. **Text-wrap defaults:** `balance` on `Heading`, `pretty` on prose at the token layer. **Press-scale:** an opt-in, default-off tactile compress granted to a single consequential button, which would mint a ruling and a motion value. **Touch hit-areas:** invisible ≥44×44 targets under `pointer: coarse`, visible geometry unchanged.
>
> **Nothing in the system implements the media edge ring, press-scale or touch hit-areas.** Verified when this entry was written: no `--ds-stroke-media` and no `--ds-press-scale` exists anywhere in the repository, and the single `@media (pointer: coarse)` block in `components.css` is an iOS zoom guard (a 16px font-size floor on the CommandPalette input), not a hit-area extension. **The text-wrap defaults mint neither a token nor a ruling as scoped**, so when they ship they amend this entry rather than adding a new one. **One rule was DROPPED rather than deferred, and the distinction matters to anyone reading this list later:** the ruleset's `ToggleButton` icon cross-fade was decided against — the pressed-icon swap stays instant (ruled 2026-08-01). It is not pending; it is settled, and reopening it needs a new decision rather than a scheduling slot. **[type-and-target-density](#type-and-target-density)(c) is UNAMENDED:** the shipped target-size behaviour is the 24×24 pointer floor everywhere. No surface says the extension shipped.
>
> **Two items did NOT land, and are open rather than complete.** The field clear-✕ enter animation is not implemented — the clear affordances still appear as a cut, held until the maintainer decides. The `filter (blur)` scope statement for §7's animatable-properties table was deliberately not written: the bound as drafted turned out to be circular, and no shipped blur is animated, so the question was escalated rather than answered with a sentence that would have to be unwritten.
>
> **Amend this entry when a deferred task ships** — extended in place with what landed and at which layer, never a second adoption ruling. Two entries answering one question is how a ledger starts disagreeing with itself.

### text-element-attributes

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`. **Ruled.** 2026-08-12.

**`Text` keeps the attributes of each element its `as` prop selects, so `<Text as="label" htmlFor>` compiles.**

**Fix.** Radix types `Text` as a union over `as`: `span`, `div`, `label` and `p`. `TextProps` omits the props the wrapper replaces from each arm of that union separately, a distributive omit, so each element keeps its own attributes.

**Breaking patterns.** `TextProps` is a `type` alias under the same exported name, because an `interface` cannot extend a distributed union. No import changes, but two patterns no longer compile:

- `interface Foo extends TextProps`
- `declare module` merging onto `TextProps`

The supported replacement for both is `type Foo = TextProps & { … }`.

**Guarded.** `src/foundations/Text.type-check.tsx` holds both directions. Five valid forms must compile, and two `@ts-expect-error` lines prove the type accepts neither `htmlFor` on a `span` nor an unknown prop on any arm. `tsconfig.build.json` excludes the file, so it does not ship.

**Not covered.**

- On 2026-08-12, 104 story files and 12 other source files, several shipped components among them, imported the Radix `Text`. Rewrapping the shipped components would apply `useResolvedSize` twice, so neither set changed.
- Whether `Switch` takes a `label` prop of its own is a separate question. The asymmetry with `Checkbox`, which takes `label` and renders `Field.Root` itself, stands.

**Changed from.** `<Text as="label" htmlFor>` failed to compile with TS2322, while `as="label"` alone compiled. A consumer could build a labelled row with a plain `<label>` or the Radix `Text`, a peer dependency, but not with a label that follows the global UI size, because `useResolvedSize` and `Field.Root` were absent from the package's public entry point. The labelled-switch row the Switch page teaches compiled only because its story imported the Radix `Text`.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-08-12. No later ruling amends it.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **`Text` keeps its per-element attributes (2026-08-12).** Radix types `Text` as a union over `as` (`span | div | label | p`), and the wrapper applied `Omit<…, "size">` to it. `Omit` does not distribute over a union — it keeps only the keys every arm shares — so the per-element attributes were silently dropped and `<Text as="label" htmlFor>` failed to compile (`TS2322: Property 'htmlFor' does not exist`) while `as="label"` alone succeeded. **This was reachable from the system's own documentation:** the labelled-switch row is the pattern the Switch page teaches, it needs `htmlFor`, and it compiled only because that story imported Radix's `Text` instead of ours. **What a consumer could and could not do, stated exactly, because the blunter claim is false:** they could always build the row — a plain `<label htmlFor>` is HTML, and `@radix-ui/themes` is a **peer dependency**, so Radix's own `Text` is importable and is what the story used. What had no route was building it with a label that **follows the global UI size**: our `Text` resolves the text lane and rejected `htmlFor`, Radix's accepts `htmlFor` and ignores the lane, and `useResolvedSize` — the call that would restore it — is not exported (`src/index.ts` publishes only `type UISize` from `SizeContext`). `Field.Root` is unexported too, so the field route does not exist either. Fixed with a distributive omit. **`TextProps` becomes a `type` alias** (an `interface` cannot extend a distributed union) under the same exported name, so no consumer *import* changes — but it is a published name, so **two patterns break, named here rather than left to be discovered:** `interface Foo extends TextProps` no longer compiles, and `declare module` merging onto `TextProps` no longer compiles. The supported replacement for both is `type Foo = TextProps & { … }`; nothing in this repo uses either. `Text.type-check.tsx` locks both directions — five valid forms must compile, and two `@ts-expect-error` assertions prove the type was not widened into accepting `htmlFor` on a `span` or an unknown prop on any arm — and it is excluded from `tsconfig.build.json` so it does not ship. **Residuals, stated so this is not read as a sweep:** 104 story files still import Radix's `Text` (100 under `components/ui`, 5 under `foundations`, minus the one this change moved), as do 12 non-story source files including several shipped components; re-wrapping the latter would double-apply `useResolvedSize`, so neither set is touched here. Whether `Switch` should take a `label` prop of its own is a separate question and is **not** decided here — the asymmetry with `Checkbox` (which takes `label` and renders `Field.Root` itself) stands.

### disabled-paint-arm

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`, `ACCESSIBILITY`. **Ruled.** 2026-08-19.

**A component paint rule that outranks the disabled skin of Radix must carry its own `[data-disabled]` arm.**

**Why.** `.radix-themes .rt-ds-lightbox-control` set `background-color` and `color` in every state. At (0,2,0), and later in the cascade, it outranked the Radix ghost disabled rule at (0,1,0) and erased the disabled skin. The inert gallery arrow and its live neighbour differed only in `cursor: not-allowed`, which touch and keyboard users never receive, so the state rode one channel, against WCAG 1.4.1.

**Fix.** `.radix-themes .rt-ds-lightbox-control[data-disabled] { color: var(--ds-icon-disabled) }`. The scrim disc stays, so the control keeps its shape over any media, and the glyph drops to the existing disabled icon role, so no token is new. The disabled glyph reads 2.90:1 against the disc, the intended reading for a disabled control, and `--ds-icon-disabled` sits on the contrast-exempt list in `src/foundations/_assert.ts`.

**Scope.** A sweep of every renderable story, each control against a twin in the other state, found one true positive, this one. Two apparent hits are not defects:

- A disabled `TreeList` row dims its descendant `.rt-ds-item-content` to `opacity: 0.5`.
- The stop button of `ChatComposer` stays enabled by design while the composer around it is disabled.

Every other control repaints on `[data-disabled]`, dims by opacity, or adds no competing paint and leaves the Radix skin in force, as `Pagination` does.

**Guard.** `assertDisabledPaintDiffers` in `src/foundations/_disabledPaint.ts`, asserted at both ends of the range in the Lightbox behaviour suite. It compares colour, background, border, shadow, filter and the opacity every ancestor multiplies in, and ignores `cursor` and `pointer-events`. It reads the element that paints, so a container whose treatment sits on a child must pass that child.

**Changed from.** The Lightbox control rule painted every state alike, so a disabled arrow looked live.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-08-19. No later ruling amends it.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **A component paint rule that outranks Radix's disabled skin must carry its own `[data-disabled]` arm (2026-08-19).** `.radix-themes .rt-ds-lightbox-control` set `background-color` and `color` unconditionally. At (0,2,0), loading after Radix, it outranked `.rt-BaseButton:where(.rt-variant-ghost):where([data-disabled])` at (0,1,0) and erased the disabled skin entirely. **Measured on the shipped build:** the gallery's inert end-of-range arrow and its live neighbour resolved to the same `color`, the same `background-color`, the same `opacity` and the same `box-shadow`, and were pixel-identical once mirrored (max channel delta 6 of 255, zero of 576 pixels differing by more than 8). The only surviving difference was `cursor: not-allowed`, which a touch user never receives, a keyboard user never receives, and a pointer user only meets on hover. That is state carried on one channel, against WCAG 1.4.1. **Fix:** `.radix-themes .rt-ds-lightbox-control[data-disabled] { color: var(--ds-icon-disabled) }`. The scrim disc stays, because the control has to keep its shape over arbitrary media; the glyph drops to the existing disabled icon role, so no token is minted. After: the disabled glyph resolves `rgba(217, 237, 255, 0.365)` against the live `rgb(237, 238, 240)`, 2.90:1 against the disc versus 17.45:1, which is the intended reading for a disabled control and is why `--ds-icon-disabled` is already on the contrast-exempt list in `_assert.ts`. **Scope, established by measurement rather than by grep.** A static scan of the token CSS named eleven candidates; a sweep of all 497 renderable stories, comparing every control against a same-class twin in the other state, returned exactly one true positive, this one. Two apparent hits were instrument error and are recorded so nobody re-opens them: a disabled `TreeList` row carries its dimming on the descendant `.rt-ds-item-content` at `opacity: 0.5`, and `ChatComposer`'s stop button is deliberately never disabled while the composer around it is. Everything else either repaints on `[data-disabled]`, dims by `opacity`, or adds no competing paint and lets Radix's skin through, `Pagination` among them, whose disabled arrow resolves the disabled grey while its live one resolves the accent. **Locked by** `assertDisabledPaintDiffers` (`src/foundations/_disabledPaint.ts`), asserted at both ends of the range in the Lightbox behaviour suite. The helper compares colour, background, border, shadow and the opacity every ancestor multiplies in; it deliberately ignores `cursor` and `pointer-events`, and it compares the element that paints, so a container whose treatment sits on a child must be passed that child.

### overlay-scrim-ink

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`, `COLOUR`. **Ruled.** 2026-09-02.

**`Overlay`'s scrim sets the ink of its content slot, so content passed as `children` reads on the veil with no colour from the consumer.**

**What you see.** `.rt-ds-overlay-scrim` sets `color: var(--ds-on-scrim)`, and `var(--ds-on-scrim-light)` under `[data-scrim="light"]`, the paired foregrounds of [scrim-foreground-tokens](#scrim-foreground-tokens). A child with its own colour still wins. The same two rules re-point the stack of the focus ring, so veil, ink and ring move together ([focus-ring](#focus-ring)).

**Contract change.** A consumer can see this: content in `children` takes the scrim's ink in place of the page's.

**Why the container.** `children` is the consumer's own node, and `Theme` is not exported from the package's public entry point, so a consumer cannot reach the pinned-appearance idiom of Thumbnail and Lightbox and would have to hardcode a colour. This follows [container-size-seeding](#container-size-seeding), a container that resolves a value seeds it to its slots, applied to colour.

**Paired.** The scrim and its ink change together, because a scrim with the page's ink is the 1.00:1 pairing that [scrim-foreground-tokens](#scrim-foreground-tokens) records.

**Documentation.** The `Overlay` specimens set no colour, so the page shows the mechanism, and two measured rows read `color` off the rendered scrim in each mode.

**Changed from.** Content in `children` inherited the page's ink, near-black in the light appearance on a near-black veil, and the `Overlay` stories set two colour literals by hand.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-09-02.

- [scrim-focus-ring](#scrim-focus-ring) makes the scrim seed the colour of its focus ring beside its ink.
- [light-scrim-focus-ring](#light-scrim-focus-ring) rings a focused button on the light scrim in a deep shade of its own colour.
- [focus-ring](#focus-ring) replaces both scrim rings with the accent ring, and the scrim re-points only its stack, to `--accent-ring-stack-scrim` and `--accent-ring-stack-scrim-light`.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **`Overlay`'s scrim seeds its own content slot (2026-09-02).** `.rt-ds-overlay-scrim` now sets `color` alongside the background it already painted: `--ds-on-scrim`, or `--ds-on-scrim-light` under `[data-scrim="light"]`. **This is an observable contract change and a consumer can see it.** Content passed to `children` previously inherited the page's ink, which is near-black in the light appearance and sat on a near-black veil. It now inherits the scrim's paired foreground ([scrim-foreground-tokens](#scrim-foreground-tokens)). An explicitly coloured child still wins, as it should. **Why the container carries this rather than the consumer:** `children` is the consumer's own node, and `Theme` is deliberately unexported (`src/index.ts` states the reason and the consequence), so they cannot reach for the pinned-appearance idiom Thumbnail and Lightbox use. Leaving the ink to them means they hardcode a colour, which is precisely what this system's own documentation did for three months. Same shape as **[container-size-seeding](#container-size-seeding)**, "a container that resolves a size seeds it to its slots", applied to colour instead of size. **Both properties move together:** changing the scrim without its ink is the 1.00:1 pairing [scrim-foreground-tokens](#scrim-foreground-tokens) records. The two literals in `Overlay.stories.tsx` are deleted and the specimens set no colour at all, so the page demonstrates the mechanism rather than a workaround for its absence. A story that reached past it would keep passing if the mechanism broke. Documented by two live `MeasuredRow`s reading `color` off the rendered scrim in each mode, which is legal under the token-row rule because the paint now comes from a CSS rule rather than from the story. **[Update 2026-09-24 ([scrim-focus-ring](#scrim-focus-ring)): the scrim seeds its focus ring as well as its ink. The same two rules set `--ds-stroke-focus-hairline` to `--ds-on-scrim` and `--ds-on-scrim-light`, so veil, ink and ring move together. A consumer sees one change: in the light appearance a focused control on the dark scrim rings white instead of near-black. The page documents it with two measured focus-ring rows beside the two ink rows.]**

### seam-ownership

**Tags.** `LAYOUT`. **Ruled.** 2026-09-18.

**Exactly one part draws any given boundary between regions, and section 8a of `docs/GUIDELINES.md` names that part.**

**Who draws the seam.**

| Boundary | Drawn by |
|---|---|
| Two `Layout` areas | The `Layout` divider |
| A resizable panel and its neighbour | The panel's `ResizeHandle` |
| `SideNav` and its content | The `SideNav` trailing border |
| Two plain regions | Whichever side the author picks, once |

**Layout.** `Layout` resolves the owner from both sides of each boundary: a start-docked resizable panel owns the boundary after it, and an end-docked one owns the boundary before it. `Layout` draws no divider on a boundary a `ResizeHandle` owns.

**Scroll gutter.** A `ScrollArea` track is not a seam, and flush against a divider it reads as a second rule. The inset goes on the scrolling region's parent, because padding on the `ScrollArea` root barely moves a scrollbar Radix pins to the root. On 2026-09-18, 7px of clearance read as doubled and 10.5px did not.

**Why.** Every candidate paints the same `--ds-stroke-weak` hairline, so a doubled seam shows only in the rendered pixels. Four of the eight recreations, each by a separate author, doubled a seam, which points at a gap in the guidance rather than at the authors.

**Gap.** A regression story covers the end-docked `Layout` case. No guard sweeps the showcase pages for two vertical strokes at one x, and such a sweep needs a tolerance chosen against the scroll gutter case before it can run without noise.

**Changed from.** `Layout` suppressed only the divider after a resizable panel, so every layout with an end-docked resizable panel drew two hairlines a pixel apart. Nothing in `docs/GUIDELINES.md` said which part draws a seam.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-09-18. No later ruling amends it.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **A seam is drawn once, and `Layout` only half-enforced it (2026-09-18).** `Layout` suppresses its own divider next to a resizable panel, because the panel's `ResizeHandle` paints the same `--ds-stroke-weak` hairline and is the seam. The suppression looked FORWARD only: `!isLast && !isResizablePanel` drops the rule that would follow a resizable panel. That is correct for a start-docked panel, whose handle sits on its trailing edge, and wrong for an end-docked one, whose handle sits on its LEADING edge — there the doubled rule is emitted by the previous sibling and nothing suppressed it. **So every layout with a right-hand resizable panel shipped two hairlines a pixel apart.** Fixed by resolving ownership from both sides of each boundary: a start-docked resizable panel owns the boundary after it, an end-docked one owns the boundary before it. Measured in Chrome by collecting every vertical stroke on all eight showcase recreations and reporting any two within 8px of the same x. Four of the eight doubled a seam. **That ratio is the finding.** The pages were written by eight authors working in parallel who never communicated, so four of them independently making the same mistake is a gap in the guidance, not carelessness in the authors. Three added a `Separator` or a border beside a component that already drew the rule; one bordered both sides of the same boundary. Nothing in `GUIDELINES.md` said who owns a seam, and every candidate paints from the same token, so there was no way to be right except by inspecting the rendered pixels. **Ruling: exactly one thing draws any given boundary, and `GUIDELINES.md` §8a now names the part that draws it in each case** — `Layout`'s divider between areas, the `ResizeHandle` at a resizable panel, `SideNav`'s trailing border against its content, and for two plain regions whichever side you pick, once. **A scroll gutter is not a seam.** A `ScrollArea` track is ~4px of chrome pinned to the scroll root, and flush against a divider it reads as a second rule; the inset belongs on the scrolling region's PARENT, because padding the `ScrollArea` root barely moves a scrollbar Radix pins to it. Measured on the agent-run recreation: 7px of clearance read as doubled, 10.5px does not. **Verified:** all eight recreations report zero doubled seams on the same probe that found them. **Mechanism gap, named rather than implied:** the probe was a throwaway, so this is a measurement and not yet an invariant. The guard that would make it one is a browser-lane sweep over the showcase pages asserting no two vertical strokes share an x, which is cheap to write and needs a tolerance chosen against the scrollbar case above before it can run without noise.

### select-affix-width

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`, `LAYOUT`. **Ruled.** 2026-09-18.

**A `Select` with affixes keeps its own width in a flex row, and a consumer who wants it to fill the row sets `flex: 1` at the call site.**

**What you see.** `.rt-ds-select-affix`, the wrapper that holds the leading icon and the clear control, declares no width. The trigger's own `.rt-ds-select-affix .rt-SelectTrigger { width: 100% }` fills the wrapper, in a `Field` column and in a toolbar or filter row alike.

**Measured.** On the Select anatomy page on 2026-09-18, in a 900px row, the select measured 820.9px wide against the 216.4px it should be. After the fix it measured 216.4px in the row and still filled a 260px field.

**Changed from.** The wrapper declared `width: 100%`, which in a flex row resolved against the whole row, so the select took the whole row.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-09-18. No later ruling amends it.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **A `Select` with a leading icon stretched to fill any flex row, and its own wrapper caused it (2026-09-18).** `Select` renders its leading icon and clear ✕ as absolutely positioned overlays inside a `.rt-ds-select-affix` wrapper, because Radix's `Select.Trigger` has no slots. That wrapper declared `width: 100%`. Inside a `Field` (a column) that is invisible, because a block child fills its parent anyway. Inside a flex ROW — a toolbar, a filter bar — `width: 100%` resolves against the whole row and the select swallows it. **Measured on the Select anatomy page, in a 900px row: 820.9px wide against the 216.4px it should be.** **Fix: delete the declaration.** The trigger's own `.rt-ds-select-affix .rt-SelectTrigger { width: 100% }` is what actually makes it fill, and it does so in BOTH contexts — measured after: 216.4px in the row, still 260px filling a 260px field, trigger flush to the wrapper in each. The affix rule was belt-and-braces that only ever did harm. **A consumer who genuinely wants a select to fill a flex row sets `flex: 1` at the call site**, which is where that intent belongs.

### empty-state-size

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`, `SIZING`. **Ruled.** 2026-09-18.

**`EmptyState` takes a three-step `size` that scales its icon and its title together, apart from its heading level.**

**Why.** The title took the ambient heading lane, which fits a page and fails in a container. On the project board recreation, an empty column 264px wide rendered its `h3` title at 20px under a column `h2` at 14px, and `headingAs` could change the level but not the size.

**Steps.**

| `size` | Title | Icon |
|---|---|---|
| `"3"`, the default | The page heading lane, as before the prop existed | `--ds-icon-h3` |
| `"2"` | A smaller lane that steps with the size tier | `--ds-icon-h4` |
| `"1"` | A smaller lane again, which steps with the size tier | `--ds-icon-h5` |

The icon and the title move together because they are one visual unit, and a large glyph over small copy reads wrong. Step `"3"` moves no existing instance.

**Size and level.** `headingAs` still sets the heading level. An `h3` that looks smaller than the `h2` above it is correct, and an `h3` that looks larger is the defect.

**Applied.** The project board's empty column renders its title at 14px, level with the column heading.

**Changed from.** The title rendered on the ambient heading lane with no smaller size, and the docblock called that deliberate.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-09-18.

- [chrome-heading-lane](#chrome-heading-lane) replaces the literal heading steps `"3"` and `"2"` that steps `"2"` and `"1"` first used with size lanes, which step with the tier and remove an inversion at the large tier.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **`EmptyState` takes a `size`, because its title outranked the heading above it (2026-09-18).** The title rendered on the ambient heading lane with no way to step it down, and the docblock called that deliberate: "the size is the heading lane's". It holds on a page and fails in a container. **Measured on the project-board recreation:** an empty column 264px wide rendered its `h3` title at 20px above a column `h2` at 14px, so the heading LEVELS said one thing and the sizes said the opposite. `headingAs` could change the level but not the size, which made the inversion unfixable at the call site. **Fix: a three-step `size` scaling the icon and the title together**, because they are one visual unit and sizing only the heading leaves a large glyph over small copy. Step `"3"` is the default and resolves to exactly what shipped before — the ambient lane plus `--ds-icon-h3` — so no existing instance moves. Steps `"2"` and `"1"` drop to heading `"3"`/`"2"` with `--ds-icon-h4`/`--ds-icon-h5`. **Size and structure stay independent on purpose.** `headingAs` still decides the LEVEL. An `h3` that looks smaller than the `h2` above it is correct; an `h3` that looks bigger is the defect. Applied at the one shipped site that needed it: the board's empty column now renders its title at 14px, level with the column heading rather than above it.

### app-shell-gutter

**Tags.** `LAYOUT`, `COMPONENTS`. **Ruled.** 2026-09-18.

**`AppShell` takes a `gutter` prop for the padding around `main`, on `Layout`'s padding scale, and it defaults to the 24px that shipped before.**
