**Values.** `theme.css` sets `--accent-part-edge`, which is `--color-transparent` on every colour and appearance outside this table.

| Appearance | Colours | Edge |
|---|---|---|
| Light | amber, lime, mint, sky, yellow | `--black-a6` |
| Dark | pink | `--white-a1` |
| Dark | gray, plum | `--white-a3` |
| Dark | purple, violet, iris, indigo | `--white-a4` |
| Dark | oxblood | `--white-a6` |

Each is the lightest step whose stack on the fill clears WCAG 3:1 and APCA Lc 30 on all six neutrals against the page, the subtle recess, a card and a panel, and against the track for the progress bar and the slider range.

**What you see.** `components.css` paints the edge as the top 1px inset ring on each part, over Radix's own shadow for that part and variant. On the selected card, outside forced colours, `::after` moves to the card's edge and paints the 2px band as an inset ring with the edge on its outer 1px. Every other colour paints what it painted before.

**Not covered.** A disabled part and the soft variant keep Radix's paint, and a seeded brand keeps the transparent base. Under forced colours the card keeps its outline and `forced-colors.css` owns every other part, so the forced render does not change.

**Guidance.** The maintainer approved, on 2026-09-25, the 1px edge on the six colours that [textless-part-fills](#textless-part-fills) left under 3:1.

**Changed from.** After [textless-part-fills](#textless-part-fills), light amber, lime, mint, sky and yellow and dark oxblood kept a part fill at 1.31 to 2.08:1 against the page, because their ink passes as text on step 9 and [text-on-solid-fill-contrast](#text-on-solid-fill-contrast) did not deepen them. This ruling closes the gap [textless-part-fills](#textless-part-fills) recorded.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-09-25.

- [radio-cards-band-edge](#radio-cards-band-edge) gives the selected RadioCards band the same edge.
- [indicator-mark-edges](#indicator-mark-edges) stacks the edge on seven more marks that paint the part fill.
- [colour-prop-and-high-contrast](#colour-prop-and-high-contrast) extends the edge to a part given Radix's `color` prop or `highContrast`.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **Parts without text on light amber, lime, mint, sky and yellow and on dark oxblood stack a 1px edge on their fill (2026-09-25).** Approved by the maintainer as column A of the six-colour review page, and it closes the open gap [textless-part-fills](#textless-part-fills) records. After [textless-part-fills](#textless-part-fills) these six colours kept a part fill under 3:1 against the page, 1.31 to 1.56:1 in light and 2.06 to 2.08:1 on dark oxblood across the six neutrals, because their ink passes as text on step 9 and [text-on-solid-fill-contrast](#text-on-solid-fill-contrast) did not deepen them. `theme.css` adds `--accent-part-edge`, which is `--color-transparent` on every colour and appearance except six: `--black-a5` on light amber, `--black-a6` on light lime, mint, sky and yellow, and `--white-a4` on dark oxblood. Each is the lightest step of Radix's black or white alpha scale whose stack on the fill clears 3:1 on all six neutrals, where `--black-a4` reads 2.42 on amber, `--black-a5` reads 2.71 to 2.96 on the other four and `--white-a3` reads 2.87 on oxblood. `components.css` paints it as the top 1px inset ring on the checked or indeterminate checkbox, the checked radio and switch track, the slider range, the progress bar, the active tab line of Tabs and of Tabs.Nav, the accent status dot and the selected CheckboxCards band, and restates Radix's own shadow for that part and variant under it ([interaction-state-alphas](#interaction-state-alphas)). The edge takes each part's outer pixel to at least 3.13:1 on amber, 3.59 on lime, 3.77 on mint, 3.90 on sky, 3.62 on yellow and 3.26 on dark oxblood, the lowest of the six neutrals. A switch track and a slider range read higher, because Radix's `--gray-a5` hairline sits under the edge. The selected card keeps its 2px band where it sat, 1px inside and 1px outside its `::after` box. That outline paints above every layer `::after` paints, so outside forced colours `::after` moves to the card's edge and paints the same band as a 2px inset ring with the edge on its outer 1px, and Radix's card border ring under the band goes with the outline. Forced colours keep the outline, and `forced-colors.css` still owns every other part there, so the forced render is pixel-identical to the render before [part-fill-edge](#part-fill-edge) on all 27 accents. Every other colour paints the colours it painted before. Measured over 27 accents, both appearances and the surface and classic variants, the seven other parts compute the same shadows and outlines once the transparent layer is removed, and the rendered pixels differ only in antialiasing: up to 5 of 255 at the progress bar's scaled end, up to 14 on the status dot's rim, 1 on the slider range in two renders, and up to 62 on the outer arc of the card's corners at 2x. Left on Radix's paint, as in [textless-part-fills](#textless-part-fills): `highContrast`, the soft variant, a disabled part and a part given Radix's `color` prop, read on the element or on the group root that carries it. The PartsWithoutText play in `_non-text-contrast.stories.tsx` now reads each part's outer pixel, its fill with every inset ring flattened over it, and holds that at 3:1 against the page on all 27 accents in both appearances. `PAGE_RESIDUAL` is gone, so no colour is exempt. The play went red with light amber's value removed from `theme.css`, 8 parts at 1.54 to 2.37:1, and with the card rule removed from `components.css`, the card on all six colours at 1.32 to 2.08:1. The temporary review page `_six-colours.proto.stories.tsx` is deleted. **[Update 2026-09-27 ([status-dot-edges](#status-dot-edges)): the edge is now held at WCAG 3:1 AND APCA Lc 30 on four surfaces, and on the progress bar and the slider range against their track as well. Light amber takes `--black-a6`, dark oxblood takes `--white-a6`, and dark pink, gray, plum, purple, violet, iris and indigo take a step too.]**

### radio-cards-band-edge

**Tags.** `ACCESSIBILITY`, `COLOUR`. **Ruled.** 2026-09-25.

**The selected RadioCards card paints the same edged band as the selected CheckboxCards card.**

**What you see.** A selected RadioCards card shows a 2px inset band in `--accent-indicator` with `--accent-part-edge` on its outer 1px, the band [part-fill-edge](#part-fill-edge) gives CheckboxCards. On the six colours [part-fill-edge](#part-fill-edge) names, light amber, lime, mint, sky and yellow and dark oxblood, the band's outer pixel clears 3:1 against the page. Every other colour paints as before, apart from antialiasing at the four corners.

**Why.** [part-fill-edge](#part-fill-edge) left RadioCards on Radix's outline, so the two card pickers no longer matched, and the selected RadioCards outline read as low as 1.33:1 against the page on those six colours.

**Mechanism.** In `components.css` the selector `.rt-RadioCardsItem[data-state="checked"]::after` joins the [part-fill-edge](#part-fill-edge) card rule inside `@media (forced-colors: none)`. The `::after` moves to the card's edge and paints the band as inset shadows, and Radix's card border ring under the band is dropped. A RadioCards item is the radio button itself, so the rule reads the checked, disabled and focus states on the item, where the CheckboxCards rule reads them on its inner checkbox through `:has()`.

**Not covered.** Forced colours and a disabled card keep Radix's outline. A focused card shows the focus ring where the band would paint.

**Guidance.** The maintainer approved the change on 2026-09-25.

**Changed from.** A selected RadioCards card wore Radix's outline, under 3:1 against the page on the six colours, while a selected CheckboxCards card wore the edged band.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-09-25.

- [colour-prop-and-high-contrast](#colour-prop-and-high-contrast) extends the band to a card given Radix's `color` prop and to `highContrast`, whose band paints `--accent-12`.
- [status-dot-edges](#status-dot-edges) raises some `--accent-part-edge` steps so the edge clears APCA Lc 30 as well as WCAG 3:1.
- [card-picker-focus-width](#card-picker-focus-width) paints a 4px focus ring where the band would paint on a focused card.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **The selected RadioCards band stacks the [part-fill-edge](#part-fill-edge) edge, as the CheckboxCards band does (2026-09-25).** Approved by the maintainer. [part-fill-edge](#part-fill-edge) gave the selected CheckboxCards band the 1px `--accent-part-edge` and left RadioCards on Radix's outline, so the two card pickers stopped matching and the selected RadioCards outline stayed under 3:1 against the page on the six colours [part-fill-edge](#part-fill-edge) names. Measured on the RadioCards page, it read 1.34:1 on light yellow, 1.56 on amber, 1.33 on lime, 1.41 on mint, 1.47 on sky and 2.08 on dark oxblood. `components.css` adds `.rt-RadioCardsItem[data-state="checked"]::after` to the [part-fill-edge](#part-fill-edge) card rule inside `@media (forced-colors: none)`. Outside forced colours `::after` moves to the card's edge and paints the same 2px band as an inset ring in `--accent-indicator` with the edge on its outer 1px, and Radix's card border ring under the band is dropped with the outline. The item is the radio button itself, so the rule reads the checked, disabled and focus states on the item, where the CheckboxCards rule reads them through `:has()` on its inner checkbox. The band's outer pixel now reads 3.67:1 on light yellow, 3.18 on amber, 3.64 on lime, 3.83 on mint, 3.95 on sky and 3.28 on dark oxblood. Every other colour paints the colours it painted before. Measured on indigo, cyan, iris and gray in light and on indigo, cyan and iris in dark, every pixel outside the card's four corners is identical, and the corners differ by up to 49 of 255 in antialiasing, the outline's arc against the inset ring's arc, as [part-fill-edge](#part-fill-edge) measured on CheckboxCards. Left on Radix's outline, as in [part-fill-edge](#part-fill-edge): forced colours, `highContrast`, a focused card, a disabled card and a set given Radix's `color` prop. The PartsWithoutText play in `_non-text-contrast.stories.tsx` holds the RadioCards band at 3:1 against the page and at the Checkbox's shade across 27 accents in both appearances, and went red with the RadioCards selector removed from the rule, the card on all six colours at 1.32 to 2.08:1.

### indicator-mark-edges

**Tags.** `ACCESSIBILITY`, `COLOUR`. **Ruled.** 2026-09-25.

**The system's own marks that paint the part fill stack the same 1px edge as the parts, so each clears 3:1 against the page on the six colours whose bare fill does not.**

**Applies to.** As it stands today:

- the Calendar today bar outside a range
- the DragHandle drop line and its end dot
- the Analytics dashboard chart end point and legend swatch

**Paint.** `components.css` paints `--accent-part-edge` as a 1px inset ring on each CSS mark. None carries a shadow of its own, so the edge is the only layer, and a 2px bar or line takes the edge across its whole width. The chart end point takes a 1px ring inside the page-colour ring it carries, and the legend swatch an inset ring, as the StatusDot does.

**Why.** On light amber, lime, mint, sky and yellow and on dark oxblood these marks read 1.32 to 2.08:1 against the page on the bare fill. With the edge each read 3.18:1 or more, measured on 2026-09-25. Every other colour paints as before.

**Not covered.** A today bar in neutral ink, on an out-of-month day, a range endpoint or a selected picker option, keeps no edge. Forced colours compute `box-shadow` to none, so the CSS marks render there as before.

**Guidance.** The maintainer approved this, on 2026-09-25, as the first group of fixes from the contrast census.

**Changed from.** [part-fill-edge](#part-fill-edge) stacked the edge on the Radix parts and left the system's own marks on the bare fill.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-09-25.

### input-focus-ring-offset

**Tags.** `ACCESSIBILITY`. **Ruled.** 2026-09-25.

**Every focused input rings 2px outside its edge, the same gap as a button.**

**Applies to.** `TextField`, `TextArea`, `NumberInput`, `Select`, `MultiSelect`, `DateInput`, `DateRangeInput`, `TimeInput`, `Typeahead` and `ChatComposer`. `NumberInput`, `DateInput`, `TimeInput` and `Typeahead` take the `TextField` rule, and `MultiSelect` and `DateRangeInput` take the `Select` trigger rule.

**Mechanism.** `components.css` sets `outline-offset: 2px` on the `TextField`, `TextArea` and `Select` trigger focus rules, the `@supports not selector(:has(*))` fallback for `TextField` and the `ChatComposer` dock. This ruling changes only the offset.

**Why.** The 4px offset outlived the bands that once filled the gap, a 4px accent glow and later a 4px validation halo. Buttons, `Checkbox`, `Tokenizer` and `FileInput` ring at 2px, so the controls showed two gaps. Radix Themes 3.3 rings these inputs at `-1px`, so 4px was never the Radix default.

**Guarded by.** `_internal/Focus` RingGapOutsideEdge measures the drawn gap on all four sides of every input family at all three size tiers, beside a `Button`, a `Tokenizer` and a `FileInput`, and holds it at 2px within 0.5px.

**Not covered.** The accent rings of `Switch`, `Slider` and `SegmentedControl`, left for a later decision, which [focus-ring](#focus-ring) took.

**Guidance.** The maintainer approved this change on 2026-09-25.

**Changed from.** The inputs drew their ring at `outline-offset: 4px` at every size in both appearances, an offset that the two-colour focus ring, the first neutral focus ring and [validation-focus-paint](#validation-focus-paint) all kept.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-09-25.

- [focus-ring](#focus-ring) makes the input ring the stacked accent at 2px wide, and the 2px gap stands.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **Every focused input rings 2px outside its edge, the same gap as a button (2026-09-25).** Approved by the maintainer. The focus ring on TextField, TextArea, NumberInput, Select, MultiSelect, DateInput, DateRangeInput, TimeInput, Typeahead and ChatComposer sat at `outline-offset: 4px` at every size in both appearances, where Button, Checkbox, Tokenizer and FileInput ring at 2px. The 4px came from the two-colour focus ring, where it cleared the 4px accent glow that filled the gap under the hairline. The first neutral focus ring dropped the glow and kept a 4px validation halo in the same gap, and [validation-focus-paint](#validation-focus-paint) dropped the halo, and all three kept the 4px offset after the band that filled it was gone. [validation-focus-paint](#validation-focus-paint) names the value Radix's default focus geometry, and that claim is false: Radix Themes 3.3 rings TextField, TextArea and Select at `outline-offset: -1px`, across the edge. [button-focus-ring-offset](#button-focus-ring-offset)'s guard let the drift stand, because it probed buttons only and held a floor of 2px, which a 4px ring clears. `components.css` now gives the TextField, TextArea and Select trigger focus rules, the `@supports not selector(:has(*))` TextField fallback and the ChatComposer dock `outline-offset: 2px`, which amends the two-colour focus ring, the first neutral focus ring and [validation-focus-paint](#validation-focus-paint). NumberInput, DateInput, TimeInput and Typeahead take the TextField rule, and MultiSelect and DateRangeInput the Select trigger rule. Ring width and colour do not change: inputs keep the 1px hairline and buttons their 2px ring. `_internal/Focus` → *RingGapOutsideEdge* now mounts a real control of every input family, with a Button, a Tokenizer and a FileInput as the reference, at the small, medium and large tiers, focuses each with keyboard modality, and measures the drawn gap on all four sides, from the outer edge of the ring carrier's own border, inset box-shadow or fill to the inner edge of the ring. Each must read 2px within 0.5px with the ring unclipped by any ancestor. In the light and dark lanes all 42 cells read 2.00px. The guard went red with the TextArea rule at 4px again, and named TextArea at all three tiers at 4.00px on every side in both lanes. The accent rings of Switch, Slider and SegmentedControl stay out of scope for a later decision. **[Update 2026-09-25 ([focus-ring](#focus-ring)): the inputs ring at 2px, not 1px, in [focus-ring](#focus-ring)'s stacked accent. The gap stands.]**

### light-scrim-focus-ring

**Tags.** `ACCESSIBILITY`, `COLOUR`. **Ruled.** 2026-09-25.

**On the light scrim a focused control rings in its own accent fill with a black alpha stacked on it, deep enough to read 3:1 over any media.**

**What you see.** A focused button on the light scrim shows a ring in a deep shade of its own colour. The ring paints `--ds-fill-accent`, not `--accent-indicator`, although it carries no text, because it frames the button and matches its fill ([textless-part-fills](#textless-part-fills)).

**Stack.** `--accent-ring-stack-scrim-light` holds the lightest Radix black alpha whose stack on `--ds-fill-accent` clears WCAG 3:1 and APCA Lc 30 against rgb(153, 153, 153), the darkest composite the light scrim makes. Neither the fill nor the veil changes with the appearance, so each colour takes one step in both.

| Stack | Accent colours |
|---|---|
| `--black-a5` | gray, gold, bronze, brown, red, ruby, crimson, pink, violet, iris, indigo |
| `--black-a6` | orange, tomato, plum, purple, blue, cyan, teal, jade, green, grass |
| `--black-a9` | yellow, amber, lime, mint, sky |
| None | oxblood, whose fill clears alone |

**Method.** Inside `@media (forced-colors: none)` the ring paints as two outlines on sibling pseudo-elements: `::before` carries the fill and `::after` the stack, each with the control's radius, outline width, style and offset inherited, and the control's own outline turns transparent. Siblings paint in tree order in every engine, so the stack always sits on the fill, while an element's own outline may paint above or below its positioned pseudo-elements. `_internal/Focus` *ScrimRingContrast* focuses a real control in a real scrim, flattens each painted outline over media from 0 to 255, and holds the ring at 3:1 on all 27 accents in both appearances.

**Exceptions.** Forced colours keep the single outline, which `forced-colors.css` paints in Highlight. A classic Button, whose `::after` Radix paints, keeps an outline in the base colour alone, and the system's Button and IconButton never render classic.

**Rejected.** Layered box shadows on one pseudo-element. The ring's outer corner is the button's radius plus 4px, CSS cannot add to an inherited radius, and a shadow ring with the button's own radius differed from the outline ring at every corner. An outline on each pseudo-element matched it with no differing pixel.

**Guidance.** The maintainer approved, on 2026-09-25, a focus ring on the light scrim in a deep shade of the button's own colour. The approved method was layered shadows, and measurement replaced it with two outlines.

**Changed from.** [scrim-focus-ring](#scrim-focus-ring) set the ring inside the light scrim to `--ds-on-scrim-light`, a fixed near-black, so a focused Button or IconButton showed none of its own colour there.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-09-25. It amends [scrim-focus-ring](#scrim-focus-ring).

- [focus-ring](#focus-ring) draws every ring in the system with this two-outline method, extends the accent ring to every control on the light scrim, renames the stack to `--accent-ring-stack-scrim-light`, adds APCA Lc 30 to the floor and moves purple from `--black-a5` to `--black-a6`.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **On the light scrim a focused button rings in a deep shade of its own colour (2026-09-25).** Approved by the maintainer from the Light accent and Dark accent columns of the scrim ring review page, and it amends [scrim-focus-ring](#scrim-focus-ring). [scrim-focus-ring](#scrim-focus-ring) pointed the ring inside the light scrim at `--ds-on-scrim-light`, a fixed near-black, so a focused Button or IconButton showed none of its own colour there. `theme.css` adds `--accent-scrim-ring-stack`, the lightest step of Radix's black alpha scale whose stack on `--ds-fill-accent` clears 3:1 against `--ds-scrim-light` over black media, rgb(153, 153, 153), the darkest composite the light scrim makes. It is `--black-a5` on gray, gold, bronze, brown, red, ruby, crimson, pink, purple, violet, iris and indigo (3.03 to 3.33:1), `--black-a6` on orange, tomato, plum, blue, cyan, teal, jade, green and grass (3.30 to 3.54), `--black-a9` on yellow, amber, lime, mint and sky (3.42 to 3.81), and `--color-transparent` on oxblood, whose fill reads 3.19 alone. The fill and the veil do not change with the appearance, so each colour takes one step in both. `components.css` paints the ring inside `@media (forced-colors: none)` as two outlines on sibling pseudo-elements over the button's box. `::before` paints the fill and `::after` the stack, each with the button's radius, outline width, style and offset inherited, and the button's own outline stays under them, transparent. Siblings paint in tree order, so the stack sits on the fill in every engine, while an element's own outline may paint above or below its positioned pseudo-elements (CSS 2.2 Appendix E). The approved block named layered shadows on a pseudo-element, and measurement rejected them: the ring's outer corner is the button's radius plus 4px, CSS cannot add to an inherited radius, and a shadow ring with the button's own radius differed from the current ring at every corner, 1,040 to 2,328 pixels at 4x scale across sizes 1 to 4. Each pseudo outline matched the current ring with no differing pixel on the solid, surface, soft, ghost and outline variants at sizes 1 to 4. `position: relative` gives the pseudo-elements the button's box at specificity (0,1,0), which beats Radix's `.rt-reset` and no more, so a consumer's own position rule still wins from a later stylesheet. A classic button, whose `::after` Radix paints, and an inset button, whose `::after` the Badge chip spends on its hit area, keep the [scrim-focus-ring](#scrim-focus-ring) ring. The system's Button and IconButton never render classic. The ring is a mark without text and still paints `--ds-fill-accent`, not `--accent-indicator` ([textless-part-fills](#textless-part-fills)), because it frames the button and matches its fill. Forced colours keep the [scrim-focus-ring](#scrim-focus-ring) outline, which forced-colors.css paints in Highlight. The dark scrim keeps its white [scrim-focus-ring](#scrim-focus-ring) ring, and every other control in the light scrim keeps the near-black one. Measured on the Overlay page at 4x, the focused light-scrim Play button matches the review page's Accent columns within 2 of 255 on every pixel for yellow, iris, cyan, orange and oxblood in both appearances. Guarded by `_internal/Focus` → *ScrimRingContrast*, which focuses a real button in a real scrim, reads each outline it paints, flattens them over media 0 to 255, and holds the light-scrim ring at 3:1 and at the button's fill on 27 accents in both appearances. It went red on iris at 1.88:1 in both appearances with iris removed from the `--black-a5` set, and on all 27 accents with the `::before` outline set back to the [scrim-focus-ring](#scrim-focus-ring) ink. The Overlay page measures the fill and the stack on two focus ring rows. **[Update 2026-09-25 ([focus-ring](#focus-ring)): [light-scrim-focus-ring](#light-scrim-focus-ring)'s two-outline method draws every ring in the system, and its stack is `--accent-ring-stack-scrim-light`, with purple at `--black-a6` once APCA Lc 30 is held too.]**

### focus-ring

**Tags.** `ACCESSIBILITY`, `COLOUR`. **Ruled.** 2026-09-25.

**Every focus ring is the accent with one Radix alpha stacked on it, 2px wide, the same on every control.**

**Layers.** `semantic.css` names two. `--ds-stroke-focus` is `--ds-fill-accent`, the button's own fill ([text-on-solid-fill-contrast](#text-on-solid-fill-contrast)), and `--ds-stroke-focus-stack` is one Radix black or white alpha laid over it ([interaction-state-alphas](#interaction-state-alphas)).

**Stack values.** `theme.css` gives each colour and appearance the lightest step whose stack clears WCAG 3:1 and APCA Lc 30 on all six neutrals against 15 surfaces: the page, the subtle and sunken recesses, a card, a menu panel, a track on the page and on a card, a highlighted row, the four validation tints, the accent tint on the page and on a card, and the selected tint.

| Appearance | Colours | Stack |
|---|---|---|
| Light | the other 22 colours | none |
| Light | amber | `--black-a6` |
| Light | yellow, lime, mint, sky | `--black-a7` |
| Dark | yellow, amber, lime, mint, sky | none |
| Dark | orange | `--white-a3` |
| Dark | plum, purple, blue, cyan, teal, jade, green | `--white-a4` |
| Dark | oxblood | `--white-a7` |
| Dark | the other 13 colours | `--white-a5` |

On a scrim only the stack changes, to `--accent-ring-stack-scrim` on the dark scrim and `--accent-ring-stack-scrim-light` on the light one, so the ring is the accent on both scrims.

**Geometry.**

- Each carrier's own rule sets the ring's width, offset and base colour on its outline. Outside forced colours a section at the end of `components.css` makes that outline transparent and draws the base on `::before` and the stack on `::after`.
- Where a control spends its pseudos, the two layers move elsewhere and land on the same pixels.
- A ring sits 2px outside a control, or 2px inside where it sat inside: the Tabs trigger, the SegmentedControl item, the cards, the ScrollArea viewport, the menu and Select rows and a button inside a field.
- ClickableCard rings inside its edge like every card, the tab panel and the Calendar caption ring 2px outside, and no ScrollArea viewport shows the browser's own outline.
- Under forced colours the outline is the whole ring, `Highlight` at 2px, and the stack paints nothing.

**Limits.**

- A TextArea with a resize handle keeps a ring of the base alone, because the `overflow: hidden` the handle needs clips a pseudo.
- A Link that wraps rings the box of its first and last line.
- A seeded brand keeps a transparent stack.
- The Slider thumb and the Pagination dot lose their hit extender while they hold keyboard focus.

**Guidance.** The maintainer approved, on 2026-09-25, the stacked accent ring with one amendment, a ring width of 2px.

**Changed from.** Text fields drew a 1px neutral `gray-12` ring and buttons a 2px one, nine Radix controls kept Radix's accent-8 ring at as low as 1.47:1 against a tint, each scrim drew its own ring, and the menu and Select rows spent the ring token on their highlight edge. This ruling supersedes the first neutral focus ring and [validation-focus-paint](#validation-focus-paint) on colour and width, deletes `--ds-stroke-focus-hairline`, and supersedes [scrim-focus-ring](#scrim-focus-ring) and [light-scrim-focus-ring](#light-scrim-focus-ring) on the scrim rings.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-09-25.

- [card-picker-focus-width](#card-picker-focus-width) rings a focused CheckboxCards or RadioCards card at 4px, selected or not.
- [part-colour-parity](#part-colour-parity) keeps the page accent on the ring of a part given its own colour.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **Every focus ring is the accent with a Radix alpha stacked on it, 2px wide, the same on every control (2026-09-25).** Approved by the maintainer with one amendment, a ring width of 2px, and it supersedes the first neutral focus ring and [validation-focus-paint](#validation-focus-paint) on colour and width and [scrim-focus-ring](#scrim-focus-ring) and [light-scrim-focus-ring](#light-scrim-focus-ring) on the scrim rings. Before it, text fields drew a 1px neutral gray-12 ring and buttons a 2px one, nine Radix controls kept Radix's own 2px accent-8 ring at as low as 1.47:1 against a tint, each scrim drew its own ring, and the menu and Select rows spent the ring token on their highlight edge. `semantic.css` names two layers: `--ds-stroke-focus`, which is `--ds-fill-accent`, the button's own fill ([text-on-solid-fill-contrast](#text-on-solid-fill-contrast)), and `--ds-stroke-focus-stack`, one Radix black or white alpha laid over it ([interaction-state-alphas](#interaction-state-alphas)). `--ds-stroke-focus-hairline` is deleted. `theme.css` gives each colour and appearance the lightest step whose stack clears WCAG 3:1 AND APCA Lc 30 against 15 surfaces on all six neutrals: the page, the subtle and sunken recesses, a card, a menu panel, a track on the page and on a card, a highlighted row, the four validation tints, the accent tint on the page and on a card, and the selected tint. In light 22 colours clear on the fill alone, the lowest orange at 3.14:1, amber takes `--black-a6`, and yellow, lime, mint and sky take `--black-a7`. In dark yellow, amber, lime, mint and sky clear alone, orange takes `--white-a3`, plum, purple, blue, cyan, teal, jade and green take `--white-a4`, oxblood takes `--white-a7` and the other 13 take `--white-a5`. Overlay re-points only the stack on each scrim, to `--accent-ring-stack-scrim` (`--white-a8` or `--white-a9`, and nothing on the five light colours) and `--accent-ring-stack-scrim-light` ([light-scrim-focus-ring](#light-scrim-focus-ring)'s table renamed, with purple moved from `--black-a5` at 2.99:1 to `--black-a6`). The dark scrim ring is no longer white. **The method is [light-scrim-focus-ring](#light-scrim-focus-ring)'s, everywhere.** Each carrier's own rule sets the ring's width, offset and base colour on its outline, which is the whole ring under forced colours, where `forced-colors.css` paints it Highlight at 2px and the stack paints nothing. Outside forced colours a section at the end of `components.css` makes that outline transparent and draws the base on `::before` and the stack on `::after`, and both inherit its geometry, because siblings paint in tree order in every engine. Where a control spends its pseudos the layers move and land on the same pixels: the Checkbox and Switch ring their `::before` box with a matching `::after`, the Radio carries the stack on its dot scaled 0.4, the Slider thumb and the Pagination dot lend their hit extender to the ring while keyboard focus lasts, the Calendar day and option and every card paint both layers as inset box-shadows on `::after`, the ResizeHandle rings its grab zone, and the Thumbnail rings its frame from its root. Rings sit 2px outside a control, or inside at -2px where they sat inside: the Tabs trigger, the SegmentedControl item, the cards, the ScrollArea viewport, the menu and Select rows and a button inside a field. Three rings move. ClickableCard goes inside its edge like every card, because a card clips its content and spends both pseudos. The tab panel and the Calendar caption move from 0 to 2px outside. The UA outline on a focusable ScrollArea viewport is dropped for every ScrollArea, where only the chat log dropped it before. **Measured:** a keyboard sweep of every Usage story on light amber and on dark oxblood read every system ring as the fill underneath and the stack on it, 2px wide. With the base painted lime and the stack magenta, no base pixel showed outside the stack on 126 focused controls at 2x. **Limits, stated:** a TextArea given a resize handle keeps Radix's `overflow: hidden`, which the handle needs and which clips a pseudo, so it keeps a base-only ring. A Link that wraps rings the box of its first and last line. A seeded brand keeps a transparent stack. The Slider thumb and the Pagination dot lose their hit extender while they hold keyboard focus. **Guarded by** `_internal/Focus` → RingTokensResolve, FocusRingContrast, ScrimRingContrast, ControlRingsUseAccent and EveryRingIsTheStackedAccent, and `_internal/Non-text contrast` → FocusRingOnParts. They went red with light amber's stack removed from `theme.css` (1.54:1 and Lc 24.3 on the page) and with the TextField ring at 1px (1.00px on every TextField).

### selected-row-cue

**Tags.** `ACCESSIBILITY`, `COMPONENTS`. **Ruled.** 2026-09-26.

**A selected row reads bold in strong ink with a solid icon, and every other row reads regular with an outline icon.**

**What you see.** In SideNav and its collapsed rail, List, TopNav, TreeList, MobileNav and the CommandPalette, the selected row keeps the `--ds-fill-selected-subtle` tint, and its label takes `--ds-font-weight-strong` (600) in `--ds-text-strong`. Its icon takes Phosphor's `fill` weight, and the icon on every other row takes `regular`.

**Why.** The tint alone reads 1.22 to 1.87:1 against the surface under it, so selection rested on colour alone. The selected label reads 8.16:1 or more on the tint.

**Mechanism.** `Item.tsx` exports `SelectionIconWeight`, which wraps a row's icon in Phosphor's `IconContext`. It spreads the parent context first, so an app-level size or colour still reaches the icon, and a solid weight set above a row cannot leak into it. Item wraps its start slot in it, and the SideNav rail button, the SideNav rail parent trigger, the TopNav menu trigger and the CommandPalette option wrap the icons they draw outside Item. An icon that sets its own `weight` keeps it, so a consumer passes no weight.

**Cards.** A ProjectBoard card has no single label to set bold, so a selected card takes the [part-fill-edge](#part-fill-edge) card band: 2px of `--accent-indicator` at its edge with `--accent-part-edge` on the outer 1px, in place of the card's `--gray-a5` edge ring.

**Limit.** A bold label is wider, so on a TopNav bar a change of selection moves the items after it by the difference, 1.39px for "Dashboard" at the default size.

**Guidance.** The maintainer approved this cue on 2026-09-26.

**Changed from.** A selected row carried only the tint, and the List specimen drew every row's icon solid, so a solid icon could not mark the selected one.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-09-26.

- [status-dot-edges](#status-dot-edges) sets the selected row's description in `--ds-text-strong` as well.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **A selected row reads bold in strong ink with a solid icon, and every other row reads regular with an outline icon (2026-09-26).** Approved by the maintainer as column C of decision 03 on the decision review page, with the review's note on the List specimen. Before it, a selected row in SideNav, the collapsed rail, List, TopNav, TreeList, MobileNav and the CommandPalette carried only the `--ds-fill-selected-subtle` tint, which reads 1.22 to 1.87:1 against the surface under it across 27 colours in both appearances. The List specimen drew every row's icon solid, so a solid icon could not mark the selected one. `components.css` sets the selected Item label and the picked CommandPalette option label at `--ds-font-weight-strong` (600) in `--ds-text-strong`, and the tint stays. `Item.tsx` adds `SelectionIconWeight`, which wraps a row's icon in Phosphor's `IconContext` at `fill` on the selected row and at `regular` on every other row. It spreads the parent context first, so an app-level size or colour still reaches the icon, and a solid weight set above a row cannot leak into it. Item wraps its start slot in it, and the SideNav rail button, the SideNav rail parent trigger, the TopNav menu trigger and the CommandPalette option wrap the icons they draw outside Item. An icon that sets its own `weight` keeps it, so no consumer passes a weight, and the List, TreeList, MobileNav and CommandPalette stories drop the weights they hard-coded. Measured across 27 colours in both appearances on SideNav, List, TreeList and the CommandPalette, the selected label reads 8.16:1 or more on the tint and APCA Lc 76 or more. A ProjectBoard card has no single label to set bold, so the selected card takes the [part-fill-edge](#part-fill-edge) card band, 2px of `--accent-indicator` flush with its edge with `--accent-part-edge` on the outer 1px. The card root is a stacking context and its opaque `::before` panel covers anything the root paints, so the band rides the card's `::after` through Radix's `--base-card-surface-box-shadow` and replaces the card's `--gray-a5` edge ring, as [part-fill-edge](#part-fill-edge)'s band does. Its outer pixel reads 3.21:1 or more against the column, the lowest on light amber. The temporary review page drops its stories 01 to 03. **Limit, stated:** a bold label is wider, so a TopNav bar moves the items after a selection change by the difference, 1.39px for "Dashboard" at the default size. **Guarded by** `_internal/Item` → SelectionCue, which renders Item, List, the SideNav rows, the collapsed rail with a parent trigger, TopNav with a menu trigger, TreeList and the CommandPalette picker, each with one selected row and the same Star with no weight of its own, once bare and once under a solid `IconContext`. Cloned into 27 colours in both appearances, it holds the selected label at `--ds-font-weight-strong` in `--ds-text-strong`, every other label at `--ds-font-weight-base`, the selected icon at Phosphor's solid shape and every other icon at its outline shape. It went red with the label weight removed from the Item rule in `components.css` (540 labels at 400) and with the start slot unwrapped in `Item.tsx` (702 icons at the wrong weight).

### mark-on-tint-edge

**Tags.** `ACCESSIBILITY`, `COLOUR`. **Ruled.** 2026-09-26.

**A mark that sits on a tint stacks its own Radix alpha step, so it clears WCAG 3:1 and APCA Lc 30 against the tint as well as the surface.**

**Applies to.**

- The Calendar today bar inside a committed or a previewed range, on the range band, held on the page and on the popover panel, `--ds-bg-overlay`, where DateInput and DateRangeInput pick a range.
- The Outline bar on its rail, held on the page.
- The Analytics dashboard chart line on its area fill, held on its card.
- The current Pagination dot, since [neutral-part-stacks](#neutral-part-stacks).

**What you see.** `theme.css` sets `--accent-mark-edge` for each colour and appearance, the lightest step of Radix's black or white alpha scale whose stack on the fill clears both floors against the tint and the surface around the mark, on all six neutrals. `components.css` paints it as the 1px inset ring on the today bar and the Outline bar, and the chart in `AnalyticsDashboard.stories.tsx` draws its line a second time in it at the same width. It replaces the [indicator-mark-edges](#indicator-mark-edges) edge on these marks, so each mark stacks one alpha ([contrast-by-alpha-stacking](#contrast-by-alpha-stacking)). The `MarksAndDashesOnTint` story in `_internal/Non-text contrast` holds each mark at both floors across 27 accents, both appearances and six neutrals.

**Not covered.** A today bar outside a range keeps the [indicator-mark-edges](#indicator-mark-edges) edge, and an endpoint or an out-of-month day paints the bar in a neutral ink with no edge. The drop line and its end dot, the chart end point and the legend swatch keep `--accent-part-edge`. Forced colours compute `box-shadow` to none, so the two CSS marks render there as before, and the chart line keeps its SVG stroke.

**Why.** With the [indicator-mark-edges](#indicator-mark-edges) edge, these marks read as low as 1.82, 1.95 and 2.18:1 against their tint on dark oxblood, and 26 of the 54 colour and appearance pairs fell below a floor on at least one of the three.

**Guidance.** The maintainer approved the stack for marks held on the page on 2026-09-26. The build also held the today bar on the popover panel and on the preview band, and the maintainer saw both named the same day, though no ruling of their own records them.

**Changed from.** These marks carried the [indicator-mark-edges](#indicator-mark-edges) edge, `--accent-part-edge`, which did not clear 3:1 and Lc 30 against the tint on every colour.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-09-26.

- [neutral-part-stacks](#neutral-part-stacks) stacks `--accent-mark-edge` on the current Pagination dot too, held on the page, the subtle recess, a card and a panel.
- [part-colour-parity](#part-colour-parity) extends the `--accent-mark-edge` table to a part that sets its own colour.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

Two parts of its scope went past the approved block, which named the page only: the today bar held on the popover panel, and the today bar on the preview band. The build chose both, the maintainer saw both named on 2026-09-26, and neither has a ruling yet. The Calendar today bar inside a range sits on the range band, the Outline bar on its rail and the Analytics dashboard chart line on its area fill. With the [indicator-mark-edges](#indicator-mark-edges) edge on them they read as low as 1.82, 1.95 and 2.18:1 against that tint on dark oxblood, and 26 of the 54 colour and appearance pairs fall under WCAG 3:1 or APCA Lc 30 on at least one of the three. `theme.css` adds `--accent-mark-edge`, the lightest step of Radix's black or white alpha scale whose stack on the fill clears WCAG 3:1 and APCA Lc 30 against the tint and the surface around the mark, on all six neutrals. The today bar is held on the page and on the popover panel, `--ds-bg-overlay`, where DateInput and DateRangeInput pick a range. The Outline bar is held on the page and the chart line on its card. In light, yellow, amber, lime, mint and sky take `--black-a7`, and the other 22 clear on the fill alone. In dark, yellow, amber, orange, lime, mint and sky clear alone, brown and cyan take `--white-a1`, gold, bronze, tomato, red, ruby, crimson, blue, teal, jade, green and grass take `--white-a2`, pink takes `--white-a3`, gray, plum, purple, violet, iris and indigo take `--white-a5`, and oxblood takes `--white-a7`. The lowest reading at the step is 3.00:1 on dark jade and Lc 30.8 on dark ruby, and the step one lighter fails on every colour that takes a step. A step held on the page alone is lighter or absent on 16 dark colours, and leaves the today bar in a popover as low as 2.67:1 on dark jade and Lc 27.2 on dark bronze, so the popover panel sets the step there. `components.css` paints the step as the 1px inset ring on the Outline bar and on the today bar inside a committed or a previewed range, in place of `--accent-part-edge`. Both bars are 2px, so the ring covers each whole bar. The preview band is the lighter tint, and the today bar clears both floors on it too, 3.83:1 or more. A today bar outside a range keeps the [indicator-mark-edges](#indicator-mark-edges) edge, and an endpoint and an out-of-month day paint the bar in a neutral ink and keep no edge. ### drop-target-dash

**Tags.** `ACCESSIBILITY`, `COLOUR`. **Ruled.** 2026-09-26.

**The dashed edge on a drop target stacks a Radix alpha on its step 7 dash, so it clears WCAG 3:1 and APCA Lc 30 against its tint and its surface.**

**Applies to.** The DragHandle empty drop slot and the FileInput drop target. While a card or a file is dragged over them, each paints a 1px dashed edge in `--ds-stroke-accent`, accent step 7, around a tint of the same colour, `--ds-fill-accent-weak`.

**What you see.** `theme.css` sets `--accent-dash-stack`, the lightest step of Radix's black or white alpha scale whose stack on step 7 clears both floors against the tint and against the page, the subtle recess, a card and a panel, on all six neutrals. Every colour takes a step, `--black-a5` or `--black-a6` in light and `--white-a5` or `--white-a6` in dark, so every dash reads darker in light and lighter in dark. Nothing else about the slot or the zone moves.

**Drawing.** `components.css` draws the stack as a second 1px dash on the same box, so it lands dash for dash.

- On the slot, a dashed outline on the slot's `::after`, drawn 1px inward over the border's band.
- On the drop zone, a dashed border with the zone's `--ds-radius-4` on the FileInput shell's `::after`, because the zone's own pseudo-elements carry the [focus-ring](#focus-ring) focus ring and a zone can hold focus and a drag at once.
- Both rules sit inside `@media (forced-colors: none)`, so forced colours keep the border alone.

**Why.** The bare step 7 dash read 1.31 to 2.41:1 against the lower of its tint and its surface on every colour, and as low as Lc 0.0 on dark oxblood. No colour clears on step 7 alone.

**Guarded by.** The `MarksAndDashesOnTint` story in `_internal/Non-text contrast` holds each dash at both floors against its tint and the four surfaces, and holds where each stack is drawn.

**Changed from.** Each drop target painted its step 7 dash alone.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-09-26.

- [part-colour-parity](#part-colour-parity) extends the `--accent-dash-stack` table to a part that sets its own colour.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **The dashed edge on a drop target stacks a Radix alpha on its step 7 dash (2026-09-26).** Approved by the maintainer as column C of decision 05 on the decision review page. While a card or a file is dragged over it, the DragHandle's empty drop slot and the FileInput drop target paint a 1px dashed edge in accent step 7, `--ds-stroke-accent`, around a tint of the same colour, `--ds-fill-accent-weak`. Measured on the six neutrals, the dash read 1.31 to 2.41:1 against the lower of its tint and its surface on every colour, and as low as Lc 0.0 on dark oxblood. `theme.css` adds `--accent-dash-stack`, the lightest step of Radix's black or white alpha scale whose stack on step 7 clears WCAG 3:1 and APCA Lc 30 against the tint and the surface, where the surface is the page, the subtle recess, a card and a panel, on all six neutrals. No colour clears on step 7 alone. In light, gray, gold, bronze and brown take `--black-a6` and the other 23 take `--black-a5`. In dark, gray and oxblood take `--white-a6` and the other 25 take `--white-a5`. The lowest reading at the step is 3.01:1 on light yellow and Lc 30.4 on dark bronze and crimson, and the tint is the limiting surface in every light case. `components.css` lays the stack on each dash as a second 1px dash on the same box, so it lands dash for dash. On the slot it is a dashed outline on the slot's `::after`, drawn 1px inward onto the border's band. On the drop zone it is a dashed border on the FileInput shell's `::after`, because the zone's own pseudos carry the [focus-ring](#focus-ring) focus ring and a zone can hold focus and a drag at once. The zone is the shell's one in-flow child, so the shell's box is the zone's border box, and the border takes the zone's `--ds-radius-4`. Both rules sit inside `@media (forced-colors: none)`, so forced colours keep the border alone. Every colour takes a step, so every dash changes shade, darker in light and lighter in dark, and nothing else about the slot or the zone moves. Measured in the test browser at 4x on light iris and dark yellow, with the zone at rest and with it focused, no pixel of the bare step 7 dash is left. The slot dash moves from #b8baf8 to #8082ad on light iris and from #4a4a95 to #8181b5 on dark iris. **Guarded by** `_internal/Non-text contrast` → MarksAndDashesOnTint, which renders the empty slot and a FileInput held in its drag state beside the marks, and holds each dash with its stack flattened on it at WCAG 3:1 and APCA Lc 30 against its tint and each of the four surfaces. It also holds where each stack is drawn: a 1px dashed outline at -1px on the slot's 1px dashed border, and a 1px dashed border of the zone's radius on a box of the zone's size. It went red with light gray removed from the `--black-a6` set in `theme.css`, 96 readings, the slot dash at 1.31:1 against its tint on the subtle recess, and with the zone rule removed from `components.css`, on all 324 themes. The temporary review page drops its story 05.

### secondary-text-contrast-gap

**Tags.** `ACCESSIBILITY`, `COLOUR`. **Ruled.** 2026-09-26.

**Link, warning and success text stay on step 11 in light and read just below 4.5:1 on some colours and surfaces, a recorded gap with a planned fix.**

**Measured.** Across 27 colours, six neutrals and two surfaces in light:

| Text | Worst on the page | Worst on `--ds-bg-subtle` | Cases that fail |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--ds-text-link` | 4.395:1, failing on yellow, amber, orange and teal | 4.264:1, with jade and green failing too | 54 of 324 |
| `--ds-text-warning` | 4.497:1 on iris, and 4.395 to 4.457:1 where a brand moves warning to orange | 4.264:1, failing on all 27 colours | 235 of 324 |
| `--ds-text-success` | 4.542:1, passing | 4.407:1, failing on 22 of 27 colours | 132 of 324 |

**Passes.** Every case clears in dark, at 8.26:1 or more, and error and info text clear in both appearances.

**Why nothing moves now.**

- Step 12 clears every case but reads close to primary text, so the secondary token would no longer read as secondary.
- A Radix alpha stacked on the text ([contrast-by-alpha-stacking](#contrast-by-alpha-stacking)) paints only the text the system draws itself, does nothing for a consumer who paints the token directly on step 11, and hides the text from automated checkers such as axe.
- Radix offers no step between 11 and 12.

**Planned fix.** A generated colour between step 11 and step 12, once the system generates its own tokens, as [interaction-state-alphas](#interaction-state-alphas) records. The text guards read these roles against `--ds-bg-base` only, so the cases on the subtle surface have no guard, and the fix adds one.

**Guidance.** The maintainer ruled, on 2026-09-26, to record the gap rather than lose the difference between primary and secondary text, with the aim of a primary and a secondary text token that both meet the contrast floor.

**Changed from.** No earlier ruling covered this.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-09-26. No later ruling amends it.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **Link, warning and success text stay on step 11 in light and fall just under 4.5:1 on some colours and surfaces, an open gap with a planned fix (2026-09-26).** Ruled by the maintainer, whose stated aim is a primary and a secondary text token that are both accessible, and who chose to record the gap rather than lose the difference between the two. Measured over 27 colours, six neutrals and two surfaces in light, through a 1x1 sRGB canvas: link text reads as low as 4.395:1 on the page, orange step 11 on the gray neutral, and fails there on yellow, amber, orange and teal. On `--ds-bg-subtle` it reads as low as 4.264:1, where jade and green fail as well, 54 of 324 cases in all. Warning text reads 4.497:1 on iris on the page and 4.395 to 4.457 where a brand moves warning to orange, and it fails on the subtle surface on all 27 colours, worst 4.264, 235 of 324 cases. Success text clears the page, worst 4.542, and fails on the subtle surface on 22 of 27 colours, worst 4.407, 132 of 324 cases. Every case clears in dark, at 8.26:1 or more, and error and info text clear in both. **Why nothing moves now.** Step 12 clears every case but reads close to primary text, so the secondary token would stop reading as secondary. Stacking a Radix alpha on text ([contrast-by-alpha-stacking](#contrast-by-alpha-stacking)) paints only the text the system draws itself, leaves a consumer who paints the token directly on step 11, and hides the text from automated checkers such as axe. Radix offers no step between 11 and 12. **The follow-up** is a generated colour between the two steps, once the system generates its own tokens, which [interaction-state-alphas](#interaction-state-alphas) already anticipates. The text guards read these roles against `--ds-bg-base` only, so the subtle-surface cases have no guard today, and the follow-up adds one.

### neutral-part-stacks

**Tags.** `ACCESSIBILITY`, `COLOUR`. **Ruled.** 2026-09-26.

**The grey and white parts that read under 3:1 stack a Radix alpha, and the current Pagination dot becomes a pill.**

**Steps.** Each part stacks the lightest step of Radix's black or white alpha scale that clears WCAG 3:1 and APCA Lc 30 against every surface it sits on (the page, the subtle recess, a card and a panel) and against its neighbours, on all six neutrals. The two neutral stacks take the same step on every colour.

| Token | Part | Light | Dark |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--neutral-ring-stack` | Pagination dot ring, selected SegmentedControl segment | `--black-a6` | `--white-a6` |
| `--neutral-thumb-stack` | ScrollArea thumb | `--black-a5` | `--white-a3` |
| `--accent-slider-thumb-stack` | Slider thumb | `--black-a5` | `--black-a6` on yellow, amber, orange, lime, mint and sky, transparent on the other 21 |

**Pagination.** An inactive dot is a 1px ring with a clear centre, `--neutral-ring-stack` over `--ds-fill-press`, and hover fills it with `--ds-fill-medium`. The current dot is a pill `--ds-space-20` long at sizes 1, 2 and 3, at the height of the dot. It keeps `--accent-indicator`, stacks `--accent-mark-edge` as its 1px ring in place of the [indicator-mark-edges](#indicator-mark-edges) edge, and its width does not animate. A focused dot or pill takes a [focus-ring](#focus-ring) ring of its own shape, and every dot keeps the target spacing of WCAG 2.5.8.

**Forced colours.** `forced-colors.css` gives every dot a 1px `ButtonBorder` border, the current dot a `Highlight` fill and border, and a disabled dot `GrayText`. The Slider thumb, the segment and the ScrollArea thumb lose their stack there, as `docs/GUIDELINES.md` section 9 records.

**Not covered.** The classic and soft variants and a disabled thumb keep Radix's paint. A seeded brand keeps the base value of the thumb stack, as [part-fill-edge](#part-fill-edge) records.

**Guidance.** The maintainer approved, on 2026-09-26, the wider scope of the dots, the Slider thumb, the selected segment and the ScrollArea thumb. The maintainer judged a pill 20px long at every size clearly identifiable, and accepted an edge on the pill that reuses the [mark-on-tint-edge](#mark-on-tint-edge) step although it reads one step darker than it needs.

**Changed from.** An inactive dot was a `--ds-fill-press` fill that read as low as 1.29:1 against its surface, the current dot differed from it by colour alone, and under forced colours every dot painted Canvas on Canvas. The Slider thumb, the selected segment and the ScrollArea thumb read under 3:1 against their range, track or lane.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-09-26.

- [colour-prop-and-high-contrast](#colour-prop-and-high-contrast) extends the Slider thumb stack to `highContrast` and to a slider given Radix's `color` prop.
- [part-colour-parity](#part-colour-parity) adds oxblood to the base arm of the Slider thumb stack.

### colour-prop-and-high-contrast

**Tags.** `ACCESSIBILITY`, `COLOUR`. **Ruled.** 2026-09-27.

**A part given Radix's `color` prop or `highContrast` takes the contrast fixes, and Switch, Slider and Progress offer no `soft` variant.**

**What you see.** A part that sets its own colour, or sets `highContrast`, paints the fill, the edge, the thumb rings and the card band that the same part paints on a theme of its own colour. Every edge and card band holds 3:1 against the page, the white switch thumb or its stroke holds 3:1 against its track, and the Slider thumb holds 3:1 against its range and its track.

**Mechanism.** Radix writes the `color` prop as `data-accent-color` on the part, so the `--accent-part-edge`, `--accent-thumb-stroke`, `--accent-slider-thumb-stack`, `--accent-indicator` and `--accent-track` tables in `theme.css` name the part beside the theme root. The dark arms follow [dark-override-selectors](#dark-override-selectors) and skip a light theme nested in a dark one, and a part of a colour outside a table takes the base value.

**Variants.** `Switch.tsx`, `Slider.tsx` and `Progress.tsx` narrow `variant` to `"surface" | "classic"`, so `variant="soft"` is a TypeScript error ([published-aschild-props](#published-aschild-props)). Progress loses `soft` as well, which goes further than [soft-variant-scope](#soft-variant-scope), since that ruling allows `soft` on a display part.

**Limits.**

- A `highContrast` classic switch track and slider range, and a `highContrast` switch thumb, take the rings of the default part, where Radix drew one `--black-a2` ring.
- A dark theme inside a light theme inside a dark page reads the light arm.
- `soft` is still a runtime value, so a cast still paints it.

**Guidance.** The maintainer approved, on 2026-09-27, the extension of the fixes to these parts at WCAG 3:1 with no change to any `--accent-part-edge` value, the removal of `soft` from the types only with no swap at runtime, its removal from Progress as well, and a later audit for APCA Lc 30 and the default Progress bar on dark iris.

**Changed from.** [textless-part-fills](#textless-part-fills), [part-fill-edge](#part-fill-edge), [radio-cards-band-edge](#radio-cards-band-edge) and [neutral-part-stacks](#neutral-part-stacks) excluded a part given `color` or `highContrast`, so a coloured part read as low as 1.31:1 against the page, on light lime. The soft Switch track read 1.24:1 on light yellow.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-09-27. The `_internal/Non-text contrast` story ColourPropAndHighContrast holds these readings.

- [part-colour-parity](#part-colour-parity) applies the same method to every other accent value, so a part takes oxblood, a coloured card picker takes its own selected tint, a dark orange checkbox takes the `#21201c` check, and the textless fills read the part's own `--accent-solid` on a P3 display. The focus ring stays the page accent.
- [status-dot-edges](#status-dot-edges) completes the APCA audit: every part edge clears Lc 30 as well as 3:1, and the default Progress bar on dark iris reads 3.47:1 against its track.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:
