### card-picker-focus-width

**Tags.** `ACCESSIBILITY`, `COMPONENTS`. **Ruled.** 2026-09-27.

**A focused CheckboxCards or RadioCards card shows a 4px focus ring, selected or not, so focus reads apart from selection.**

**What you see.** The ring on a focused card is 4px wide, twice the selection band, in `--ds-stroke-focus` with `--ds-stroke-focus-stack` stacked on it, inset at the card's edge. A card given `color` or `highContrast` takes the same ring, still in the page accent. Card, ClickableCard and every other ring stay at 2px, and no ring changes colour.

**Why.** At 2px the ring painted exactly where the band paints. Measured before the change, a focused selected card looked the same as at rest on 49 of the 54 themes, and a focused card that was not selected looked selected.

**Mechanism.** No stroke-width token exists, so the ring takes a literal `4px`, as every other ring takes a literal `2px`. Outside forced colours both layers paint as 4px inset shadows on the card's `::after`. The card pickers leave the rule Card and ClickableCard share, and a later rule restates the width at the same specificity. The band keeps its focus exclusion, so a focused card paints the ring where the band would paint. Under forced colours the card's own outline is the ring, 4px wide at an offset of `-4px`.

**Limits.**

- The ring stays the page accent, as the maintainer ruled for every ring.
- Where `--ds-stroke-focus` matches the band, the outer 2px of a focused selected card still reads as the band, and the card differs by its inner 2px alone.
- Under forced colours Radix still paints a 2px outline on the `::after` of a focused RadioCards card, so that card shows the text colour on its outer 2px and the ring colour on its inner 2px. No guard runs under forced colours for this ring.

**Guidance.** On 2026-09-27 the maintainer rejected a proposal that moved the ring 2px inside the selection band with a strip of the card's tint between them, and directed instead that the focus stroke on these two cards grow to 4px, or the equivalent token, whether or not the card is selected.

**Changed from.** A focused card picker took the 2px ring [focus-ring](#focus-ring) sets for every control, in the place the selection band paints.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-09-27. It amends [focus-ring](#focus-ring) for these two cards. No later ruling amends it.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **A focused CheckboxCards or RadioCards card rings 4px, selected or not, so focus differs from selection (2026-09-27).** Approved by the maintainer with an amendment, and it amends [focus-ring](#focus-ring) for these two cards. The approved block moved the ring 2px inside the selection band, with a strip of the card's tint between them. The maintainer rejected both options and ruled instead that the focus stroke on these cards grows thicker, 4px or the equivalent token, so a focused card reads apart from a selected one, and that the thicker ring applies whether or not the card is selected. **Measured before**, by a pixel census. Each card on the CheckboxCards and RadioCards Props pages, 334 by 62px, was captured at 2x at rest and under keyboard focus, and the census counts the pixels whose relative luminance differs by 3:1 or more. A focused selected card changed 0 pixels on 23 light colours and 26 dark ones, light and dark iris among them, and 3,060 on light yellow, lime, mint and sky and on dark oxblood. The ring painted where the band paints: the [radio-cards-band-edge](#radio-cards-band-edge) and [colour-prop-and-high-contrast](#colour-prop-and-high-contrast) bands do not paint on a focused card, and the [focus-ring](#focus-ring) ring took their 2px in `--ds-stroke-focus` with its stack, whose contrast with the band's `--accent-indicator` stays under 3:1 on those 49 themes. Over its outer 8px, a focused card that was not selected differed from a selected card at rest by 0 pixels on the same 49 themes, so it looked selected. Forced colours showed the same fault on light iris, dark iris and light yellow, 0 to 20 pixels on a focused selected card in both emulated palettes. **The mechanism.** No stroke-width token exists. Every ring width in `components.css` is a literal `2px`, and `--ds-space-4` is a spacing step that scales with Radix's `--scaling`, so the ring takes a literal `4px` the same way. Outside forced colours the [focus-ring](#focus-ring) section at the end of `components.css` draws both layers, `--ds-stroke-focus` with `--ds-stroke-focus-stack` stacked on it, as 4px inset shadows on the card's `::after` at the card's edge. The card pickers leave the rule that Card and ClickableCard share, and a rule after it restates the width at the same specificity. The [radio-cards-band-edge](#radio-cards-band-edge) and [colour-prop-and-high-contrast](#colour-prop-and-high-contrast) bands keep their focus exclusions, so a focused card paints the ring where the band would paint, twice as wide. A card given `color` or `highContrast` takes the same ring, still in the page's accent. Under forced colours the card's own outline is the ring, and it goes from 2px at -2px to 4px at -4px. Card, ClickableCard and every other ring stay at 2px, and no ring changes colour. In `_assert.ts`, `ringWidthFor` names 4px for the two card items and 2px for every other carrier, `readDrawnRing` reads every inset shadow at least 2px wide as a ring layer, and `checkDrawnRing` holds each layer at the carrier's width. **Measured after**, the same way on 27 colours in both appearances. A focused selected card differs from itself at rest over 6,088 to 9,176 pixels, a focused card that was not selected over 12,276 to 12,312, and a focused card that was not selected differs from a selected card at rest over 6,080 to 9,176. The 2px strip the thicker ring adds, 2px to 4px in from the edge, covers 6,144 pixels of the card at 2x, so the census counts at least 98.9% of it on every colour, and the pixels it misses sit on the antialiased corners. Under forced colours a focused selected card differs from itself at rest over 6,092 to 6,128 pixels in both palettes, on the same three themes. **Limits.** The ring stays the page's accent, as the maintainer ruled for every ring. Where `--ds-stroke-focus` matches the band, the outer 2px of a focused selected card still reads as the band, and the card differs by the inner 2px alone. Under forced colours Radix still paints a 2px outline on the `::after` of a focused RadioCards card, which the palette forces to the text colour, so that card shows the text colour on its outer 2px and the ring colour on the inner 2px. No guard runs under forced colours for this ring. **Guarded by** `_internal/Non-text contrast` → FocusRingOnParts. Its specimen adds a CheckboxCards card and a RadioCards card that are not selected beside the selected ones. For each of the four cards on 27 accents in both appearances, it holds each ring layer at 4px on the card itself, and it reads the card's paint in 1px bands from its edge inward, at rest and focused, from the card's own box and its two pseudos. It holds the focused paint at 3:1 against the rest paint, and against a selected card at rest, over at least the area of the 2px strip the 4px ring adds, 4 x (w + h) - 48 CSS px, which is 1,248 px on the specimen's 288 by 36 card. The model counts whole bands and does not model the corners, so it demands the whole strip. With the [card-picker-focus-width](#card-picker-focus-width) width rule set back to 2px it went red with 648 failures in each lane: 324 ring layers at 2px, all 108 selected cards under 1,248 px against themselves at rest, and all 216 cards under 1,248 px against a selected card at rest. Restored, the file matched its snapshot and the story passed in both lanes.

### tab-panel-focus-clearance

**Tags.** `ACCESSIBILITY`, `LAYOUT`. **Ruled.** 2026-09-27.

**Tabs owns a 16px gap above every panel, so the focus ring of a panel clears the tab list.**

**Why.** The tab panel rings 2px outside its edge in a 2px band, so the ring reaches 4px above the panel top. A panel flush with its list put the ring over the list's 2px underline, a clearance of -4px, and pages hid the fault with a hand-written `Box pt="4"` wrapper.

**Mechanism.** One rule in `components.css` gives `.rt-TabsContent` a `margin-top` of `var(--ds-space-16)`, the 16px the wrappers gave, and the story files dropped their wrappers. The guard `_internal/Focus → TabPanelRingClearsList` mounts real Tabs with no wrapper at the small, medium and large sizes, focuses each panel with keyboard modality and holds every ring layer at least 2px below the list.

**What you see.** The panel sits 16px below the list, and the ring clears the list by 12px on every panel. An inactive panel carries the `hidden` attribute and takes no room, and a `forceMount` panel with no content adds 16px below its list.

**Exception.** A panel given its own margin prop, `m`, `my` or `mt`, keeps that margin in place of the gap, so `mt="0"` removes it. Space a consumer adds above the panel sums with the gap, so the `Box pt="3"` wrapper the Radix Themes docs show gives 28px.

**Guidance.** The maintainer approved, on 2026-09-27, the option in which Tabs owns the gap above the panel, with the limit that space a consumer adds above the panel doubles it.

**Changed from.** A panel sat flush under its tab list, and each page that wanted room above it added its own `Box pt="4"` wrapper.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-09-27. No later ruling amends it.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **Tabs owns a 16px gap above every panel, so the panel's focus ring clears the tab list (2026-09-27).** Approved by the maintainer, who chose the first of two options, the one in which Tabs owns a 16px gap above the panel. The tab panel rings 2px outside its edge in a 2px band, so the ring reaches 4px above the panel top. **Measured before**, in Chromium at 1280px wide on iris light: on the tabs specimen of `_internal/Non-text contrast → FocusRingOnParts` the panel is empty and flush with the list, so the ring's top band lies 4px to 2px above the panel top, over the list's 2px underline, a clearance of -4px. On the Tabs Usage page a `Box pt="4"` wrapper placed the panel 16px below the list, and the ring cleared the underline by 12px. The same hand-written wrapper sat under the tabs on the Tabs Keyboard and Props stories, the `_internal/Tabs behavior → Roving` specimen and the `_internal/Composition` fixture. **The mechanism** is one rule in `components.css`: `.rt-TabsContent` takes `margin-top: var(--ds-space-16)`, the 16px the wrappers gave, and the `pt` wrappers are gone from those three story files. **Measured after**: 16px from the list bottom to the panel top on all five stories, the same as before, and a clearance of 12px from the list to the ring on every panel, the flush specimen included. An inactive panel carries the `hidden` attribute and takes no room. A `forceMount` panel with no content now adds 16px below its list. The rule skips a panel given its own margin prop (`m`, `my` or `mt`), so `mt="0"` on the panel removes the gap. **The limit**, named in the option the maintainer chose: a consumer who adds their own space above the panel, such as the `Box pt="3"` wrapper the Radix Themes docs show, gets double, 28px in that case. **The guard** is `_internal/Focus → TabPanelRingClearsList`. It mounts real Tabs with the panel directly after the list and no wrapper, one panel empty and one with text, at the small, medium and large tiers, focuses each panel with keyboard modality and reads the ring off every layer it paints. Each layer's top edge must lie at least 2px below the list. With the margin rule removed it went red in both lanes, 18 findings, each at -4.00px, six on `::before` in light and twelve on `::before` and `::after` in dark, and green again after the restore. Prior art is in `REFERENCES.md`.

### part-colour-parity

**Tags.** `ACCESSIBILITY`, `COLOUR`. **Ruled.** 2026-09-27.

**A part given its own colour paints what the same part paints on a page of that colour, oxblood included.**

**What you see.** A part with its own `color` matches its twin on a theme of that colour in both appearances: label, fill, check, radio dot and card tint. Each label holds 4.5:1 and each check and radio dot 3:1 against its fill, and a part given oxblood paints oxblood. The guard is the `ColourPropAndHighContrast` story under `_internal/Non-text contrast`.

**Mechanism.** It extends the method of [colour-prop-and-high-contrast](#colour-prop-and-high-contrast) to every accent value. Each table names the part beside the theme root, with the [dark-override-selectors](#dark-override-selectors) skip on its dark arms.

- `theme.css`: one text-fill table at the top holds `--on-accent`, `--on-accent-weak`, `--on-accent-disabled` and `--accent-solid`, with the colour pins and the gray pins keyed on the neutral. The `--accent-mark-edge` and `--accent-dash-stack` tables and the dark orange `--accent-contrast` also name the part.
- `semantic.css`: the accent roles, among them `--ds-fill-accent`, `--ds-text-link` and `--ds-stroke-accent`, sit in their own block with the same two arms.
- `oxblood.css`: maps the oxblood scale onto any part inside a theme that sets oxblood, the way Radix maps its own colours.
- `components.css`: the solid Button, IconButton and Code chip rules no longer exclude a part given `color`. They keep the `[data-tone]`, `highContrast` and disabled exclusions, so tone still wins ([destructive-tone](#destructive-tone)).

**Excluded.**

- The focus ring, `--ds-stroke-focus`, `--ds-stroke-focus-stack` and the `--accent-ring-stack` tables, so every part keeps one focus colour.
- `--ds-fill-selected` and `--ds-stroke-selected`, whose one consumer is `forced-colors.css`, which maps them to `Highlight` on the theme root.
- The error, warning, success and info families and their collision shifts, which key on the brand and never on a part ([destructive-tone](#destructive-tone)).
- The APCA orange arm in `contrast.css`, which changes nothing on a part.

**The type.** The package exports `AccentColor`, the 26 Radix colours plus oxblood, which the `accentColor` of `Provider` and the `color` prop of every wrapper read. Radix `extractProps` drops a colour outside its own 26, so two internal helpers in `src/theme/Provider.tsx` write `data-accent-color="oxblood"`. `accentColorProps` spreads it ahead of the caller's props, so an explicit `data-accent-color` from the caller wins, and `useAccentColorRef` writes it through a ref where Radix writes the attribute after the props or on another element.

**Limits.**

- A part that takes oxblood through the ref paints the theme's colour in a server render until the page hydrates.
- The Badge wrapper locks the soft variant, so the Radix solid Badge keeps step 9 under its ink.
- A gray part three nested neutral themes deep takes the base fill, and a dark theme inside a light theme inside a dark page reads the light arm.
- Under forced colours both selected roles stay on the root. A later consumer of either role on a coloured part needs the roles block of `forced-colors.css` widened to `.radix-themes, .radix-themes :where([data-accent-color]:not([data-accent-color=""]))`.

**Guidance.** The maintainer approved this ruling on 2026-09-27 with two decisions: one focus colour for every part, so a coloured part keeps the page accent on its focus ring, and one exported colour type for the `color` prop of every wrapper.

**Changed from.** A part read the accent roles of the theme root, not of its own colour. A primary Button given `color="teal"` read 3.07:1 for its label where its twin on a teal page read 4.56:1, a part given oxblood painted iris, and a cast `color="oxblood"` never reached the DOM.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-09-27.

- [documentation-and-markup-gaps](#documentation-and-markup-gaps) records that the Colors page now reads every block for a colour, so the limit about the Colors page alias no longer holds.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **A part given its own colour paints what the same part paints on a page of that colour, oxblood included (2026-09-27).** Approved by the maintainer, with two decisions, and it amends [colour-prop-and-high-contrast](#colour-prop-and-high-contrast). Decision 3 keeps one focus colour throughout for consistency, so the focus ring on a coloured part stays the page's accent. Decision 4 approves one exported colour type for every wrapper. An earlier ruling holds that oxblood, an accent added to fill a gap, behaves in the same way as every other colour. **Measured before**, through a 1x1 sRGB canvas under the default slate neutral, with a real part cloned under an iris theme and compared with the same part on a plain theme of its colour. A primary Button given `color="teal"` read 3.07:1 for its label, where its twin read 4.56:1. On gold, bronze, brown, orange, tomato, red, ruby, crimson, pink, blue, cyan, teal, jade, green and grass the label read 2.97 to 4.12:1 in both appearances, where the twin read 4.51 to 5.91:1, and gray read 3.30:1 in light against 5.94:1, a 16th colour the approved block did not name. A checked Checkbox given orange in dark drew a white check at 2.97:1 on orange-9, where the twin drew #21201c at 5.47:1. A part given oxblood painted iris-9, #5b5bd6. A CheckboxCards set given any colour kept the theme's tint, #ecedfc on light iris. Radix's extractProps also replaces a `color` outside its own 26 with the default, so a cast `color="oxblood"` never reached the DOM at all. **The mechanism** is the [colour-prop-and-high-contrast](#colour-prop-and-high-contrast) method, applied to every remaining accent value. The `--ds-*` accent roles and the theme.css pins resolved on the theme root, so a part that sets `data-accent-color` never saw them. Each table now names the part beside the root, with the [colour-prop-and-high-contrast](#colour-prop-and-high-contrast) [dark-override-selectors](#dark-override-selectors) skip on the dark arms and a base arm on every part with a non-empty `data-accent-color`. **Widened**: the ink and the fill that carry text, `--on-accent`, `--on-accent-weak`, `--on-accent-disabled` and `--accent-solid`, which move out of the collision blocks into one text-fill table at the top of theme.css, with the 15 colour pins, the white orange ink and the six gray pins keyed on the neutral, whose part arm skips a part inside a nested theme of another neutral. The dark orange glyph ink, `--accent-contrast: #21201c`. The [mark-on-tint-edge](#mark-on-tint-edge) `--accent-mark-edge` and the [drop-target-dash](#drop-target-dash) `--accent-dash-stack` tables. The [textless-part-fills](#textless-part-fills) indicator and track part arm, which now reads the part's own `--accent-solid` in place of `--accent-11`, so the [colour-prop-and-high-contrast](#colour-prop-and-high-contrast) P3 limit closes. Oxblood joins the base arms of the [textless-part-fills](#textless-part-fills) thumb stroke, the [part-fill-edge](#part-fill-edge) part edge and the [neutral-part-stacks](#neutral-part-stacks) Slider thumb stack, and the dark oxblood part edge names the part. In semantic.css the accent roles move into their own block with the same two arms: `--ds-bg-high-contrast`, `--ds-text-link`, `--ds-icon-interactive`, `--ds-fill-accent`, `--ds-fill-accent-hover`, `--ds-fill-accent-med`, `--ds-fill-accent-weak`, `--ds-fill-selected-subtle`, `--ds-stroke-accent` and `--ds-stroke-accent-weak`, and the white hover overlay under a dark ink. oxblood.css maps the oxblood scale onto any part inside a theme that sets oxblood, the way Radix maps its own colours. In components.css the solid Button, IconButton and Code chip rules drop their exclusion of a part given `color`, and keep the `[data-tone]`, `highContrast` and disabled exclusions, so tone still wins ([destructive-tone](#destructive-tone)). **Excluded**: the focus ring, `--ds-stroke-focus`, `--ds-stroke-focus-stack` and the three `--accent-ring-stack` tables, by decision 3. `--ds-fill-selected` and `--ds-stroke-selected`, whose one consumer is forced-colors.css, which re-points them to Highlight on the theme root, so a part that declared them would paint its own step in place of Highlight under forced colours. The error, warning, success and info families and their collision shifts, which key on the brand and never on a part ([destructive-tone](#destructive-tone)). The contrast.css APCA orange arm, which changes nothing on a part, because the Radix orange ink is already white in light. **The type and the helpers.** Provider.tsx exports `AccentColor`, the 26 Radix colours plus oxblood, which the named `accentColor` of Provider reads, published through registry.json and `npm run barrel`. The `color` prop of the 44 parts in the 31 wrappers takes it. Because extractProps drops oxblood, Provider.tsx holds two internal helpers. `accentColorProps` returns the Radix `color` for the 26 and `data-accent-color="oxblood"` for oxblood, spread ahead of the caller's props, so an explicit `data-accent-color` from the caller still wins. `useAccentColorRef` writes the attribute through a ref where Radix writes it after the rest of the props or on another element: DataList.Label, Link, and the TextArea and TextField roots. Avatar reaches its root span through `asChild`, and CheckboxGroup and RadioGroup hand oxblood to each item. The menu checkbox and radio items read `color` with no list, so the value passes through as is. Rendered with teal and with oxblood, all 44 parts carry the attribute on the same element, and on the Button, Checkbox, Badge, Code, Switch, Callout and Heading an explicit `data-accent-color` from the caller wins. **Measured after**, the same way: every row of the census matches its twin in both appearances, the lowest label reads 4.51:1 on orange, the teal label reads 4.56:1, the dark orange check reads 5.47:1 in #21201c, the lowest check reads 3.00:1 on dark cyan, the reading of a cyan theme itself, a part given oxblood paints #8a2119, and a lime card set paints the lime tint, #ecf4d5 in light and #1f2a19 in dark. `node .probe/color-props.mjs` lists 44 of 44 parts with oxblood in `color`. **Limits.** A part that takes oxblood through the ref paints the theme's colour in a server render until the page hydrates. The Badge wrapper locks the soft variant, so no system solid badge carries text, and the Radix solid Badge keeps step 9 under its ink on a theme and on a part alike. A gray part inside a theme of one neutral, inside a theme of another neutral, inside a theme of the first, takes the base fill. A dark theme inside a light theme inside a dark page reads the light arm, as [colour-prop-and-high-contrast](#colour-prop-and-high-contrast) records. The Colors page reads the first theme.css block that names an accent, so it now names the error alias of gold, orange, tomato, red, ruby, crimson and pink as a pin, where the value is oxblood-9. Under forced colours `--ds-fill-selected` and `--ds-stroke-selected` stay on the root, so a coloured checkbox keeps Highlight, and a later consumer of either role on a coloured part needs the forced-colors.css roles block widened to `.radix-themes, .radix-themes :where([data-accent-color]:not([data-accent-color=""]))`. **Guarded by** `_internal/Non-text contrast` → ColourPropAndHighContrast, which now also renders a solid Button, IconButton and Code chip, sweeps 27 colours with oxblood, holds each label at 4.5:1 and each check and radio dot at 3:1 against its fill, and holds each label, fill, check, dot and card tint at the paint of its twin, in six frames, both appearances and six neutrals. It went red with the part arm removed from the teal text-fill pin in theme.css, 450 failures in each lane with the teal Button label at 3.07:1, and with the part arm removed from the oxblood map in oxblood.css, 864 failures in each lane with the oxblood checkbox at #ffdc00 and 1.32:1. Both went green on restore.

### documentation-and-markup-gaps

**Tags.** `DOCUMENTATION`, `ACCESSIBILITY`. **Ruled.** 2026-09-27.

**Six documentation and markup gaps are recorded here and left unfixed, so the release carries them in writing.**

**Found during.** The [card-picker-focus-width](#card-picker-focus-width), [tab-panel-focus-clearance](#tab-panel-focus-clearance) and [part-colour-parity](#part-colour-parity) builds, on 2026-09-27.

**Gaps, as found.**

1. The comment in the card picker section of `components.css` says Radix keeps the focus outline untouched, which stopped being true at [focus-ring](#focus-ring).
2. The Enforcement page and the header of `axe-scope.node-check.ts` say 18 stories opt out of axe, where the registered set counted 24.
3. The Tabs entry in `registry.json` carried no `priorArt`, so the React Aria and Radix Tabs sources reached it only through [tab-panel-focus-clearance](#tab-panel-focus-clearance). Closed, see Status.
4. A comment in `DragHandle.tsx` and one in `PowerSearch.tsx` describe a neutral focus ring, which [focus-ring](#focus-ring) replaced with the accent.
5. Two tables on the Table Usage page have no accessible name.
6. `MultiSelect` options carry no `aria-posinset` or `aria-setsize`, which [select-option-numbering](#select-option-numbering) added to `Select` only.

**Correction.** One [part-colour-parity](#part-colour-parity) limit no longer holds. The Colors page alias reader reads every block for a colour, so it names oxblood-9 as the error fill of gold, orange, tomato, red, ruby, crimson and pink again.

**Changed from.** No earlier ruling covered this.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-09-27.

- [tabs-open-on-navigation](#tabs-open-on-navigation) closes item 3 and gives the Tabs entry in `registry.json` its `priorArt`.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **Six small documentation and markup gaps, recorded and NOT FIXED (2026-09-27).** Found during the [card-picker-focus-width](#card-picker-focus-width), [tab-panel-focus-clearance](#tab-panel-focus-clearance) and [part-colour-parity](#part-colour-parity) builds, and written here so the release carries them in writing. (1) The comment in the card picker section of `components.css` says the focus outline is handed back to Radix untouched, which stopped being true at [focus-ring](#focus-ring). (2) The Enforcement page and the `axe-scope.node-check.ts` header say 18 stories opt out of axe, where the registered set now counts 24. (3) The Tabs entry in `registry.json` carries no `priorArt`, so the React Aria and Radix Tabs sources reach it only through [tab-panel-focus-clearance](#tab-panel-focus-clearance). (4) `DragHandle.tsx` line 28 and `PowerSearch.tsx` lines 69 and 70 still describe a neutral focus ring, which [focus-ring](#focus-ring) replaced with the accent. (5) Two tables on the Table Usage page have no accessible name. (6) MultiSelect options carry no `aria-posinset` or `aria-setsize`, which [select-option-numbering](#select-option-numbering) added to Select only. One [part-colour-parity](#part-colour-parity) limit no longer holds: the Colors page alias reader now reads every block for a colour, so it names oxblood-9 as the error fill of gold, orange, tomato, red, ruby, crimson and pink again. Item (3) is closed by [tabs-open-on-navigation](#tabs-open-on-navigation), which gives the Tabs entry in `registry.json` its priorArt.

### status-dot-edges

**Tags.** `ACCESSIBILITY`, `COLOUR`. **Ruled.** 2026-09-27.

**Every status dot, Progress bar and checked control clears WCAG 3:1 and APCA Lc 30 with its centre colour unchanged, and the description of a selected row reads in strong ink.**

**Dot edges.** The warning, success and error StatusDot each stack a 1px inset edge on the fill, `--warning-dot-edge`, `--success-dot-edge` or `--error-dot-edge`, and the centre keeps its colour. The Avatar status dot is a StatusDot and paints the same edge inside its 2px cutout border.

**Edge steps.** Each edge is the lightest step of Radix's black alpha scale in light, or white alpha scale in dark, whose stack on the fill clears both floors against the page, the subtle recess, a card and a panel on all six neutrals. `theme.css` keys the table on the brand at the theme root, because the status families shift with the brand ([brand-status-collision-gate](#brand-status-collision-gate)) and never with a part, so a part given its own colour takes the edge of the brand whose fill it paints.

| Edge | Appearance | Brands | Step |
|---|---|---|---|
| Warning | Light | Gold, yellow, amber, lime | `--black-a1` |
| Warning | Light | Brown | `--black-a6` |
| Warning | Light | The other 22 | `--black-a5` |
| Success | Light | Teal, jade, green, grass | `--black-a6` |
| Success | Light | The other 23 | `--black-a1` |
| Error | Dark | Gold, yellow, amber, orange, tomato, red, ruby, crimson, pink, lime | `--white-a6` |
| Error | Dark | Bronze | `--white-a4` |
| Error | Dark | The other 16 | `--white-a3` |

Light error and dark warning and success clear on the fill alone and keep the transparent base.

**Part edge.** `--accent-part-edge` clears both floors on the four surfaces, and the Progress bar and the Slider range clear them against their track on each surface. Light amber takes `--black-a6`. In dark, pink takes `--white-a1`, gray and plum take `--white-a3`, purple, violet, iris and indigo take `--white-a4`, and oxblood takes `--white-a6`.

**Selected row.** A selected row keeps `--ds-fill-selected-subtle` in both appearances, the tint Select, the CommandPalette and the current Pagination page share, and its description takes `--ds-text-strong`. The rule reaches the row's own description only, as [selected-row-cue](#selected-row-cue) reaches its label.

**Limits.**

- A standalone StatusDot shows nothing under forced colours, because `forced-colors.css` names no rule for it ([forced-colours](#forced-colours)). This ruling leaves that gap open.
- A seeded brand keeps the transparent base of the three dot edges, as [part-fill-edge](#part-fill-edge) records for the part edge.
- A dot given `isPulsing` dims to half opacity at the low point of its pulse, edge included, so the floors hold at rest.
- The change bar in `CodeEditor.stories.tsx` stacks the warning and success edges, but it sits in a showcase, which [showcases-and-fixture](#showcases-and-fixture) bars from a play, so no guard holds it.
- Gap: in `CodeEditor.stories.tsx` the "M" mark in `--ds-text-warning` on the selected TreeList row reads as low as 3.19:1 on the selected tint in light on iris, brown and teal. This ruling sets strong ink on the description alone, and the end slot holds content the consumer supplies.

**Guidance.** The maintainer approved the proposed fix on 2026-09-27, with a preference for the weaker tint `--ds-fill-accent-weak` on a selected row in light if every WCAG and APCA check still passed, and accepted the proposed fix in both appearances if that mix proved impractical. The mix proved impractical: `.rt-ds-item[data-selected]` paints the selected row in SideNav, TopNav, TreeList, MobileNav and List, so the weaker tint would give those rows a paler selection than Select, the CommandPalette and the current Pagination page. The build took the proposed fix in both appearances.

**Changed from.** The three status dots painted their fill alone and failed 3:1 on all 27 colours, warning and success in light and error in dark. The part edge failed on light amber and on eight dark colours, and a selected row's description read in weak ink, under 4.5:1 on 25 light colours and all 27 dark ones.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-09-27. No later ruling amends it.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **Every status dot, Progress bar and checked control clears WCAG 3:1 and APCA Lc 30 with its colour unchanged at the centre, and a selected row's description reads in strong ink (2026-09-27).** Approved by the maintainer as column 2 of story 10 on the decision review page, the proposed fix. The maintainer preferred the weaker tint in light and the proposed fix in dark if every WCAG and APCA check still passed, and accepted the proposed fix in both appearances if that mix proved impossible or impractical, since every check passes with it. Column 3 painted a selected row in the weaker accent tint, `--ds-fill-accent-weak`, and left its description in weak ink. The mix proved impractical, so the build took the second option, the proposed fix, for this reason: `.rt-ds-item[data-selected]` paints the selected row in SideNav, TopNav, TreeList, MobileNav and List, so the weaker tint in light would give those rows a paler selection than Select, the CommandPalette and the current Pagination page, two selected tints in one light UI. A selected row keeps `--ds-fill-selected-subtle` in both appearances, and its description takes `--ds-text-strong`. [status-dot-edges](#status-dot-edges) closes the APCA audit that [colour-prop-and-high-contrast](#colour-prop-and-high-contrast) left open for the [part-fill-edge](#part-fill-edge), [radio-cards-band-edge](#radio-cards-band-edge) and [indicator-mark-edges](#indicator-mark-edges) part edges, the default Progress bar on dark iris among them, and it retires the warning dot gap that [apca-contrast-mode](#apca-contrast-mode) recorded. **Measured before**, through a 1x1 sRGB canvas on 27 colours, six neutrals and both appearances, against the page, the subtle recess, a card and a panel. The warning dot read as low as 1.20:1 and Lc 9.1 in light, the yellow of a brown brand on the subtle recess on sage, and failed on all 27 colours. The success dot read as low as 1.27:1 and Lc 13.0 in light, the lime of a teal brand, and failed on all 27, since green-9 reads 2.87 to 2.99:1 on the subtle recess. The error dot read as low as 1.74:1 and Lc 10.1 in dark, the oxblood of a gold brand on a panel, and failed on all 27, since red-9 reads Lc 28.6 on a panel. Against its cutout ring the Avatar away dot read 1.23:1 and the online dot 1.31:1 in light, and the busy dot 2.06:1 and Lc 12.0 in dark. The part edge failed on light amber, 2.68:1 against the Progress track on the subtle recess, and on eight dark colours, gray, pink, plum, purple, violet, iris, indigo and oxblood, as low as 2.21:1 and Lc 17.7 for the oxblood Progress bar against its track on a panel. With the track on the page alone the dark Progress bar read as low as 2.73:1 and Lc 20.9, on oxblood, and failed on the seven colours the approved block named. The dark iris bar read 2.37:1 and Lc 19.6 against its track on a panel. The description on the selected tint read as low as 3.64:1 and Lc 49.9 in light, on oxblood over the subtle recess on mauve, and 4.03:1 and Lc 47.0 in dark on a panel, and failed on 25 light colours and all 27 dark ones. Light error, dark warning and success, and the neutral dot cleared. **The steps.** Each is the lightest step of Radix's black alpha scale in light, or white alpha scale in dark, whose stack on the fill clears WCAG 3:1 AND APCA Lc 30 against the four surfaces on all six neutrals. The lowest reading at the step comes first, then the step one lighter. `theme.css` adds `--warning-dot-edge`, `--success-dot-edge` and `--error-dot-edge` in one table keyed on the brand. The status families shift with the brand ([brand-status-collision-gate](#brand-status-collision-gate)) and never with a part ([destructive-tone](#destructive-tone), [part-colour-parity](#part-colour-parity)), so the table names the theme root alone, in both [dark-override-selectors](#dark-override-selectors) dark shapes, and a part given its own colour inherits the edge of the brand whose fill it paints. LIGHT WARNING: `--black-a1` on gold, yellow, amber and lime, which move warning to orange (3.10:1, the fill alone reads 2.81), `--black-a6` on brown, which moves it to yellow (3.31, `--black-a5` reads 2.49), and `--black-a5` on the other 22 (3.04, `--black-a4` reads 2.34). LIGHT SUCCESS: `--black-a6` on teal, jade, green and grass, which move success to lime (3.49, `--black-a5` reads 2.63), and `--black-a1` on the other 23 (3.16 on mint, the fill alone reads 2.87 to 2.99). DARK ERROR: `--white-a6` on gold, yellow, amber, orange, tomato, red, ruby, crimson, pink and lime, which move error to oxblood (4.53:1 and Lc 36.9, `--white-a5` reads Lc 28.5), `--white-a4` on bronze, which moves it to ruby (Lc 32.1, `--white-a3` reads Lc 29.5), and `--white-a3` on the other 16 (Lc 30.7, `--white-a2` reads Lc 28.6). Light error and dark warning and success clear on the fill alone (4.93:1 and Lc 70.3, 5.31:1 and Lc 43.8, 5.00:1 and Lc 40.9) and keep the transparent base. The dot steps match the review page on every colour. `--accent-part-edge` is now held at both floors on the four surfaces, and the Progress bar and the Slider range against their track on each surface as well. Light amber moves from `--black-a5` to `--black-a6`, beside yellow, lime, mint and sky (3.07:1 on lime against its track on the subtle recess, `--black-a5` reads 2.32 to 2.68). In dark the track on a panel sets every step. Pink takes `--white-a1` (3.27:1 and Lc 30.5, the fill alone reads Lc 28.7), gray and plum take `--white-a3` (Lc 30.1 on gray, `--white-a2` reads Lc 26.9 to 28.8), purple, violet, iris and indigo take `--white-a4` (Lc 31.8 on violet, `--white-a3` reads Lc 28.4 to 29.3), and oxblood moves from `--white-a4` to `--white-a6` (3.65:1 and Lc 33.7, `--white-a5` reads Lc 25.3). The review page held the track on the page alone, so it drew `--white-a2` on plum, `--white-a3` on purple, violet, iris and indigo, and no step on pink. The build takes one step more on those five and adds pink, a colour the approved block did not name, because the track on a panel reads under Lc 30 at the lighter steps. The [colour-prop-and-high-contrast](#colour-prop-and-high-contrast) and [part-colour-parity](#part-colour-parity) part arms and the [dark-override-selectors](#dark-override-selectors) skips stay on every part edge arm. **The paint.** In `components.css` the warning, success and error StatusDot rules stack their edge as a 1px inset box-shadow on the fill, and the centre keeps its colour. The Avatar status dot is a StatusDot and takes the same edge, which an inset shadow paints inside its 2px cutout border. The pulse keyframes and the reduced-motion rule do not change. The description of a selected row takes `--ds-text-strong` through `.rt-ds-item[data-selected] > :is(.rt-ds-item-content, .rt-ds-item-body) > .rt-ds-item-description`, whose child combinators reach the row's own description only, as [selected-row-cue](#selected-row-cue) reaches its label. `CodeEditor.stories.tsx` stacks `--warning-dot-edge` and `--success-dot-edge` on the change bar, which is 2px wide, so the ring covers all of it. The modified bar on light iris moves from 1.54:1 to 3.13:1 against its line. **Forced colours.** Forced colours compute box-shadow to none and paint the dot fill Canvas. Measured under emulation at 4x on the dot specimen, the light palette render is byte-identical before and after, and the dark palette render is byte-identical to a render of the stylesheets at HEAD. In both the Avatar dot shows its 2px cutout border in CanvasText, and a standalone StatusDot paints Canvas on Canvas and shows nothing, before [status-dot-edges](#status-dot-edges) and after it ([forced-colours](#forced-colours)). **Measured after**, the same way. The warning dot reads 3.04:1 and Lc 55.3 or more in light, the success dot 3.16:1 and Lc 56.7, and the error dot 3.71:1 and Lc 30.7 in dark. The Avatar dots read 3.13:1 or more against their ring in light, and 4.41:1 and Lc 32.7 or more in dark. Every part edge reads 3.07:1 and Lc 52.1 or more in light and 3.25:1 and Lc 30.1 or more in dark, the Progress bar and the Slider range against their track included, and the dark iris bar reads 3.47:1 and Lc 31.9 against its track on a panel. The selected description reads 10.13:1 and Lc 73.6 or more in light and 7.28:1 and Lc 82.1 or more in dark. **Limits.** A standalone StatusDot shows nothing under forced colours, because forced-colors.css names no rule for it, an open gap that [status-dot-edges](#status-dot-edges) does not change. A seeded brand (ds-custom) keeps the transparent base of the three dot edges, as [part-fill-edge](#part-fill-edge) records for the part edge. A dot given `isPulsing` dims to half opacity at the trough of its breathe, its edge included, so the floors hold at rest. On 23 light colours the success edge is `--black-a1`, which only the subtle recess needs. The Avatar dot is held against its cutout ring, which paints `--ds-bg-base` on any surface. The change bar sits in a showcase, which [showcases-and-fixture](#showcases-and-fixture) bars from a play, so no guard holds it. **Found on the way, recorded and NOT FIXED:** in `CodeEditor.stories.tsx` the "M" mark in `--ds-text-warning` on the selected TreeList row reads 3.19 to 3.33:1 and Lc 48.3 to 50.5 on the selected tint in light on iris, brown and teal. [status-dot-edges](#status-dot-edges) sets strong ink on the description alone, and the end slot holds content the consumer supplies. **Guarded by** `_internal/Non-text contrast` → DotsEdgesAndSelectedRows. It renders every StatusDot variant, an Avatar with each status, a List with a static and a clickable selected row that each carry a description, the PartsWithoutText parts and the Analytics dashboard chart card, clones them into 27 accents, both appearances and six neutrals, and holds each dot and each part that stacks `--accent-part-edge` at WCAG 3:1 and APCA Lc 30 against the four surfaces, each Avatar dot against its cutout ring, the Progress bar and the Slider range against their track on each surface, and each selected description at 4.5:1 and Lc 60 on its tint. It went red with the dark `--white-a4` arm removed from the `--accent-part-edge` table in `theme.css`, 1,206 failures in each appearance lane, the purple Progress bar at 2.49:1 and Lc 21.0 against its track on a panel, and with the warning edge removed from the StatusDot rule in `components.css`, 810 failures in each lane, every light warning dot and Avatar away dot on 27 colours and six neutrals. Both went green on restore. The temporary review page `_decisions.proto.stories.tsx` is deleted.

### tabs-open-on-navigation

**Tags.** `ACCESSIBILITY`, `COMPONENTS`. **Ruled.** 2026-09-28.

**Only navigation opens a tab, so a screen reader cursor that moves focus opens nothing.**

**Why.** Radix's automatic mode opens a tab on every focus event, whatever moved the focus (Radix #1047). VoiceOver moves keyboard focus as its cursor reads, so a VoiceOver user who read across the tab row opened each tab on the way.

**What opens a tab.**

- An unmodified ArrowLeft, ArrowRight, ArrowUp, ArrowDown, Home, End, PageUp or PageDown that moves focus to it.
- Enter, Space or a pointer press.
- A click that no press began, such as the click VoiceOver sends on its modifier key (VO) plus Space and the click `element.click()` sends.

A bare focus opens nothing. `activationMode="manual"` keeps manual, so arrow keys move focus only, and an explicit `activationMode="automatic"` takes the default behaviour above. `Tabs.Nav` links navigate and do not change.

**How.** `Tabs.Root` holds the value, controlled or uncontrolled, runs Radix in manual mode and shares an activation context. `Tabs.Trigger` marks a navigation keydown, and a focus that arrives while the mark stands opens that tab. A key with no focus intent for the list's orientation, such as ArrowUp in a horizontal list, drops the mark in a microtask, and otherwise the mark clears 100ms later. The click that ends a pointer press, Enter or Space selects nothing, so a controlled Root receives one `onValueChange` call per action, the shape [dropdown-assistive-click](#dropdown-assistive-click) gives DropdownMenu. The rule matches the WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices automatic tabs example, which opens a tab in its keydown and click handlers and registers no focus listener.

**Limits.**

- No VoiceOver run confirms the fix yet, and [wcag-claim-scope](#wcag-claim-scope) keeps its assistive technology item open until that pass runs.
- The mark relies on Radix moving roving focus within 100ms of the keydown, which its zero-delay timeout does today.
- Home or PageUp on the first tab, and End or PageDown on the last, move no focus, so a focus from any source within 100ms after one of them still opens its tab.

**Guidance.** The maintainer approved this rule on 2026-09-28, and chose that an explicit `activationMode="automatic"` take the same behaviour as the default.

**Changed from.** `Tabs` was a thin wrap over Radix's automatic mode, so any focus on a trigger opened its tab ([floating-surface-wraps](#floating-surface-wraps)). The registry entry for Tabs carried no `priorArt`, item 3 of [documentation-and-markup-gaps](#documentation-and-markup-gaps), which this ruling closes.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-09-28. No later ruling amends it.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **Only navigation opens a tab, so a screen reader cursor that moves focus opens nothing (2026-09-28).** Approved by the maintainer as option C of decision 09, with the maintainer's choice that an explicit `activationMode="automatic"` take the same behaviour as the default. It amends [floating-surface-wraps](#floating-surface-wraps), which listed Tabs among the thin wraps, and it closes item (3) of [documentation-and-markup-gaps](#documentation-and-markup-gaps), the missing Tabs `priorArt`. Radix's automatic mode opens a tab on every focus event, whatever moved the focus (Radix #1047). VoiceOver moves keyboard focus as its cursor reads, so a VoiceOver user who read across the tab row opened each tab on the way. **Measured before**, in the test browser on the Tabs Keyboard page: a bare `focus()` on Activity, with no key and no click, moved `aria-selected` from Overview to Activity and swapped the panel. **The change.** `Tabs.Root` holds the value, controlled or uncontrolled, runs Radix in manual mode, and shares an activation context. `Tabs.Trigger` marks an unmodified ArrowLeft, ArrowRight, ArrowUp, ArrowDown, Home, End, PageUp or PageDown keydown, the keys Radix's roving focus moves on, and a focus that arrives while the mark stands opens that tab. A key that Radix ignores, one with no focus intent for the list's orientation such as ArrowUp in a horizontal list, drops the mark in a microtask, because Radix's roving handler runs after the wrap's and prevents the default exactly when the key has a focus intent. Otherwise the mark clears 100ms later, after the zero-delay timeout in which Radix moves roving focus, so a focus from any later cursor move meets no mark. Enter, Space and a pointer press open a tab through Radix's own manual handlers. A click that no press began, the click VoiceOver sends on VO+Space and the click `element.click()` sends, opens its tab too. The click that ends a pointer press, Enter or Space selects nothing, because Radix answered the press already, the shape [dropdown-assistive-click](#dropdown-assistive-click) gives DropdownMenu. Without that skip, a controlled Root that re-renders a task late, a router-backed tab among them, heard `onValueChange` twice for one click. A consumer who passes `activationMode="manual"` keeps manual, so arrow keys move focus only. This follows the rule of the WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices automatic tabs example, which opens a tab in its keydown and click handlers and registers no focus listener. The wrap reaches the same rule by another route: the keydown only marks, and the focus that Radix then moves opens the tab. **Measured after**, the same way: the bare focus leaves Overview selected and its panel shown, with the focus ring on Activity. Driven by real key and mouse input through the Chrome DevTools Protocol, ArrowRight opened Activity, End opened Settings, Home opened Overview, a mouse click opened Activity, ArrowLeft opened Overview, and ArrowRight then Enter left Activity open. On the final code PageDown opened Settings, PageUp opened Overview, and a bare focus on Settings straight after an ArrowUp left Activity open. The Keyboard page, the Props table and the History page of Tabs state the rule. **Guarded by** `_internal/Tabs behavior` → ScreenReaderFocus, which holds seven arms in both appearance lanes: a bare focus opens nothing, ArrowRight opens the tab it reaches, a bare focus straight after an ArrowUp that Radix ignores opens nothing, a bare focus 300ms after an End on the last tab opens nothing, `element.click()` opens its tab, a Root given `activationMode="manual"` opens nothing on ArrowRight, and a controlled Root that declines every change hears one `onValueChange` for a pointer press and its click, one for Enter and its click, and one for a bare click. Each arm went red alone: Radix in automatic mode failed the bare focus arm with Activity selected, a trigger that never marks failed the arrow arm, a microtask that keeps the mark failed the ignored key arm with Settings selected, a mark that never clears failed the End arm with Overview selected, a click handler that selects nothing failed the click arm, a click that skips no press failed the press arm with two calls, and a manual flag forced off failed the manual arm with Activity selected. All seven went green on restore, and the Roving play still passes unchanged. **Limits.** No VoiceOver run confirms the fix yet. Step 1 of the VoiceOver pass is that check, with the VoiceOver setting on that makes keyboard focus follow the cursor, and [wcag-claim-scope](#wcag-claim-scope) keeps its assistive-technology item open until the pass runs. The mark relies on Radix moving roving focus within 100ms of the keydown, which its zero-delay timeout does today. Home or PageUp on the first tab, and End or PageDown on the last, have a focus intent and move no focus, so a focus from any source within 100ms after one of them still opens its tab. Radix's any-focus automatic mode is no longer reachable through the wrap. `Tabs.Nav` links navigate and do not change.

### chat-layout-tag

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`. **Ruled.** 2026-09-22.

**`ChatLayout` takes an `as` prop with the closed union `"div" | "main" | "section"`, and `ChatMessage` and `ChatSystemMessage` take none.**

**Why ChatLayout.** A dedicated chat page with no `AppShell` above it needs the shell to be the page's `main`, so the skip link and the landmark are right. The alternative, a consumer wrapper, costs a second height contract that fails silently.

**What you see.** At every tag the root keeps `rt-ds-chat-layout`, and the transcript, the composer, the `role="log"` tab stop and the imperative handle all hold. The default renders a `div`, identical to the render before the prop.

**Refused.** `ChatMessage` and `ChatSystemMessage` get no `as`, against the recommendation of [api-seam-criterion](#api-seam-criterion), on measurement: the wrapper a consumer would write instead paints identically, and an `li` notice draws an axe list violation.

**Why closed.** Autocomplete gives an agent the valid set, and a tag the component's CSS does not survive is a compile error rather than a broken layout. The union follows `Item`, which swaps its own root tag, and `BreadcrumbItem` sets no precedent, because its open `ElementType` swaps the link inside the `li`, not the component's own root.

**Caution.** An unnamed `section` is not exposed as a region, so the prop, the Props table and the control description all say to name it.

**Changed from.** [api-seam-criterion](#api-seam-criterion) recommended `as` for all three components. Testing each need again before building it, as that ruling requires, changed the answer for two of them.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-09-22. No later ruling amends it.

**Evidence.** The entry before the rewrite of 2026-10-01:

> **Three components were recommended a tag valve and only one earned it (2026-09-22).** [api-seam-criterion](#api-seam-criterion) recommended `as` for `ChatLayout`, `ChatMessage` and `ChatSystemMessage`, under the standing rule that a pattern is standardized only where it fits the component, and that every component stays easy to use for people and for agents. Re-testing each need before implementing it, which [api-seam-criterion](#api-seam-criterion) requires, changed the answer for two of the three. **`ChatLayout` earned it:** a dedicated chat page with no `AppShell` above it needs the shell to BE the page's `main`, so the skip link and the landmark are right, and the alternative of a consumer wrapper costs a second height contract that fails silently. Measured at all three tags: the root is the requested element, keeps `rt-ds-chat-layout`, and the transcript, the composer, the `role="log"` tab stop and the imperative handle all survive. The default render is byte-identical to the previous one. **`ChatMessage` and `ChatSystemMessage` were REFUSED**, against the recommendation, on measurement rather than taste: the wrapping element a consumer would write instead paints identically, and swapping the notice to an `li` draws an axe list violation, so the swap trades one correct idiom for a broken one. The union is CLOSED, `"div" | "main" | "section"`, following `Item`, which is the only shipped component that swaps its own root tag. **A closed union is the choice that serves both audiences:** autocomplete hands an agent the valid set, and a tag the component's CSS does not survive is a compile error rather than a broken layout. `BreadcrumbItem` carries an open `ElementType` and is NOT precedent, because it swaps the link inside the `li` rather than a component's own root. One footgun is documented rather than coded around: an unnamed `section` is exposed as nothing, so the prop, the Props table and the control description all say to name it.

### token-pressed-state

**Tags.** `COMPONENTS`, `ACCESSIBILITY`. **Ruled.** 2026-10-01.

**A clickable Token takes `pressed` and becomes a toggle, and a pressed Token shows a tinted fill and bold strong ink at the one width it keeps in both states.**

**Markup.** `pressed` is allowed only with `onClick`, so it is a type error with `href` or with neither. The body button carries `aria-pressed` when the prop is given and no attribute when it is omitted, and its label stays the same in both states.

**What you see.**

- A pressed Token paints `--ds-fill-selected-subtle` under `--ds-text-strong` at `--ds-font-weight-strong`, the paint of a pressed ToggleButton, and shows no glyph.
- A Token given `pressed` keeps one width in both states, the width of its label at the bold weight, so a press moves no Token beside it. A Token with no `pressed` keeps the width of its label at the resting weight.
- The fill does not change on hover, and the focus ring is the same ring as on a Token at rest, as [focus-ring](#focus-ring) sets it.
- A disabled pressed Token keeps the disabled dim and the weight.
- Under forced colours a pressed Token paints `Highlight` under `HighlightText`.
- A screen reader announces a pressed Token as pressed and reads its label once.

**Why.** A filter row built from Tokens had no pressed state, and a button with no `aria-pressed` gave a screen reader no state to announce. The tint alone reads 1.23 to 1.87:1 against the page over all 27 toolbar accents in both appearances, so colour cannot carry the state, and the weight carries it beside the colour. The label reads 8.61:1 or more on the tint. A check mark before the label widened a pressed Token by 18px and moved every Token after it, so the label holds its bold width at rest instead, as the label of a ToggleButton does.

**Guidance.** The maintainer approved a pressed state for Token and chose, on 2026-10-01, a check mark as its cue beside colour over a bolder label alone. The maintainer then chose, on 2026-10-01, a pressed Token that keeps one width and shows no check mark, after seeing the check widen each tag and move the row.

**Changed from.** A clickable Token was a button with no `aria-pressed`, and nothing in its paint showed a pressed state. Before the second choice, a pressed Token showed a 12px check mark before its label, which widened it by 18px and moved every Token after it.

**Status.** Ruled 2026-10-01. It amends [token-chip](#token-chip) with the `pressed` prop. No later ruling amends it.

- Revised on 2026-10-01: a pressed Token shows no check mark and keeps the width it has at rest.

**Evidence.** The entry as first written:

> **A clickable Token takes `pressed` and becomes a toggle, and a pressed Token shows a check mark before its label beside a tinted fill and bold strong ink.**
>
> **Markup.** `pressed` is allowed only with `onClick`, so it is a type error with `href` or with neither. The body button carries `aria-pressed` when the prop is given and no attribute when it is omitted, and its label stays the same in both states.
>
> **What you see.**
>
> - A pressed Token paints `--ds-fill-selected-subtle` under `--ds-text-strong` at `--ds-font-weight-strong`, the paint of a pressed ToggleButton, and shows a 12px check mark before its label.
> - The fill does not change on hover, and the focus ring is the same ring as on a Token at rest, as [focus-ring](#focus-ring) sets it.
> - A disabled pressed Token keeps the disabled dim, the weight and the check mark.
> - Under forced colours a pressed Token paints `Highlight` under `HighlightText`.
> - A screen reader announces a pressed Token as pressed.
>
> **Why.** A filter row built from Tokens had no pressed state, and a button with no `aria-pressed` gave a screen reader no state to announce. The tint alone reads 1.23 to 1.87:1 against the page over all 27 toolbar accents in both appearances, so colour cannot carry the state, and the check mark and the weight carry it beside the colour. The label reads 8.61:1 or more on the tint, and the check mark the same, since it takes the ink of the label.
>
> **Guidance.** The maintainer approved a pressed state for Token and chose, on 2026-10-01, a check mark as its cue beside colour over a bolder label alone.
>
> **Changed from.** A clickable Token was a button with no `aria-pressed`, and nothing in its paint showed a pressed state.
>
